bdag po'i 'bras bu.acip: ,BDAG PO'I 'BRAS BU'AM DBANG GI 'BRAS BU NI, SROG BCAD PA LAS PHYI SNOD KYI 'JIG RTEN GYI BZA' BTUNG DANG SMAN DANG 'BRAS BU LA SOGS PA MTHU CHUNG BA DANG BSNYEMS PA DANG NUS PA DANG STOBS CHUNG BA DANG 'JU DKA' ZHING NAD BSKYED PAS SEMS CAN PHAL CHER TSE MA ZAD PAR YANG 'CHI BAR 'GYUR BA DANG,
bdag po'i 'bras bu.wylie: bdag po'i 'bras bu'am dbang gi 'bras bu ni, srog bcad pa las phyi snod kyi 'jig rten gyi bza' btung dang sman dang 'bras bu la sogs pa mthu chung ba dang bsnyems pa dang nus pa dang stobs chung ba dang 'ju dka' zhing nad bskyed pas sems can phal cher tshe ma zad par yang 'chi bar 'gyur ba dang
bdag po'i 'bras bu.english: Next is what we call the "environmental" or "dominant" consequence. Here for example the consequence of killing expresses itself in the outer world around you. Food, drink, medicine, the crops in the fields, and other such things have very little power; they are always inferior; they have little nutrition or potency; they are hard to digest, and they cause disease in you. Because of this the majority of the living beings around you die before reaching the end of a full life.

bla ma gong ma.acip: ,BLA MA GONG MA RNAMS MIR SKYES NA YANG SROG GCOD SOGS DE DAG LA DGA' BAR 'GYUR BA BYED PA RGYU MTHUN GYI 'BRAS BU DANG SNGA MA RNAMS MYONG BA RGYU MTHUN GYI 'BRAS BUR BZHED DO,
bla ma gong ma.wylie: bla ma gong ma rnams mir skyes na yang srog gcod sogs de dag la dga' bar 'gyur ba byed pa rgyu mthun gyi 'bras bu dang snga ma rnams myong ba rgyu mthun gyi 'bras bur bzhed do

bla ma gong ma.english: I raise this offering To the holy lips Of the Protectors bound by pledge: Those on whom the Lamas of the past relied; Those whom They reached; Those who swore to protect All who ever saw the Buddhas, And all who ever heard the Dharma, And all who ever took themselves To the Community of beings Who have seen emptiness. I offer it to These, Who swore to protect the teachings, And the four groups of followers. Om ah hung.

bla ma gong ma.acip: DE LTAR YIN NA MA SBAS PAR GSAL BAR BYAS PA GANG DU YOD SNYAM NA, DE NI RGYAL PO AINDRA BH'U TI'I PHAG MO ZHAL GNYIS MA'I SNGAGS BTU LAS BYUNG ZHING, PHAG MO GZHAN GYI LAM LA MA TSANG BA THAMS CAD 'DI NYID NAS KHA BSKANG DGOS PAR BLA MA GONG MA RNAMS GSUNG GSUNGS,
bla ma gong ma.wylie: de ltar yin na ma sbas par gsal bar byas pa gang du yod snyam na, de ni rgyal po aindra bhU ti'i phag mo zhal gnyis ma'i sngags btu las byung zhing, phag mo gzhan gyi lam la ma tshang ba thams cad 'di nyid nas kha bskang dgos par bla ma gong ma rnams gsung gsungs
bla ma gong ma.english: "If that's the case," one may continue, "then where is it that these words are taken out of hiding, and revealed?"  It is found in the explanation of the construction of the secret words of the two headed Sow, composed by Indrabhuti.  And the Lamas of old, said our Lama, have spoken that it is precisely these secret words that should be used to fill anything lacking in the teachings of any of the other Sows.

bla ma gong ma.acip: 'DI YI MAN NGAG LA GTZO BOR MDZAD PA'I BLA MA GONG MA RNAMS, BDE MCHOG LA MDZAD PA MANG STE, SGAM PO PAS NI ZANGS DKAR GYI SLOB MA MAR YUL BLO LDAN LA BRTEN NAS, ZANGS DKAR GYI LUGS KYI BDE MCHOG DANG, DPAL PHAG MO GRU PAS NI, LO CHUNG NAS BRGYUD PA MAR LUGS KYI BDE MCHOG DANG, CHOS RJE 'BRI GUNG PAS NI, MAR DO NAS BRGYUD PA'I COG RO LUGS KYI BDE MCHOG LA MDZAD SNANG STE, DE GSUM GA YANG DPAL L'U AI PA'I LUGS KYI BDE MCHOG DRUG CU RTZA GNYIS PA'I DKYIL 'KHOR LA BRTEN PA'O,,
bla ma gong ma.wylie: 'di yi man ngag la gtso bor mdzad pa'i bla ma gong ma rnams, bde mchog la mdzad pa mang ste, sgam po pas ni zangs dkar gyi slob ma mar yul blo ldan la brten nas, zangs dkar gyi lugs kyi bde mchog dang, dpal phag mo gru pas ni, lo chung nas brgyud pa mar lugs kyi bde mchog dang, chos rje 'bri gung pas ni, mar do nas brgyud pa'i cog ro lugs kyi bde mchog la mdzad snang ste, de gsum ga yang dpal lU ai pa'i lugs kyi bde mchog drug cu rtsa gnyis pa'i dkyil 'khor la brten pa'o
bla ma gong ma.english: Among the Lamas of the past who made the advices on this practice their principal practice, there were many that followed the way of Highest Bliss.  Gampopa sat at the feet of Maryul Londen, a disciple of Sangkar, and learned the secret teachings of Highest Bliss according to the system of Sangkar.  The glorious Pakmo Drupa practiced the teachings of Highest Bliss according to the system of Marpa, as it was passed down from Lochung.  And the Dharma lord Drigungpa also followed the way of Highest Bliss, according to the system of Chokro, as passed down from Mardo.  All three of these Lamas also kept the practice of the secret world of the 62 Angels of Highest Bliss, in keeping with the system of the glorious Luipa. [Translator's note: The places of Marpa (Mardo), Gampopa, and Pakmo Drupa in the lineage of the Six Practices have been discussed above.  Maryul Londen and Sangkar have also appeared before.  Chokro Chukyi Gyeltsen (1108-1176)  is described in A Treasury of the Names of the Wise and Accomplished Beings Who Appeared Over the Years in the Snowy Land as having studied the teachings of Highest Bliss with Namka Uw, the spiritual son of Marpa.  Lochung Lekpay Sherab (fl. 1050), whose first name means "Younger Translator," was the assistant of the "Great Translator" Rinchen Sangpo (958-1055).]

bla ma gong ma.acip: DE YANG MING DANG TSIG GIS BTAGS PA TZAM LA 'JOG PA DANG, DNGOS POR SNANG BA'I RTEN 'BREL DANG, RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA MED PA'I STONG PA GNYIS, NGO BO GCIG TU GNAS PAS SNANG STONG, GCIG GIS GCIG MA DOR BAR GSUNGS PA NI, LUGS 'DI'I BLA MA GONG MA'I KHYAD CHOS CIG TU SNANG BAS,
bla ma gong ma.wylie: de yang ming dang tshig gis btags pa tsam la 'jog pa dang, dngos por snang ba'i rten 'brel dang, rang bzhin gyis grub pa med pa'i stong pa gnyis, ngo bo gcig tu gnas pas snang stong, gcig gis gcig ma dor bar gsungs pa ni, lugs 'di'i bla ma gong ma'i khyad chos cig tu snang bas
bla ma gong ma.english: And all of this is established only through names and words.  The fact of dependent origination, which appears to us as different things, and the fact of emptiness, where nothing has any nature of its own, exist as a single essence: the appearance of things and emptiness.  The teachings which say that neither of these two obviates the other are an extraordinary feature among the Lamas of this system in days gone by.

bla ma gong ma.acip: BSGOM RGYU'I LAM GYI DBANG DU BYAS NAS BYED NA, RDZOGS RIM GYI LAM DKYUS MA'I DBANG DU BYAS PA CIG DANG, DE LA BOGS 'BYIN PA'I THABS SPYOD PA DANG GNYIS DGOS PA'I PHYI MA 'DI, LUGS 'DI'I BLA MA GONG MA GDAMS NGAG TZAM LA GTZO BOR MDZAD PA RNAMS KYI MAN NGAG PHAL CHER LA MI SNANG YANG, MAR LUGS KYI RGYUD KYI BSHAD SROL 'DZIN PA RNAMS KYIS BSHAD 'DUG PA BZHIN DGOS SO,,
bla ma gong ma.wylie: bsgom rgyu'i lam gyi dbang du byas nas byed na, rdzogs rim gyi lam dkyus ma'i dbang du byas pa cig dang, de la bogs 'byin pa'i thabs spyod pa dang gnyis dgos pa'i phyi ma 'di, lugs 'di'i bla ma gong ma gdams ngag tsam la gtso bor mdzad pa rnams kyi man ngag phal cher la mi snang yang, mar lugs kyi rgyud kyi bshad srol 'dzin pa rnams kyis bshad 'dug pa bzhin dgos so
bla ma gong ma.english: If though you make the division according to the path to be practicied, then you would have to say there are two sections: one relating to the normal course of the stage of completion, and a second concerning special methods which can be used to ignite this course. Now the second of these two cannot be found in the great majority of the instructions of those Lamas of the past who relied primarily upon the method of oral instruction.  Nonetheless, it has been elucidated by those who have maintained Lord Marpa's system of explaining the secret teachings.  This is what you should follow.

bsnyems pa.english: Next is what we call the "environmental" or "dominant" consequence. Here for example the consequence of killing expresses itself in the outer world around you. Because of this the majority of the living beings around you die before reaching the end of a full life.

bsnyems pa.acip: HA S+YE'I SKABS, RDO RJE KHU TSUR GNYIS KHA PHYIR BSTAN TE KHA 'GRAM GNYIS SU BZHAG PA BZHAD PA'I TSUL DANG, LA S+YE'I SKABS, RDO RJE KHU TSUR GNYIS DKUR BZHAG STE BSNYEMS PA'I TSUL DANG, GI RTI'I SKABS RDO RJE KHU TSUR GNYIS KYIS SNYING GA'I THAD DU TING SHAGS 'KHROL BA'I TSUL DANG,
bsnyems pa.wylie: ha s+ye'i skabs, rdo rje khu tshur gnyis kha phyir bstan te kha 'gram gnyis su bzhag pa bzhad pa'i tshul dang, la s+ye'i skabs, rdo rje khu tshur gnyis dkur bzhag ste bsnyems pa'i tshul dang, gi rti'i skabs rdo rje khu tshur gnyis kyis snying ga'i thad du ting shags 'khrol ba'i tshul dang
bsnyems pa.english: For hasye, make your two hands into diamond fists and face them away from you on either side of your jaws, to imitate laughter.  At lasye, put your two diamond fists on your hips, in the way of a dancer.  For girti, keep the two diamond fists out in front of your heart as though you where playing hand cymbals.

byed pa rgyu mthun.acip: ,BLA MA GONG MA RNAMS MIR SKYES NA YANG SROG GCOD SOGS DE DAG LA DGA' BAR 'GYUR BA BYED PA RGYU MTHUN GYI 'BRAS BU DANG SNGA MA RNAMS MYONG BA RGYU MTHUN GYI 'BRAS BUR BZHED DO,

byed pa rgyu mthun.english: Great lamas of the past have expressed the position that it is a consequence of consistent action where as a karmic result of killing you become someone who takes pleasure in killing and the rest. byed pa rgyu mthun.acip: DER MA ZAD SDIG PA RE RE LA'ANG RNAM SMIN DANG, MYONG BA DANG BYED PA RGYU MTHUN, BDAG 'BRAS TE 'BRAS BU BZHI BZHI 'BYUNG,
byed pa rgyu mthun.wylie: der ma zad sdig pa re re la'ang rnam smin dang, myong ba dang byed pa rgyu mthun, bdag 'bras te 'bras bu bzhi bzhi 'byung
byed pa rgyu mthun.english: And that's not all.  The bad deed you do may be only one, but every bad deed has four separate consequences: one result where the karma actually ripens back on to you; two results where you undergo painful personal experiences, and are plagued by bad habits, that continue the same flavor of what you did wrong; and finally a result that affects the very environment in which you live.

dga' bar.acip: MI MDZA' BA NAD KYIS BTAB PA LA DGA' BAR SEMS PA DANG, MI MDZA' BA NAD SOS NA MI DGA' BAR SEMS PA DANG, NAD PA LA SMAN MA YIN PA BYIN PA DANG, ZAS MA ZHU BAR BSTABS PA,

dga' bar.english: Being happy when someone you don't like falls ill. Being unhappy when someone you don't like recovers from a sickness. Giving a sick person food which would be difficult for them to digest, and thus hurt their recovery.

dga' bar.acip: ,TSE'I MTHAR 'CHI BDAG GIS BCOM NAS 'JIG RTEN PHA ROL TU 'GRO BAR MA ZAD DE'I BAR RNAMS SU YANG 'GRO 'CHAG NYAL GSUM GANG BYED KYANG TSE BRI NAS MI 'GRO BA'I SKABS YE MED PAS, MNGAL DU ZHUGS PA NAS 'GO BZUNG STE SKAD CIG TZAM YANG MI SDOD PAR 'JIG RTEN PHA ROL TU KHA BLTAS NAS 'GRO BA YIN NO, , DES NA BAR GYI GSON PA'ANG NA BA DANG RGA BA'I PHO NYA BAS KHRID NAS 'CHI BA'I PHYIR DU 'GRO BA KHO NAR ZAD PAS GSON PA'I SKABS LA 'JIG RTEN PHYI MAR MI 'GRO BA'I SDOD PAR BZUNG NAS DGA' BAR MI BYA STE, DPER NA, BRAG MTHON PO'I RTZE MO NAS LHUNG BA'I TSE, SA LA MA LHUNG BA'I BAR SNANG LA 'GRO BA'I SKABS DE LA DGA' BAR MI 'OS PA BZHIN NO,
dga' bar.wylie: tshe'i mthar 'chi bdag gis bcom nas 'jig rten pha rol tu 'gro bar ma zad de'i bar rnams su yang 'gro 'chag nyal gsum gang byed kyang tshe bri nas mi 'gro ba'i skabs ye med pas, mngal du zhugs pa nas 'go bzung ste skad cig tsam yang mi sdod par 'jig rten pha rol tu kha bltas nas 'gro ba yin no, , des na bar gyi gson pa'ang na ba dang rga ba'i pho nya bas khrid nas 'chi ba'i phyir du 'gro ba kho nar zad pas gson pa'i skabs la 'jig rten phyi mar mi 'gro ba'i sdod par bzung nas dga' bar mi bya ste, dper na, brag mthon po'i rtse mo nas lhung ba'i tshe, sa la ma lhung ba'i bar snang la 'gro ba'i skabs de la dga' bar mi 'os pa bzhin no
dga' bar.english: At the end of our life, the Lord of Death comes and destroys us, and we travel on to our next life. But there is something else too that happens all during the interim, during every hour of our life here. There is not a single moment at all when our lifetime is not slipping away, when it is not getting shorter and shorter, even as we go somewhere, or stay somewhere, waking or sleeping. So in a sense we are always on our way to our next life, we are travelling there now, and we have been on the move every second from the day we first entered our mother's womb. Therefore even in these days, while we still live, we are living only to die: those emissaries of death, the ones called Sickness and Aging, are dragging us towards him. Don't take any comfort then in the fact that you haven't died yet, don't get the idea that you are staying anywhere, and that you haven't yet started off on your journey to the next life. You are like a man who just fell off the edge of a great rock crag; you would be foolish to take some comfort from the fact that you are still in mid-air, and haven't hit ground yet.

dga' bar.acip: ,DE LTAR NA TSE 'DI'I PHUN TSOGS THAMS CAD NI RMI LAM THUN GCIG NA BDE BA SPYAD BSAD NAS DRAN PA LTAR 'CHI BA'I DUS SU DRAN PA'I YUL TZAM DU 'GYUR LA, 'CHI BA'I DGRA NI DGAG TU MED PAR NGES PAR 'ONG NA CI'I PHYIR TSE 'DI'I BSLU BRID LA DGA' BAR BYA SNYAM DU BSAMS TE CHOS BYA DGOS PA LA THAG BCAD CING ZHE DAM MANG DU BYA STE, SKYES RABS LAS, KYE MA'O 'JIG RTEN NYON MONGS DAG, GNAS PA MI BRTAN DGA' MI 'GYUR, , KU MU TA YI DPAL 'DI YANG , , DRAN PAR BYA BA NYID DU 'GYUR, , 'GRO BA 'DI LTA BUR NI 'KHOD PA LA, , SKYE BO 'JIGS PA MED PA NGO MTSAR KYE, , LAM RNAMS THAMS CAD 'CHI BDAG NYID KYIS BKAG, DOGS PA MED PAR RAB TU DGA' ZHING SPYOD, , NA DANG RGA DANG 'CHI BA'I GNOD BYED DGRA, , MTHU CHEN DGAG TU MI NUS YOD BZHIN LA, , 'JIG RTEN PHA ROL NYAM NGAR NGES 'GRO NA, , SEMS SHES SU ZHIG 'DI LA DGA' BAR SEMS, , ZHES DANG ,
dga' bar.wylie: de ltar na tshe 'di'i phun tshogs thams cad ni rmi lam thun gcig na bde ba spyad bsad nas dran pa ltar 'chi ba'i dus su dran pa'i yul tsam du 'gyur la, 'chi ba'i dgra ni dgag tu med par nges par 'ong na ci'i phyir tshe 'di'i bslu brid la dga' bar bya snyam du bsams te chos bya dgos pa la thag bcad cing zhe dam mang du bya ste, skyes rabs las, kye ma'o 'jig rten nyon mongs dag, gnas pa mi brtan dga' mi 'gyur, , ku mu ta yi dpal 'di yang , , dran par bya ba nyid du 'gyur, , 'gro ba 'di lta bur ni 'khod pa la, , skye bo 'jigs pa med pa ngo mtshar kye, , lam rnams thams cad 'chi bdag nyid kyis bkag, dogs pa med par rab tu dga' zhing spyod, , na dang rga dang 'chi ba'i gnod byed dgra, , mthu chen dgag tu mi nus yod bzhin la, , 'jig rten pha rol nyam ngar nges 'gro na, , sems shes su zhig 'di la dga' bar sems, , zhes dang
dga' bar.english: And so all the good things of this life are like the happiness within one night's dream: you wake, and then it's nothing more than a memory. The time comes to die, and everything good you ever had lives only in a dim remembrance. This great enemy, death, will surely come; nothing can stop him. You should contemplate this fact--try to wonder, "Why do I take such pleasure in the lie of this life?" Make up your mind that you absolutely must now practice some Dharma; swear it to yourself, continually. Remember the Birth Stories, where it says: Alas, you worldly ones so full of affliction of the mind; Why do you take such pleasure in a land of shifting sands? The shining glory of the kumuda bloom, opening to the moon, Soon enough turns nothing more than a simple memory. It's something of a pure amazement too that all of us Thrust into a life like this are not consumed by total fear; Damn the Lord of Death, who stands and blocks all pathways out, While we oblivious feel content, and have an enjoyable day. We all share enemies, dreadfully powerful, ones we cannot stop: Their names are sickness, age, and death; they attack us even now. If it's certain that we are headed for agony in the world beyond, How could anyone with a mind be content in the one here now?

dga' bar.acip: ,BLA MA GONG MA RNAMS MIR SKYES NA YANG SROG GCOD SOGS DE DAG LA DGA' BAR 'GYUR BA BYED PA RGYU MTHUN GYI 'BRAS BU DANG SNGA MA RNAMS MYONG BA RGYU MTHUN GYI 'BRAS BUR BZHED DO,

dga' bar.english: Great lamas of the past have expressed the position that the "consistent" consequence is where, even if you do manage to take birth as a human, you enjoy killing things, and so on. They say then that experiencing the various results just listed is a "ripened" consequence [the second rgyu mthun here is likely a text error for rnam smin; this is the corrected reading].

dga' bar.acip: ,BDAG GIS DI RING SKYOB PA THAMS CAD KYI, ,SPYAN SNGAR 'GRO BA BDE GSHEGS NYID DANG NI, ,BAR DU BDE LA MGRON DU BOS ZIN GYIS, ,LHA DANG LHA MIN LA SOGS DGA' BAR GYIS,
dga' bar.wylie: bdag gis di ring skyob pa thams cad kyi, ,spyan sngar 'gro ba bde gshegs nyid dang ni, ,bar du bde la mgron du bos zin gyis, ,lha dang lha min la sogs dga' bar gyis
dga' bar.english: I stand today in the presence Of all the Protectors. I invite every living creature As my guest, to partake In the very state of Those Who have Gone to Bliss, and in Happiness until they reach it. I call on every pleasure being, On near pleasure beings, and All such creatures, to take joy In this as well.

dga' bar.acip: ,GNYIS PA NI, BDAG GIS DE RING RGYAL BA SRAS DANG BCAS PA'I SKYOB PA THAMS CAD KYI SPYAN SNGAR 'GRO BA SEMS CAN THAMS CAD MTHAR THUG PHAN BDE THAMS CAD RDZOGS PA'I BDE BAR GSHEGS PA NYID DANG NI DE MA THOB KYI BAR DU'ANG LHA MI'I BDE BA LA TSIM PAR LONGS SPYAD PAS CHOG PA'I MGRON DU BOS ZIN GYIS DENG PHYIN CHAD LHA DANG LHA MIN DANG LTO 'PHYE LA SOGS PA RNAMS KYANG DGA' BAR GYIS SHIG CES GZHAN LA DGA' BA BSKYED DU GZHUG PA'O,
dga' bar.wylie: gnyis pa ni, bdag gis de ring rgyal ba sras dang bcas pa'i skyob pa thams cad kyi spyan sngar 'gro ba sems can thams cad mthar thug phan bde thams cad rdzogs pa'i bde bar gshegs pa nyid dang ni de ma thob kyi bar du'ang lha mi'i bde ba la tshim par longs spyad pas chog pa'i mgron du bos zin gyis deng phyin chad lha dang lha min dang lto 'phye la sogs pa rnams kyang dga' bar gyis shig ces gzhan la dga' ba bskyed du gzhug pa'o
dga' bar.english: With this we have reached how to bring joy to others. I stand today in the presence of all the Protectors: the victorious Buddhas, and their sons and daughters. And in your presence I invite every living creature, every being, to come here as my guest, for I will serve them to their heart's content the very state of Those Who have Gone to Bliss: the ultimate culmination of every kind of help and happiness. And until they reach this state I offer them as well to partake, to their own satisfaction, all the happiness that can be found among humans and pleasure beings. And once I have made this invitation, I ask others to take joy as well: I call on every pleasure being, and near pleasure being, and serpent-like naga, and all such creatures to feel gladness.

dga' bar.acip: ,DE LTAR YUN RING RGYUN CHAGS DGRAR GYUR PA, ,GNOD PA'I TSOGS RAB 'PHEL BA'I RGYU GCIG PU, ,BDAG GI SNYING LA NGES PAR GNAS 'CHA' NA, ,'KHOR BAR 'JIGS MED DGA' BAR GA LA 'GYUR,
dga' bar.wylie: de ltar yun ring rgyun chags dgrar gyur pa, ,gnod pa'i tshogs rab 'phel ba'i rgyu gcig pu, ,bdag gi snying la nges par gnas 'cha' na, ,'khor bar 'jigs med dga' bar ga la 'gyur
dga' bar.english: They've been thus my constant enemy for a very long time; And are the one single cause that feeds and nourishes The entire mass of harmful things. How could I ever be free of all the terrors Of cyclic life, and feel gladness so long as They are rooted and fixed in my very heart?

dga' bar.acip: ,GNYIS PA LA GNYIS, SEMS LA GNOD PA BYED PA DANG , LUS LA GNOD PA BYED PAR BSAM PA'O, , DANG PO NI, DE LTAR YUN RING PO THOG MA MED PA NAS RGYUN CHAGS SU DGRAR GYUR PA SDUG BSNGAL LA SOGS PA'I GNOD PA'I TSOGS THAMS CAD RAB TU 'PHEL BA'I RGYU GCIG PU ZLA MED PA BDAG GI SNYING PA LA NGES PAR GNAS 'CHA' ZHING RTEN NA 'KHOR BAR 'JIGS PA MED PA DANG YID DGA' BAR GA LA 'GYUR BDE BA'I SKABS MED PAS NYON MONGS GZHOM PA LA BRTZON PAR BYA'O,
dga' bar.wylie: gnyis pa la gnyis, sems la gnod pa byed pa dang , lus la gnod pa byed par bsam pa'o, , dang po ni, de ltar yun ring po thog ma med pa nas rgyun chags su dgrar gyur pa sdug bsngal la sogs pa'i gnod pa'i tshogs thams cad rab tu 'phel ba'i rgyu gcig pu zla med pa bdag gi snying pa la nges par gnas 'cha' zhing rten na 'khor bar 'jigs pa med pa dang yid dga' bar ga la 'gyur bde ba'i skabs med pas nyon mongs gzhom pa la brtson par bya'o
dga' bar.english: There are two parts to the explanation of why it is wrong to tolerate the mental afflictions: considering how they hurt the mind, and considering how they hurt the body. Here is the first. They--the mental afflictions--have been thus my constant enemy for a very long time, for time with no beginning: they are the one single and matchless cause that feeds and nourishes the entire mass of harmful things, of suffering and all the rest. How could it ever happen then, so long as these afflictions are rooted and fixed in my very heart, that I could ever reach any point where I was free of all the terrors of cyclic life, and feel any kind of gladness? Happiness would be an impossibility. I must therefore make true efforts in destroying my mental afflictions.

dga' bar.acip: ,GNYIS PA NI, GANG LA YID MI BDE SKYE BA'I YUL DE LA GAL TE BCOS SU YOD NA NI DE LA MI DGA' BAR BYA BA'I RGYU CI ZHIG YOD, DE MA THAG BCOS PAS YID MI BDE BA MED PAR 'GYUR BA'I PHYIR RO, , GAL TE BCOS SU MED NA YANG DE LA MI DGA' BA BYAS PAS CI PHAN TE NAM MKHA' THOGS BCAS KYIS STONG PA LA MI DGA' BA BYAS KYANG MI PHAN PA BZHIN NO,
dga' bar.wylie: gnyis pa ni, gang la yid mi bde skye ba'i yul de la gal te bcos su yod na ni de la mi dga' bar bya ba'i rgyu ci zhig yod, de ma thag bcos pas yid mi bde ba med par 'gyur ba'i phyir ro, , gal te bcos su med na yang de la mi dga' ba byas pas ci phan te nam mkha' thogs bcas kyis stong pa la mi dga' ba byas kyang mi phan pa bzhin no
dga' bar.english: Let us consider any of the objects over which we feel upset. If there is something you can do about it, then why should you ever feel upset at all? You could take the necessary action to fix it immediately, and never need to feel upset. If on the other hand there is nothing you can do about it, then what is the use of being upset? It would be as useless as getting upset at empty space, at a place where nothing was. Contemplation Four Perfect patience is like any other habit, and can be developed with practice

dga' bar.acip: ,DANG PO NI, GANG ZAG GZHAN GYIS BDAG GI DGRA BO LA YON TAN DANG LDAN PA YIN NO ZHES BSTOD NAS GAL TE BSTOD PA PO DE NYID KYANG YID DGA' BA'I BDE BA THOB NA BDAG GI YID KHYOD KYANG NI DGRA DE BSTOD NAS CI'I PHYIR GANG ZAG GZHAN DE LTAR DGA' BAR MI BYED DE DE LTAR BYAS NA KHYOD NYID GZHAN GYI YON TAN LA DGA' BA'I BDE BA 'DI, MA 'ONGS PA NA BDE BA'I 'BYUNG GNAS KHA NA MA THO BA MED PAR RGYAL BA SRAS BCAS YON TAN DANG LDAN PA RNAMS KYIS GNANG ZHING BSNGAGS PA DANG , GDUL BYA GZHAN SDUD PA'I MCHOG KYANG YIN NO,
dga' bar.wylie: dang po ni, gang zag gzhan gyis bdag gi dgra bo la yon tan dang ldan pa yin no zhes bstod nas gal te bstod pa po de nyid kyang yid dga' ba'i bde ba thob na bdag gi yid khyod kyang ni dgra de bstod nas ci'i phyir gang zag gzhan de ltar dga' bar mi byed de de ltar byas na khyod nyid gzhan gyi yon tan la dga' ba'i bde ba 'di, ma 'ongs pa na bde ba'i 'byung gnas kha na ma tho ba med par rgyal ba sras bcas yon tan dang ldan pa rnams kyis gnang zhing bsngags pa dang , gdul bya gzhan sdud pa'i mchog kyang yin no
dga' bar.english: Here is the first point, which covers the reasons why it is appropriate to hope that someone will sing the praises of our enemies, since this can cause us to be happy ourselves. Suppose that any particular person praises another, our enemy, by saying, "They have certain good qualities." And suppose that he--meaning the one who does the praising--derives some kind of joy from doing so. Why is it, my mind, that you don't then sing the praises of this person yourself, and find the very same joy as the other has already? If you did, then the happiness of taking this joy in the good qualities of others would become an irreproachable source of happiness for you yourself in the future; the joy has been admitted--that is, praised--by all of those who possess high qualities (which refers to the victorious Buddhas and their sons and daughters) as being something which provides exactly this kind of source. This kind of behavior is also the very best method for gathering other disciples.

dga' bar.acip: ,GNYIS PA NI, GZHAN GYIS RANG GI YON TAN BRJOD PA'I TSE GZHAN BRJOD MKHAN LA'ANG YID BDE BA 'DOD PAR BYED LA RANG GIS GZHAN GYI YON BRJOD PA'I TSE BRJOD MKHAN RANG LA'ANG BDE BA MI 'DOD PAR BYED PA MI RIGS SHING 'GAL BAS, RANG BSTOD PAS GZHAN DGA' BAR 'DOD PA BZHIN DU GZHAN BSTOD DE RANG DGA' BAR BYA'O,
dga' bar.wylie: gnyis pa ni, gzhan gyis rang gi yon tan brjod pa'i tshe gzhan brjod mkhan la'ang yid bde ba 'dod par byed la rang gis gzhan gyi yon brjod pa'i tshe brjod mkhan rang la'ang bde ba mi 'dod par byed pa mi rigs shing 'gal bas, rang bstod pas gzhan dga' bar 'dod pa bzhin du gzhan bstod de rang dga' bar bya'o
dga' bar.english: Here is the second step. When someone else praises my own good qualities, it is my hope that this other person--meaning the one who is doing the praising--might thereby find some happiness. But at the same time I have no hope or wish that I myself (the one doing the praising now) should ever find this same happiness, the happiness which comes from praising others. This kind of attitude is very wrong, very contradictory, and I should therefore try to praise others, and feel joy over it, in exactly the way that I hope that others will feel happiness whenever they sing my own praises.

dga' bar.acip: ,GNYIS PA NI, SEMS CAN THAMS CAD BLA NA MED PA'I BDE BA LA 'GOD PAR 'DOD PAS BYANG CHUB TU NI SEMS BSKYED NAS SPYOD PA LA SLOB PAR KHAS BLANGS PA LA, SEMS CAN RANG GIS BDE BA CUNG ZAD TZAM RNYED NAS 'DOD PA GRUB PA LA DA KO DA NI KHRO BAR BYED DGA' BAR RIGS SO,
dga' bar.wylie: gnyis pa ni, sems can thams cad bla na med pa'i bde ba la 'god par 'dod pas byang chub tu ni sems bskyed nas spyod pa la slob par khas blangs pa la, sems can rang gis bde ba cung zad tsam rnyed nas 'dod pa grub pa la da ko da ni khro bar byed dga' bar rigs so
dga' bar.english: Here is the second overall point, which is to give up any feeling of being unable to tolerate those people who bring happiness to our enemies. By my hope that I could bring every living being to the experience of matchless happiness, I've developed the wish for enlightenment, and pledged to train myself in the activities of a bodhisattva. When any one of these living beings finds some minor happiness by himself, my wishes have been accomplished. Why on earth then does it make you angry, my mind, when this happens? The proper thing would be to feel joy. Contemplation Sixteen On taking joy in the misfortunes of those you dislike

dga' bar.acip: ,DANG PO LA GSUM, DGRA MI DGA' BAS RANG LA MI PHAN PA DANG , DGRA LA GNOD SEMS BSKYED PAS DE LA MI GNOD PA DANG , RANG LA GNOD PA'O, , DANG PO NI, GAL TE DGRA LA GNOD PA BYUNG NA DGA' ZHING DE'I GEGS BYED PA LA KHRO ZHE NA, GAL TE DGRA ZHIG MI DGA' ZHING MI BDE NA'ANG DE LA KHYOD DGA' BAR BYAR CI ZHIG YOD, KHYOD LA PHAN PA MED CING GNOD PA'I PHYIR RO,
dga' bar.wylie: dang po la gsum, dgra mi dga' bas rang la mi phan pa dang , dgra la gnod sems bskyed pas de la mi gnod pa dang , rang la gnod pa'o, , dang po ni, gal te dgra la gnod pa byung na dga' zhing de'i gegs byed pa la khro zhe na, gal te dgra zhig mi dga' zhing mi bde na'ang de la khyod dga' bar byar ci zhig yod, khyod la phan pa med cing gnod pa'i phyir ro
dga' bar.english: The first point, which is why it is wrong to feel that we cannot tolerate things that block the harms which we wish upon our enemies, has three parts of its own: why disliking our enemies does no help to us; why hoping to harm out enemies does no harm to our enemies; and why it does hurt ourselves. Here is the first. Suppose you say, "If something happens to hurt my enemy, I feel glad; and if something happens to block these harms which I wish upon my enemy, I feel angry." But even should your enemy become upset, and unhappy, how then could you feel glad about it? It does absolutely no good to you, and in fact only hurts you.

dga' bar.acip: ,GSUM PA LA GNYIS, DGRA LA GNOD PA BYUNG BA LA DGA' BAR MI RIGS PA DANG , DE LA DGA' BAR BZUNG NA RANG NYID LA SDUG BSNGAL CHEN PO'I RGYUR 'GYUR PA'O, , DANG PO NI,

dga' bar.acip: ,DE BAS NGAL BAS MA BSGRUBS PA'I, ,KHYIM DU GTER NI BYUNG BA LTAR, ,BYANG CHUB SPYOD PA'I GROGS GYUR PAS, ,BDAG GIS DGRA LA DGA' BAR BYA,

dga' bar.acip: ,DANG PO NI SBYIN PA'I ZHING LAS BZOD PA'I ZHING DKON PAS DE LA DGA' BAR RIGS TE, 'JIG RTEN NA NI SBYIN PA'I ZHING SLONG BA MOD LA BZOD PA'I ZHING GNOD PAR BYED PA DKON PA STE, CI PHYIR CE NA, 'DI LTAR RANG GIS PHAR GNOD MA BYAS NA 'GA' YANG TSUR GNOD PA MI BYED DO,
dga' bar.wylie: dang po ni sbyin pa'i zhing las bzod pa'i zhing dkon pas de la dga' bar rigs te, 'jig rten na ni sbyin pa'i zhing slong ba mod la bzod pa'i zhing gnod par byed pa dkon pa ste, ci phyir ce na, 'di ltar rang gis phar gnod ma byas na 'ga' yang tshur gnod pa mi byed do
dga' bar.english: Here is the first point, which is that exceptional objects of virtue are extremely rare. Objects towards which you can practice your patience are much more rare than those towards which you can practice your charity, so the right thing to do would be to feel joy when you find them. Now the world may be full of beggars, but finding someone to do me harm is truly a rare occurrence. Why so? This is true since there could never be a person who did any hurt to me in any way at all if I did not do any hurt to them first.

dga' bar.acip: ,GNYIS PA NI, BZOD PA'I ZHING DKON PA DE BAS NA JI LTAR NGAL BAS MA SGRUB PA'I KHYIM DU GTER NI BYUNG BA LTAR, BDAG GI BZOD PA SGOM PA'I BYANG CHUB KYI SPYOD PA'I GROGS SU GYUR PAS BDAG GIS DGRA LA DRIN DU GZO BA'I BSAM PAS DGA' BAR BYA'O,
dga' bar.wylie: gnyis pa ni, bzod pa'i zhing dkon pa de bas na ji ltar ngal bas ma sgrub pa'i khyim du gter ni byung ba ltar, bdag gi bzod pa sgom pa'i byang chub kyi spyod pa'i grogs su gyur pas bdag gis dgra la drin du gzo ba'i bsam pas dga' bar bya'o
dga' bar.english: Here is the second point: why it is right to be glad about those who block us from accomplishing merit. Think about the rarity of objects towards which you can practice patience. Now suppose that, without an ounce of effort, I came across a treasure chest that had been hidden in my house. My enemies are just the same: I should thus feel joy for them, by reflecting about how grateful I feel for the aid they give me when they provide me with objects towards which I can practice the activities of a bodhisattva, in the form of people towards whom I can develop patience.

dga' bar.acip: ,GNYIS PA BYA BA NGAN PA LA ZHEN PA'I LE LO SPANG BA NI 'DI PHYI THAMS CAD DGA' BA'I RGYU NI MTHA' YAS PA'I THABS DAM PA'I CHOS NYAMS SU LEN PA LA DGA' BA'I MCHOG SPANGS NAS, 'BRAS BU SDUG BSNGAL GYI RGYU SDIG PA DANG 'DU 'DZI MANG PO'I GA YENG BA DANG RGOD PA SOGS BYA BA MA YIN PA MANG PO LA KHYOD CI'I PHYIR DGA', DGA' BAR MI RIGS TE SDUG BSNGAL GYI RGYU YIN PA'I PHYIR RO,
dga' bar.wylie: gnyis pa bya ba ngan pa la zhen pa'i le lo spang ba ni 'di phyi thams cad dga' ba'i rgyu ni mtha' yas pa'i thabs dam pa'i chos nyams su len pa la dga' ba'i mchog spangs nas, 'bras bu sdug bsngal gyi rgyu sdig pa dang 'du 'dzi mang po'i ga yeng ba dang rgod pa sogs bya ba ma yin pa mang po la khyod ci'i phyir dga', dga' bar mi rigs te sdug bsngal gyi rgyu yin pa'i phyir ro
dga' bar.english: To achieve a life of these leisures and fortunes is something very rare, and thus this boat is something hard to find again later. And so Master Shantideva calls to us, "Oh ignorant ones, do not sit there, at this present moment when you have found this boat, quietly asleep. You must cross over now the great river of the circle of suffering, by putting into practice the three paths designed for people of lesser, medium, and greater scope." This is a teaching then on the need to make efforts when you have finally found the spiritual leisures and fortunes which are so very hard to find. Here is the second overall point, which is eliminating the kind of laziness where you are attracted to bad activities. The highest kind of pleasure is that which comes from putting into actual practice the holy Dharma, which is a specific method for planting infinite numbers of causes that bring you pleasure in this and your future lives. And yet in your actions you give up this highest pleasure, and then you throw yourself into negative behavior: into bad deeds that will only act as causes that bring you the result of pain; into the distraction that comes from exposing yourself to great hustle and bustle; and into busyness of the mind, and the like. Why is it that you are attracted so much to these things? It is something very wrong, for they can only bring you suffering. Part One of An Outline of the Explanation of the Chapter on Effort from the Guide to the Bodhisattva's Way of Life, to accom

dga' bar.english: The third section, describes how, if we make effort, we will be able to stop our laziness, and then achieve enlightenment. Here there are four parts: contemplating the fact that, if we are able to raise the force of effort, we will find ourselves able to achieve enlightenment; why it is right to bear gladly those hardships required to reach enlightenment, given the fact that they involve not even the tiniest fraction of the pain of the lower realms; why it is right to bear gladly with any pain required, given the fact that the King of Physicians cures the great illness with a technique which is very gentle; and why it is right for us to feel glad over the treatment of our great illness, since it involves no pain at all, but rather causes our happiness to flourish. Here is the first.

dga' bar.acip: BYIS PA KHA CIG RTZED MO'I BDE BA'I 'BRAS BU 'DOD PA LTAR BYANG CHUB SEMS DPA' 'DI YIS GZHAN DON BYA BA'I LAS GANG YIN PA'I LAS THOS BSAM DANG BYANG CHUB KYI SEMS BSGOM PA LA SOGS PA'I LAS DE LA NI ZHEN PA STE SPRO BZHIN DU BYA STE, LAS DES MI NGOMS SHING RGYUN MA CHAD PAR BYA BAR 'DOD PAS DGA' BAR BYA'O,
dga' bar.wylie: byis pa kha cig rtsed mo'i bde ba'i 'bras bu 'dod pa ltar byang chub sems dpa' 'di yis gzhan don bya ba'i las gang yin pa'i las thos bsam dang byang chub kyi sems bsgom pa la sogs pa'i las de la ni zhen pa ste spro bzhin du bya ste, las des mi ngoms shing rgyun ma chad par bya bar 'dod pas dga' bar bya'o
dga' bar.english: Think about children playing a game, from which they seek a feeling of fun. These ones as well, these bodhisattvas, should cultivate a craving for--that is, come to feel excited about doing--all those kinds of activities where they work for the sake of others: this work of studying and contemplating, and then meditating upon the wish for enlightenment. We should try to reach a point where we become insatiable in seeking this work; and where we want do it continuously, without a break; in short, we should take great joy in it. Contemplation Twenty-Two The razor and the honey

dga' bar.acip: DES NA SKYE BO RNAMS BDAG LA RMONGS PA'I 'BAD PA YIS NYON MONGS PAS RGYUD 'KHRUL PA'I SMYOS PAS SA 'DI KUN TU 'KHRUGS PA STE, GANG ZHING KHYAB PA YIN NO, , DUR KHROD DU RUS GONG 'BA' ZHIG MTHONG NAS NI LUS LA DUR KHROD DU NI YID 'BYUNG NA KUN SLONG GI DBANG GIS 'GUL ZHING G-YO BA'I RUS GONG GIS KHYAB PA'I GRONG GI DUR KHROD LA DGA' BA 'AM DGA' BAR MI RIGS SO,
dga' bar.wylie: des na skye bo rnams bdag la rmongs pa'i 'bad pa yis nyon mongs pas rgyud 'khrul pa'i smyos pas sa 'di kun tu 'khrugs pa ste, gang zhing khyab pa yin no, , dur khrod du rus gong 'ba' zhig mthong nas ni lus la dur khrod du ni yid 'byung na kun slong gi dbang gis 'gul zhing g-yo ba'i rus gong gis khyab pa'i grong gi dur khrod la dga' ba 'am dga' bar mi rigs so
dga' bar.english: And so our entire planet is chaos, and filled to overflowing, covered, with people who are madmen, mad with a madness created by the error brought to their minds by the mental afflictions, by the struggle of ignorance with some so-called "self." You know your heart fails, and you think of your own body in a graveyard, whenever you go to a burial ground and see nothing there but stacks of sun-dried bones. Why then is it that you take such pleasure here in the city, a cemetery covered as it is with bones driven into motion, goaded into moving, by nothing more than will power? You should feel no such pleasure at all. Contemplation Eleven Life in the world

dga' bar.acip: ,DANG PO NI, DBEN PA'I GNAS JI LTA BUR GNAS PAR BYA ZHE NA 'KHOR LO SGYUR BA'I RGYAL PO 'GRAN ZLA BA DANG BRAL ZHING 'DOD PA'I YON TAN LA BDE BAR LONGS SPYOD PA LTAR, PHYI'I RTZOD PA DANG GZHAN GYI CHAGS SDANG GI RKYEN LA SOGS PA'I NYON MONGS KYIS STONG BA'I RNAM G-YENG ZHI BA'I NAGS KYI NANG DAG TU, SNGON LEGS PAR SPYAD PA'I SKYE BO SKAL LDAN DAG ZLA 'OD BSIL BA TZAN DAN GYIS BYUGS NAS BSIL BA'I GNAS LTAR, SHIN TU YANGS PA'I RDO LEB KHANG BZANG DANG 'DRA BA NYAMS DGA' BAR YID DANG MI MTHUN PA'I SGRA MED CING , 'JAM ZHING ZHI BA'I NAGS KYI RLUNG G-YOB PA YIS MDZES PAR BYAS PA'I GNAS SU BYANG CHUB KYI SEMS BSGOM PA LA SOGS PA GZHAN LA PHAN PA'I DON SEMS SHING 'CHAG PAR BYED PAS, RNAL 'BYOR PA RNAMS KYIS DBEN PA BSTEN PA NI 'JIG RTEN PA'I BDE BA GANG LAS KYANG KHYAD PAR DU 'PHAGS PA'O,
dga' bar.wylie: dang po ni, dben pa'i gnas ji lta bur gnas par bya zhe na 'khor lo sgyur ba'i rgyal po 'gran zla ba dang bral zhing 'dod pa'i yon tan la bde bar longs spyod pa ltar, phyi'i rtsod pa dang gzhan gyi chags sdang gi rkyen la sogs pa'i nyon mongs kyis stong ba'i rnam g-yeng zhi ba'i nags kyi nang dag tu, sngon legs par spyad pa'i skye bo skal ldan dag zla 'od bsil ba tsan dan gyis byugs nas bsil ba'i gnas ltar, shin tu yangs pa'i rdo leb khang bzang dang 'dra ba nyams dga' bar yid dang mi mthun pa'i sgra med cing , 'jam zhing zhi ba'i nags kyi rlung g-yob pa yis mdzes par byas pa'i gnas su byang chub kyi sems bsgom pa la sogs pa gzhan la phan pa'i don sems shing 'chag par byed pas, rnal 'byor pa rnams kyis dben pa bsten pa ni 'jig rten pa'i bde ba gang las kyang khyad par du 'phags pa'o
dga' bar.english: Here is the first point, which describes one of the feature of living in isolation: that the place and so on are so perfectly excellent. "If I go into isolation," you may ask, "where should it be?" Think of a wheel-empowered emperor, who has no one at all to compete with him, and who revels in the objects of the senses at his own complete leisure. Just like this emperor do we live, deep within the woods of peacefulness, at rest from all the various distractions, in a place completely emptied of both any outer conflict and any kind of mental affliction--completely free of any of the objects that could trigger within us emotions such as liking or disliking another person. We live doing as we please under some very wide, flat rock as a roof, which is just like a mansion for us. The place is cool, made cool by the touch of sweet sandalwood scent smeared all over--the soft moonlight of the presence of the holy beings who have stayed there in the past. Here the forest is silent, with no kinds of sound to clash with our thoughts, and peaceful with the soft velvet breezes that flow past to grace the ground of our meditation. We spend our days here in gentle walks, and thoughts of things we can do that will help others--in the practice of the wish for enlightenment. And so it is, that when great practitioners go into isolation, the pleasure they feel is infinitely greater than anything felt by those who follow the worldly way of life.

dga' bar.wylie: byang sems rnams myang 'das la dga' bar mi bya zhing , de la rgyab kyi phyogs par bya, nyon mongs pa 'jigs par mi bya zhing , de dag las sems shin tu dben par mi bya ste, bskal pa grangs med gsum du 'khor bar 'khor zhing , byang chub bsgrub dgos pa blta zhing , de skad smra na 'khor bar gcig bu 'grod par sems pa'i nyes byas 1a4
dga' bar.english: (14) The secondary offense of thinking that you only have to travel through the circle of suffering life You commit this when you think to yourself, and also say to others, the following: "Bodhisattvas don't like to reach nirvana; in fact, they work for the opposite. They have no fear of the mental afflictions, and they do not try to keep their minds totally away from these thoughts. They only want to achieve Buddhahood, and they wander around in the circle of suffering life for three 'countless' eons."

dga' bar.acip: ,TSE'I MTHAR 'CHI BDAG GIS BCOM NAS 'JIG RTEN PHA ROL TU 'GRO BAR MA ZAD DE'I BAR RNAMS SU YANG 'GRO 'CHAG NYAL GSUM GANG BYED KYANG TSE BRI NAS MI 'GRO BA'I SKABS YE MED PAS, MNGAL DU ZHUGS PA NAS 'GO BZUNG STE SKAD CIG TZAM YANG MI SDOD PAR 'JIG RTEN PHA ROL TU KHA BLTAS NAS 'GRO BA YIN NO, , DES NA BAR GYI GSON PA'ANG NA BA DANG RGA BA'I PHO NYA BAS KHRID NAS 'CHI BA'I PHYIR DU 'GRO BA KHO NAR ZAD PAS GSON PA'I SKABS LA 'JIG RTEN PHYI MAR MI 'GRO BA'I SDOD PAR BZUNG NAS DGA' BAR MI BYA STE, DPER NA, BRAG MTHON PO'I RTZE MO NAS LHUNG BA'I TSE, SA LA MA LHUNG BA'I BAR SNANG LA 'GRO BA'I SKABS DE LA DGA' BAR MI 'OS PA BZHIN NO,
dga' bar.wylie: tshe'i mthar 'chi bdag gis bcom nas 'jig rten pha rol tu 'gro bar ma zad de'i bar rnams su yang 'gro 'chag nyal gsum gang byed kyang tshe bri nas mi 'gro ba'i skabs ye med pas, mngal du zhugs pa nas 'go bzung ste skad cig tsam yang mi sdod par 'jig rten pha rol tu kha bltas nas 'gro ba yin no, , des na bar gyi gson pa'ang na ba dang rga ba'i pho nya bas khrid nas 'chi ba'i phyir du 'gro ba kho nar zad pas gson pa'i skabs la 'jig rten phyi mar mi 'gro ba'i sdod par bzung nas dga' bar mi bya ste, dper na, brag mthon po'i rtse mo nas lhung ba'i tshe, sa la ma lhung ba'i bar snang la 'gro ba'i skabs de la dga' bar mi 'os pa bzhin no
dga' bar.english: At the end of our life, the Lord of Death comes and destroys us, and we travel on to our next life. But there is something else too that happens all during the interim, during every hour of our life here. There is not a single moment at all when our lifetime is not slipping away, when it is not getting shorter and shorter, even as we go somewhere, or stay somewhere, waking or sleeping. So in a sense we are always on our way to our next life, we are travelling there now, and we have been on the move every second from the day we first entered our mother's womb. Therefore even in these days, while we still live, we are living only to die: those emissaries of death, the ones called Sickness and Aging, are dragging us towards him. Don't take any comfort then in the fact that you haven't died yet, don't get the idea that you are staying anywhere, and that you haven't yet started off on your journey to the next life. You are like a man who just fell off the edge of a great rock crag; you would be foolish to take some comfort from the fact that you are still in mid-air, and haven't hit ground yet.

dga' bar.acip: ,DE LTAR NA TSE 'DI'I PHUN TSOGS THAMS CAD NI RMI LAM THUN GCIG NA BDE BA SPYAD BSAD NAS DRAN PA LTAR 'CHI BA'I DUS SU DRAN PA'I YUL TZAM DU 'GYUR LA, 'CHI BA'I DGRA NI DGAG TU MED PAR NGES PAR 'ONG NA CI'I PHYIR TSE 'DI'I BSLU BRID LA DGA' BAR BYA SNYAM DU BSAMS TE CHOS BYA DGOS PA LA THAG BCAD CING ZHE DAM MANG DU BYA STE, SKYES RABS LAS, KYE MA'O 'JIG RTEN NYON MONGS DAG, GNAS PA MI BRTAN DGA' MI 'GYUR, , KU MU TA YI DPAL 'DI YANG , , DRAN PAR BYA BA NYID DU 'GYUR, , 'GRO BA 'DI LTA BUR NI 'KHOD PA LA, , SKYE BO 'JIGS PA MED PA NGO MTSAR KYE, , LAM RNAMS THAMS CAD 'CHI BDAG NYID KYIS BKAG, DOGS PA MED PAR RAB TU DGA' ZHING SPYOD, , NA DANG RGA DANG 'CHI BA'I GNOD BYED DGRA, , MTHU CHEN DGAG TU MI NUS YOD BZHIN LA, , 'JIG RTEN PHA ROL NYAM NGAR NGES 'GRO NA, , SEMS SHES SU ZHIG 'DI LA DGA' BAR SEMS, , ZHES DANG ,
dga' bar.wylie: de ltar na tshe 'di'i phun tshogs thams cad ni rmi lam thun gcig na bde ba spyad bsad nas dran pa ltar 'chi ba'i dus su dran pa'i yul tsam du 'gyur la, 'chi ba'i dgra ni dgag tu med par nges par 'ong na ci'i phyir tshe 'di'i bslu brid la dga' bar bya snyam du bsams te chos bya dgos pa la thag bcad cing zhe dam mang du bya ste, skyes rabs las, kye ma'o 'jig rten nyon mongs dag, gnas pa mi brtan dga' mi 'gyur, , ku mu ta yi dpal 'di yang , , dran par bya ba nyid du 'gyur, , 'gro ba 'di lta bur ni 'khod pa la, , skye bo 'jigs pa med pa ngo mtshar kye, , lam rnams thams cad 'chi bdag nyid kyis bkag, dogs pa med par rab tu dga' zhing spyod, , na dang rga dang 'chi ba'i gnod byed dgra, , mthu chen dgag tu mi nus yod bzhin la, , 'jig rten pha rol nyam ngar nges 'gro na, , sems shes su zhig 'di la dga' bar sems, , zhes dang
dga' bar.english: And so all the good things of this life are like the happiness within one night's dream: you wake, and then it's nothing more than a memory. The time comes to die, and everything good you ever had lives only in a dim remembrance. This great enemy, death, will surely come; nothing can stop him. You should contemplate this fact--try to wonder, "Why do I take such pleasure in the lie of this life?" Make up your mind that you absolutely must now practice some Dharma; swear it to yourself, continually. Remember the Birth Stories, where it says: Alas, you worldly ones so full of affliction of the mind; Why do you take such pleasure in a land of shifting sands? The shining glory of the kumuda bloom, opening to the moon, Soon enough turns nothing more than a simple memory. It's something of a pure amazement too that all of us Thrust into a life like this are not consumed by total fear; Damn the Lord of Death, who stands and blocks all pathways out, While we oblivious feel content, and have an enjoyable day. We all share enemies, dreadfully powerful, ones we cannot stop: Their names are sickness, age, and death; they attack us even now. If it's certain that we are headed for agony in the world beyond, How could anyone with a mind be content in the one here now?

dga' bar.acip: ,BLA MA GONG MA RNAMS MIR SKYES NA YANG SROG GCOD SOGS DE DAG LA DGA' BAR 'GYUR BA BYED PA RGYU MTHUN GYI 'BRAS BU DANG SNGA MA RNAMS MYONG BA RGYU MTHUN GYI 'BRAS BUR BZHED DO,
dga' bar.wylie: bla ma gong ma rnams mir skyes na yang srog gcod sogs de dag la dga' bar 'gyur ba byed pa rgyu mthun gyi 'bras bu dang snga ma rnams myong ba rgyu mthun gyi 'bras bur bzhed do
dga' bar.english: Great lamas of the past have expressed the position that the "consistent" consequence is where, even if you do manage to take birth as a human, you enjoy killing things, and so on. They say then that experiencing the various results just listed is a "ripened" consequence [the second rgyu mthun here is likely a text error for rnam smin; this is the corrected reading]. 13 The Environmental Consequences of the Ten Bad Deeds

dga' bar.acip: ,BDAG GIS DI RING SKYOB PA THAMS CAD KYI, ,SPYAN SNGAR 'GRO BA BDE GSHEGS NYID DANG NI, ,BAR DU BDE LA MGRON DU BOS ZIN GYIS, ,LHA DANG LHA MIN LA SOGS DGA' BAR GYIS,
dga' bar.wylie: bdag gis di ring skyob pa thams cad kyi, ,spyan sngar 'gro ba bde gshegs nyid dang ni, ,bar du bde la mgron du bos zin gyis, ,lha dang lha min la sogs dga' bar gyis
dga' bar.english: I stand today in the presence Of all the Protectors. I invite every living creature As my guest, to partake In the very state of Those Who have Gone to Bliss, and in Happiness until they reach it. I call on every pleasure being, On near pleasure beings, and All such creatures, to take joy In this as well. 5 The Great Enemy

dga' bar.acip: ,DE LTAR YUN RING RGYUN CHAGS DGRAR GYUR PA, ,GNOD PA'I TSOGS RAB 'PHEL BA'I RGYU GCIG PU, ,BDAG GI SNYING LA NGES PAR GNAS 'CHA' NA, ,'KHOR BAR 'JIGS MED DGA' BAR GA LA 'GYUR,
dga' bar.wylie: de ltar yun ring rgyun chags dgrar gyur pa, ,gnod pa'i tshogs rab 'phel ba'i rgyu gcig pu, ,bdag gi snying la nges par gnas 'cha' na, ,'khor bar 'jigs med dga' bar ga la 'gyur
dga' bar.english: They've been thus my constant enemy for a very long time; And are the one single cause that feeds and nourishes The entire mass of harmful things. How could I ever be free of all the terrors Of cyclic life, and feel gladness so long as They are rooted and fixed in my very heart?

dga' bar.acip: ,GNYIS PA NI, GANG LA YID MI BDE SKYE BA'I YUL DE LA GAL TE BCOS SU YOD NA NI DE LA MI DGA' BAR BYA BA'I RGYU CI ZHIG YOD, DE MA THAG BCOS PAS YID MI BDE BA MED PAR 'GYUR BA'I PHYIR RO, , GAL TE BCOS SU MED NA YANG DE LA MI DGA' BA BYAS PAS CI PHAN TE NAM MKHA' THOGS BCAS KYIS STONG PA LA MI DGA' BA BYAS KYANG MI PHAN PA BZHIN NO,
dga' bar.wylie: gnyis pa ni, gang la yid mi bde skye ba'i yul de la gal te bcos su yod na ni de la mi dga' bar bya ba'i rgyu ci zhig yod, de ma thag bcos pas yid mi bde ba med par 'gyur ba'i phyir ro, , gal te bcos su med na yang de la mi dga' ba byas pas ci phan te nam mkha' thogs bcas kyis stong pa la mi dga' ba byas kyang mi phan pa bzhin no
dga' bar.english: Let us consider any of the objects over which we feel upset. If there is something you can do about it, then why should you ever feel upset at all? You could take the necessary action to fix it immediately, and never need to feel upset. If on the other hand there is nothing you can do about it, then what is the use of being upset? It would be as useless as getting upset at empty space, at a place where nothing was. Contemplation Three Perfect patience is like any other habit, and can be developed with practice

dga' bar.acip: ,DE BAS NGAL BAS MA BSGRUBS PA'I, ,KHYIM DU GTER NI BYUNG BA LTAR, ,BYANG CHUB SPYOD PA'I GROGS GYUR PAS, ,BDAG GIS DGRA LA DGA' BAR BYA,
dga' bar.wylie: de bas ngal bas ma bsgrubs pa'i, ,khyim du gter ni byung ba ltar, ,byang chub spyod pa'i grogs gyur pas, ,bdag gis dgra la dga' bar bya
dga' bar.english: Suppose that without an ounce Of effort you came across A treasure chest hidden in your house; You should thus feel grateful for Your enemies, who aid you in Your bodhisattva practice.

dga' bar.acip: ,RTZED MO'I BDE 'BRAS 'DOD PA LTAR, ,'DI YIS BYA BA'I LAS GANG YIN, ,LAS DE LA NI ZHEN BYA STE, ,LAS DES MI NGOMS DGA' BAR BYA,
dga' bar.wylie: rtsed mo'i bde 'bras 'dod pa ltar, ,'di yis bya ba'i las gang yin, ,las de la ni zhen bya ste, ,las des mi ngoms dga' bar bya
dga' bar.english: Like those who seek a feeling of fun From playing a game, these ones as well Should cultivate a craving for This work, all those that work for them, And come to be insatiable In seeking it, and taking joy.

dga' bar.english: Think about children playing a game, from which they seek a feeling of fun. These ones as well, these bodhisattvas, should cultivate a craving for--that is, come to feel excited about doing--all those kinds of activities where they work for the sake of others: this work of studying and contemplating, and then meditating upon the wish for enlightenment. We should try to reach a point where we become insatiable in seeking this work; and where we want do it continuously, without a break; in short, we should take great joy in it. Contemplation Eighteen The razor and the honey

dga' bar.acip: DES NA DE RNAMS NI SBYIN PA'I 'BRAS BU MNGON SUM DU MI MTHONG BA'I PHYIR SBYIN PA LA MI 'JUG PA YANG SRID NA, 'GRO BA THAMS CAD LA PHUGS SU PHAN PA DANG, 'PHRAL DU BDE BA SGRUB PAR DAM BCAS PA'I YID CAN GYI BYANG SEMS RNAMS, SBYIN PAS RING POR MI THOGS PAR SLONG BA PO TSIM PAR BYAS PA MTHONG BA'I MJUG THOGS NYID DU, SBYIN PA'I 'BRAS BU DGA' BA MCHOG TU GYUR BA 'THOB CING SBYIN 'BRAS LA LONGS SPYOD PAS, DUS THAMS CAD KYI TSE SBYIN PA BYED PA LA DGA' BAR 'GYUR RO,,
dga' bar.wylie: des na de rnams ni sbyin pa'i 'bras bu mngon sum du mi mthong ba'i phyir sbyin pa la mi 'jug pa yang srid na, 'gro ba thams cad la phugs su phan pa dang, 'phral du bde ba sgrub par dam bcas pa'i yid can gyi byang sems rnams, sbyin pas ring por mi thogs par slong ba po tshim par byas pa mthong ba'i mjug thogs nyid du, sbyin pa'i 'bras bu dga' ba mchog tu gyur ba 'thob cing sbyin 'bras la longs spyod pas, dus thams cad kyi tshe sbyin pa byed pa la dga' bar 'gyur ro
dga' bar.english: As such—because they don't see the results of their giving in a direct way—there is a possibility that they will fail to engage in the act of giving. But the bodhisattvas—who have resolved in their hearts to be of benefit to every living being in the long run, and in the short run to make them happy—undertake acts of giving and then not long afterwards (meaning immediately subsequent to seeing that their giving has satisfied the needs of those who have asked them for something) these acts make them feel a supreme form of happiness as the result of their giving. Having thus enjoyed the fruits of their giving, they are at all times very pleased to engage in giving. Why giving is the most important [I.13b]

dga' bar.acip: BLO LDAN SA RAB TU DGA' BAR GNAS PAS YON TAN BRGYA PHRAG BCU GNYIS PO DE DAG NI THOB PAR GYUR NAS, SA GNYIS PAR 'PHOS PA NAS DANG PO LA BSHAD PA DE BZHIN KHO NAR SA DRI MA MED PA LA GNAS PAS, YON TAN SDE TSAN BCU GNYIS PO DE DAG NI STONG DU BYAS PA YANG DAG PAR 'THOB PAR 'GYUR RO,,
dga' bar.wylie: blo ldan sa rab tu dga' bar gnas pas yon tan brgya phrag bcu gnyis po de dag ni thob par gyur nas, sa gnyis par 'phos pa nas dang po la bshad pa de bzhin kho nar sa dri ma med pa la gnas pas, yon tan sde tshan bcu gnyis po de dag ni stong du byas pa yang dag par 'thob par 'gyur ro
dga' bar.english: When this intelligent one residing at (1) the level of Perfect Happiness has attained those twelve different groups of a hundred high qualities each, they move to the second bodhisattva level. And then they reside at (2) this level known as “Immaculate,” just as we explained them doing at the first level. And they attain, perfectly, this same number of groups of high qualities (twelve), except that these are now composed of a thousand members of features each. [afterword.5] Sanskrit unavailable

dga' bar.acip: DRIL BU G-YER KA'I DRA BA DE DAG KYANG RLUNG GIS BSKYOD CING BSKUL BA NA LHA'I SGRA DBYANGS YID DU 'ONG BA SEMS CAN THAMS CAD YANG DAG PAR DGA' BAR BYED PA, DNGOS PO MED PA'I NGO BO NYID KYI CHOS KYI SGRA SKAD 'BYUNG BA,

dga' bar.english: When breezes come through and inspire the bells with a nudge, they ring out with a lovely song of the gods, filling the beings who hear it with pure joy.  So too these sounds speak of the very essence of things—of the way that things are not themselves.

dga' bar.acip: DES NA BAR GYI GSON PA'ANG NA BA DANG RGA BA'I PHO, NYA BAS KHRID NAS 'CHI BA'I PHYIR DU 'GRO BA KHO NAR ZAD PAS GSON PA'I SKABS LA 'JIG RTEN PHYI MAR MI 'GRO BA'I SDOD PAR BZUNG NAS DGA' BAR MI BYA STE DPER NA BRAG MTHON PO'I RTZE MO NAS LHUNG BA'I TSE SA LA MA LHUNG BA'I BAR SNANG LA 'GRO BA'I SKABS DE LA DGA' BAR MI 'OS PA BZHIN NO
dga' bar.wylie: des na bar gyi gson pa'ang na ba dang rga ba'i pho, nya bas khrid nas 'chi ba'i phyir du 'gro ba kho nar zad pas gson pa'i skabs la 'jig rten phyi mar mi 'gro ba'i sdod par bzung nas dga' bar mi bya ste dper na brag mthon po'i rtse mo nas lhung ba'i tshe sa la ma lhung ba'i bar snang la 'gro ba'i skabs de la dga' bar mi 'os pa bzhin no
dga' bar.english: Therefore even in these days, while we still live, we are livingonly to die: those emissaries of Death, the ones called Sickness and Aging, are dragging us towards him. Don't take any comfort then in the fact that you haven't died yet, don't get the idea that you are stayinganywhere, and that you haven't yet started off on your journey to the next life. You are like a man who just fell off the edge of a great rock crag; you would be foolish to take some comfort from the fact that you are still in mid-air, and haven't hit ground yet.

dga' bar.acip: DE LTAR NA TSE 'DI'I PHUN TSOGS THAMS CAD NI RMI, LAM THUN GCIG NA BDE BA SPYAD BSAD NAS DRAN PA LTAR 'CHI BA'I DUS SU DRAN PA'I YUL TZAM DU 'GYUR LA 'CHI BA'I DGRA NI DGAG TU MED PAR NGES PAR 'ONG NA CI'I PHYIR TSE 'DI'I BSLU BRID LA DGA' BAR BYA SNYAM DU BSAMS TE CHOS BYA DGOS PA LA THAG BCAD CING ZHE DAM MANG DU BYA STE
dga' bar.wylie: de ltar na tshe 'di'i phun tshogs thams cad ni rmi, lam thun gcig na bde ba spyad bsad nas dran pa ltar 'chi ba'i dus su dran pa'i yul tsam du 'gyur la 'chi ba'i dgra ni dgag tu med par nges par 'ong na ci'i phyir tshe 'di'i bslu brid la dga' bar bya snyam du bsams te chos bya dgos pa la thag bcad cing zhe dam mang du bya ste
dga' bar.english: And so all the good things of this life are like the happiness within one night's dream: you wake, and then it's nothingmore than a memory. The time comes to die, and everythinggood you ever had lives only in a dim remembrance. This great enemy, death, will surely come; You should contemplate this fact— try to wonder, “Why do I take such pleasure in the lie of this life?” Make up your mind that you absolutely must now practice some Dharma; swear it to yourself,

dga' bar.acip: NA DANG RGA DANG 'CHI BA'I GNOD BYED DGRA MTHU, CHEN DGAG TU MI NUS YOD BZHIN LA 'JIG RTEN PHA ROL NYAM NGAR NGES 'GRO NA SEMS SHES SU ZHIG 'DI LA DGA' BAR SEMS ZHES DANG
dga' bar.wylie: na dang rga dang 'chi ba'i gnod byed dgra mthu, chen dgag tu mi nus yod bzhin la 'jig rten pha rol nyam ngar nges 'gro na sems shes su zhig 'di la dga' bar sems zhes dang
dga' bar.english: We all share enemies, dreadfully powerful, ones we cannot stop: Their names are sickness, age, and death; If it's certain that we are headed for agony in the world beyond, How could anyone with a mind be content in the one here now?

dga' bar.acip: DANG PO NI DBEN PA'I GNAS JI LTA BUR GNAS PAR BYA ZHE NA 'KHOR LO SGYUR BA'I RGYAL PO, 'GRAN ZLA BA DANG BRAL ZHING 'DOD PA'I YON TAN LA BDE BAR LONGS SPYOD PA LTAR PHYI'I RTZOD PA DANG GZHAN GYI CHAGS SDANG GI RKYEN LA SOGS PA'I NYON MONGS KYIS STONG BA'I RNAM G.YENG ZHI BA'I NAGS KYI NANG DAG TU SNGON LEGS PAR SPYAD PA'I SKYE BO SKAL LDAN DAG ZLA 'OD BSIL BA TZAN DAN GYIS BYUGS NAS BSIL BA'I GNAS LTAR SHIN TU YANGS PA'I RDO LEB KHANG BZANG DANG 'DRA BA NYAMS DGA' BAR YID DANG MI MTHUN PA'I SGRA MED CING 'JAM ZHING ZHI BA'I NAGS KYI RLUNG G.YOB PA YIS MDZES PAR BYAS PA'I GNAS SU BYANG CHUB KYI SEMS BSGOM PA LA SOGS PA GZHAN LA PHAN PA'I DON SEMS SHING 'CHAG PAR BYED PAS RNAL 'BYOR PA RNAMS KYIS DBEN PA BSTEN PA NI 'JIG RTEN PA'I BDE BA GANG LAS KYANG KHYAD PAR DU 'PHAGS PA'O
dga' bar.wylie: dang po ni dben pa'i gnas ji lta bur gnas par bya zhe na 'khor lo sgyur ba'i rgyal po, 'gran zla ba dang bral zhing 'dod pa'i yon tan la bde bar longs spyod pa ltar phyi'i rtsod pa dang gzhan gyi chags sdang gi rkyen la sogs pa'i nyon mongs kyis stong ba'i rnam g.yeng zhi ba'i nags kyi nang dag tu sngon legs par spyad pa'i skye bo skal ldan dag zla 'od bsil ba tsan dan gyis byugs nas bsil ba'i gnas ltar shin tu yangs pa'i rdo leb khang bzang dang 'dra ba nyams dga' bar yid dang mi mthun pa'i sgra med cing 'jam zhing zhi ba'i nags kyi rlung g.yob pa yis mdzes par byas pa'i gnas su byang chub kyi sems bsgom pa la sogs pa gzhan la phan pa'i don sems shing 'chag par byed pas rnal 'byor pa rnams kyis dben pa bsten pa ni 'jig rten pa'i bde ba gang las kyang khyad par du 'phags pa'o
dga' bar.english: Here is the first point, which describes one of the feature of livingin isolation: that the place and so on are so perfectly excellent. "If I go into isolation," you may ask, "where should it be?" Think of a wheel-empowered emperor, who has no one at all to compete with him, and who revels in the objects of the senses at his own complete leisure. Just like this emperor do we live, deep within the woods of peacefulness, at rest from all the various distractions, in a place completely emptied of both any outer conflict and any kind of mental affliction—completely free of any of the objects that could trigger within us emotions such as likingor dislikinganother person. We live doing as we please under some very wide, flat rock as a roof, which is just like a mansion for us. The place is cool, made cool by the touch of sweet sandalwood scent smeared all over—the soft moonlight of the presence of the holy beings who have stayed there in the past. Here the forest is silent, with no kinds of sound to clash with our thoughts, and peaceful with the soft velvet breezes that flow past to grace the ground of our meditation. We spend our days here in gentle walks, and thoughts of things we can do that will help others—in the practice of the wish for enlightenment. And so it is, that when great practitioners go into isolation, the pleasure they feel is infinitely greater than anything felt by those who follow the worldly way of

dga' bar.acip: DE LA RIGS MTHUN PA'I LHA DANG MI RNAMS DGA' BAR 'GYUR RO NAD MED CING TSE, RING BAR 'GYUR RO ZHES BYA BA LA SOGS PA GSUNGS SO
dga' bar.wylie: de la rigs mthun pa'i lha dang mi rnams dga' bar 'gyur ro nad med cing tshe, ring bar 'gyur ro zhes bya ba la sogs pa gsungs so
dga' bar.english: When you start acting this way, then all the gods and men who think the same way are pleased. You stop ever becoming sick, and your life becomes longer. The sutra continues on in the same vein. Set a Do-able Goal It is unrealistic for most of us to say that we can stop ourselves from ever doing a certain negative action again. Here are two selections about setting goals for yourself that you can actually meet. The first is from A Ritual for the Purifying Yourself of Bad Deeds, by Je Tsongkapa.

dga' bar.acip: DES NA RANG GCES PAR 'DZIN PA BZHIN DU GZHAN GCES PAR 'DZIN DGOS TE, GZHAN GYIS RANG GCES PAR BZUNG NA RANG DGA' BA BZHIN DU, RANG GIS KYANG GZHAN GCES PAR BZUNG NA GZHAN DGA' BAR 'GYUR BAS SO,,
dga' bar.wylie: des na rang gces par 'dzin pa bzhin du gzhan gces par 'dzin dgos te, gzhan gyis rang gces par bzung na rang dga' ba bzhin du, rang gis kyang gzhan gces par bzung na gzhan dga' bar 'gyur bas so
dga' bar.english: And so I must cherish others just as I cherish myself.  When I know that others cherish me, I feel a sense of joy.  Now, when they know that I cherish them, then others will feel the same joy.

When I know that others cherish me, I feel a sense of joy.  Now, when they know that I cherish them, then others will feel the same joy."}

dga' bar.acip: GZHAN GYIS RANG LA DRANG POR SMRA ZHING DGA' BAR BYED CING , DON 'DRI BA LA KHONG KHRO 'AM, LE LO'I DBANG GIS RJES SU MTHUN PA'I LAN MI 'DEBS NA, DRIS PA RNAMS LA LAN MI 'DEBS PA'I NYES BYAS 4,
dga' bar.wylie: gzhan gyis rang la drang por smra zhing dga' bar byed cing , don 'dri ba la khong khro 'am, le lo'i dbang gis rjes su mthun pa'i lan mi 'debs na, dris pa rnams la lan mi 'debs pa'i nyes byas 4
dga' bar.english: (4) The secondary offense of failing to answer questions You commit this when, out of anger or laziness, you fail to give an appropriate answer to a person who has asked you a question in a sincere and well-meaning way.

dga' bar.acip: BYANG SEMS RNAMS MYANG 'DAS LA DGA' BAR MI BYA ZHING , DE LA RGYAB KYI PHYOGS PAR BYA, NYON MONGS PA 'JIGS PAR MI BYA ZHING , DE DAG LAS SEMS SHIN TU DBEN PAR MI BYA STE, BSKAL PA GRANGS MED GSUM DU 'KHOR BAR 'KHOR ZHING , BYANG CHUB BSGRUB DGOS PA BLTA ZHING , DE SKAD SMRA NA 'KHOR BAR GCIG BU 'GROD PAR SEMS PA'I NYES BYAS 14,
dga' bar.wylie: byang sems rnams myang 'das la dga' bar mi bya zhing , de la rgyab kyi phyogs par bya, nyon mongs pa 'jigs par mi bya zhing , de dag las sems shin tu dben par mi bya ste, bskal pa grangs med gsum du 'khor bar 'khor zhing , byang chub bsgrub dgos pa blta zhing , de skad smra na 'khor bar gcig bu 'grod par sems pa'i nyes byas 14
dga' bar.english: (14) The secondary offense of thinking that you only have to travel through the circle of suffering life You commit this when you think to yourself, and also say to others, the following: "Bodhisattvas don't like to reach nirvana; in fact, they work for the opposite. They have no fear of the mental afflictions, and they do not try to keep their minds totally away from these thoughts. They only want to achieve Buddhahood, and they wander around in the circle of suffering life for three 'countless' eons."

dga' bar.acip: DANG POR SLOB DPON LA BSNYEN BKUR BYAS TE THOS BSAM GYIS DE KHO NA NYID RTOGS NAS DA NI 'DIS CI ZHIG BYA ZHES BLA MA LA BRNYAS PAR BYED PA NI, SNYING NAS SLOB DPON SMOD PA STE DE DANG LHAN CIG TU ZANG ZING GI LONGS SPYOD KYIS DGA' BAR BYED PAS KYANG MI 'GRUB NA DES MI 'GRUB PA SMOS CI DGOS, ZHES CHOS SPONG DANG MTSAMS MED LAS KYANG SDIG CHE BAR GSUNGS SO,
dga' bar.wylie: dang por slob dpon la bsnyen bkur byas te thos bsam gyis de kho na nyid rtogs nas da ni 'dis ci zhig bya zhes bla ma la brnyas par byed pa ni, snying nas slob dpon smod pa ste de dang lhan cig tu zang zing gi longs spyod kyis dga' bar byed pas kyang mi 'grub na des mi 'grub pa smos ci dgos, zhes chos spong dang mtshams med las kyang sdig che bar gsungs so
dga' bar.english: What does it mean here to "disparage your Master from the bottom of your heart"?  As the texts say, this is where you disparage your Lama in the following way:  At first you pay Them proper respect.  You study with Them, and contemplate what you've studied, and you come to understand suchness.  And then you say to yourself, "So what do I need them for anymore?" If a person who has committed those other actions can no longer reach attainments, the texts say, even by pleasing their Lama by sharing their material possessions with them; then what need is there to say that a person like this could never reach any attainments? The point of this last part is to say that the act of disparaging ones Master is more serious even than actions such as giving up the Dharma, or committing one of the "immediate" misdeeds. ***

dga' bar.wylie: yang dang yang du smod par byed pa dang , des kyang dga' bar byed kyi 'gyod par ni mi byed pa dang chos bzhin du phyir 'chos par mi byed pa gang yin pa de ni snying nas slob dpon smod pa ste, zhes snying nas slob dpon smod pa la dga' bar byed pa sogs de rnams dgos par gsungs pas rtsa ltung du 'gyur pa la chos de rnams kyang tshang dgos so
dga' bar.english: The texts state that someone is disparaging their Master from their heart when they do so over and over again; and they do it with a sense of satisfaction, without feeling any regret; and they make no attempt to repair the damage in the proper way.  The point being made here is that, in order to disparage your Master "from your heart," these conditions such as a sense of satisfaction must be present.  As such, these same conditions must be present in order for our action to become the root downfall. ***

dga' bar.acip: RTZA LTUNG DE LA KUN DKRIS CHEN PO'I CHOS RNAMS TSANG BA DGOS PAS NA RTZA LTUNG GZHAN LA'ANG RIGS PA MTSUNGS SO, ,DE LA YANG DANG YANG DU ZHES PA NI RGYUN MA CHAD PA'I DON TE SNGA MA SPYAD NAS DA DUNG SPYOD 'DOD MA LOG PA'O, ,DES KYANG DGA' BAR BYED PA NI BYA BA DES SEMS LA RANGS PA 'THOB PA'O, ,'GYOD PAR MI BYED PA NI YON TAN DU LTA BA ZHES GSUNGS PA'I DON NYES DMIGS SU MI LTA BA'O, ,PHYIR 'CHOS PAR MI BYED PA NI RANG LA LTOS PA'I NGO TSA SHES PA DANG GZHAN LA LTOS PA'I KHREL YOD KYIS NYES PA DE DANG DE DAG LA 'DZEM PA MED PA'O,
dga' bar.wylie: rtsa ltung de la kun dkris chen po'i chos rnams tshang ba dgos pas na rtsa ltung gzhan la'ang rigs pa mtshungs so, ,de la yang dang yang du zhes pa ni rgyun ma chad pa'i don te snga ma spyad nas da dung spyod 'dod ma log pa'o, ,des kyang dga' bar byed pa ni bya ba des sems la rangs pa 'thob pa'o, ,'gyod par mi byed pa ni yon tan du lta ba zhes gsungs pa'i don nyes dmigs su mi lta ba'o, ,phyir 'chos par mi byed pa ni rang la ltos pa'i ngo tsha shes pa dang gzhan la ltos pa'i khrel yod kyis nyes pa de dang de dag la 'dzem pa med pa'o
dga' bar.english: The conditions of the various "greater chains" must be present for us to commit this particular root downfall, of disparaging our Master; as such, this same rule follows for all the other root downfalls as well.  When they say "doing it over and over again," it means committing this action constantly, having done it in the past and having no desire to stop doing it again now and later. The person should as well do it "with a sense of satisfaction," which refers to the person feeling glad for having committed the action.  "Without any feeling of regret" means "seeing it as a virtue," which itself means failing to see that the action was a mistake.  "Making no attempt to repair the damage" means failing to avoid doing the particular negative act, as one possesses no sense of shame relative to oneself, and no sense of consideration for how it will cause others to feel. ***

dga' bar.acip: RIN CHEN NI MNYAM NYID YE SHES YIN LA, RIGS NI DE LAS BYUNG BAS NA RIN CHEN 'BYUNG LDAN NO, RNAL 'BYOR NI DE'I RNAM PAR SEMS RTZE GCIG GIS YANG DANG YANG DU SBYOR BA RIN 'BYUNG GI RIGS KYI SGRUB PA PO STE DE'I 'DA' BAR MI BYA BAR NYAMS SU BLANG BAR BYA BA'I DAM TSIG NI SBYIN PA LA DGA' BA RNAMS DE LA SBYOR BAS DE DAG DGA' BAR BYED PA'I PHYIR YID DU 'ONG BA DE LA'O,
dga' bar.wylie: rin chen ni mnyam nyid ye shes yin la, rigs ni de las byung bas na rin chen 'byung ldan no, rnal 'byor ni de'i rnam par sems rtse gcig gis yang dang yang du sbyor ba rin 'byung gi rigs kyi sgrub pa po ste de'i 'da' bar mi bya bar nyams su blang bar bya ba'i dam tshig ni sbyin pa la dga' ba rnams de la sbyor bas de dag dga' bar byed pa'i phyir yid du 'ong ba de la'o
dga' bar.english: The "jewel" in the name of the Angel called "Source of Jewels" is the wisdom referred to as "equivalent wisdom."  Because the family here is produced by this wisdom, the Angel is named "Source of Jewels."  The yoga of this Angel is where we unite ourselves, over and over, with this Angel, single-pointedly.  And this is what makes someone a practitioner of this particular family. The pledge that we take upon ourselves here--the action which we cannot transgress--is to delight in the various forms of giving. And when we "join" or apply ourselves to this act of giving, it brings us delight: thus it is that giving is described as "wonderful." ***

dga' bar.acip: RDZOGS RIM DNGOS GRUB SNYE MA LAS, LUGS LDOG GI SNANG MCHED THOB GSUM 'OD GSAL GYI YE SHES SU MI RUNG YANG , LUGS LDOG GI DGA' BA GZHAN GSUM LHAN SKYES SU 'JOG PA GCIG BSHAD LA, DE BZHIN DU LUGS MTHUN GYI SNANG MCHED THOB GSUM DANG DE GSUM DGA' BA GSUM DU BZHAG PA LHAN SKYES KYI DGA' BAR MI 'JOG KYANG , LUGS MTHUN YAS BABS KYI DGA' BA GSUM LHAN SKYES KYI DGA' BAR 'JOG PA'I SKABS GCIG KYANG YOD PAR MNGON NO, ,ZHES GSUNGS PA TZAM LAS GSAL BAR BSHAD PA MI SNANG LA,
dga' bar.wylie: rdzogs rim dngos grub snye ma las, lugs ldog gi snang mched thob gsum 'od gsal gyi ye shes su mi rung yang , lugs ldog gi dga' ba gzhan gsum lhan skyes su 'jog pa gcig bshad la, de bzhin du lugs mthun gyi snang mched thob gsum dang de gsum dga' ba gsum du bzhag pa lhan skyes kyi dga' bar mi 'jog kyang , lugs mthun yas babs kyi dga' ba gsum lhan skyes kyi dga' bar 'jog pa'i skabs gcig kyang yod par mngon no, ,zhes gsungs pa tsam las gsal bar bshad pa mi snang la
dga' bar.english: Here the text on the stage of completion entitled The Golden Harvest of Attainments says, It would be incorrect to say that the three stages of light, proliferation, and attainment as the process reverses itself constitute the wisdom of the clear light.  Nonetheless, there is an explanation that the other three forms of bliss during this reversal of the process are the simultaneous form.  We do see, in the same way, the three of light, proliferation, and attainment spoken of as the process moves in its forward progression--and we see these three spoken of as being three of the forms of bliss, even though they are not said to be simultaneous bliss.  It does appear though that there is another point where the three forms of bliss during the forward progression are said to be simultaneous bliss. We don't find any more specific reference on this point than what is here.

dga' bar.english: And so the Prince replied, "I will agree then to make a household; but only one which is in no way contrary to the teachings of the Dharma." His holy parents then were overjoyed, and took the Prince by the hand, exclaiming "Excellent, excellent, o highest of sons!  You have made your parents happy!  You have filled the two of us, your father and mother, with gladness and joy!"  And then they threw themselves on the ground and made prostrations to Him. His Marriage to the Lady Immaculate

dga' bar.english: And the Hag says to Naropa, "What is it you're looking at here?" He replies, "These are sacred books, on the subjects of classical languages and the art of reasoning--using scriptural authority and logic to prove things." "And do you understand those books?"  She asks. "I do," He says. "But do you understand the words, or the meaning?" "I understand the words," He answers.  This makes the Witch so pleased that She jumps up and down, wildly, waving Her staff in the air and darting here and there. Thinking to make Her even happier, Naropa adds, "I also understand the meaning."

dga' bar.english: With this, She moans in displeasure; Her body is racked with sobs, She smashes Her staff to the ground. Naropa says, "Why did it make you so happy when I said I understood the words; but now when all I added was that I understood the meaning, it makes you so unhappy?" dga' bar.acip: GNYIS PA BYANG SEMS ZHU BA LA BRTEN NAS DGA' BZHI SKYED TSUL NI, BYANG SEMS ZHU BAS GNAS GANG DU SLEB PA NA YAS BABS KYI DGA' BZHI SKYE TSUL NI, RGYUD RDO RJE 'PHRENG BA LAS, ,DE RJES LUGS 'BYUNG BSHAD BYA STE, ,BDE CHEN 'KHOR LO SPYI BO LA, ,DE NI DGA' BAR BSHAD PA YIN, ,LONG SPYOD 'KHOR LOR MCHOG DGA' DANG, ,BRAL DGA' CHOS KYI 'KHOR LOR GNAS, ,SPRUL PA'I 'KHOR LOR LHAN CIG SKYES, ,DGA' BA NYAMS SU MYONG BAR BYED,
dga' bar.wylie: gnyis pa byang sems zhu ba la brten nas dga' bzhi skyed tshul ni, byang sems zhu bas gnas gang du sleb pa na yas babs kyi dga' bzhi skye tshul ni, rgyud rdo rje 'phreng ba las, ,de rjes lugs 'byung bshad bya ste, ,bde chen 'khor lo spyi bo la, ,de ni dga' bar bshad pa yin, ,long spyod 'khor lor mchog dga' dang, ,bral dga' chos kyi 'khor lor gnas, ,sprul pa'i 'khor lor lhan cig skyes, ,dga' ba nyams su myong bar byed
dga' bar.english: We move on now to our second part: how it is that the four kinds of bliss are brought on through the meltdown of the element of enlightenment.  Here is how the four types of bliss arise, coming down, as the element of enlightenment melts down and reaches different places.  The secret teaching called The String of Diamonds says: Following that we explain How they come going forward: It's said that what you get At the tip of the head, In the chakra of great bliss, Is what we call "ecstasy." At the chakra of experience Is the one called "high ecstasy"; At the chakra of the dharma Is the "ecstasy of abandonment," And the ecstasy that you come to experience In the chakra of emanation Is called the "simultaneous."

dga' bar.acip: BZHI PA LA GSUM, RIG MA DANG SNYOMS PAR ZHUGS PAS BSKYED PA'I BDUD RTZI ZOS PA'I BCUD LEN GYIS LUS KYI STOBS RGYAS PAR BYA BA, GSUNG RDO RJE'I LCES RTZA BSKUL NAS BDE BA BSKYED DE LAS BYUNG BA'I BDUD RTZI LCES MYANG BA DANG, PADMA CAN LA SOGS PA'I PHYAG RGYA RNAMS KYIS YID DGA' BAR BYA ZHING DE RNAMS KYI THUGS SUN MI DBYUNG PA MJUG SDUD DANG BCAS PA'O,,

dga' bar.english: The fourth topic has three parts: (1) A description of how we partake of the nectar that is produced when we engage in union with our Lady of Knowledge, and how this acts as a nutritive essence which strengthens the body; (2) How we use our tongue--as the diamond of enlightened speech--to stimulate the lower end of the partner's inner channel, and produce bliss in Her; and then use our tongue again to partake of the nectar that comes from Her because of this bliss; (3) How partners such as the Lady of the Lotus are pleased, and how we must be careful never to upset their minds--along with a concluding section. * * * Choney Lama Drakpa Shedrup (1675-1748) gives some additional, useful detail on the need for both inner and outer aids in his Book to Please Those with a Core of Goodness: A Brief Explanation of the Very Essence of "The Lamp that Illuminates, Totally, the Teaching on the Five Steps," on the Stage of Completion in the Teachings of the Glorious Secret Collection (ACIP digital text S00260, ff. 26b-27a):

dga' bar.acip: (KHA CIG SUN DBYUNG BAR MI BYA BA'I SKAD DOD LA 'DOD CHAGS DANG BRAL BAR MI BYA ZHES PAR YOD PAS, THIG LE NYAMS PAS 'DOD CHAGS DANG BRAL BAR MI BYA BA LA 'CHAD PA NI SKABS DON MA RTOGS PAR SNANG STE, THUGS KYI RDO RJE MI SMAD PA NI SMOD TSIG GIS BUD MED KYI SEMS MA DGA' BAR MI BYA BA'I DON YIN GYI, SGRUB PA PO RANG GI SEMS LA BYED PA MIN PA'I PHYIR RO,,)
dga' bar.wylie: (kha cig sun dbyung bar mi bya ba'i skad dod la 'dod chags dang bral bar mi bya zhes par yod pas, thig le nyams pas 'dod chags dang bral bar mi bya ba la 'chad pa ni skabs don ma rtogs par snang ste, thugs kyi rdo rje mi smad pa ni smod tshig gis bud med kyi sems ma dga' bar mi bya ba'i don yin gyi, sgrub pa po rang gi sems la byed pa min pa'i phyir ro,,)
dga' bar.english: Now some commentators have pointed out that the original Sanskrit for "don't upset the mind" can also mean "never lose your passion."  And so they explain this section as meaning that we should never lose our sexual passion, since this would then hurt the essential drops within our body. This interpretation though misses the context of the current line.  When it says that we should "never disparage the diamond of enlightened mind," what it's talking about is never displeasing the heart of our Lady.  It's not however a reference to the mind of the practitioner themselves.

dga' bar.acip: DER TZU MBA NA BYA BYA ZHING LCE RTZE 'DRIL BAS DRUD LA, CHANG GI BTUNG BA DANG LDAN PAS SEMS RAB TU DGA' BAR BYAS NAS, RDO RJE DANG PAD MA SBYOR BAS ROL BAR BYA'O,,

dga' bar.english: It is here we are to perform the chumba of our kiss, massaging it with the turn of the tip of our tongue.  Make the minds happy with the drinking of liquor, and then play, in the union of the diamond rod and lotus.

dga' bar.acip: ,ZHES GSUNGS PA LTAR MKHA' 'GRO MA'I PHO NYA MANG PO ZHIG G-YON PA'I KUN SPYOD LA DGYES SHING BYA BA DES 'JUG PAS G-YON PA'I KUN SPYOD DE RNAMS DANG MTHUN PAR SPYAD PAS DE DAG YID DGA' BAR 'GYUR BA YANG YIN NO,,
dga' bar.wylie: zhes gsungs pa ltar mkha' 'gro ma'i pho nya mang po zhig g-yon pa'i kun spyod la dgyes shing bya ba des 'jug pas g-yon pa'i kun spyod de rnams dang mthun par spyad pas de dag yid dga' bar 'gyur ba yang yin no
dga' bar.english: The point of these lines is that a great many Angel Messengers take pleasure in leftways behavior, and do what they do following this behavior.  If we go through our daily life in harmony with their kind of behavior, then these Angels will be glad with us.   KHYAD PAR DU LAG PA G-YON PA MCHOD PA'I KUN SPYOD BYED PA NI PHO NYA MO KHYAD PAR CAN DANG 'DU BA LA SNGON DU BRDA BSTAN DGOS LA, BRDA YANG LAG PA G-YON PAS BYED DE, RTZA RGYUD LAS, The most special thing here is the leftways behavior of making the offering of the left hand.  The point is that, before one engages in union with one of these extraordinary Messengers, you must first make a special sign.  And this sign must be made with your left hand.  As the root secret teaching states,
