snga ma.acip: ,GZUGS SKU'I MTSAN DPE RNAMS NI RI MOS BRIS PA'I GZUGS BRNYAN LTAR RKYEN TSOGS PA LAS BYUNG BA'I KUN RDZOB BRDZUN PA'I GNAS TSUL YIN GYI, BDEN PA'I RANG BZHIN MIN NO ZHES STON PA NI, BCOM LDAN 'DAS KYIS RAB 'BYOR LA CI TZAM DU MTSAN PHUN SUM TSOGS PA DE TZAM DU BRDZUN NO ZHES GSUNGS, 'O NA MI BRDZUN PA GANG ZHE NA, JI TZAM DU MTSAN DPE PHUN SUM TSOGS PA RNAMS BDEN PAR MED PA DE TZAM NI MI BRDZUN ZHING BDEN TE, DE LTAR DE BZHIN GSHEGS PA LA BDEN PAR GRUB PA'I MTSAN DANG MTSAN MA MED PAR BLTA BAR BYA'O, , 'DIS GZUGS SKU LA MTHA' GNYIS SEL TE, GZUGS SKU DANG DE'I MTSAN DPE RNAMS KUN RDZOB BRDZUN PA'I STONG TSUL DU YOD PAS SKUR 'DEBS SEL ZHING , BDEN GRUB KYI MTSAN DANG MTSAN MA MED PAR BSTAN PAS SGRO 'DOGS KYI MTHA' SEL BA'I PHYIR RO, , DE'I SNGA MAS GZUGS SKU DANG PHYI MAS CHOS KYI SKU BSTAN TE NGO BO NYID SKU GTZO CHE'O,
snga ma.wylie: gzugs sku'i mtshan dpe rnams ni ri mos bris pa'i gzugs brnyan ltar rkyen tshogs pa las byung ba'i kun rdzob brdzun pa'i gnas tshul yin gyi, bden pa'i rang bzhin min no zhes ston pa ni, bcom ldan 'das kyis rab 'byor la ci tsam du mtshan phun sum tshogs pa de tsam du brdzun no zhes gsungs, 'o na mi brdzun pa gang zhe na, ji tsam du mtshan dpe phun sum tshogs pa rnams bden par med pa de tsam ni mi brdzun zhing bden te, de ltar de bzhin gshegs pa la bden par grub pa'i mtshan dang mtshan ma med par blta bar bya'o, , 'dis gzugs sku la mtha' gnyis sel te, gzugs sku dang de'i mtshan dpe rnams kun rdzob brdzun pa'i stong tshul du yod pas skur 'debs sel zhing , bden grub kyi mtshan dang mtshan ma med par bstan pas sgro 'dogs kyi mtha' sel ba'i phyir ro, , de'i snga mas gzugs sku dang phyi mas chos kyi sku bstan te ngo bo nyid sku gtso che'o
snga ma.english: The marks and signs on the physical body of the Buddha are like an image drawn on a piece of paper: they are not the real thing--they exist in a deceptive manner, as things that occur when all of their causes have gathered together. They do not exist as something with a true nature. To indicate this fact, Lord Buddha says to Subhuti, "Insofar as the totally exquisite marks on a Buddha's body exist, as such they are deceptive. "Just what," you may ask, "is meant by the word deceptive?" The totally exquisite marks and signs on a Buddha's body are also not deceptive, and true, but only insofar as they do not exist truly. Thus you should see the One Thus Gone as having no marks, no marks to indicate his nature, at all. The section here helps to prevent us from falling into either one of the two extremes. The physical body of the Buddha and its various marks and signs do exist--albeit in a deceptive way, in a false or empty way--and this fact keeps us from the extreme of denying the existence of something which actually does exist. The text though also states that there exist no marks, and no marks that would indicate any nature, which also exist truly. This fact keeps us from the extreme of asserting the existence of something which actually does not exist. The former of these two [marks] is referring to the physical body of a Buddha. The latter is referring to the dharma body, and chiefly to the essence body. 9 On the Future of the Buddha's Teachings

snga ma.english: Here in a statement over and above the one before, Lord Buddha says, O Subhuti, consider any son or daughter of noble family who takes up this sutra, who holds it in their hands, and so on--any living being who does these things and then puts the meaning of the sutra into practice. It is entirely possible that such a person could experience some pain, that they could suffer, and suffer intensely, through various kinds of illness, or conflict with others, or being criticized, or chained, or beaten, or anything of the like. It could happen, but it would be no great problem, because. . .

snga ma.acip: , DE CI'I PHYIR ZHE NA, RAB 'BYOR, SEMS CAN DE DAG GIS TSE RABS SNGA MA'I MI DGE BA'I LAS NGAN SONG DU SKYE BAR 'GYUR BA GANG DAG BYAS PA DAG TSE 'DI NYID LA MNAR BAS, TSE RABS SNGA MA'I MI DGE BA'I LAS DE DAG 'BYANG BAR 'GYUR TE, SANGS RGYAS KYI BYANG CHUB KYANG 'THOB PAR 'GYUR BA'I PHYIR RO,
snga ma.wylie: de ci'i phyir zhe na, rab 'byor, sems can de dag gis tshe rabs snga ma'i mi dge ba'i las ngan song du skye bar 'gyur ba gang dag byas pa dag tshe 'di nyid la mnar bas, tshe rabs snga ma'i mi dge ba'i las de dag 'byang bar 'gyur te, sangs rgyas kyi byang chub kyang 'thob par 'gyur ba'i phyir ro
snga ma.english: Why is it so? Because, o Subhuti, such beings are purifying non-virtuous karma from the entire string of their previous lives, karma that would have taken them to the three lower realms. As they purify this karma, it causes them to suffer here in this life. As such they will succeed in cleaning away the karma of these non-virtuous deeds of their previous lifetimes, and they will as well achieve the enlightenment of a Buddha.

snga ma.wylie: rgyu mtshan de ci'i phyir zhe na, sems can de dag gis ni tshe rabs 'di dang snga ma'i dus su mi dge ba'i las chen po ngan song gsum du skye bar 'gyur ba'i las gang dag byas pa de dag thams cad kyi 'bras bu ni tshe 'di nyid kyi thog la smin te sdug bsngal gyis mnar ba de'i stobs kyis tshe rabs snga ma'i mi dge ba'i las de dag thams cad 'byang ba ste dag par 'gyur te, sangs rgyas kyi byang chub kyang myur du thob par 'gyur ro, , sher phyin la brtson pa'i gnyen po kun tu spyod pa'i stobs kyis ni sdig las rnams kyi rtsa ba bdag 'dzin bcom ste thar pa dang thams cad mkhyen pa yang thob par 'gyur zhes bshad na, ngan 'gror skye ba'i las rnams 'joms pa lta ci smos so, , tshul de ltar rtog ge 'bar ba sogs nas bshad cing , thar pa chen po las kyang , ngan 'gror skye ba'i sdig yod kyang , , mgo bo na ba tsam gyis 'byang , , zhes gsungs so, , dper na sa bon btab kyang chu lud drod gsher sogs gtan med na myu gu mi skye ba ltar bdag 'dzin spong nus na ni, bsags pa'i las ci yod kyang grogs nyon mongs med pas rnam smin 'byin mi nus te, rnam 'grel las, srid pa'i sred las rnam brgal ba'i, , las gzhan 'phen nus ma yin te, , lhan cig byed pa zad phyir ro, , zhes gsungs pa ltar ro
snga ma.english: For what reason is it so? Because such beings are purifying great non- virtuous karma that they have committed both in this life and in their lifetimes past--karma so serious that it would normally have taken them to the three lower realms. As such, the results of all these deeds are ripening here in this very life. Thus one is suffering pain, and by force of this suffering he or she is "cleaning away"--that is, purifying--all of this non-virtuous karma. As such, one will quickly achieve the enlightenment of a Buddha. The force of an antidote action consisting of making great efforts in the perfection of wisdom is destroying the grasping to some self-existence, the very root of all non-virtuous deeds. This is why the text goes on to say that one will achieve freedom and the state of omniscience. And since the text does say this, then needless to say one could destroy the karma that is leading you to a birth in the lower realms. The way in which this works is explained in texts such as the Blaze of Reasoning and others. As the Sutra of the Great Liberation says as well, Even though one may have the bad karma To take his birth in the three lower realms, A simple headache will clean it away. Suppose for example that a seed is planted, but is then deprived completely of water, or fertilizer, or warmth, or the rest. Then it would never sprout. Here the case is the same. If you are able to eliminate grasping to some self- nature, then none of the karmas you have collected, regardle

snga ma.acip: RANG GI DE RING GI RIG PA 'DI KHA SANG GI RIG PA'I RIG RGYUN DANG , DA LO'I RIG PA 'DI LO SNGA MA'I RIG PA'I RIG RGYUN YIN PA BZHIN DU, RANG GI TSE 'DI'I RIG PA 'DI TSE SNGA MA'I RIG PA'I RIG RGYUN DANG , TSE SNGA MA'I RIG PA DE YANG DE'I TSE SNGA MA SNGA MA'I RIG RGYUN YIN PAS DE GA NANG BZHIN PHAR DED NA 'DI PHAN CHAD DU MED BYA BA GTAN NAS MED PAR RIG PA'I YA MTHA' THUG MED DU 'GRUB CING ,
snga ma.wylie: rang gi de ring gi rig pa 'di kha sang gi rig pa'i rig rgyun dang , da lo'i rig pa 'di lo snga ma'i rig pa'i rig rgyun yin pa bzhin du, rang gi tshe 'di'i rig pa 'di tshe snga ma'i rig pa'i rig rgyun dang , tshe snga ma'i rig pa de yang de'i tshe snga ma snga ma'i rig rgyun yin pas de ga nang bzhin phar ded na 'di phan chad du med bya ba gtan nas med par rig pa'i ya mtha' thug med du 'grub cing
snga ma.english: Your awareness of today is a mental continuation of the awareness you had yesterday. This year's awareness is a mental continuation of the awareness you had the year before. Just so, your awareness over this entire life is a mental continuation of the awareness you had in your former life. The awareness you had in your former life was, in turn, a mental continuation of the awareness you had in the life before that. You can continue back in a regression like this and absolutely never reach some point where you can say, "Prior to this, I had no awareness." This then proves the infinite regression of one's awareness.

snga ma.acip: ,ZHES RANG GI TSE SNGA MA'I PHA TSE 'DI LA BUR 'GYUR BA DANG , SNGA MA'I MA CHUNG MAR 'GYUR BA DANG , DGRA MDZA' BSHES SU 'GYUR BA DANG , YANG DE LAS GO LDOG STE SNGA MA'I BU TSE 'DI'I PHAR 'GYUR BA SOGS SHIN TU MA NGES PAR MA ZAD, TSE 'DIR YANG LO SNGA MA GCIG GIS GCIG GSOD PAR BRTZAMS PA'I DGRA ZHIG LO PHYI MA GNYEN GYI DVANG MAR 'GYUR BA SOGS NGES PA MED PA MNGON SUM GYIS GRUB PA LA, NGES PA YOD YOD 'DRA BAR BZUNG STE CHAGS SDANG DRAG POS PHAN GNOD BYED PA MANG BA NI KHYI 'THOM THANG LA 'KHYAMS PA DANG 'DRA STE KHYI 'THOM ZHIG DON CHEN PO YOD YOD 'DRA BAR PHYOGS GCIG LA LDUR LDUR RGYUG PA NA MI ZHIG GIS SKAD CHEN POS KHYOD BYAS NA STABS KYIS LOG STE YANG PHYOGS GZHAN ZHIG LA SNGAR LTAR RGYUG GO, DES NA DGRA GNYEN LA RIGS SU BCAD NAS CHAGS SDANG SKYE BA BKAG STE 'KHOR BA'I CHOS LA BLO GTAD SA GANG YANG MED PAR BLTAS LA SKYO BAR BYA'O,
snga ma.wylie: zhes rang gi tshe snga ma'i pha tshe 'di la bur 'gyur ba dang , snga ma'i ma chung mar 'gyur ba dang , dgra mdza' bshes su 'gyur ba dang , yang de las go ldog ste snga ma'i bu tshe 'di'i phar 'gyur ba sogs shin tu ma nges par ma zad, tshe 'dir yang lo snga ma gcig gis gcig gsod par brtsams pa'i dgra zhig lo phyi ma gnyen gyi dvang mar 'gyur ba sogs nges pa med pa mngon sum gyis grub pa la, nges pa yod yod 'dra bar bzung ste chags sdang drag pos phan gnod byed pa mang ba ni khyi 'thom thang la 'khyams pa dang 'dra ste khyi 'thom zhig don chen po yod yod 'dra bar phyogs gcig la ldur ldur rgyug pa na mi zhig gis skad chen pos khyod byas na stabs kyis log ste yang phyogs gzhan zhig la sngar ltar rgyug go, des na dgra gnyen la rigs su bcad nas chags sdang skye ba bkag ste 'khor ba'i chos la blo gtad sa gang yang med par bltas la skyo bar bya'o
snga ma.english: What this verse is saying is that it is possible for the person who was your father in your last life to turn into your son in this life. Your mother in your last life then can turn to your wife in this one. Your worst enemy can turn into your dearest relative, and the complete reverse of all these can happen as well: your son in your past life turns into your father in this one, and all the rest--there is no absolutely no certainty who is who. And that's not all. Even in this present life, we can see with our own two eyes how uncertain life can be: a person who was ready to murder someone the year before becomes in the following year their bosom friend, and so on. People though grasp to the occasional appearance that these relationships are something that are certain, and then begin to feel strong emotions of attachment, or anger. These lead them to spend their lives helping some people, and hurting others. They act like some kind of animal, dazed and confused, wandering aimlessly across some great wasteland. The animal runs, with no idea what it does, exhausting itself in the pursuit of what seems to be some great goal. And then some man appears and shouts at it, "What are you doing!" And then the animal reverses direction, and runs just as purposefully the opposite way. So give up now this tendency you have of making any distinction between your friends and your enemies, this habit of liking the friends, and disliking the enemies. Come to realize that there is not a single

snga ma.acip: ,KA MA BA LA DMIGS PA SPO BAR ZHUS TZA NA SNGA MA SKYOR SKAD, 'PHRO NAS ZHUS TZA NA 'PHRO YE MA THOD PA ZHES GSUNG LO, , DE LTAR NA BLOS LCOGS NA SNGAR BSHAD PA BZHIN BSGOM ZHING , MA LCOGS NA RTZA BA GSUM LA RGYU MTSAN DGU JI LTAR 'TSAM PA RE BZUNG LA, GSOD SAR 'KHRID PA LA RGYAN BTAGS PA LTAR TSE 'DI'I BYA BA RNAMS LAS YID MA LOG GI BAR DU YANG DANG YANG DU BSGOM PAR BYA'O, , BSHES GNYEN BSTEN PA DANG DAL 'BYOR DANG MI RTAG PA'I SKOR RNAMS GSUNG RAB DGONGS 'GREL DANG BCAS PA GA NA 'DUG KYANG SKABS DE DANG DE'I NYAMS LEN DU SHES PAR BYAS NAS BSKYANGS NA RGYAL BA'I DGONGS PA RNAMS BDE BLAG TU RNYED PAR 'GYUR TE SKABS GZHAN DU 'ANG DE LTAR SHES PAR BYA'O,
snga ma.wylie: ka ma ba la dmigs pa spo bar zhus tsa na snga ma skyor skad, 'phro nas zhus tsa na 'phro ye ma thod pa zhes gsung lo, , de ltar na blos lcogs na sngar bshad pa bzhin bsgom zhing , ma lcogs na rtsa ba gsum la rgyu mtshan dgu ji ltar 'tsham pa re bzung la, gsod sar 'khrid pa la rgyan btags pa ltar tshe 'di'i bya ba rnams las yid ma log gi bar du yang dang yang du bsgom par bya'o, , bshes gnyen bsten pa dang dal 'byor dang mi rtag pa'i skor rnams gsung rab dgongs 'grel dang bcas pa ga na 'dug kyang skabs de dang de'i nyams len du shes par byas nas bskyangs na rgyal ba'i dgongs pa rnams bde blag tu rnyed par 'gyur te skabs gzhan du 'ang de ltar shes par bya'o
snga ma.english: They say too that when someone would ask Kamawa if they could move on to a new spiritual topic he would say, "Work again on the old one." When they asked if he could finish up the old one, he would say, "There is no finish to the old one." So if your mind can handle it, do the meditation as I have described it above. If your mind cannot handle it, then try to absorb as many of the nine reasons for the three principles as fits your capacity. Meditate over and over on your death until you gain a complete disgust for the activities of this life; until you can think of them like a man on his way to the site of his execution, stopping to put on some fine jewelry. The subjects of how to serve a spiritual guide, of the spiritual fortune and leisure of this life, and of our impermanence are found throughout the supreme form of speech, the word of the Buddha, and the commentaries upon it. You must come to realize that these are instructions to be put into practice at each point where they occur, and so you should actually undertake them at each step. If you do so, then you will be able to grasp the true intent of the victorious Buddhas quite easily. You should apply this advice to each of the other sections here as well. 205 The Asian Classics Institute Course XVII: The Great Ideas of Buddhism, Part Two Reading Seven: The Ethical Life, Part One 1 The Ethical Life Empowers You for Meditation and Wisdom The first reading for this class comes from Je Tsongkapa's Epistle to Ngawang Drakpa

snga ma.acip: ,BLA MA GONG MA RNAMS MIR SKYES NA YANG SROG GCOD SOGS DE DAG LA DGA' BAR 'GYUR BA BYED PA RGYU MTHUN GYI 'BRAS BU DANG SNGA MA RNAMS MYONG BA RGYU MTHUN GYI 'BRAS BUR BZHED DO,
snga ma.wylie: bla ma gong ma rnams mir skyes na yang srog gcod sogs de dag la dga' bar 'gyur ba byed pa rgyu mthun gyi 'bras bu dang snga ma rnams myong ba rgyu mthun gyi 'bras bur bzhed do
snga ma.english: Great lamas of the past have expressed the position that the "consistent" consequence is where, even if you do manage to take birth as a human, you enjoy killing things, and so on. snga ma.acip: ,DE NAS BYAMS PA DANG SNYING RJE'I RTZA BA CAN GYI BYANG CHUB KYI MCHOG TU SEMS BSKYED PA LA 'KHOR LO SGYUR BA'I RGYAL PO SPYAN 'DREN PA'I GNAS KHANG SOGS BYI DOR BYED PA BZHIN DU 'GAL RKYEN SGRIB PA BSHAGS PA DANG , MTHUN RKYEN TSOGS BSAGS NAS BYANG CHUB KYI SEMS GZUNG DGOS PA'I SNGA MA LE'U GNYIS PA DANG , PHYI MA LE'U GSUM PAS BSTAN TO,
snga ma.wylie: de nas byams pa dang snying rje'i rtsa ba can gyi byang chub kyi mchog tu sems bskyed pa la 'khor lo sgyur ba'i rgyal po spyan 'dren pa'i gnas khang sogs byi dor byed pa bzhin du 'gal rkyen sgrib pa bshags pa dang , mthun rkyen tshogs bsags nas byang chub kyi sems gzung dgos pa'i snga ma le'u gnyis pa dang , phyi ma le'u gsum pas bstan to
snga ma.english: You must go about developing the wish to achieve supreme enlightenment, that wish whose very root is love and compassion, in the same way that you would go about preparing to welcome a King who ruled the entire world by cleaning your house, and so on. You will be able to acquire this wish by purifying all of the factors which obstruct your spiritual realizations, and gathering together the power of good deeds which promote them. These two subjects are covered respectively in the second and third chapters.

snga ma.acip: ,NYON MONGS 'DI NI RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PAS STONG BZHIN DU RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PAR SNANG BA SGYU MA DANG 'DRA BA DE'I DUS RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PAS RTZA BA NAS SPONG MI NUS SNYAM DU SNYING LA 'JIGS PA SPONG LA STONG NYID RTOGS PA'I SHES RAB BSKYED NAS NYON MONGS SPANG BA'I PHYIR BRTZON PA BSTEN PAR RIGS KYI DE LTAR NUS BZHIN DU DON MED PA NYID DU BDAG LA DMYAL BA LA SOGS PA'I NGAN SONG RNAMS SU CI STE GNOD PA BYED DU 'JUG STE 'JUG PAR MI RIGS SO, , SNGA MA RNAMS SA BON PHYUNG NA GNAS DE DAG TU MI GNAS PA LA YANG BSHAD DO,
snga ma.wylie: nyon mongs 'di ni rang bzhin gyis grub pas stong bzhin du rang bzhin gyis grub par snang ba sgyu ma dang 'dra ba de'i dus rang bzhin gyis grub pas rtsa ba nas spong mi nus snyam du snying la 'jigs pa spong la stong nyid rtogs pa'i shes rab bskyed nas nyon mongs spang ba'i phyir brtson pa bsten par rigs kyi de ltar nus bzhin du don med pa nyid du bdag la dmyal ba la sogs pa'i ngan song rnams su ci ste gnod pa byed du 'jug ste 'jug par mi rigs so, , snga ma rnams sa bon phyung na gnas de dag tu mi gnas pa la yang bshad do
snga ma.english: One might have the following thought: "These mental afflictions are empty of any natural kind of existence, but at the same time they do appear to have natural existence, and so they are like an illusion. As long as this is the case--because they do exist through some nature of their own--I could never eliminate them from their root." It is good though if I can eliminate this fear from my heart, and rely on the practice of making great efforts to remove my mental afflictions, through working to develop the wisdom which perceives emptiness. Given that I therefore have at the present moment the ability to remove these afflictions, it is not good on the other hand that I subject myself pointlessly to the sufferings of the lower realms, to hells and the rest. Why should I put myself through these pains? Some commentators have also explained the previous lines as referring to the fact that, once we remove the seeds for the mental afflictions, they can no longer stay in these various places. 10 Listening to the Doctor

snga ma.acip: ,GSUM PA NI, DE LTAR 'BRAS BU BSKYED PA'I BYA BA THAMS CAD GZHAN GYI DBANG CAN YIN LA RKYEN DE RNAMS KYANG RGYU RKYEN SNGA MA SNGA MA DE'I DBANG GIS 'BYUNG BAS 'BRAS BU DE 'BYUNG MI 'BYUNG GI DBANG MED PA SGYU MA DANG SPRUL PA LTA BU'O, , DNGOS PO THAMS CAD RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PAS STONG BZHIN DU BYA BA BYED PA DE LTAR SHES NAS SPRUL PA LTA BU'I DNGOS PO KUN LA KHRO BAR MI 'GYUR BAS, NYON MONGS KYI SA BON 'JOMS PA'I RTEN 'BYUNG RANG BZHIN MED PAR RTOGS PA LA BSLAB PAR BYA'O,
snga ma.wylie: gsum pa ni, de ltar 'bras bu bskyed pa'i bya ba thams cad gzhan gyi dbang can yin la rkyen de rnams kyang rgyu rkyen snga ma snga ma de'i dbang gis 'byung bas 'bras bu de 'byung mi 'byung gi dbang med pa sgyu ma dang sprul pa lta bu'o, , dngos po thams cad rang bzhin gyis grub pas stong bzhin du bya ba byed pa de ltar shes nas sprul pa lta bu'i dngos po kun la khro bar mi 'gyur bas, nyon mongs kyi sa bon 'joms pa'i rten 'byung rang bzhin med par rtogs pa la bslab par bya'o
snga ma.english: Here is the third point from before, which is an explanation of why it is improper to feel anger once you have understood that all beings are like a magical show. And so it is that everything in the production of a result depends on other influences, while these influences depend themselves on other, previous causes and influences, they on theirs, and so on. In a sense then it is inevitable whether a particular result will come out or not, it is all up to the causes, and so these things are like a magical show, like pictures of illusion. You must understand this fact, that each and everything which does something is empty of any nature of its own, and yet still functions perfectly well. If you do so, then you will feel no anger towards any of these things that are like pictures of illusion. Thus you must train yourself in the realization of the fact that dependent origination has no nature of its own, for it is this realization which destroys the very seeds of mental affliction. Contemplation Seven People do so much harm to themselves that it is no surprise if they hurt us

snga ma.acip: ,BLA MA GNYEN LA SOGS PA DANG , ,BSHES LA GNOD PA BYED RNAMS LA'ANG , ,SNGA MA'I TSUL GYIS RKYEN DAG LAS, ,'GYUR BAR MTHONG NAS KHRO BA
snga ma.wylie: bla ma gnyen la sogs pa dang , ,bshes la gnod pa byed rnams la'ang , ,snga ma'i tshul gyis rkyen dag las, ,'gyur bar mthong nas khro ba
snga ma.english: And even too when harm is done To Lamas or relatives or the like, And those who are our friends, Turn back your anger by seeing the fact That, as the way before, It all comes from causes.

snga ma.acip: ,GNYIS PA NI, RANG LA CHOS STON PA'I BLA MA DANG DUS GCIG PA'I GNYEN LA SOGS PA DANG MDZA' BSHES LA GNOD PA BYED PA RNAMS LA'ANG GZHAN GYIS GNOD PA BYED PA MTHONG NA KHRO BAR MI RIGS TE GNYEN LA SOGS PA DE DAG GIS SNGON MI RIGS PA BYAS PA'I LAS KYIS BSKUL BA'I SNGA MA SNGAR BSHAD PA'I TSUL GYIS LAS KYI RKYEN DAG LAS 'BYUNG BAR 'GYUR BA MTHONG NAS RANG NYID KHRO BA LDOG PAR BYA'O,
snga ma.wylie: gnyis pa ni, rang la chos ston pa'i bla ma dang dus gcig pa'i gnyen la sogs pa dang mdza' bshes la gnod pa byed pa rnams la'ang gzhan gyis gnod pa byed pa mthong na khro bar mi rigs te gnyen la sogs pa de dag gis sngon mi rigs pa byas pa'i las kyis bskul ba'i snga ma sngar bshad pa'i tshul gyis las kyi rkyen dag las 'byung bar 'gyur ba mthong nas rang nyid khro ba ldog par bya'o
snga ma.english: Here is the second point, which is why it is appropriate to practice, in the same way, patience for those who do harm to those who are close to us. Even too when you see someone hurting another, when persons do harm to the Lamas that are teaching you the Dharma; or else to the relatives or the like with whom you share a family relationship [reading rus for dus in the commentary]; and to those who are your friends, it is wrong to feel anger. This is because of the fact that, in the way that was explained before, what is happening to them has all come about through certain causes: that is, through their own past karma--the injuries are dictated by the karma come from the wrongs that these relatives and so on committed themselves before. And you should turn back your own anger by seeing this fact. Contemplation Thirteen On not being able to bear the happiness of others

snga ma.acip: GAL TE SEMS CAN DE LA SDUG BSNGAL BYUNG BAS BDAG LA MI GNOD PA'I PHYIR MI BSRUNG NGO ZHE NA, DE NI CHES MI RIGS TE RGAS PA'I TSE SDUG BSNGAL BYUNG DOGS NAS GZHON PA'I TSE NOR GSOG PA DANG , DE BZHIN DU SANG DANG PHYI DRO SDUG BSNGAL BYUNG DOGS NAS DI RING DANG SNGA DRO'I DUS NAS SDUG BSNGAL SEL BA'I THABS LA 'BAD PAR MI RIGS PAR THAL, , PHYI MA'I DUS KYI SDUG BSNGAL MA 'ONGS PA'I SDUG BSNGAL YANG SNGA MA'I DUS KYI GANG ZAG DE LA GNOD PAR MI BYED NA DE BYUNG DOGS NAS CIS BSRUNG BSRUNG MI RIGS PAR THAL LO,
snga ma.wylie: gal te sems can de la sdug bsngal byung bas bdag la mi gnod pa'i phyir mi bsrung ngo zhe na, de ni ches mi rigs te rgas pa'i tshe sdug bsngal byung dogs nas gzhon pa'i tshe nor gsog pa dang , de bzhin du sang dang phyi dro sdug bsngal byung dogs nas di ring dang snga dro'i dus nas sdug bsngal sel ba'i thabs la 'bad par mi rigs par thal, , phyi ma'i dus kyi sdug bsngal ma 'ongs pa'i sdug bsngal yang snga ma'i dus kyi gang zag de la gnod par mi byed na de byung dogs nas cis bsrung bsrung mi rigs par thal lo
snga ma.english: Suppose you say the following: "The reason why I don't try to protect all living beings from their suffering is that when this pain comes to them it doesn't hurt to me personally." This though is totally wrong. According to this way of thinking, it must be a mistake for people to try to accumulate money during their younger years out of a concern that they will undergo some kind of suffering during their later years; or for any one of us to try to find some way today, or this morning, to prevent some suffering that we think may come to us tomorrow, or later in the day. Why then do you try to protect yourself from some future pain, from some suffering that you are afraid might come later, since it doesn't do any hurt to you, to the person who exists at the earlier point in time, either? According to your way of thinking, it must be incorrect to do so.

snga ma.acip: GSUM PA NI, DE GNYIS MI MTSUNGS TE GANG ZAG SO SO BA 'BREL MED YIN LA GANG ZAG GCIG GI RKANG LAG TSOGS PA GCIG CING , RGAN GZHON DANG TSE SNGA PHYI RGYUD GCIG YIN PAS PHYI MA LA GCIG GI SDUG BSNGAL GCIG GIS SEL BAR RIGS LA, SNGA MA LA DE MI RIGS SO ZHE NA, RANG DBANG BA'I RGYUD DANG TSOGS PA YANG MED PAR THAL, RGYUD DANG TSOGS PA ZHES BYA BA NI PHRENG BA DANG DMAG LA SOGS PA RANG GI CHA DU MA LA BTAGS PA'I RDZUN PA YIN PA BZHIN DU RGYUN CAN SNGA PHYI DU MA DANG , TSOGS PA CAN LA BTAGS NAS BZHAG PA'I RDZUN PA YIN PA'I PHYIR,
snga ma.wylie: gsum pa ni, de gnyis mi mtshungs te gang zag so so ba 'brel med yin la gang zag gcig gi rkang lag tshogs pa gcig cing , rgan gzhon dang tshe snga phyi rgyud gcig yin pas phyi ma la gcig gi sdug bsngal gcig gis sel bar rigs la, snga ma la de mi rigs so zhe na, rang dbang ba'i rgyud dang tshogs pa yang med par thal, rgyud dang tshogs pa zhes bya ba ni phreng ba dang dmag la sogs pa rang gi cha du ma la btags pa'i rdzun pa yin pa bzhin du rgyun can snga phyi du ma dang , tshogs pa can la btags nas bzhag pa'i rdzun pa yin pa'i phyir
snga ma.english: Here is the third point, which is disproving the objection of thinking that it is wrong to engage in the practice of treating myself and others the same. Someone may make the following objection: The two cases are not the same; [in the former case, of myself and others,] the two beings involved are separate and have no connection. The feet and hands of any one person though are one collection of parts, and the person in his younger and older years, or else in his previous and succeeding lives, is one continuum. Therefore in this latter case it is logical that one of the members should undertake to remove the suffering of the other, whereas in the former case it is not logical. Isn't it true though that there is no collection, and no continuum either, which can act on its own accord? Because isn't it the case that the things we call a "continuum" and a "collection" are simply unreal, in being concepts applied to multiple parts--just like the concepts of a string of things [such as a rosary of beads, or a garland of flowers], or an army, or anything similar? Isn't a continuum simply a concept applied to the combination of what came before and what came later, and isn't a collection simply a concept applied to the components that make it up? Aren't they both therefore unreal?

The feet and hands of any one person though are one collection of parts, and the person in his younger and older years, or else in his previous and succeeding lives, is one continuum. Therefore in this latter case it is logical that one of the members should undertake to remove the suffering of the other, whereas in the former case it is not logical. Isn't it true though that there is no collection, and no continuum either, which can act on its own accord? Because isn't it the case that the things we call a \"continuum\" and a \"collection\" are simply unreal, in being concepts applied to multiple parts--just like the concepts of a string of things [such as a rosary of beads, or a garland of flowers], or an army, or anything similar? Isn't a continuum simply a concept applied to the combination of what came before and what came later, and isn't a collection simply a concept applied to the components that make it up? Aren't they both therefore unreal?"}

snga ma.acip: ,YAN LAG 'DI DAG CES PA LE'U BRGYAD PA NAS BSHAD PA'I ZHI GNAS TZAM LA 'CHAD PA DANG , SBYIN SOGS PHAR PHYIN LHAG MA THAMS CAD LA 'CHAD PA'I LUGS GNYIS LAS, LE'U SNGA PHYI GNYIS TZAM GYI 'BREL BA LA SBYAR NA SNGA MA YANG RUNG MOD KYANG 'DIR PHYI MA LTAR BSHAD NA LEGS SO,
snga ma.wylie: yan lag 'di dag ces pa le'u brgyad pa nas bshad pa'i zhi gnas tsam la 'chad pa dang , sbyin sogs phar phyin lhag ma thams cad la 'chad pa'i lugs gnyis las, le'u snga phyi gnyis tsam gyi 'brel ba la sbyar na snga ma yang rung mod kyang 'dir phyi ma ltar bshad na legs so
snga ma.english: There are two different ways of explaining the phrase "these branches" in the root text at this point. Sometimes it is explained as referring only to the practice of quietude which was covered in the eighth chapter. But it is also explained as referring to all of the remaining perfections, of giving and the rest. If we restrict ourselves only to the relation between the present and the preceding chapters, then the former method of explaining the phrase is also admittedly appropriate. Here though it would be better if we commented upon the phrase in its latter sense.

snga ma.acip: 'DI DAG NI DNGOS PO RANG BZHIN GYIS MED NA YE MED DU 'GYUR ZHING YOD NA RANG BZHIN GYIS YOD DGOS SNYAM PA BDEN GNYIS 'GAL BAR 'DZIN PA'I RTZOD PA'O, , DBU MA PA DANG DNGOS POR SMRA BA'I 'JIG RTEN PA YIS ME LA SOGS PA'I DNGOS PO GNYIS KAS TSAD MAS MTHONG ZHING KHAS LEN PA YIN YANG DNGOS POR SMRA BAS YANG DAG PAR GRUB PA NYID DU RTOG CING KHAS LEN PAR BYED CING BDEN STONG SGYU MA LTA BUR KHONG DU CHUD PA MIN LA, DBU MA PAS KHONG DU CHUD PAS 'DIR YANG RNAL 'BYOR PA DBU MA PA DANG 'JIG RTEN DNGOS POR SMRA BA RTZOD PA YIN NO, , YANG NA 'JIG RTEN PA SNGA MA DNGOS POR SMRA BA 'BA' ZHIG LA SBYAR RO,
snga ma.wylie: 'di dag ni dngos po rang bzhin gyis med na ye med du 'gyur zhing yod na rang bzhin gyis yod dgos snyam pa bden gnyis 'gal bar 'dzin pa'i rtsod pa'o, , dbu ma pa dang dngos por smra ba'i 'jig rten pa yis me la sogs pa'i dngos po gnyis kas tshad mas mthong zhing khas len pa yin yang dngos por smra bas yang dag par grub pa nyid du rtog cing khas len par byed cing bden stong sgyu ma lta bur khong du chud pa min la, dbu ma pas khong du chud pas 'dir yang rnal 'byor pa dbu ma pa dang 'jig rten dngos por smra ba rtsod pa yin no, , yang na 'jig rten pa snga ma dngos por smra ba 'ba' zhig la sbyar ro
snga ma.english: Your argument though is one based on the idea that the two truths cannot coexist: you think that if functional things have no nature of their own, then they must not exist at all; and that if these things do exist, then they must exist with some nature of their own. It is true that those in the world who are of the Middle-Way school and those who are members of the group which asserts that functional things must exist truly can both see things that function, such as fire, with valid perception, and both therefore accept the existence of these objects. Those who believe that functional things exist truly though imagine or believe that these things exist purely; they cannot grasp the fact that they are void of any true existence, that they are just like an illusion. Those of the Middle-Way school though do grasp this fact, and thus there really is an argument here between the "high practitioners," those of the Middle-Way school, and those in the world who assert that things which perform a function exist truly. By the way, you can also interpret the first reference to "those in the world" here as applying only to those who assert that functional things exist truly. Contemplation Six Empty Virtues Do Work Perfectly

snga ma.acip: ,NYON MONGS SPANGS PAS GROL NA ZHES PA NI PHYOGS SNGA MA'I LUGS BRJOD PA YIN LA DE'I DON NI BDEN PA MTHONG BAS GROL 'GYUR GYI, ZHES BSHAD PA BZHIN DU MI RTAG SOGS BCU DRUG GI LAM BSGOMS PAS NYON MONGS SPANGS TE GROL BA 'THOB NA ZHES BSHAD RGYU YIN TE SKABS 'DIR MI RTAG SOGS BCU DRUG GI LAM TZAM GYIS NYON MONGS LAS GROL BA 'THOB MI 'THOB LA RTZOD PA'I PHYIR DANG , BDEN PA MTHONG BAS ZHES SOGS KYI RTZOD PA LAS SHIN TU GSAL BA'I PHYIR RO, , DES NA MI RTAG SOGS BCU DRUG GI LAM GYIS NYON MONGS ZAD PAR NUS PA KHAS BLANGS NAS DES SDUG BSNGAL THAMS CAD LAS GROL BA MIN NO ZHES 'CHAD PA NI 'DI'I DON GTAN MIN NO,
snga ma.wylie: nyon mongs spangs pas grol na zhes pa ni phyogs snga ma'i lugs brjod pa yin la de'i don ni bden pa mthong bas grol 'gyur gyi, zhes bshad pa bzhin du mi rtag sogs bcu drug gi lam bsgoms pas nyon mongs spangs te grol ba 'thob na zhes bshad rgyu yin te skabs 'dir mi rtag sogs bcu drug gi lam tsam gyis nyon mongs las grol ba 'thob mi 'thob la rtsod pa'i phyir dang , bden pa mthong bas zhes sogs kyi rtsod pa las shin tu gsal ba'i phyir ro, , des na mi rtag sogs bcu drug gi lam gyis nyon mongs zad par nus pa khas blangs nas des sdug bsngal thams cad las grol ba min no zhes 'chad pa ni 'di'i don gtan min no
snga ma.english: The lines in the root text that say "If one were liberated by eliminating afflictions..." are a statement of the opponent's position; their purpose is similar to the lines before that went, "One achieves liberation by seeing the truth." The former lines should be explained as saying, "If a person eliminated their mental afflictions, and thereby attained liberation, by means of meditating upon the path of the sixteen aspects of impermanence and the rest..." This is because the debate at this point is about whether or not one can attain liberation from the mental afflictions solely by using the path of the sixteen aspects of impermanence and the rest. Moreover, the fact that they should be explained this way is totally obvious from the debate about liberation occurring "through seeing the truth," and so on. As such, it is not at all the point of these lines to say that, "Although we accept that the path of the sixteen aspects of impermanence and the rest has the power to eliminate your mental afflictions, this doesn't mean you are liberated then from every kind of suffering."

snga ma.acip: GOMDOR NA GRUB MTHA'I DPYAD PA LA MA LTOS PAR NGAM NGAM SHUGS KYIS SKYE BA'I BDAG 'DZIN GNYIS NI LHAN SKYES YIN LA DE LAS GZHAN PA'I BDAG 'DZIN NI KUN BRTAGS SO, , SNGA MA'I ZHEN YUL DGAG BYA'I GTZO BO YIN LA PHYI MA'I ZHEN YUL 'GOG PA SNGA MA 'GOG PA'I YAN LAG TU SHES PAR BYA'O,
snga ma.wylie: gomdor na grub mtha'i dpyad pa la ma ltos par ngam ngam shugs kyis skye ba'i bdag 'dzin gnyis ni lhan skyes yin la de las gzhan pa'i bdag 'dzin ni kun brtags so, , snga ma'i zhen yul dgag bya'i gtso bo yin la phyi ma'i zhen yul 'gog pa snga ma 'gog pa'i yan lag tu shes par bya'o
snga ma.english: In brief, the two forms of the kind of tendency to grasp to things as existing truly which comes in the mind automatically, without relying on analysis according to some philosophical school, are the innate type. All the other tendencies to hold that things have some self-nature are the intellectual kind. It should be understood that the principal object which we deny when we speak of emptiness is the object that the former tendency believes in; disproving the object believed in by the latter tendency is ancillary to disproving that believed in by the former. Contemplation Seventeen The Person and the Parts

snga ma.acip: , PHUNG PO'I YA GYAL BDAG GI MTSAN GZHI YIN PA 'GOG PA NI SO DANG SEN MO BDAG MA YIN BDAG GI MTSAN GZHI NI RUS PA DANG KHRAG MA YIN SNABS MA YIN BAD KAN MA YIN TE DE DAG LA BDAG TU BTAGS PA TZAM DU ZAD PA'I PHYIR, CHU SER DANG NI RNAG KYANG NGA'I MTSAN GZHI MIN BDAG GI MTSAN GZHI NI ZHAG DANG RDUL MIN TE RGYU MTSAN SNGA MA'O,
snga ma.wylie: phung po'i ya gyal bdag gi mtshan gzhi yin pa 'gog pa ni so dang sen mo bdag ma yin bdag gi mtshan gzhi ni rus pa dang khrag ma yin snabs ma yin bad kan ma yin te de dag la bdag tu btags pa tsam du zad pa'i phyir, chu ser dang ni rnag kyang nga'i mtshan gzhi min bdag gi mtshan gzhi ni zhag dang rdul min te rgyu mtshan snga ma'o
snga ma.english: Here is our refutation that the individual members of the various heaps could ever be what "myself" refers to. Neither my teeth nor nails are myself; the bones and blood are not what "myself" refers to; neither is the snot, nor the phlegm; all these are, rather, only something which the idea of a "me" is imposed upon, and nothing more. Nor is the lymph, nor the pus, what "me" refers to; and the fat and particles of the body are nothing that "myself" refers to either--for the exact same reasons that we mentioned earlier.

snga ma.english: Here is an example to illustrate what we have just been talking about. Until such time as you are able to form a mental picture of the child of a barren woman, you can never form a picture of this same child dying.

snga ma.acip: ,DE LTAR LAS DANG LAS GSOG PA PO LA SOGS PA RNAMS LA DPYAD NA GSON PO'I 'JIG RTEN SEMS CAN 'DI, GANG ZHIG SRID PA 'DIR NI 'CHI 'GYUR TE, 'CHI BA RANG BZHIN GYIS MA GRUB PA'I PHYIR, TSE PHYI MA 'BYUNG 'GYUR GANG YIN SKYE BA SNGA MAR 'BYUNG 'GYUR GANG , PHAN 'DOGS PA'I GNYEN GANG YID DU 'ONG BA'I BSHES KYANG GANG ZHIG YIN TE RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA CUNG ZAD KYANG MED DO, , DE LTAR GNAS LUGS KYI DON KHONG DU CHUD PAR BYAS NAS 'JIG RTEN GYI CHOS BRGYAD RO SNYOMS PA LA 'BAD PAR BYA'O,
snga ma.wylie: de ltar las dang las gsog pa po la sogs pa rnams la dpyad na gson po'i 'jig rten sems can 'di, gang zhig srid pa 'dir ni 'chi 'gyur te, 'chi ba rang bzhin gyis ma grub pa'i phyir, tshe phyi ma 'byung 'gyur gang yin skye ba snga mar 'byung 'gyur gang , phan 'dogs pa'i gnyen gang yid du 'ong ba'i bshes kyang gang zhig yin te rang bzhin gyis grub pa cung zad kyang med do, , de ltar gnas lugs kyi don khong du chud par byas nas 'jig rten gyi chos brgyad ro snyoms pa la 'bad par bya'o
snga ma.english: You should in this same way analyze karma, the person collecting the karma, and so on. When you look at all these beings, all those who are alive in the world, who is it then that dies here in this suffering existence? Death itself is nothing that has any nature of its own. Who is it that is going to come and take the future life? Who is it that went and took the last life? Who is the relative that is helping you so much? Who is the friend you feel so attracted to? None of them has the least nature of their own. You must thus come to comprehend the real nature of things, and make great efforts to neutralize the eight worldly thoughts within you. [The eight worldly thoughts consist of having the following emotions, based on a misperception of reality: 1) Being happy when we acquire some thing, 2) And unhappy when we don't. 3) Being happy when we feel good, 4) And unhappy when we don't. 5) Being happy when we become well known, 6) And unhappy when we don't. 7) Being happy when someone speaks well of us, 8) And unhappy when someone speaks ill of us.] Contemplation Thirty-Six The Final End (The following is the last contemplation in the "Chapter on Wisdom")

[The eight worldly thoughts consist of having the following emotions, based on a misperception of reality: 1) Being happy when we acquire some thing, 2) And unhappy when we don't. 3) Being happy when we feel good, 4) And unhappy when we don't. 5) Being happy when we become well known, 6) And unhappy when we don't. 7) Being happy when someone speaks well of us, 8) And unhappy when someone speaks ill of us.] Contemplation Thirty-Six The Final End (The following is the last contemplation in the \"Chapter on Wisdom\")"}

snga ma.acip: BTAGS PA'I TSIG GI MTSAN MA'I GZHI BTAGS PA'I TSIG GI MTSAN MA'I RTEN DU GYUR PA, BRJOD DU MED PA'I BDAG NYID KYIS DON DAM PAR YOD PA YANG DAG PA'I DNGOS PO LA THAMS CAD KYI THAMS CAD DU MED DO ZHES SKUR BA 'DEBS SHING CHUD GZON PAR BYED PA GANG YIN PA 'DI GNYIS NI CHOS 'DUL BA 'DI LAS RAB TU NYAMS PA YIN PAR RIG PAR BYA'O, , ZHES PA SNGA MAS NI SKUR PA 'DEBS TSUL BSTAN LA CHUD GZON ZHES PA MAN CHAD KYIS NI THEG PA CHEN PO'I CHOS ZAB MO LAS NYAMS PAR BSTAN NO, ,
snga ma.wylie: btags pa'i tshig gi mtshan ma'i gzhi btags pa'i tshig gi mtshan ma'i rten du gyur pa, brjod du med pa'i bdag nyid kyis don dam par yod pa yang dag pa'i dngos po la thams cad kyi thams cad du med do zhes skur ba 'debs shing chud gzon par byed pa gang yin pa 'di gnyis ni chos 'dul ba 'di las rab tu nyams pa yin par rig par bya'o, , zhes pa snga mas ni skur pa 'debs tshul bstan la chud gzon zhes pa man chad kyis ni theg pa chen po'i chos zab mo las nyams par bstan no,
snga ma.english: Discounting things is like this; it is saying that the following do not, all in all, exist: that which is the foundation, with the typical features, of the words used to make constructs--that which provides the basis, with the characteristics, of the words used to make constructs; that which exists ultimately, through an identity beyond all expression; and that which is a pure, functioning thing. They are, in short, things that waste one's opportunity; you should understand that these two will cause you to fall from this spiritual way of discipline. The beginning part of this second section constitutes a description of what it is to discount something; and the part including the words "waste one's opportunity" on down is describing how a person would then fall from the profound teaching of the greater way.

snga ma.acip: ,SKAD CIG SNGA MA'I RJES MI GCOD, ,SKAD CIG PHYI MA'I SDUN MI BSU, ,DA LTAR SHES PA SO MA LA, ,BCOS SLAD MED PAR BSGOM PA 'DI,
snga ma.wylie: skad cig snga ma'i rjes mi gcod, ,skad cig phyi ma'i sdun mi bsu, ,da ltar shes pa so ma la, ,bcos slad med par bsgom pa 'di
snga ma.english: They tell us never to revisit The moment that came before; They tell us not to anticipate The moment that comes after: Meditate upon the mind As it's been forever more, No complications, no additions. Here begins a long list of useless meditations that were current in Middle Asia in the time of our author, about 400 years ago.  They didn't help anybody then, and they won't help anybody now, except that we can learn how not to do our own meditations by studying these past mistakes. Modern emptiness mismeditators have added their own uninformed creations to this list, but we should be able to catch them once we finish this review of the old ones. The fact that the mind is in constant flux, and the fact that this state of change is flowing from seed-pictures, are vastly different things.

snga ma.acip: ,SKAD CIG SNGA MA YOD ZER NA, ,SEMS KYI SKAD CIG SNGA MA DE'I, ,BDEN PAR SNANG BA'I SNANG TSUL DE, ,SEMS DANG LHAN CIG 'GYUR MED CING, ,RANG BZHIN GZHAN DU MI 'GYUR DANG, ,RTAG BRTAN THER ZUG GYUR PAS NA, ,MA RIG PA DANG KHAS BLANGS 'GAL,
snga ma.wylie: skad cig snga ma yod zer na, ,sems kyi skad cig snga ma de'i, ,bden par snang ba'i snang tshul de, ,sems dang lhan cig 'gyur med cing, ,rang bzhin gzhan du mi 'gyur dang, ,rtag brtan ther zug gyur pas na, ,ma rig pa dang khas blangs 'gal
snga ma.english: If you reply That there ever was A previous moment In the mind's history, Then let's take a look At how real that former moment Appears to us to be. This way of perceiving That previous moment of mind Is not a thing that accompanies The mind itself; But then again, Neither can we say That its nature is to be Something apart from the mind. You see these moments Within the mind As something frozen solid; Which contradicts Your saying, In the very same breath, That this mind Misunderstands things. Even as we sit in a chair and observe thoughts coming up inside of our mind, we are faced with the logical problem that the mind is both seer and seen in the same moment; whereas clear thinking tells us that a thought must happen first, before we can hear it.  Something else is going on: something different than the normal way we think of the flow of events, and thoughts. First and next

snga ma.acip: ,GTI MUG LA SOGS GA NA MCHIS, ,GTI MUG DANG NI LHAN CIG TU, ,GNAS SO ZHE NA SNGA MA YI, ,SKYON NI 'DIR YANG SO NA GNAS,
snga ma.wylie: gti mug la sogs ga na mchis, ,gti mug dang ni lhan cig tu, ,gnas so zhe na snga ma yi, ,skyon ni 'dir yang so na gnas
snga ma.english: In that case then, How could we ever progress To the darkest thoughts Of ignorance, And other such delights? What, are you going to claim now That you can reside In thoughts of ignorance? You'd be stuck with the exact Same problems That we mentioned before. The one form of mind that the Devil seems to be comfortable with is what the ancient books call “dark ignorance.”  This is just another name for misunderstanding, which is the preferred term in general since we are talking about a mis-knowing of the world rather than an un-knowing of the world.  Even misunderstanding though has to follow the rules of where things really come from, so technically the Devil is going to have trouble staying in it as well. The mind as a whole

snga ma.acip: ,NYON MONGS SKAD CIG SNGA MA NI, ,'GAG BZHIN PA LA'ANG NGA YOD MOD, ,SKAD CIG GNYIS PAR SKYE BZHIN LA'ANG, ,GRUB TZAM LTOS MED NGA YOD PAS,
snga ma.wylie: nyon mongs skad cig snga ma ni, ,'gag bzhin pa la'ang nga yod mod, ,skad cig gnyis par skye bzhin la'ang, ,grub tsam ltos med nga yod pas
snga ma.english: When an earlier instant Of a negative emotion Is in the process of stopping, Admittedly I Must still be there. And even as that of The second instant Is in the act of arising, I am still there too: I arrive from the very occurrence; And I rely on nothing. The Devil is failing here to make a distinction between the way that negative emotions start (through my own seed-pictures) and the solidity that they seem to have when I misunderstand where they have come from. Just because the Devil is “natural” to our mind, from the viewpoint of having always been there so far, doesn't mean that his own existence doesn't depend on anything.  In fact he depends upon the same kind of seed-pictures that everybody and everything else does. A great and total darkness

snga ma.acip: ,SNANG NA SKYON NI SNGA MAR GNAS, ,SNANG BA MED PAR 'JOG ZER NA, ,SNANG BA BSDUS DANG YID BYED BKAG ,YID LA BYAR MED BSGOM PA DANG, ,CI YANG MED PA'I SGOM RNAMS NI, ,NGA YI PHYOGS NAS BLTAS TZA NA, ,KHYAD PAR DBYE BA MED PAR GO ,KHYOD RANG DBYE BA CI YIS 'BYED,
snga ma.wylie: snang na skyon ni snga mar gnas, ,snang ba med par 'jog zer na, ,snang ba bsdus dang yid byed bkag ,yid la byar med bsgom pa dang, ,ci yang med pa'i sgom rnams ni, ,nga yi phyogs nas bltas tsa na, ,khyad par dbye ba med par go ,khyod rang dbye ba ci yis 'byed
snga ma.english: If you say they appear, Then the problem as we Raised it before remains. If you say things Are established as They fail to appear To our perceptions, Then the appearance Is withdrawn, And any turning Of the mind is ended. Which means that now You have a meditation Where you don't turn Your mind to anything, Or where you are meditating On nothing at all. And if you compare this To my interpretation of things, We would have to understand That no distinction between them Could ever be made! And on what basis then Could you make Your own distinctions? The debate here sort of boils down to the question of whether it's better to continue with slightly mistaken meditations on emptiness, or just not meditate at all, given the power with which meditation plants mental seeds! The answer is that the intention to learn to meditate upon emptiness correctly is so karmically wonderful that it makes even our clumsy, childlike attempts at emptiness meditation well worth it.

snga ma.english: Well let me ask you Just where that mental function Is staying then? And if you reply That it is there during The balanced meditation, Then the issues which I raised before remain. As a mental entity, the direct perception of emptiness is in a constant state of flux; but that doesn't mean that it drops the unchanging state of emptiness as its object, every millisecond.  We can focus on the fact that 2+2=4 with an ever-shifting, human mind, without that sum ever shifting to something like 2+2=3, or 2+2=5. Competing with the Numerists

snga ma.wylie: mnyam gzhag dus su yod zer na, ,mnyam gzhag rang dus stong nyid yin, ,stong nyid rang gi dus su ni, ,nga rgyal yod na snga ma yi, ,skyon ni so na gnas pa yin
snga ma.english: And suppose you say That the emptiness is there During the time Of that deep meditation. In that case, The meditation is— During its own duration— Emptiness itself. And then if there Is a divine pride Within the time frame Of the emptiness, Then the problems That we mentioned before Remain there, just the same. The Devil is saying that the part of the mind which is trying to identify with the emptiness that the mind itself sees—again, because this particular emptiness actually is a traditional part of the being of a Buddha—is itself empty, and thus becomes a part of the object of the mind, rather than the subject mind.  But it's no contradiction to say that even while we are watching emptiness in a way which is not direct, we are indeed watching something that our own watching mind cannot be. snga ma.acip: ,YOD NA SNGA MA'I CHU DE GANG, ,MED NA SNGA MA'I CHU DE NI, ,RTING MAR BLUG PA MA YIN NAM, ,BLUG NA MING GI KHYAD BYUNG BAS, ,DE YANG KHYOD LA 'GAL BA YIN,
snga ma.wylie: yod na snga ma'i chu de gang, ,med na snga ma'i chu de ni, ,rting mar blug pa ma yin nam, ,blug na ming gi khyad byung bas, ,de yang khyod la 'gal ba yin
snga ma.english: If there is a difference, Then which of the waters Is the earlier? And if there is No such difference, Then wouldn't it be The case that the Earlier water Was the one on the bottom? And if it were, Then wouldn't there be A difference there? And wouldn't that In itself contradict Your views? It seems that we need to picture here water poured into a cup to fill it halfway; then repeat that process for a full cup; then pour the combined two into a pitcher—which at least theoretically might put the first water poured at the top of the pitcher.

snga ma.acip: SNGA MA LA KHYAB PA YOD DE, GANG ZAG RANG GI PHUNG PO LA BRTEN NAS 'JOG DGOS PA'I PHYIR RO,,
snga ma.wylie: snga ma la khyab pa yod de, gang zag rang gi phung po la brten nas 'jog dgos pa'i phyir ro
snga ma.english: Then I disagree that—just because the group of things that we call “a person,” the five parts of a person, are changing things, and things that are at the mercy of other forces—then it must be a contradiction to describe the person as “unchanging, singular, and autonomous.” And yet it must be, because we use the five parts that belong to a person to establish what that person is!

snga ma.wylie: rtags snga ma sgrub pa ni, de chos can, phung po dang tha dad du snang ba yin te, de dang rang rkya bar snang ba'i phyir ro
snga ma.english: Let's go back and prove the reason given just before this last one: the one that says, “A self that seems to be self-standing appears to be different from the body & mind.” Consider this self—the one that seems to be self-standing. It is too something which appears to be different from the body & mind, Because it appears to be standing by itself, apart from the body & mind.

snga ma.acip: PHYOGS CHOS KYI ZUR SNGA MA'I RTAGS NI, 'GAL ZLA DMIGS BA'I RTAGS YIN LA,
snga ma.wylie: phyogs chos kyi zur snga ma'i rtags ni, 'gal zla dmigs ba'i rtags yin la
snga ma.english: The reason in the first half of the relationship between the original subject and reason is a reason of the type where the presence of a quality which is incompatible with another quality proves the absence of this second quality.

snga ma.english: There are also three different thoughts elicited by these three appearances. The first of the three appearances is occurring due to a seed of a consistent type; and so we don't deny it. But we do deny that the latter two exist in the way they appear to—this point I will cover below. The Three Reasonings of Master Asanga, on naming things

snga ma.acip: DE YANG MI 'THAD DE, DE RANG GI SKAD CIG SNGA MA DANG 'BREL BA'I CHA DANG BCAS PA'I PHYIR,
snga ma.wylie: de yang mi 'thad de, de rang gi skad cig snga ma dang 'brel ba'i cha dang bcas pa'i phyir
snga ma.english: That idea too is mistaken—for even the briefest length of time has a part of it which is connected to the instant that came before it.

snga ma.wylie: der thal, rang gi skad cig snga ma med par 'byung mi srid pa'i phyir ro

snga ma.acip: GANG ZAG GCIG GI RGYUD KYI SHES PA LA'ANG GSAL MI GSAL DANG DUS KYI RIM PA'I CHA DU MA DANG, SHES PA SKAD CIG THA MA YANG RANG GI SKAD CIG SNGA MA DANG 'BREL BA'I CHA DANG BCAS PA'I PHYIR RO,,
snga ma.wylie: gang zag gcig gi rgyud kyi shes pa la'ang gsal mi gsal dang dus kyi rim pa'i cha du ma dang, shes pa skad cig tha ma yang rang gi skad cig snga ma dang 'brel ba'i cha dang bcas pa'i phyir ro
snga ma.english: Even with reference to the states of mind in the mindstream of a single person, there are many different parts: sometimes the mind is clear, and sometimes it is not clear; and there are furthermore all the different parts of the mind that are present at different times. Even the final instant of one's mind in this life has different parts—such as the part which is connected to the mind of the moment before.

snga ma.acip: GZHAN YANG, BDAG SKYE MED PAR THAL, DE YOD NA, TSE 'DI'I MIR SKYE BA LEN PA'I TSE SKYE BA SNGA MA'I BDAG NYID BZHIN DU SKYE DGOS PAS 'GRO BA RIGS DRUG GI GZHI MTHUN YOD PAR THAL BA DANG, RGAN PO'I LUS 'DI BZHIN DU'ANG MA'I MNGAL NA YOD PAR 'GYUR BA'I PHYIR RO,,
snga ma.wylie: gzhan yang, bdag skye med par thal, de yod na, tshe 'di'i mir skye ba len pa'i tshe skye ba snga ma'i bdag nyid bzhin du skye dgos pas 'gro ba rigs drug gi gzhi mthun yod par thal ba dang, rgan po'i lus 'di bzhin du'ang ma'i mngal na yod par 'gyur ba'i phyir ro
snga ma.english: We can further put it like this: Isn't it indeed the case that nothing can start from itself? Why do you say that? Because if something could start from itself, then when we take a birth into this present life as a human, we would have to take birth as an embodiment of all our past lives as well. And this means that we would have to be a single person who exhibited all six different forms of birth at once. Moreover, our body would have to exist within our mother's womb holding the same appearance as it does now, when we are older.

snga ma.acip: GZHAN YANG, RMA BYA'I MDONGS DE RANG GI RGYU LAS SKYES PAR THAL, DE RMA BYA'I THUN MONG MA YIN PA'I LAS DANG RANG GI NYER LEN SNGA MA LAS SKYES PA'I PHYIR,
snga ma.wylie: gzhan yang, rma bya'i mdongs de rang gi rgyu las skyes par thal, de rma bya'i thun mong ma yin pa'i las dang rang gi nyer len snga ma las skyes pa'i phyir
snga ma.english: Or we could argue it like this: Isn't it, indeed, the case that the colored spot in the design of a peacock's feather is something that starts from its own particular cause? Why do you say that? Because isn't that spot something that grows due to the peacock's own unique karma; and from its own unique material cause, which is something that came before it?

snga ma.english: This position too is mistaken, since the first part of it is to deny the existence of something that actually does exist; while the second part also has a bit of a problem with it.

snga ma.english: The viewpoints of the various Buddhist schools that I've described here are—as we proceed up through these schools—each one superior to that of the school below it. Nonetheless, all of the viewpoints can plant within you a seed for reaching spiritual freedom, no matter which one you meditate upon.

snga ma.acip: DMIGS RTEN DE DANG DE YID YUL DU BYED PA LAS MIG GIS BLTAS TE SGRUB PA MIN, GZHAN PHYOGS KHA CIG GIS DMIGS RTEN LA MIG GIS BLTAS TE SGRUB PA NI SNGA MA GNYIS LAS KYANG DMAN TE,

snga ma.english: It's important to say though that to actually reach quietude, the meditation object you select has to be something inside the mind: there's no way to achieve quietude just by staring at something on the outside. Those groups of practitioners who have recommended simply sitting down and staring at some visible object in front of you are even worse than the two traditions we've just mentioned.

Those groups of practitioners who have recommended simply sitting down and staring at some visible object in front of you are even worse than the two traditions we've just mentioned."}

snga ma.english: Or you could put it like this. We might have a Lama in our life that—generally speaking—we feel faith for; but where the intensity of that faith is not particularly high. And then from time to time in the relationship something happens to make us feel faith which is stronger than usual—almost overwhelming. In this case we can say that the strength of our grip on “the object” has suddenly gotten stronger than before—there is a considerable difference between the two.

snga ma.acip: BOD SNGA MA DAG GIS GLOD RAB LA BSGOM RAB CES GLOD MTSAMS NGOS MA ZIN PAR 'DI'I GONG DU DRAN PA GLOD PA NI 'KHRUL BA YIN PA'I PHYIR DE'I RJES SU MI 'BRANG NGO,,

As such, I would not encourage you to follow their advice.

snga ma.english: As such, there is a difference between this and the previous level regarding how long we spend in the distraction. snga ma.acip: BZHI PA NI, DRAN PA SHUGS CAN DU BSKYED NAS DMIGS RTEN LA 'JOG PA STE, 'DI NAS DMIGS RTEN SHOR MI SRID PAS SNGA MA GSUM LAS KHYAD ZHUGS PA YIN, 'ON KYANG DMIGS RTEN MA SHOR BZHIN DU BYING RGOD SHUGS CHEN PO 'BYUNG BAS BYING RGOD KYI GNYEN PO BSTEN DGOS,
snga ma.wylie: bzhi pa ni, dran pa shugs can du bskyed nas dmigs rten la 'jog pa ste, 'di nas dmigs rten shor mi srid pas snga ma gsum las khyad zhugs pa yin, 'on kyang dmigs rten ma shor bzhin du bying rgod shugs chen po 'byung bas bying rgod kyi gnyen po bsten dgos
snga ma.english: Then comes the fourth level. At this point, our ability to hold the mind on the object is building up strength, and we are able to maintain the mind on the object. This level is markedly different from the three that come before it, in that at this point it is entirely impossible for the mind to completely lose the meditation object. That said, even as we can no longer lose this object, we still get dullness and agitation coming up with strength. As such, we will have to be relying upon the antidotes for these two.

snga ma.acip: DES BYA RA BYAS TE TING NGE 'DZIN GYI YON TAN BSAMS NAS SEMS GZENGS BSTOD, 'DI DANG SNGA MA GNYIS LA BYING RGOD RAGS PA 'BYUNG MI 'BYUNG GI KHYAD YOD,

snga ma.english: The watchfulness now serves as a mental sentry; and we learn to uplift our thoughts by contemplating the great benefits of learning to meditate properly. And so the difference between this level and the one before it is a question of whether or not we are liable to experience gross forms of dullness and agitation. 6) Quieting the mind

snga ma.acip: SNGA MA LAS 'DI SKABS BYING BA PHRA MO'I NYEN CHE BA MED PA'I KHYAD YOD, LNGA PA DANG DRUG PA GNYIS SHES BZHIN GYI STOBS KYIS 'GRUB, 'DI NAS SHES BZHIN GYI STOBS RDZOGS PAR GSUNGS,

snga ma.english: The difference between this level and the one before it is that—at this point—there is no great danger that subtle dullness will be coming up. The fifth and sixth levels are achieved through the power of watchfulness; and from this point—our Lama told us—the power of our watchfulness is complete. 7) Completely quieting the mind

snga ma.acip: 'DI DANG SNGA MA GNYIS LA BYING RGOD PHRA MOR SHOR BA'I NYEN DOGS CHER BYED DGOS MI DGOS KYI KHYAD YOD,

snga ma.english: The difference between this level and the two that come before it is the question of whether we need to have any serious concern that we will lose our mind to subtle forms of dullness and agitation.

snga ma.english: The fifth and sixth meditation levels are differentiated by whether or not we have to entertain any serious doubt that the subtle form of dullness could appear. And not only that—even though subtle agitation could possibly occur at this level, the chance of this is significantly less than before.

snga ma.acip: SNOD BCUD SNGA MA STONG BA'I TSE 'BYUNG BZHI'I RDUL PHRA RAB SO NA YAN GAR DU GNAS PA RNAMS DBANG PHYUG GI BLO'I G-YO BA SNGON DU BTANG NAS BYAS PAR 'DOD PA'I PHYIR RO,,

snga ma.english: They say that, in the beginning, the universe and all its beings existed in a void, and that all the separate atoms of the universe—the atoms of the four elements—remained apart from one another. snga ma.english: Thus we might compare these four belief systems to steps up a stairway, where each one serves as an impetus for the next.  The way this works—to name one example—would be the way in which the outside belief systems fail to describe, accurately, things like either the self, or past & future lives.  The Detailists then tread there and use it to climb up to the next step, where they do describe these with accuracy.

snga ma.acip: [E15] DE DAG LA KHYAB PA YOD DE, LUS LEN PA'I RNAM SHES NI SKYE BA SNGA MA'I LAS KYI MTHUS TSE JI SRID KYI BAR DU RGYUN MA CHAD PAR 'JUG PA'I RNAM SMIN YIN PA DANG, RTAG TU MA BSGRIBS LUNG MA BSTAN GYI NGO BOR GNAS PA DANG, TSE JI SRID KYI BAR DU LUS THAMS CAD LA KHYAB NAS 'DZIN PA ZHIG DGOS PA'I PHYIR RO,,
snga ma.wylie: [e15] de dag la khyab pa yod de, lus len pa'i rnam shes ni skye ba snga ma'i las kyi mthus tshe ji srid kyi bar du rgyun ma chad par 'jug pa'i rnam smin yin pa dang, rtag tu ma bsgribs lung ma bstan gyi ngo bor gnas pa dang, tshe ji srid kyi bar du lus thams cad la khyab nas 'dzin pa zhig dgos pa'i phyir ro
snga ma.english: There is a logical necessity within these arguments because, first of all, the consciousness that takes on the body should be one that represents a ripening of karma which occurs through the power of karma committed in a previous lifetime, and should continue on in an unbroken stream for the duration of our life.  Moreover, its fundamental nature should be karmically neutral, of the type which does not cause any spiritual obstacle.  And lastly it should hold its objects even as it extends over the entire body—again for the entire length of our life. Second argument: How could one arise first?

snga ma.acip: [E19] PHYOGS SNGA MA 'GOG PA NI, 'DOD PA'I RTEN CAN GYI SO SO SKYE BO GCIG GI RGYUD LA RNAM SHES DU MA GCIG CAR SKYE BA YOD DE, DE 'DRA BA'I SKYO {%SO} SKYE LA GZUGS SOGS YUL DRUG NYE BAR GNAS SHING, TSOGS DRUG GA'I RGYU RKYEN SA BON DANG MIG SOGS DBANG PO DRUG DANG, YUL DRUG LA NYE RING MED PA'I YID BYED TSOGS DRUG GA'I DE MA THAG RKYEN BYED NUS PA ZHIG STOBS CHE CHUNG MED PAR TSOGS PA NA, DE'I MJUG THOGS SU TSOGS DRUG KA GCIG CAR SKYE BA MA GTOGS TSOGS DRUG LAS DANG POR DE NYID SKYE ZHES PA'I KHYAD PAR MI RUNG BA'I PHYIR TE, RGYU TSOGS TSANG BA LA KHYAD PAR MED PA'I PHYIR RO,,
snga ma.wylie: [e19] phyogs snga ma 'gog pa ni, 'dod pa'i rten can gyi so so skye bo gcig gi rgyud la rnam shes du ma gcig car skye ba yod de, de 'dra ba'i skyo {%so} skye la gzugs sogs yul drug nye bar gnas shing, tshogs drug ga'i rgyu rkyen sa bon dang mig sogs dbang po drug dang, yul drug la nye ring med pa'i yid byed tshogs drug ga'i de ma thag rkyen byed nus pa zhig stobs che chung med par tshogs pa na, de'i mjug thogs su tshogs drug ka gcig car skye ba ma gtogs tshogs drug las dang por de nyid skye zhes pa'i khyad par mi rung ba'i phyir te, rgyu tshogs tshang ba la khyad par med pa'i phyir ro
snga ma.english: Here is how they would refute the opposite position here: It is indeed the case that multiple types of consciousness can arise, all at the same time, in the mind of a normal being with a body and mind based in the desire realm. And that's because of the following.  Suppose that—for this particular kind of normal being—specific entities which possess the capacity to act as immediate conditions for all six of the different types of consciousness come together, without any distinction where one is stronger than another. That is, first of all, the six objects of the senses—visible forms and such—are close at hand; and moreover the causes and conditions for all six types of consciousness are also present—the requisite mental seeds, and the six sense powers of the eye and so on.  Finally, the mind is turning to the six objects of these senses, without one being closer or another being farther. In such an instance, all six consciousnesses of the collection must arise, in the next moment, all together.  It would be a problem at this juncture if you tried to draw a distinction: if you said that only a certain one of the six arose, before any of the others. That in turn is true because there is no distinction between any of these six with regard to all the necessary causes assembling for it to arise.

snga ma.acip: 'DIR PHYOGS SNGA MA SMRA BAS, BYANG SEMS RNAMS RGYAL BA'I SRAS YIN PAS, BYANG SEMS RGYAL BA LAS 'KHRUNGS PA RIGS KYI, DE LAS BZLOG NAS SMRA BA MI RIGS ZHES BRTZAD PA LA,
snga ma.wylie: 'dir phyogs snga ma smra bas, byang sems rnams rgyal ba'i sras yin pas, byang sems rgyal ba las 'khrungs pa rigs kyi, de las bzlog nas smra ba mi rigs zhes brtsad pa la
snga ma.english: At this point, a person who had raised the original issue might persist, expressing the following thought: An argument has been raised which says that—since bodhisattvas are the “sons & daughters” of the victorious Buddhas—it makes sense to say that bodhisattvas are born from the Victorious Ones; but that asserting the reverse does not.

snga ma.wylie: 'di snga ma gnyis la ltos na gsal mod kyang, da dung lam gyi rim pa rnams rtogs dka' ba la, slob dpon gyi lugs 'dzin chen po zhi ba lhas, spyir bslab spyod gnyis ka dang khyad par du mdo btus kyi don gyi 'grel pa bslab btus las shin tu gsal zhing rgyas par gsungs te
snga ma.english: It is admittedly true that this last work gives a more explicit presentation than the two mentioned before it; but certain steps of the path can still be difficult for a person to grasp. And so Shantideva, that great upholder of the system of the Master, has described these steps even more explicitly, and in much greater detail, in a general way in his Compendium of All the Trainings and his Guide to the Bodhisattva's Way of Life—and in a much more specific way in his Compendium of All the Trainings which is a commentary explaining the meaning of the Compendium of All the Sutras.

snga ma.acip: GZHAN ZHIG GIS CHOS KYI RJES 'BRANG GCIG LA, NYIN GCIG ZAN GCIG BYIN NA SNGA MA BAS BSOD NAMS CHES GRANGS MED PA BSKYED PA DANG,
snga ma.wylie: gzhan zhig gis chos kyi rjes 'brang gcig la, nyin gcig zan gcig byin na snga ma bas bsod nams ches grangs med pa bskyed pa dang
snga ma.english: And then this text speaks of “another practitioner” (referring to one who is following after the teachings) and states that—if they present a single article of food on only a single day—they create good karma which is infinitely greater than that of the follower after faith just mentioned.

snga ma.english: And then it speaks of making the presentation mentioned to followers after the teachings who are equal in number to the living beings mentioned; and says that if we present a single article of food to a single person of the eighth, we again create good karma which is infinitely greater than in the former case. The description relates here because the two mentions of “followers” are clearly a reference to the points at which one is on the path of accumulation or of preparation. The high qualities where our being is made beautiful

snga ma.acip: DE BZHIN DU ZLA BA'I ZHABS LA BOD RNAMS KYIS SKYON BZUNG BA 'GA' ZHIG SNANG BA YANG, PHYOGS SNGA MA ZHIB TU YE MA GO BAR SKYON LTAR SNANG BRJOD PAS, RANG GI DE NYID STON PA MKHAS PAS MTHONG NA SHIN TU NGO TSA BA'I GNAS KHO NAR SNANG NGO,,
snga ma.wylie: de bzhin du zla ba'i zhabs la bod rnams kyis skyon bzung ba 'ga' zhig snang ba yang, phyogs snga ma zhib tu ye ma go bar skyon ltar snang brjod pas, rang gi de nyid ston pa mkhas pas mthong na shin tu ngo tsha ba'i gnas kho nar snang ngo
snga ma.english: So too we have seen some Tibetans of the past who considered the great Chandrakirti to have made some kind of errors—but these are just false errors seen by a person who has no understanding at all of the finer points of the former position. And so if a sage were to see the way that these people themselves describe suchness, it seems that it would be no more than a total embarrassment.

snga ma.acip: ZHES PA'I PHYOGS SNGA MA SMRA BA NI SLOB DPON LEGS LDAN YIN TE, SANGS RGYAS BSKYANGS KYIS RAB BYED BDUN PA'I 'GREL PAR THEG DMAN GYI MDOR CHOS THAMS CAD BDAG MED PAR GSUNGS PA'I DON, CHOS RNAMS NGO BO NYID KYIS GRUB PA MED PA'I DON DU BSHAD PA LA, SHES RAB SGRON MAR DE LTA YIN NA, THEG CHEN BSTAN PA DON MED DU 'GYUR RO ZHES DGAG PA MDZAD DO,,
snga ma.wylie: zhes pa'i phyogs snga ma smra ba ni slob dpon legs ldan yin te, sangs rgyas bskyangs kyis rab byed bdun pa'i 'grel par theg dman gyi mdor chos thams cad bdag med par gsungs pa'i don, chos rnams ngo bo nyid kyis grub pa med pa'i don du bshad pa la, shes rab sgron mar de lta yin na, theg chen bstan pa don med du 'gyur ro zhes dgag pa mdzad do
snga ma.english: The person who expressed the first position found in this citation is Master Bhavaviveka. Master Buddha Palita, in commenting upon the seventh section of Wisdom, had described the statement that the sutras of the lower way speak of how nothing has any nature of its own as referring to the way in which nothing exists through any unique quality of its own. And then in his Lamp on Wisdom, Master Bhavaviveka tries to refute this position, saying that if this were the case, then the presentation found in the greater way would be pointless.

snga ma.acip: GZHI GRUB PA CIG GI STENG DU, CHOS KYI BDAG MED TSAD MAS GRUB PA CIG BYUNG NA, DE NAS GZHI GZHAN LA BDEN PAR YOD MED KYI DPYOD PA ZHUGS NA, RIGS PA SNGA MA LA BRTEN NAS BDEN MED DU RTOGS PAR NUS PA'I PHYIR RO,,
snga ma.wylie: gzhi grub pa cig gi steng du, chos kyi bdag med tshad mas grub pa cig byung na, de nas gzhi gzhan la bden par yod med kyi dpyod pa zhugs na, rigs pa snga ma la brten nas bden med du rtogs par nus pa'i phyir ro
snga ma.english: And this is because—if one is able to establish, by using an accurate perception, that the lack of a self-nature to things is true with regard to any single existent thing—then when one engages in an examination of whether things exist in truth with regard to any other object, they will be able to perceive that in fact it does not exist in truth, simply by using the same reasoning that they have employed previously.

snga ma.acip: SNGA MA NI, BDEN TSAD LEGS POR MA ZIN PAR RAGS PA CIG LAS MA KHEGS PAR 'DUG PA'I SKYON DU SNANG LA, PHYI MA NI DNGOS PO BDEN PA BKAG PAR RLOM YANG, TSAD MAS KHEGS PAR MI SNANG GI DNGOS PO LA SKUR 'DEBS KYI LTA BAR 'DUG PAS, DE DAG GIS MA NGES PA MED DO,,
snga ma.wylie: snga ma ni, bden tshad legs por ma zin par rags pa cig las ma khegs par 'dug pa'i skyon du snang la, phyi ma ni dngos po bden pa bkag par rlom yang, tshad mas khegs par mi snang gi dngos po la skur 'debs kyi lta bar 'dug pas, de dag gis ma nges pa med do
snga ma.english: The former of these two positions would appear to have the problem that—because this person has failed to identify, correctly, the point at which something can be said to exist “in truth”—it refutes no more than a very gross version of some object. Those who have put forth the latter position may entertain the delusion that they have managed to disprove that a functioning thing could exist in truth, but it would not appear that they have been able to do so with any accurate perception; rather, their position only serves to deny the existence of functioning things which do in fact exist. As such, there is no doubt in our assessment of these positions.

snga ma.acip: THEG DMAN LA NI RIGS PA MDOR BSDUS PA CIG GIS DE KHO NA NYID TSAD MAS GRUB NA, SNGA MA LTAR MI BYED PAS DE KHO NA NYID LA BLO RGYAS PA MED PAS RGYAS BSDUS DANG, BDAG MED SGOM PA RDZOGS MA RDZOGS SU GSUNGS SO,,
snga ma.wylie: theg dman la ni rigs pa mdor bsdus pa cig gis de kho na nyid tshad mas grub na, snga ma ltar mi byed pas de kho na nyid la blo rgyas pa med pas rgyas bsdus dang, bdag med sgom pa rdzogs ma rdzogs su gsungs so
snga ma.english: Those of the lower way, on the other hand, employ only abbreviated forms of reasoning to prove suchness with accurate perception. Since they fail to do what those other ones do, they lack any broadening of their mind towards suchness. Thus it is that pronouncements have been made about the relative detail of the two approaches; and whether or not one has meditated in a complete way upon the lack of a self-nature.

snga ma.acip: SPYIR PHAR PHYIN SNGA MA RNAMS LAS PHYI MA RNAMS LHAG PA YIN KYANG, SA 'DIR SBYIN PA LHAG PAR GSUNGS PA NI, SA 'DIR SBYIN PA NYAMS SU LEN PA LA MTHU PHUL DU BYUNG BA DE'I TSOD TZAM TSUL KHRIMS LA SOGS PA NYAMS SU LEN PA LA MED PA'I DON TE,
snga ma.wylie: spyir phar phyin snga ma rnams las phyi ma rnams lhag pa yin kyang, sa 'dir sbyin pa lhag par gsungs pa ni, sa 'dir sbyin pa nyams su len pa la mthu phul du byung ba de'i tshod tsam tshul khrims la sogs pa nyams su len pa la med pa'i don te
snga ma.english: As a general rule, each of the perfections is higher than the one preceding it in the list; but saying that giving at this particular level is higher is only meant to indicate that—at this level—ones practice of an ethical way of life and the other perfections is not as incredibly powerful as the way one puts giving into practice.

snga ma.acip: 'GREL PAR KYANG GI SGRA NI BZOD PA'I RGYU BSDU BAR BYA BA'I PHYIR RO,, ZHES MI 'KHRUG PA'I RGYU SNGA MAR MA ZAD, BSHAD MA THAG PA 'DIS KYANG BZOD CES PA YIN PA'I PHYIR DANG, 'DI'I PHYIR YANG ZHES GSUNGS PAS, MTHONG BA DES KYANG ZHES BSGYUR RGYU YIN NO,,
snga ma.wylie: 'grel par kyang gi sgra ni bzod pa'i rgyu bsdu bar bya ba'i phyir ro,, zhes mi 'khrug pa'i rgyu snga mar ma zad, bshad ma thag pa 'dis kyang bzod ces pa yin pa'i phyir dang, 'di'i phyir yang zhes gsungs pas, mthong ba des kyang zhes bsgyur rgyu yin no

The autocommentary here also contains the phrase “for this reason too,” which should be interpreted as “and because they see them all.” How others practice patience

snga ma.acip: DES NA LUNG SNGA MA'I DON NI, 'BRAS BU PHYUNG BAS MI ZAD PA YIN GYI, KHONG KHROS MI 'DZAD PA MIN LA, GNYIS PA'I DON KYANG SEMS BSKYED LA BRTEN NAS, LAS NYON GTAN ZAD NUS PA LTAR LAS NYON GYIS TSUR MI NUS PA'O,,
snga ma.wylie: des na lung snga ma'i don ni, 'bras bu phyung bas mi zad pa yin gyi, khong khros mi 'dzad pa min la, gnyis pa'i don kyang sems bskyed la brten nas, las nyon gtan zad nus pa ltar las nyon gyis tshur mi nus pa'o
snga ma.english: Therefore the meaning of the first of the two quotations is that the karmic result in question cannot be exhausted by its coming out; but not that it cannot be finished off by anger. And the meaning of the latter citation is that—by relying upon the Wish for enlightenment—we can finish off our karma and negative emotions permanently; but this is not the case in the other direction, for our karma and negative emotions have no power to do the same thing to our Wish.

snga ma.acip: 'DI NI SA DANG PO NAS KYANG 'THOB MOD KYANG, SA 'DIR LHAG PA'I TING NGE 'DZIN GYI BSLAB PA SNGA MA RNAMS LAS CHES MCHOG TU GYUR PA 'THOB PAS, DE'I DBANG GIS SKYE'AM SNYAM PA'I DOGS PA CHE BAS SMOS SO,,
snga ma.wylie: 'di ni sa dang po nas kyang 'thob mod kyang, sa 'dir lhag pa'i ting nge 'dzin gyi bslab pa snga ma rnams las ches mchog tu gyur pa 'thob pas, de'i dbang gis skye'am snyam pa'i dogs pa che bas smos so
snga ma.english: Now admittedly these abilities have already been achieved from the first of the bodhisattva levels; yet they are referred to by the root text with regard to this level because it is understood that at this point the bodhisattva will have achieved a capacity in the extraordinary training of concentration which is far superior to that at previous levels, and there is thus a greater chance that someone might start to wonder whether or not this capacity could force the normally corresponding rebirth.

snga ma.acip: BYANG CHUB KYI YAN LAG BDUN NI, DRAN PA DANG CHOS RAB TU RNAM PAR 'BYED PA DANG, BRTZON 'GRUS DANG DGA' BA DANG, SHIN TU SBYANGS PA DANG TING NGE 'DZIN DANG, BTANG SNYOMS YANG DAG BYANG CHUB KYI YAN LAG STE YANG DAG MAN CHAD SNGA MA DRUG GI MTHAR YANG SBYAR RO,,
snga ma.wylie: byang chub kyi yan lag bdun ni, dran pa dang chos rab tu rnam par 'byed pa dang, brtson 'grus dang dga' ba dang, shin tu sbyangs pa dang ting nge 'dzin dang, btang snyoms yang dag byang chub kyi yan lag ste yang dag man chad snga ma drug gi mthar yang sbyar ro
snga ma.english: The seven components of enlightenment are [23] awareness; [24] perfect discrimination between things; [25] joyful effort; [26] joy itself; [27] practiced ease; [28] concentration; and [29] the component of enlightenment which consists of equanimity (also add this last phrase to the beginning of all the first six).

snga ma.acip: 'PHAGS LAM YAN LAG BRGYAD NI, YANG DAG PA'I LTA BA DANG RTOG PA DANG, NGAG DANG LAS KYI MTHA' DANG, 'TSO BA DANG RTZOL BA DANG, DRAN PA DANG TING NGE 'DZIN YANG DAG 'PHAGS PA'I LAM YAN LAG GO, YANG DAG PA'I ZHES PA RTOG PA MAN CHAD LA SBYAR ZHING, YANG DAG PA'I 'PHAGS PA'I LAM YAN LAG CES PA SNGA MA BDUN GYI MTHAR YANG SBYAR RO,,
snga ma.wylie: 'phags lam yan lag brgyad ni, yang dag pa'i lta ba dang rtog pa dang, ngag dang las kyi mtha' dang, 'tsho ba dang rtsol ba dang, dran pa dang ting nge 'dzin yang dag 'phags pa'i lam yan lag go, yang dag pa'i zhes pa rtog pa man chad la sbyar zhing, yang dag pa'i 'phags pa'i lam yan lag ces pa snga ma bdun gyi mthar yang sbyar ro
snga ma.english: The eight components of the path of the realized ones are [30] the component of the path of the realized consisting of correct views and [31] thoughts; [32] speech and [33] the point of actions; [34] livelihood and [35] effort; and [36] awareness and [37] concentration. The expression “component of the path of the realized consisting of” should be applied to the beginning of each of the latter seven here as well.

snga ma.english: In the Great Drum it is explained that this monk would be a bodhisattva at the seventh level. And yet no one could say with certainty that this position contradicts the one expressed earlier. Certain great kings for example are said in some scriptures to have been stream enterers, while other scriptures say they were Buddhas; we see many variants like this in the teachings of the Word. Who is a worthy vessel for the profound

snga ma.acip: DES NA PHYI MA'I DON DAM DU YOD PA LA SNGA MA'I DON DAM DU YOD PAS KHYAB YANG, SNGA MA'I YOD 'DZIN NI LHAN SKYES KYI BDEN 'DZIN MIN LA, DE'I BDEN 'DZIN LA NI PHYI MA'I YOD 'DZIN DGOS SO,,
snga ma.wylie: des na phyi ma'i don dam du yod pa la snga ma'i don dam du yod pas khyab yang, snga ma'i yod 'dzin ni lhan skyes kyi bden 'dzin min la, de'i bden 'dzin la ni phyi ma'i yod 'dzin dgos so
snga ma.english: We can say thus that in the case of something existing ultimately in the latter sense, there would have to be something existing ultimately in the former sense; but that believing in the existence of the former is not the inborn tendency to hold that things are real—and for something to be that kind of tendency, it would have to be holding to the existence of the latter.
