snga ma.acip: DNGOS POR SMRA BA RNAMS KYI LUGS KYIS KYANG BDEN GRUB KHEGS PAR 'GYUR RO SNYAM DU, PHYOGS DE GNYIS 'DRES PA PHYED PAR 'GYUR TE, TSAD MA'I DBANG GIS GZHAL BYA 'JOG PA NI GZHAL BYA GNYIS KYI SDOD LUGS TSAD MAS RTOGS PA'I DON YIN PAS, DE DANG SNGA MA GNYIS GTAN MI 'DRA BA'I PHYIR RO,,
snga ma.wylie: dngos por smra ba rnams kyi lugs kyis kyang bden grub khegs par 'gyur ro snyam du, phyogs de gnyis 'dres pa phyed par 'gyur te, tshad ma'i dbang gis gzhal bya 'jog pa ni gzhal bya gnyis kyi sdod lugs tshad mas rtogs pa'i don yin pas, de dang snga ma gnyis gtan mi 'dra ba'i phyir ro
snga ma.english: Now you might then think to yourself that the Functionalist system also denies that things could exist really; but you need to look at these two positions that you've blended together and separate them back out from each other. When we say that existent objects are established by force of accurate perception, what we mean is that the nature of the two types of existents is something perceived by accurate perception. As such, the case here and the case before are completely dissimilar.

snga ma.acip: ZHES GSUNGS PA'I DON NI RKANG PA PHYI MA GNYIS KYIS DAM BCA' DANG, SNGA MA GNYIS KYIS RTAGS BSTAN PAR 'CHAD PA LTAR SO SOR MI GCOD PAR, BDAG LAS SKYE BA YOD PA MA YIN, ZHES SBREL BAR BYA ZHES PA STE GZHAN GSUM LA'ANG DE LTAR SBREL LO,,
snga ma.wylie: zhes gsungs pa'i don ni rkang pa phyi ma gnyis kyis dam bca' dang, snga ma gnyis kyis rtags bstan par 'chad pa ltar so sor mi gcod par, bdag las skye ba yod pa ma yin, zhes sbrel bar bya zhes pa ste gzhan gsum la'ang de ltar sbrel lo
snga ma.english: What this is saying is that the second half of the verse is presenting the assertion, whereas the first half is presenting the reason to prove this assertion. And as we've explained here, we should not divorce these two from each other, but rather combine them: “There is nothing that grows from itself.” We are to combine the other three possibilities in the same manner.

snga ma.acip: RIGS PA DE RNAMS LEGS PAR RTOGS NA CHOS CAN THAMS CAD PHAN TSUN DU NGO BO THA DAD PA LA, DE RNAMS KYI CHOS NYID THAMS CAD PHAR YIN TSUR YIN GYI GCIG TU 'DOD PA DANG, GNAS SKABS SNGA MA'I DUS KYI CHOS NYID DE NYID GNAS SKABS PHYI MA'I DUS KYI CHOS NYID DE NYID DU 'DOD PA'I LOG RTOG THAMS CAD LDOG PAR 'GYUR RO,,

snga ma.english: If a person is able to grasp this line of reasoning well, they avoid a pair of misconceptions which say that—starting from the point of particular objects not being such that to be one were to be the other—each & every example of the true nature of these objects is one, in the sense that to be one is to be the other; or that the true nature of an object at an earlier stage is precisely the same true nature of the same object at a later stage. snga ma.acip: RGYUD GCIG KYANG SKYED BYED MIN PA SKAD CIG MA PHYI MAS SNGA MA MI SKYED PAS, RGYUD GCIG PA'I SNGA MAS PHYI MA SKYED PAR BYED PA LAS SKYE BA DE YI PHYIR, SA LU'I MYU GU NI NAS LA SOGS PA LAS NAS KYI MYU GU LA SOGS PA SKYE BA DE LTAR SKYE BA MIN PAS THAMS CAD LAS THAMS CAD MI SKYE'O ZHE NA,
snga ma.wylie: rgyud gcig kyang skyed byed min pa skad cig ma phyi mas snga ma mi skyed pas, rgyud gcig pa'i snga mas phyi ma skyed par byed pa las skye ba de yi phyir, sa lu'i myu gu ni nas la sogs pa las nas kyi myu gu la sogs pa skye ba de ltar skye ba min pas thams cad las thams cad mi skye'o zhe na
snga ma.english: Even if they are incorporated into a single flow, a later instant of an object—which is not something which is functioning to produce the certain thing—cannot produce an earlier instant of the same object. Rather, the case is that the object of the later instant grows from the object of the earlier instant included into the same flow—from something that does function to produce it. As such, a rice sprout is not something that can grow from a barley seed or the like, in the same way that a barley sprout or such does. Thus it is not the case that everything there is grows from everything else there is. Entirely other, with none of four qualities

snga ma.acip: SA LU'I MYU GU'I SKYED PAR BYED PAR 'DOD PA MIN PA DANG, SA LU'I MYU GU SKYED PA'I NUS PA DANG LDAN PA MIN PA DANG, RGYUD GCIG TU GTOGS PA MIN PA DANG RIGS 'DRA BA'I SNGA MA MA YIN PA NYID
snga ma.wylie: sa lu'i myu gu'i skyed par byed par 'dod pa min pa dang, sa lu'i myu gu skyed pa'i nus pa dang ldan pa min pa dang, rgyud gcig tu gtogs pa min pa dang rigs 'dra ba'i snga ma ma yin pa nyid
snga ma.english: Therefore they are (1) not at all things that we could agree act to produce a rice sprout; (2) nor do they possess the capacity to ever produce such a sprout. They are (3) not things that are included into a single flow with a rice sprout; (4) nor are they preceding entitites that are of the same type as this kind of sprout.

snga ma.acip: DE NI SKYE BA TZAM DANG THA SNYAD DU SKYE BA KHAS LEN PA LA MI RIGS PA MED KYANG, DON DAM PA DANG RANG GI MTSAN NYID KYIS SKYE BA KHAS LEN PA LA 'GAL BA YIN TE, SNGA MA LA NI RGYU 'BRAS KYI SKYE 'GAG GI BYA BA GNYIS DUS MNYAM YANG, RGYU 'BRAS GNYIS DUS MNYAM MI DGOS LA, PHYI MA LA NI BYA BA DUS MNYAM NA RGYU 'BRAS KYANG DUS MNYAM DGOS PA'I PHYIR RO,,
snga ma.wylie: de ni skye ba tsam dang tha snyad du skye ba khas len pa la mi rigs pa med kyang, don dam pa dang rang gi mtshan nyid kyis skye ba khas len pa la 'gal ba yin te, snga ma la ni rgyu 'bras kyi skye 'gag gi bya ba gnyis dus mnyam yang, rgyu 'bras gnyis dus mnyam mi dgos la, phyi ma la ni bya ba dus mnyam na rgyu 'bras kyang dus mnyam dgos pa'i phyir ro
snga ma.english: The point being made here is that there is nothing at all wrong with accepting the idea of growing per se; or the idea of something growing in a nominal manner. It would though be a contradiction to agree to the idea of growing that could occur in an ultimate way, or by definition. In the former case, the two actions of the growing & stopping of the cause and the result would be simultaneous; nonetheless, this doesn't have to imply that the cause and the result themselves are simultaneous. In the latter case, cause & results would have to be simultaneous, if the actions involved were themselves simultaneous.

snga ma.wylie: de ltar na rigs pa 'dis ni rgyu 'bras su 'dod pa la gzhan nyid yod kyang rang bzhin gyis skye ba mi srid la, de'i phyir gzhan las skye ba mi srid par ston zhing, rigs pa snga mas ni rgyu 'bras la skye ba srid kyang rang bzhin gyis gzhan yin pa mi srid la, de'i phyir gzhan skye mi srid par ston to
snga ma.english: As such, what this reasoning is indicating is that you can accept cause & effect, and that there is such a thing where these are completely separate from one another, and yet still it is impossible for things to grow through some nature of their own—and so it is impossible for things to grow from something other than themselves. The previous reasoning is indicating that—although it is possible for things to grow with cause & effect—it is impossible for these to be other than each other in a way that exists through some nature of its own; and that for this reason it is impossible for a thing to grow from something other than itself.

snga ma.acip: DE LA SKYON DANG LDAN PA'I DBANG PO CAN RNAMS KYI BSLAD PA'I SHES PA NI, DBANG PO LEGS PAR GYUR PA STE 'PHRAL GYI 'KHRUL RGYUS MA BSLAD PA'I SHES PA LA LTOS NAS, LOG PA'I SHES PAR 'DOD CING, SNGA MA NI YUL PHYIN CI MA LOG PA 'DZIN PAR 'DOD DO,,
snga ma.wylie: de la skyon dang ldan pa'i dbang po can rnams kyi bslad pa'i shes pa ni, dbang po legs par gyur pa ste 'phral gyi 'khrul rgyus ma bslad pa'i shes pa la ltos nas, log pa'i shes par 'dod cing, snga ma ni yul phyin ci ma log pa 'dzin par 'dod do
snga ma.english: Let's consider states of mind belonging to those with powers possessing a defect—that is, consider their state of mind, which is infected. Relative to powers which are sound—that is, relative to states of mind which are not infected by some adventitious condition which would cause them to be mistaken, we take the position that these other states of mind are mistaken. Our position further states that the former—the unaffected states of mind—are to be considered unmistaken.

snga ma.acip: DPER NA SHING LA 'DZEG PAS YAL GA PHYI MA MA BZUNG BAR SNGA MA BTANG BAR LTAR, LTUNG BA CHEN POS LTA BA NGAN PA'I RI SUL DU LTUNG BAR 'GYUR ZHING, BDEN GNYIS LEGS PAR MTHONG BA DANG BRAL BAS 'BRAS BU THAR PA THOB PAR MI 'GYUR RO,,

snga ma.english: These people are like those who are climbing a tree and let go of the lower branch before they have clasped the higher—and thus suffer a great fall, where they drop into the ravine of undesirable viewpoints, and fail to see the two realities clearly. As such, they are unable to attain the goal, of freedom.

snga ma.acip: SNGA MA'I DON NI, SO SKYES DON DAM PAR GRUB PAR BZUNG BA'I BUM SOGS DE NYID, SNGAR BSHAD PA'I 'PHAGS PA GSUM MNYAM GZHAG LAS LANGS PA'I RJES THOB SNANG BA CAN RNAMS KYI KUN RDZOB TZAM YIN PAR BSTAN PAS,

snga ma.acip: DE BZHIN DU SHING SDONG PO'I SA BON TZAM BTAB NAS DE LAS SHING SDONG SKYES PA NA, SHING SDONG 'DI NGAS BTZUGS SO SNYAM DU RTOG PA DES NA, 'JIG RTEN GYI NGOR GZHAN SKYE MED PA SOGS SNGA MA BZHIN DU SBYAR RO,,
snga ma.wylie: de bzhin du shing sdong po'i sa bon tsam btab nas de las shing sdong skyes pa na, shing sdong 'di ngas btsugs so snyam du rtog pa des na, 'jig rten gyi ngor gzhan skye med pa sogs snga ma bzhin du sbyar ro
snga ma.english: The case is the same, when someone plants a simple seed for a tree, and a trunk does indeed grow from that. That is, people think to themselves, “I was the one who planted the tree with this trunk”; and this is why—as we did with the previous case—we can say things like “There is no instance where, in the perceptions of the world, one thing can grow from another thing.”

snga ma.acip: DE LAS GZHAN PA'I STONG TSUL RNAMS RANG GI NGO BOS STONG PA MIN PA'I RGYU MTSAN NI, STONG TSUL SNGA MA TSAD MAS GRUB ZIN BYED PA MA NYAMS PA'I RING LA, GRUB MTHAS GZHI DE BDEN PA'AM DE'I DON DU YOD PAR 'DZIN PA'I SGRO 'DOGS SKYE MI SRID LA, PHYI MA RNAMS KYI DON TSAD MAS GRUB CING BYED PA MA NYAMS KYANG, GRUB MTHA' BDEN PA'AM BDEN PA'I DON DU SGRO 'DOGS PA MI 'GAL BA'O,,
snga ma.wylie: de las gzhan pa'i stong tshul rnams rang gi ngo bos stong pa min pa'i rgyu mtshan ni, stong tshul snga ma tshad mas grub zin byed pa ma nyams pa'i ring la, grub mthas gzhi de bden pa'am de'i don du yod par 'dzin pa'i sgro 'dogs skye mi srid la, phyi ma rnams kyi don tshad mas grub cing byed pa ma nyams kyang, grub mtha' bden pa'am bden pa'i don du sgro 'dogs pa mi 'gal ba'o
snga ma.english: And what then is the reason why we say that ways in which things could be empty that are different than these particular ways do not represent an emptiness of some kind of self-essence? Suppose that those previous ways in which we described things as being empty had already been confirmed by accurate perception; and we were all still sitting in a place where none of those confirmations had in any way declined. It would in that state be impossible for us to hold a school of thought which took those same examples of things to exist in truth; neither would it be possible for there to grow, within our minds, that form of overestimation where we held that things could exist in this same kind of truth. The idea in the latter cases here would be that a certain point had been confirmed by an accurate perception, and that the working of this perception had in no way declined; and yet this would not preclude overestimation through a learned philosophical school which said that a certain object was real; or even described what it was to be real. Normal reality cannot stand up under true analysis

snga ma.acip: DE'I BDEN PA NI MDO NYID LAS MI SLU BA'I CHOS CAN ZHES GSUNGS PAS MI SLU BA'I DON DU BSHAD KYI, RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA'I BDEN PA NI MA YIN NA, ,'DU BYED THAMS CAD NI BRDZUN PA SLU BA'I CHOS CAN ZHES GSUNGS PAS KYANG SNGA MA'I BDEN PA MI SLU BA'I DON DU SHES SO,,
snga ma.wylie: de'i bden pa ni mdo nyid las mi slu ba'i chos can zhes gsungs pas mi slu ba'i don du bshad kyi, rang bzhin gyis grub pa'i bden pa ni ma yin na, ,'du byed thams cad ni brdzun pa slu ba'i chos can zhes gsungs pas kyang snga ma'i bden pa mi slu ba'i don du shes so
snga ma.english: That type of reality is described in the sutra itself as being something that never deceives us; as such, this is what's being explained as the meaning of “never deceives.” But if saying that a truth existed by definition were not what “never deceives” refers to, then we would have to understand that “all the factors there are lie to us: they deceive us” was what it meant for the first truth to be something that did not deceive us.

snga ma.acip: GAL TE DE LTA NA NI GZUGS BRNYAN BRDZUN PAR GRAGS PA DE GRUB KYANG, DBU MA PAS BZHAG PA'I BRDZUN PAR MI 'GRUB PAS, SNGA MA DE PHYI MA'I DPER JI LTAR 'GYUR ZHE NA,
snga ma.wylie: gal te de lta na ni gzugs brnyan brdzun par grags pa de grub kyang, dbu ma pas bzhag pa'i brdzun par mi 'grub pas, snga ma de phyi ma'i dper ji ltar 'gyur zhe na
snga ma.english: One may come with the following question— If that's the way it is, and there really does exist a reflection which everyone admits is false, then it wouldn't be false in the same was as the those of the Middle Way school describe it. How then can you say that the former stands as an illustration of the latter?

snga ma.acip: PHYOGS SNGA MA'I LUGS NI, LAM MA ZHUGS DANG SLOB PA RNAMS KYI 'GRO BA'I NGO BO MA SGRIBS LUNG MA BSTAN GYI DBANG DU MDZAD PA'O,,
snga ma.wylie: phyogs snga ma'i lugs ni, lam ma zhugs dang slob pa rnams kyi 'gro ba'i ngo bo ma sgribs lung ma bstan gyi dbang du mdzad pa'o
snga ma.english: The previous position here is taken relative to the idea that the content of states of existence for those who are not entered upon a path—and those who are still learning—is neutral karma of the type that does not act as an obstacle.

snga ma.acip: SEMS BDEN PA MED NA 'JIG RTEN SNGA MA NAS 'DIR 'ONG BA DANG, 'DI NAS PHYI MAR 'GRO BA'I G-YO BA'I BYA BA MI 'THAD DO SNYAM PA'I RTZOD PA KHONG NA GNAS PA'I LAN DU,
snga ma.wylie: sems bden pa med na 'jig rten snga ma nas 'dir 'ong ba dang, 'di nas phyi mar 'gro ba'i g-yo ba'i bya ba mi 'thad do snyam pa'i rtsod pa khong na gnas pa'i lan du
snga ma.english: They would say that—if the mind were indeed not something real—then the argument remains, where we consider it incorrect to say then that one could act to shift from the world they were in before, to this one; or to shift from this one to the next one.

snga ma.acip: DANG PO NI, RNAM PAR SHES PA SMRA BA DBU MA PA'I LUGS JI SKAD BSTAN PA MI BZOD CING, RGYAL BA'I DGONGS PA MIN PAS, RANG GI RNAM RTOG GIS SBYAR BA'I LUGS BRJOD PA'I SGO NAS DON 'JOG PAR BYED PA RNAMS KYIS, RANG GI GZHUNG LAS JI SKAD DU BSHAD PA'I LUGS GSAL BAR BYA BA'I PHYIR PHYOGS SNGA MA SMRAS PA,
snga ma.wylie: dang po ni, rnam par shes pa smra ba dbu ma pa'i lugs ji skad bstan pa mi bzod cing, rgyal ba'i dgongs pa min pas, rang gi rnam rtog gis sbyar ba'i lugs brjod pa'i sgo nas don 'jog par byed pa rnams kyis, rang gi gzhung las ji skad du bshad pa'i lugs gsal bar bya ba'i phyir phyogs snga ma smras pa
snga ma.english: Here is the first. Those who assert that everything is consciousness cannot bear the position that those of the Middle Way describe, and say that it is not what the Victors really mean. Rather, these people seek to establish how things actually are by expressing a position which is just a creation of their own imagination. And so in an attempt to clarify the system presented in their own classical texts, they begin with the following opening statement.

snga ma.acip: 'GREL PA 'DIR KHYAD PAR SBYAR MA SBYAR GNYIS KA 'DUG KYANG, SKYE BA 'GOG PA LA DGAG BYA LA KHYAD PAR SBYAR BA MANG DU BYUNG NA, MA BYUNG BA'I SKABS THAMS CAD DU YANG DE 'KHYER BA BZHIN DU, 'DIR YANG DE LTAR BYA STE, 'DIR PHYOGS SNGA MA BRJOD PA'I GZHUNG THEG BSDUS SU,
snga ma.wylie: 'grel pa 'dir khyad par sbyar ma sbyar gnyis ka 'dug kyang, skye ba 'gog pa la dgag bya la khyad par sbyar ba mang du byung na, ma byung ba'i skabs thams cad du yang de 'khyer ba bzhin du, 'dir yang de ltar bya ste, 'dir phyogs snga ma brjod pa'i gzhung theg bsdus su
snga ma.english: In the autocommentary at this point we see both kinds of references: where they make qualifications of this kind, or where they do not. In the end though it's like cases where we deny that things can grow: there are many situations where qualifications are added to what we deny; and where such qualifications are not made, we are expected to assume them nonetheless. We should do the same here; as we see the previous position described in the classic Summary of the Greater Way—

snga ma.acip: 'DIR PHYOGS SNGAR MDZAD PA NI BYANG SA DANG DBUS MTHA'I 'GREL PA LAS, GANG LA GANG MED PA ZHES SOGS KYI DON SNGAR LTAR BSHAD PA DE YIN LA, RGYUD BLA MA'I 'GREL PAR GANG ZHIG GANG NA MED PA DE NI ZHES SOGS KYI DON BKRAL BA NI, SNGA MA GNYIS DANG GTAN MI 'DRA BAR DBU MA'I 'GREL TSUL DU YOD DE MANGS PAS 'JIGS NAS MA BRIS SO,,
snga ma.wylie: 'dir phyogs sngar mdzad pa ni byang sa dang dbus mtha'i 'grel pa las, gang la gang med pa zhes sogs kyi don sngar ltar bshad pa de yin la, rgyud bla ma'i 'grel par gang zhig gang na med pa de ni zhes sogs kyi don bkral ba ni, snga ma gnyis dang gtan mi 'dra bar dbu ma'i 'grel tshul du yod de mangs pas 'jigs nas ma bris so
snga ma.english: What I have presented here as the initial position represents what we described earlier, as reflected in the explanation of the wording that we see in both The Levels of the Bodhisattva and in the commentary to Distinguishing Between the Middle & the Extremes: “with what it is that what is missing.” The way though in which the commentary to The Higher Line reads the phrase “where it is that something is missing” is completely different from that found in these other two. Which is to say, there are a great number of different ways that the Middle Way explains these things. Out of a concern though that I would go on too long, I will refrain from speaking more on that point here.

snga ma.acip: DE'I PHYIR GANG ZAG GANG LA SKRA'I RNAM PA CAN GYI SHES PA SNGA MA GZHAN GYIS BZHAG PA'I BAG CHAGS SMIN PA YOD PA DE KHO NA LA, SKRA SHAD KYI RNAM PA CAN GYI SHES PA 'BYUNG GI
snga ma.wylie: de'i phyir gang zag gang la skra'i rnam pa can gyi shes pa snga ma gzhan gyis bzhag pa'i bag chags smin pa yod pa de kho na la, skra shad kyi rnam pa can gyi shes pa 'byung gi
snga ma.english: As such, it is only a person who is experiencing the ripening of a deep seed that was planted by another, previous state of mind that possessed an image of a hair that will have an awareness arise with the image of a strand of hair.

snga ma.acip: DE SMIN PA LAS DUS PHYIS SNGA MA DE'I RNAM PA'I RJES SU BYED PA'I MIG GI RNAM SHES SKYE BAR 'GYUR ZHING, RANG GI STE MIG GI RNAM SHES DE NUS PA'I SKAD CIG BAR MED PA GANG ZHIG LAS SKYE BA'I NUS PA'I SKAD CIG PAR {%BAR} MED PA RTEN DU GYUR PA DE LA, GTI MUG GIS 'JIG RTEN RNAMS DBANG PO GZUGS CAN MIG YIN NO SNYAM DU RTOGS KYI, RNAM SHES LAS THA DAD PA'I MIG DBANG NI YOD PA MIN NO,,
snga ma.wylie: de smin pa las dus phyis snga ma de'i rnam pa'i rjes su byed pa'i mig gi rnam shes skye bar 'gyur zhing, rang gi ste mig gi rnam shes de nus pa'i skad cig bar med pa gang zhig las skye ba'i nus pa'i skad cig par {%bar} med pa rten du gyur pa de la, gti mug gis 'jig rten rnams dbang po gzugs can mig yin no snyam du rtogs kyi, rnam shes las tha dad pa'i mig dbang ni yod pa min no
snga ma.english: When this deep seed ripens, a later awareness of the eyes springs forth, in a form which follows upon that of the former one. And then “its”—meaning the eye's—consciousness becomes the support for a potential which occurs without even a moment's interval, from the potential that also occurred without even a moment's interval, for the consciousness itself. And then out of dark ignorance, people of the world get an idea where they consider this support and think to themselves, “this is the eye, a physical sense power”—even though it's not the case that there exists any power of the eye which is separate from consciousness itself.

snga ma.acip: DE BZHIN DU RAB RIB DANG LDAN PA'I DBANG PO CAN DANG MTSUNGS PA'I SGYU MA DANG GZUGS BRNYAN SOGS DPER 'GOD PA LA YANG LAN GDAB TSUL SHES PAR BYA LA, CHU 'BAB PA'I KLUNG LA YI DVAGS RNAMS LA RNAG KHRAG GI BLO SKYE BA LA YANG SNGA MA BZHIN DU SHES PAR BYA'O,,
snga ma.wylie: de bzhin du rab rib dang ldan pa'i dbang po can dang mtshungs pa'i sgyu ma dang gzugs brnyan sogs dper 'god pa la yang lan gdab tshul shes par bya la, chu 'bab pa'i klung la yi dvags rnams la rnag khrag gi blo skye ba la yang snga ma bzhin du shes par bya'o
snga ma.english: You can understand, in the same way, how to reply as well to cases where someone sets forth—as an example—an illusion, or a reflection in a mirror, as being equivalent to a state of mind with a sense power that has cataracts. And you should also understand, in the same way, the illustration of when a state of mind arises in craving spirits wherein they perceive a stream of fresh water as being pus & blood.

snga ma.acip: 'DIR SEMS TZAM PAS RANG RIG JI LTA BU ZHIG KHAS BLANGS PA'I PHYOGS SNGA MA'I KHUNGS CUNG ZAD BSHAD NA, RTOG GE 'BAR BA LAS, SEMS TZAM PAS RNAM SHES NI GNYIS SU SNANG STE, RANG SNANG BA DANG YUL DU SNANG BA'O,,
snga ma.wylie: 'dir sems tsam pas rang rig ji lta bu zhig khas blangs pa'i phyogs snga ma'i khungs cung zad bshad na, rtog ge 'bar ba las, sems tsam pas rnam shes ni gnyis su snang ste, rang snang ba dang yul du snang ba'o
snga ma.english: Why don't we pause here, and say something about the earlier sources for the Mind Only's assertion of apperception: how they come to accept its existence. We can start with the Blaze of Reasoning, which talks about how— The Mind Only say that consciousness appears in two forms: one where it appears as itself, and another in which it appears as its object.

snga ma.acip: MI DGOS NA SHES PA SNGA MA LA YANG MI DGOS PAR 'GYUR LA, DGOS NA DE LA YANG GZHAN DGOS PAS THUG PA MED PA'I SKYON DU 'GYUR ZHING, THUG MED DU SONG NA NI SNGO 'DZIN DANG PO LA MYONG BA MI GRUB PA'I SKYON YOD DO,,
snga ma.wylie: mi dgos na shes pa snga ma la yang mi dgos par 'gyur la, dgos na de la yang gzhan dgos pas thug pa med pa'i skyon du 'gyur zhing, thug med du song na ni sngo 'dzin dang po la myong ba mi grub pa'i skyon yod do
snga ma.english: If you say that this following state of mind were not required, then it wouldn't be required either with the state of mind previous to it. If it were required, then yet another state of mind would be required, and you'd have the problem that the process would become endless. And if it did become endless, then you'd have the problem that there was nothing you could establish as experiencing the first perception of blue.

snga ma.acip: GNYIS PA YUL GZHAN YONGS SU MI GCOD PAR THAL BA NI, SHES PA SNGA MA PHYI MAS GCOD NA NI GZUGS SGRA LA SOGS PA'I YUL GZHAN MI GCOD PA DANG, DE LA MI 'PHO BAR 'GYUR TE, RNAM PAR SHES PA'I RGYUN LUGS TE RGYU BA MTHA' DAG SHES PA SNGA MA GZHAN DE'I YUL CAN YIN PA'I PHYIR RO,,
snga ma.wylie: gnyis pa yul gzhan yongs su mi gcod par thal ba ni, shes pa snga ma phyi mas gcod na ni gzugs sgra la sogs pa'i yul gzhan mi gcod pa dang, de la mi 'pho bar 'gyur te, rnam par shes pa'i rgyun lugs te rgyu ba mtha' dag shes pa snga ma gzhan de'i yul can yin pa'i phyir ro
snga ma.english: Here's that second problem, which is that it would have to be the case that there was no discernment of other objects. If the previous state of mind were discerned by the later one, then things like visible form, and sound—other objects—would not be discerned. There would be no moving over to them; since the flow of the consciousness—all of its motion—would be devoted to being the object state of mind for that other, earlier state of mind.

As such, that earlier scriptural citation can be understood as metaphorical.

snga ma.acip: 'DIR RANG GI SDE PA DAG NA RE PHUNG PO LAS NGO BO GZHAN PA'I BDAG GRUB PA MED PA'I PHYIR BDAG TU LTA BA STE 'JIG TSOGS LA LTA BA'I DMIGS RNAM GNYIS KYI NANG GI DMIGS PA NI PHUNG PO KHO NA YIN TE, PHUNG PO LAS NGO BO THA DAD PA DANG NANG GI PHUNG PO DMIGS PAR 'JOG PA GNYIS SU NGES PA LAS SNGA MA MI RUNG BA'I PHYIR RO,,
snga ma.wylie: 'dir rang gi sde pa dag na re phung po las ngo bo gzhan pa'i bdag grub pa med pa'i phyir bdag tu lta ba ste 'jig tshogs la lta ba'i dmigs rnam gnyis kyi nang gi dmigs pa ni phung po kho na yin te, phung po las ngo bo tha dad pa dang nang gi phung po dmigs par 'jog pa gnyis su nges pa las snga ma mi rung ba'i phyir ro
snga ma.english: Here certain of our own groups make the following argument: There is no self which exists as essentially separate from the parts to the person; as such, the tendency to see a self—which is to say, the view of destruction, which has two objects of its focus—takes as its inner object of focus only the parts to the person. And that's due to the fact that the objects of focus here are fixed at two—no more, no less: one which is essentially separate from these parts to a person, and a second which is focused on the heaps inside; and it would be inappropriate here to include the former.

snga ma.english: In response then one might have the thought that “Well, the result of the action taken by something in the previous instant would be experienced by things in the later instants; and so there would be no problem here.”

snga ma.acip: ZHES SNGA PHYI RANG BZHIN GYIS GZHAN YIN NA SNGA MA LA LTOS PA MI RUNG BAS SNGA MA DE MED PAR YANG 'BYUNG BA DANG, SNGA MA'I BDAG DE DE BZHIN DU GNAS PAS, DER MA SHI BAR 'DIR SKYE BAR 'GYUR BA SOGS GSUNGS SO,,

snga ma.english: What this is saying is that—if what came before and what came after were different from each other, by nature—then it would be wrong to say that the one was relying upon the previous. And then that would have to occur even in the absence of what had come before. The self of the previous time would have to remain in the very same manner, which means that a person would, for example, have to take their rebirth without having died first. snga ma.acip: CI'I PHYIR ZHE NA, KHYOD KYI LTAR NA SHING RTA'I 'PHANG LO LA SOGS PA'I YAN LAG RE RE LA SNGAR MA BSGRIGS PA'I DUS SU DBYIBS JI LTAR YOD PAR GYUR PA BZHIN DU, PHYIS BSGRIGS TE SHING RTAR RTOGS {%GTOGS} PA STE GRUB PA'I DUS SU'ANG SNGA MA DE BZHIN DU YOD PA YIN NA,
snga ma.wylie: ci'i phyir zhe na, khyod kyi ltar na shing rta'i 'phang lo la sogs pa'i yan lag re re la sngar ma bsgrigs pa'i dus su dbyibs ji ltar yod par gyur pa bzhin du, phyis bsgrigs te shing rtar rtogs {%gtogs} pa ste grub pa'i dus su'ang snga ma de bzhin du yod pa yin na
snga ma.english: And why is that? According to you, we should first consider the shape of each separate component part of the wagon—the wheels and all the rest—as they existed prior to the point that they were assembled into the wagon. And then their shape after they have been incorporated into the wagon—that is, after the wagon has been completed—should as well be something that exists in just the same way as it was before.

snga ma.acip: DE BZHIN DU BRTAN PA STE RTAG PAR YANG MI 'THAD DE, DE RTAG NA SNGON GYI TSE RABS SU BYUNG BA'I DUS KYI BDAG DE NYID 'DIR BYUNG BA'I BDAG YIN PA DANG, TSE SNGA MA DANG 'DI'I BDAG GNYIS KYI NYE BAR LEN PA'I PHUNG PO NGO BO THA DAD PA YIN PAS, BDAG GCIG TU MI RUNG STE NYE BAR LEN PA LAS NGO BO THA DAD PA'I BDAG MED PA'I PHYIR RO,,
snga ma.wylie: de bzhin du brtan pa ste rtag par yang mi 'thad de, de rtag na sngon gyi tshe rabs su byung ba'i dus kyi bdag de nyid 'dir byung ba'i bdag yin pa dang, tshe snga ma dang 'di'i bdag gnyis kyi nye bar len pa'i phung po ngo bo tha dad pa yin pas, bdag gcig tu mi rung ste nye bar len pa las ngo bo tha dad pa'i bdag med pa'i phyir ro
snga ma.english: It would by the same token also be incorrect to say that this self were solid—which is to say, unchanging. If it were unchanging, then the very same self that had occurred at the point of the earlier string of lifetimes would be the self that had occurred here. And since the parts to the person taken on for the two selves—that of the previous life, and that of this one—would be essentially separate, then it would be wrong to say that they were essentially one & the same. That is, there could be no self that was essentially separate from what it incorporated.

snga ma.english: First of all, they would understand; they would have the thought that neither of those two options presented earlier was the way things are. They would repeat—a thousand times—that it is the self which achieves liberation.

snga ma.acip: DES NA NAG TSO'I 'GYUR LAS, DNGOS PO GANG ZHIG RANG GI NGO BO NYID KYIS YOD PA DE NI THER ZUG TU GNAS PA'AM, NYAMS PAR 'GYUR BA ZHIG TU 'GYUR RO ZHES BSGYUR BA LTAR LEGS PAS, SNGA MA NI DGAG SGRA 'DON LUGS 'PHYUGS PAR GSAL LO,,

snga ma.english: As such, we can say that the translation by Naktso is correct here, where it says “When something is, first of all, a functioning entity, and also exists through some essential nature of its own, then it would have to be something that remained in a solid way—or as something that never declined.” It is clear that the previous version we've listed has made an error in the way it brings out the negative particle.

snga ma.wylie: de bzhin du snga ma gnyis las gzhan gang nam mkha' mtha' yas la sogs pa gzugs med pa'i snyoms par 'jug pa bzhi po de dag ,yang dag mkhyen pa yi sangs rgyas kyis mi 'khrug pa khro ba med pa'i mtshan nyid can du gsungs te, de rnams ni khro ba spangs pas 'thob pa'i phyir ro
snga ma.english: Just so we have items that are other than the two just mentioned; for example, those four states of balanced meditation for the formless realm levels of infinite space and the rest. These are what the Buddha, that Being of Perfect Knowledge, described as states whose own quality was beyond being disturbed—that is, free of all anger. And that's because these levels are attained by eliminating, within ourselves, anger.

snga ma.acip: DE LTAR NA PHYOGS SNGA MA SMRA BA POS BLO LA DE KHO NA NYID KYI RNAM PA 'CHAR RGYU MED PA DANG, YUL DE'I RNAM PA MA SHAR NA BLO YUL LA MI 'JUG PA DANG, MA ZHUGS NA YUL DE MI SHES PA DANG, MA SHES NA YUL CAN DE SHES PAR 'GAL LO ZHES SMRA BA'I
snga ma.wylie: de ltar na phyogs snga ma smra ba pos blo la de kho na nyid kyi rnam pa 'char rgyu med pa dang, yul de'i rnam pa ma shar na blo yul la mi 'jug pa dang, ma zhugs na yul de mi shes pa dang, ma shes na yul can de shes par 'gal lo zhes smra ba'i
snga ma.english: And so what those who take the former position are saying is that the aspect of suchness is not something that could ever make its appearance to the mind. And if the aspect of the object could never make its appearance, then the mind could never engage in the particular object. And if the mind did not engage, then it could never perceive this object. And if it could not, then it would be a contradiction to say that this subject state of mind were mind at all.

snga ma.acip: SANGS RGYAS THAMS CAD KYI CHOS SKU GCIG YIN NA SANGS RGYAS SNGA MA RNAMS SANGS RGYAS PA'I TSE, SNGAR SANGS MA RGYAS PA DANG 'TSANG RGYA RGYU'I CHOS SKU YANG SNGON DU THOB ZIN PA SHIN TU 'GAL BA'I PHYIR RO,,
snga ma.wylie: sangs rgyas thams cad kyi chos sku gcig yin na sangs rgyas snga ma rnams sangs rgyas pa'i tshe, sngar sangs ma rgyas pa dang 'tshang rgya rgyu'i chos sku yang sngon du thob zin pa shin tu 'gal ba'i phyir ro
snga ma.english: If the holy bodies of all things belonging to each and every one of the Buddhas were all but a single body of all things, then at the point when the earlier Buddhas reached their Buddhahood, the bodies of all things belonging to those who had not earlier reached their enlightenment, and those who were still to reach their enlightenment, would already have been attained. And that would be a total contradiction.

snga ma.acip: BYIN GYIS RLOBS ZHES PA GZI BYIN SGYUR CES PA STE RANG RGYUD SKAD CIG SNGA MA NYON, MONGS DANG MTSUNGS LDAN DU SONG BA'I BLO PHYIN CI LOG TU YOD PA DE SKAD CIG PHYI MAR BLA, MA LA DAD GUS CHEN PO'I SLO NAS TSUL BZHIN DU BRTEN NUS PA DANG LAM YONGS RDZOGS PHYIN CI MA LOG PA RGYUD LA LDAN PA'I SKAL BA CAN DU SGYUR BAR MDZOD CIG CES GSOL BA BTAB PA STE 'DI 'OG MA RNAMS LA'ANG 'GRE GSUNGS
snga ma.wylie: byin gyis rlobs zhes pa gzi byin sgyur ces pa ste rang rgyud skad cig snga ma nyon, mongs dang mtshungs ldan du song ba'i blo phyin ci log tu yod pa de skad cig phyi mar bla, ma la dad gus chen po'i slo nas tshul bzhin du brten nus pa dang lam yongs rdzogs phyin ci ma log pa rgyud la ldan pa'i skal ba can du sgyur bar mdzod cig ces gsol ba btab pa ste 'di 'og ma rnams la'ang 'gre gsungs
snga ma.english: The words "bless me" here mean "embellish me"; which is to say, "transform the condition of my mind." A minute ago my mind was twisted wrong, and joined with every kind of bad thought. Now, in the very next moment, may I be blessed with the good fortune of being able to find and follow my Lama properly, with every reverence; may my mind be straightened, and become filled with each and every Step of the path. This is the thing I ask, my Lama. The explanation of the words "bless me" here applies as well to each of the other verses in which they appear. Asian Classics Institute Reading Two: Getting the Essence of Life III. Advice to Take the Essence of Life

snga ma.english: The master teacher of Bodong, whose name was Jikdrel Chokle Namgyal, has also said: The existence of past and future lives can be understood as well through logical reasoning. If the human body could occur as well be stuffed full of human bodies. snga ma.english: In short, if it comes down to choosing between giving up your life, and letting this morality degenerate, you had surely better choose the first. The one thing here in this birth that you cherish above all else is your own life. What you are requesting fromyour Lama is that he or she grant you the power to always keep your vows and pledges properly; that you reach a point where you cherish these commitments infinitely more than your own precious life. snga ma.acip: LNGA PA DE LA BRTEN NAS GTONG LEN BSGOM TSUL NI SNYING RJE'I DMIGS PA RTZAL DU BTON NAS, LEN PA DANG BYAMS PA'I DMIGS PA RTZAL DU BTON NAS GTONG BA SBYANG BA STE RTZA BAR GTONG LEN GNYIS PO SPEL MAR SBYANG ZHES GSUNGS LA 'DI NI SNGA MA'I BSAM PA DE NYID GONG 'PHEL DU BYED PA'O
snga ma.wylie: lnga pa de la brten nas gtong len bsgom tshul ni snying rje'i dmigs pa rtsal du bton nas, len pa dang byams pa'i dmigs pa rtsal du bton nas gtong ba sbyang ba ste rtsa bar gtong len gnyis po spel mar sbyang zhes gsungs la 'di ni snga ma'i bsam pa de nyid gong 'phel du byed pa'o
snga ma.english: Here is the fifth point, which is using this practice [that is, exchanging oneself and others] as a basis for the meditation on giving and taking. We practice taking by concentrating on the object of our compassion, and we practice giving by concentrating on the object of our love. Remember the root text [of the Mental Training in Seven Points], where it says, "Alternate the two, of giving and taking." The point is that this practice of giving and taking brings the attitude of exchanging self and others to new heights.

snga ma.acip: GTONG BA DANG LEN PA GNYIS LAS SNGA MA SNGON DU BYED PAR KHRID YIG MANG PO LAS 'BYUNG, YANG LAG LEN LA PHYI MA SNGON DU BYA ZHING GTONG BA MI BYED PAR LEN PA GCIG PU BYED PA'ANG RUNG DANG POR SDUG BSNGAL MA BLANGS NA BDE BA BTANG YANG MI PHAN PAS SNYING RJE'I DMIGS PA RTZAL DU BTON NAS MA SEMS CAN THAMS CAD SDUG BSNGAL DANG BRAL BAR BYA SNYAM PA'I SNYING RJE BSKYED NAS
snga ma.wylie: gtong ba dang len pa gnyis las snga ma sngon du byed par khrid yig mang po las 'byung, yang lag len la phyi ma sngon du bya zhing gtong ba mi byed par len pa gcig pu byed pa'ang rung dang por sdug bsngal ma blangs na bde ba btang yang mi phan pas snying rje'i dmigs pa rtsal du bton nas ma sems can thams cad sdug bsngal dang bral bar bya snyam pa'i snying rje bskyed nas
snga ma.english: Now there are a lot of books of instruction which say that—of the two steps, giving and taking—we should do the former one first. In actual practice though we should carry out the latter one first; and it is also allowable to do taking alone, without the giving. Think about it though—unless we take their sufferings first, it doesn't do much good for us to give them our happiness. So first we should concentrate on the step of compassion: we should try to develop the compassionate state of mind where we say, "May I free all living beings from their pain." Contemplation Six: An explanation of the practice of giving and taking in the first reference from the Offering to Lamas The following explanation of the practice of giving and taking comes from a commentary upon the first of the two verses in the Offering to Lamas which treat the meditation. The commentary is again by Ngulchu Dharma Bhadra, and is entitled "The Fulfilment of Every Hope of Those with the Fortune Endowed by Virtue," consisting of Notes to a Teaching upon the Practices of Transfer and Confession, as found in the "Offering to Lamas, the Indivisible Union of Bliss and Voidness."

snga ma.acip: PHA MA NYE 'BREL BAR MA DGRA SOGS DANG SEMS CAN THAMS CAD KYI BAR SBYANG STE, SNGA MA SNGA MA LA 'BYONGS PA NA PHYI MA PHYI MA LA DMIGS PA SPOS KYIN SDUG BSNGAL SDIG SGRIB SOGS RANG STENG DU BLANG DE LTAR GO RIM 'DI BZHIN DU BYAS NAS SBYONG DGOS KYI DANG PO NAS DGRA SOGS KYI SDIG SDUG LEN BLO MI 'BYUNG
snga ma.wylie: pha ma nye 'brel bar ma dgra sogs dang sems can thams cad kyi bar sbyang ste, snga ma snga ma la 'byongs pa na phyi ma phyi ma la dmigs pa spos kyin sdug bsngal sdig sgrib sogs rang steng du blang de ltar go rim 'di bzhin du byas nas sbyong dgos kyi dang po nas dgra sogs kyi sdig sdug len blo mi 'byung
snga ma.english: Then clean these problems from your own parents, and then from all those close to you, and next from those towards whom you are neutral; then continue with your enemies and the like, and finally from every living being that there is. Each time you finish cleaning one group, then move your focus on to the next, and start again—and keep moving on. Take upon yourself all their sufferings; their bad deeds, spiritual obstacles, and all the rest. You should practice the meditation in a gradual progression like this; don't try at first to take on the bad karma and pain of your enemies or the like, you won't be able to have the right feeling.

snga ma.acip: SDIG PA BSHAGS PA'I YAN LAG NI 'DOD CHAGS ZHES PA'I TSIGS BCAD GCIG STE, RGYU DUG GSUM LA BRTEN NAS GZHI LUS LA SOGS PA GSUM GYIS RANG BZHIN NI BDAG GIS BGYIS PA STE DE YANG DNGOS SU RANG GIS BYA BA DE LA ZHUGS PA DANG GZHAN BYED DU BCUG PA DANG GZHAN GYIS BYAS PA LA YI RANG BA'O DE DAG THAMS CAD SPYIR BSDUS PA NI CI MCHIS PA ZHES PA STE DE DAG GI NYES DMIGS DRAN NAS SNGA MA LA 'GYOD CING PHYI MA LA BSDAM PA'I SEMS KYIS SNYING THAG PA NAS BSHAGS NA SNGAR BYAS 'PHEL BA 'CHAD CING PHYI MA RNAMS 'PHRO 'CHAD DO
snga ma.wylie: sdig pa bshags pa'i yan lag ni 'dod chags zhes pa'i tshigs bcad gcig ste, rgyu dug gsum la brten nas gzhi lus la sogs pa gsum gyis rang bzhin ni bdag gis bgyis pa ste de yang dngos su rang gis bya ba de la zhugs pa dang gzhan byed du bcug pa dang gzhan gyis byas pa la yi rang ba'o de dag thams cad spyir bsdus pa ni ci mchis pa zhes pa ste de dag gi nyes dmigs dran nas snga ma la 'gyod cing phyi ma la bsdam pa'i sems kyis snying thag pa nas bshags na sngar byas 'phel ba 'chad cing phyi ma rnams 'phro 'chad do
snga ma.english: The third ingredient is confession, and is found in the single verse with the words "like and dislike". [The full verse reads: I confess, one by one, Each and every one Of all the wrong deeds I may have committed In action or word, And also thought, Motivated by like or dislike, Or by dark ignorance.] This refers to what was done with one of the three mental poisons as its cause; and with my body or of the rest as the vehicle; and with a nature of having been committed, either directly by myself, or by someone else at my bidding, The Six Preliminaries and the Seven Ingredients or by someone else with my gladness that it was done. The words "all the wrong deeds I may have committed" are meant to include all these elements. Try to bring to mind all the problems that these deeds will bring you, and so feel regret for whatever you have done in the past, and a sense to restrain yourself in the future. Then make your confession. Doing this prevents any future wrong from starting at all.

snga ma.english: They say too that when someone would ask Kamawa if they could move on to a new spiritual topic he would say, “Work again on the old one.” When they asked if he could finish up the old one, “There is no finish to the old one.” So if your mind can handle it, do the meditation as I have described it above. If your mind cannot handle it, then try to keep as many of the nine reasons for the three principles as fits your capacity.

snga ma.wylie: rgyu mtshan de ci'i phyir zhe na sems can de dag gis ni tshe rabs 'di dang snga ma'i dus su, mi dge ba'i las chen po ngan song gsum du skye bar 'gyur ba'i las gang dag byas pa de dag thams cad kyi 'bras bu ni tshe 'di nyid kyi thog la smin te sdug bsngal gyis mnar ba de'i stobs kyis tshe rabs snga ma'i mi dge ba'i las de dag thams cad 'byang ba ste dag par 'gyur te sangs rgyas kyi byang chub kyang myur du thob par 'gyur ro sher phyin la brtson pa'i gnyen po kun tu spyod pa'i stobs kyis ni sdig las rnams kyi rtsa ba bdag 'dzin bcom ste thar pa dang thams cad mkhyen pa yang thob par 'gyur zhes bshad na ngan 'gror skye ba'i las rnams 'joms pa lta ci smos so tshul de ltar rtog ge 'bar ba sogs nas bshad cing thar pa chen po las kyang ngan 'gror skye ba'i sdig yod kyang mgo bo na, ba tsam gyis 'byang zhes gsungs so dper na sa bon btab kyang chu lud drod gsher
snga ma.english: past—karma so serious that it would normally have taken them to the three lower realms. As such, the results of all these deeds are ripening here in this very life. Thus one is suffering pain, and by force of this suffering he or she is "cleaning away"—that is, purifying—all of this non-virtuous karma. As such, one will quickly achieve the enlightenment of a Buddha. The force of an antidote action consisting of making great efforts in the perfection of wisdom is destroying the grasping to some self-existence, the very root of all non-virtuous deeds. This is why the text goes on to say that one will achieve freedom and the state of omniscience. And since the text does say this, then needless to say one could destroy the karma that is leading you to a birth in the lower realms. The way in which this works is explained in texts such as the Blaze of Reasoning and others. As the Sutra of the Great Liberation says as well, Even though one may have the bad karma To take his birth in the three lower realms, A simple headache will clean it away. Suppose for example that a seed is planted, but is then deprived completely of water, or fertilizer, or warmth, or the rest. Then it would never sprout.

snga ma.acip: DE SMIN PA LAS DUS PHYIS SNGA MA DE'I RNAM PA'I RJES SU BYED PA'I MIG GI RNAM SHES SKYE, BAR 'GYUR ZHING
snga ma.wylie: de smin pa las dus phyis snga ma de'i rnam pa'i rjes su byed pa'i mig gi rnam shes skye, bar 'gyur zhing
snga ma.english: They speak first of the mental seed, the energy, from which the "mind of the eye" (which refers to the consciousness of the eye) comes forth. Another case of consciousness, as it is in the process of stopping, in the next moment plants this mental seed in the foundation consciousness. When this seed ripens later, it produces that consciousness of the eye, one which takes after the earlier one.

snga ma.acip: YAN LAG BCU GNYIS PO THAMS CAD KYANG SEMS GCIG LA BRTEN PAR GSUNGS PA LA, BRTEN NAS TZAM GYI SGRAS SEMS GTZO BOR GYUR PAR BSTAN TE BSHAD PA SNGA MA, DGAG PHYOGS DANG PHYI MA SGRUB PHYOGS NAS YIN NO DE'I PHYIR 'GRO BA RAB TU 'JUG PA, LA SEMS NYID GTZO BO'I RGYU YIN GYI SEMS LAS GZHAN PA NI GTZO BO'I RGYU MIN PAS MDO LAS SEMS TZAM ZHIG GTZO BOR BZHAG GI GZUGS NI MA YIN NO GAL TE GZUGS YOD PAR 'DOD MOD KYI STE KYANG GZUGS DE LA NI SEMS BZHIN DU 'GRO BA'I BYED PA PO NYID NI YOD PA MA YIN NO DES NA SEMS LAS GZHAN PA'I BYED PA PO BZLOG PA STE BKAG GI PHYI ROL GYI GZUGS NI BKAG PA MA YIN NO
snga ma.wylie: yan lag bcu gnyis po thams cad kyang sems gcig la brten par gsungs pa la, brten nas tsam gyi sgras sems gtso bor gyur par bstan te bshad pa snga ma, dgag phyogs dang phyi ma sgrub phyogs nas yin no de'i phyir 'gro ba rab tu 'jug pa, la sems nyid gtso bo'i rgyu yin gyi sems las gzhan pa ni gtso bo'i rgyu min pas mdo las sems tsam zhig gtso bor bzhag gi gzugs ni ma yin no gal te gzugs yod par 'dod mod kyi ste kyang gzugs de la ni sems bzhin du 'gro ba'i byed pa po nyid ni yod pa ma yin no des na sems las gzhan pa'i byed pa po bzlog pa ste bkag gi phyi rol gyi gzugs ni bkag pa ma yin no
snga ma.english: It is stated in scripture as well that each and every one of the twelve links in the chain of interdependence depends on a single thing: the mind. These references convey yet another meaning of the word "only" in the expression "mind-only." Here the point is that mind is the main thing. The former scriptural references are putting their point in a negative way, and the latter references are putting their point in a positive way. Thus we can see that it's the mind which is the one single principal cause that sets all life into motion. The principal cause is not something other than the mind. Therefore when the sutras speak of "mind only," they are making the point that mind is the main thing, and not matter. Although we do of course admit that physical matter exists, this matter is not the one prime creator of sentient beings in the way that mind is. Therefore all these scriptural references are denying that the opposite of the mind, something other than the mind, could be the creator. They are not though saying that there are no outside physical objects at all. The Asian Classics Institute Reading Two: How Emptiness Allows Karma to Work, According to the Middle-Way School

snga ma.english: The first of our logical statements above is always true. For suppose that a person is still unable to root out the object that he thinks he sees when he hold the parts to the person, the thing which gets the label of "me," as existing through some nature of its own. As long as he goes on this way, then he will continue to find himself unable to root out the object that he thinks he sees when he holds the thing which gets the label, the "me," as existing from its own side. And as long as he continues with this, then by the power of this misperception he will continue to collect karma. And as long as he collects karma, then he will continue to spin around in this wheel of suffering life.

snga ma.acip: GNYIS PA DER THAL PHYOGS SNGA MAS BRLAN ZHING GSHER BA PHOR PA GANG LA 'GRO BA, GSUM GYIS CIG CAR DU BLTAS PA DE'I TSE NA BRLAN ZHING GSHER BA PHOR PA GANG PO DE DNGOS PO GSUM GYI GZHI MTHUN DU YANG KHAS MA BLANGS SKYES BU GCIG GI GZUGS MDZES MI MDZES GNYIS KA YIN PAR YANG KHAS MA BLANGS YI DWAGS KYIS MIG SHES DANG CHU KLUNG GI BAR DU RNAG KHRAG GI LAS GZUGS SKYE BAR KHAS MA BLANGS YI DWAGS KYI MIG GIS RNAG KHRAG GI LAS GZUGS DANG CHU KLUNG GNYIS KA MTHONG BAR YANG KHAS MA BLANGS LAS KYI DBANG GIS YI DWAGS KYI CHU KLUNG MA MTHONG BAR KHAS BLANGS PA'I PHYIR
snga ma.wylie: gnyis pa der thal phyogs snga mas brlan zhing gsher ba phor pa gang la 'gro ba, gsum gyis cig car du bltas pa de'i tshe na brlan zhing gsher ba phor pa gang po de dngos po gsum gyi gzhi mthun du yang khas ma blangs skyes bu gcig gi gzugs mdzes mi mdzes gnyis ka yin par yang khas ma blangs yi dwags kyis mig shes dang chu klung gi bar du rnag khrag gi las gzugs skye bar khas ma blangs yi dwags kyi mig gis rnag khrag gi las gzugs dang chu klung gnyis ka mthong bar yang khas ma blangs las kyi dbang gis yi dwags kyi chu klung ma mthong bar khas blangs pa'i phyir
snga ma.english: Our second point [that you have failed to comprehend the position we expressed above] is also quite true. Our original position was describing a situation where three different kinds of beings were sitting together and looking at a glass full of something wet and flowing. It is not our position that the glass full of something wet and flowing is one thing that is three different things. And it is not our position that there is such a thing as the physical appearance of a person which is at once both attractive and ugly. It is furthermore not our position that the blood and pus represent some kind of physical form which results from karma and grows up between the visual consciousness of the craving spirit and the stream of water. And it is not our position that the craving spirit's eyes see both this blood and pus as some kind of physical form resulting from karma, and the river of water at the same time. It is our position that, by force of his karma, the craving spirit is not able to see the stream of water.

snga ma.english: And yet there is no such problem. No matter how many arguments of this kind you want to present, they are all made from the point of view of denying the existence of external objects. The way these arguments go is as follows. If the color blue were to exist as an external object, then the following would occur when this color appeared directly to a sense perception grasping blue; that is, with such a perception found in the mental stream of one of those who "only sees this side" [which is another name for those who have not yet perceived emptiness directly]. When an earlier instance of the perception of blue ends, what actually happens is that it plants a mental seed which eventually grows into a later instance of the same perception of blue, when the seed ripens. Suppose the blue were not just this kind of appearance, but rather an appearance where blue as an outer object were transmitting a likeness of itself and thereby appearing to one's perceptions. Something else then would be happening when the three different beings sit down together and look at the glass full of something wet and flowing. snga ma.acip: SHES RAB KYI PHA ROL TU PHYIN ZHES PA NI 'KHOR BA'I RGYA MTSO'I PHA ROL TU PHYIN PA'I DON YIN LA, DE YANG BYED TSIG LA SBYAR BA DANG, LAS TSIG LA SBYAR BA GNYIS YOD PA'I SNGA MA LTAR NA, PHYIN PAR BYED PA'I DON YIN PAS SLOB LAM NA'ANG SHER PHYIN DNGOS YOD LA,
snga ma.wylie: shes rab kyi pha rol tu phyin zhes pa ni 'khor ba'i rgya mtsho'i pha rol tu phyin pa'i don yin la, de yang byed tshig la sbyar ba dang, las tshig la sbyar ba gnyis yod pa'i snga ma ltar na, phyin par byed pa'i don yin pas slob lam na'ang sher phyin dngos yod la
snga ma.english: When we speak of the “perfection of wisdom” in this sense, the meaning is “gone to the other side of the ocean of the cycle of pain.” Now you can take the Sanskrit here either in an agentive sense, or in the sense of an action itself. Considering it in the former sense, it is expressing “something that takes us to perfection,” rather than “perfection.” This is a reference to the paths where we are still training ourselves spiritually—which is an allusion to the actual perfection of wisdom.

snga ma.acip: DGE 'DUN NI MI MTHUN PHYOGS KYIS MI PHYED PA'I DON DANG, CHEN PO SNGA MA NI SPANGS RTOGS KYI YON TAN MTHON PO THOB PA'I DON YIN LA,
snga ma.wylie: dge 'dun ni mi mthun phyogs kyis mi phyed pa'i don dang, chen po snga ma ni spangs rtogs kyi yon tan mthon po thob pa'i don yin la
snga ma.english: The word “gathering” here has connotations, in the original Sanskrit, of a group which cannot be split up by forces that would work against it. The word “great” occurs twice here; the first of the two is to indicate that the members of the first group have attained high personal qualities which relate to having given up negativities and having reached certain realizations.

snga ma.acip: KHA CIG TU 'DAS PAR PHYIN TO ZHES 'BYUNG LA, LA LAR 'DAS PAR MTHAR PHYIN TO ZHES 'BYUNG BA'I SNGA MA LTAR BYAS NA BDE BAR SEMS PAS, DE LTAR NA SANGS RGYAS KYI SA'I MYA NGAN LAS 'DAS BAR PHYIN PA'AM, DE THOB PAR 'GYUR BA'I DON NO,,
snga ma.wylie: kha cig tu 'das par phyin to zhes 'byung la, la lar 'das par mthar phyin to zhes 'byung ba'i snga ma ltar byas na bde bar sems pas, de ltar na sangs rgyas kyi sa'i mya ngan las 'das bar phyin pa'am, de thob par 'gyur ba'i don no
snga ma.english: Now in some versions of the sutra, we see the wording here as “reach to nirvana”; and in others we see “reach to the ultimate end in nirvana.” The former reading seems to me more comfortable. snga ma.acip: SPYIR 'CHI BA'I DUS BYAS PA 'GA' ZHIG LA MYA NGAN LAS 'DAS PA ZHES ZER YANG, 'DIR THAR PA LA MYANG 'DAS SAM MYA NGAN LAS 'DAS PA'I THA SNYAD MDZAD PA LTAR YIN GYI, SNGA MA MIN LA, MYA NGAN YANG SDUG KUN GNYIS LA BYAS NAS, DE LAS 'DAS PA NI DE SPANGS PA'I DON NO,,
snga ma.wylie: spyir 'chi ba'i dus byas pa 'ga' zhig la mya ngan las 'das pa zhes zer yang, 'dir thar pa la myang 'das sam mya ngan las 'das pa'i tha snyad mdzad pa ltar yin gyi, snga ma min la, mya ngan yang sdug kun gnyis la byas nas, de las 'das pa ni de spangs pa'i don no
snga ma.english: Now admittedly people in general use the expression “passed into nirvana” to express the fact that someone has come to die; but here in the sutra we are talking about the word “nirvana” not in this first way, but rather in its other sense as spiritual freedom, which in the Tibetan is literally rendered as “grief passage,” or in full: “passing beyond all grief.” The “grief” here refers to the two truths of pain and the source of pain; passing beyond this grief then refers to ridding oneself of these two.

snga ma.acip: SNGA MAS CHAD MTHA' SEL ZHING, PHYI MAS RTAG MTHA' SEL BA'I PHYIR RTAG CHAD KYI MTHA' GNYIS BKAG GO
snga ma.wylie: snga mas chad mtha' sel zhing, phyi mas rtag mtha' sel ba'i phyir rtag chad kyi mtha' gnyis bkag go
snga ma.english: And when we do say these things, the previous statement serves to prevent the extreme idea that everything must come to a stop; while the latter statement serves to prevent the extreme idea that things must exist without ever changing. snga ma.acip: SNGA MA 'PHAGS PA DANG PHYI MA SO SKYE LA YOD PA'O, ,LAM MA ZHUGS NA SBYIN PA YOD KYANG SBYIN PA'I PHAR PHYIN MED CING GZHAN LNGA LA'ANG 'DRA'O,,
snga ma.wylie: snga ma 'phags pa dang phyi ma so skye la yod pa'o, ,lam ma zhugs na sbyin pa yod kyang sbyin pa'i phar phyin med cing gzhan lnga la'ang 'dra'o
snga ma.english: The former type of giving is possessed by realized beings; and the latter is had by normal beings. And the same is true for the other five perfections.

snga ma.acip: PHAR PHYIN ZHES PA'I SGRA DON NI, 'KHOR BA'I RGYA MTSO'I PHA ROL TU PHYIN PAR BYED PA DANG PHYIN ZIN PA'I DON TE, SNGA MA LTAR NA SLOB LAM NA YOD CING, PHYI MA NI SANGS RGYAS KYI SA NA YOD DE RNAM MKHYEN DANG DON GCIG GO ,
snga ma.wylie: phar phyin zhes pa'i sgra don ni, 'khor ba'i rgya mtsho'i pha rol tu phyin par byed pa dang phyin zin pa'i don te, snga ma ltar na slob lam na yod cing, phyi ma ni sangs rgyas kyi sa na yod de rnam mkhyen dang don gcig go
snga ma.english: Here is a bit on the literal meaning of the expression “perfection,” or “gone to the other side.” This term connotes either that thing which takes you to the other side of the ocean of cyclic life, or else the state of having already reached that other side. Taken the former way, the expression refers the perfection of wisdom as it exists on the paths of those who are still learning. Taken the latter way, it refers to the perfection of wisdom which exists at the level of a Buddha, and is equivalent to the knowledge of all objects.

snga ma.acip: SNGA MA LAS GZHAN YANG RAB 'BYOR RIGS KYI BU'AM BU MO GANG MDO SDE 'DI 'DZIN 'CHANG SOGS BYED CING DON NYAMS SU LEN PA'I SEMS CAN DE DAG NI NAD SNA TSOGS DANG 'THAB RTZOD 'TSANG 'DRU DANG BCING RDEG SOGS KYIS MNAR BA DANG SHIN TU MNAR BA'I SDUG BSNGAL MYONG BAR 'GYUR BA YOD SRID KYANG, SKYON CHEN PO MA YIN TE,

snga ma.english: There is furthermore some additional text at this point which differentiates it from the preceding, similar passage. Lord Buddha says, “Think further, o Subhuti, of any son or daughter of noble family who holds or carries or does any of the other actions mentioned with this sutra; who puts it into practice. Living beings like this may well suffer from a whole variety of illnesses; they may come to live in conflict, they may be criticized, they may be imprisoned or beaten and others of the like. It is possible that they might experience, in fact, intense suffering—but this will be no great problem for them.

It is possible that they might experience, in fact, intense suffering—but this will be no great problem for them."}

snga ma.english: And for what reason is this so? But the power of the suffering that strikes them now will purify and clean them of each and every non-virtuous deed of their previous lifetimes, and they will in fact go on to achieve the enlightenment of the Buddha very quickly.

snga ma.wylie: de ci'i phyir zhe na dang, de ci'i slad du zhe na gnyis kyi phyir dang slad du ni gtan tshigs sam, rgyu mtshan yin zhing skad dod aa tha zhes par 'dra yang, snga ma ni ston pa'i gsungs te zhe sa med la, phyi ma rab 'byor gyi gsung ni zhe sar bsgyur ba'o
snga ma.english: There are a number of terms in the Tibetan translation of the root text which we have been referring to here in expressions like “Why is it so?”—these are the Tibetan terms chiy chir she na and chiy ledu she na. The Tibetan words chir and ledu contained in these terms are both meant to refer to a reason—a reason “why” or “because of which” something is true. Now it's true that the original Sanskrit for both of these terms is the same—atha [spelled simply atha]—but the Tibetan translators used the former of the two Tibetan words when the Teacher was speaking (since it is not an honorific form, one used when speaking to a person who is higher) and the latter when Subhuti was speaking (since it is an honorific form, as he is addressing Lord Buddha).

snga ma.acip: BSAL BA SNGA MA LA DE LTAR YIN NA MA RIG STONGS {%LDONGS} PAR 'GYUR BAS SRED PA'I CHU KLUNG GI RGYUN PHYOGS SU RJES SU GZHOL BA'I TSANGS PA SOGS DANG, YUL LA SRED PA DANG BRAL BA'I MKHAS PA RNAMS DNGOS PO'I GNAS LUGS LA LTA BA MTSUNGS PAR 'GYUR TE MTSUNGS PA'I GO SKABS MED PA'I PHYIR,
snga ma.wylie: bsal ba snga ma la de ltar yin na ma rig stongs par 'gyur bas sred pa'i chu klung gi rgyun phyogs su rjes su gzhol ba'i tshangs pa sogs dang, yul la sred pa dang bral ba'i mkhas pa rnams dngos po'i gnas lugs la lta ba mtshungs par 'gyur te mtshungs pa'i go skabs med pa'i phyir
snga ma.english: Let's suppose that the conclusion which we reached in that last section is accurate. In that case, then Pure One and people like him are, truly, swept along by the strong current of desire, and have lost themselves to its path-all because they are blinded by misunderstanding. As such, they could not be the equals-there is no possibility that they could ever be the equals-of those wise ones who are free of craving for objects, as far as how they are able to perceive the true nature of things. The stages of explaining no nature

snga ma.acip: SNGA MA'I 'PHROS LA SBYOR NA, SANGS RGYAS KYIS RTEN CING 'BREL BAR 'BYUNG BA GSUNGS PA LA DGOS PA YOD DE, DE LA BRTEN NAS DNGOS PO LA BDEN 'DZIN LDOG LA, DE LOG NA 'DOD PA DANG LTA BA LA CHAGS PA DANG BCAS PA LA SOGS MI 'BYUNG BA'I PHYIR,
snga ma.wylie: snga ma'i 'phros la sbyor na, sangs rgyas kyis rten cing 'brel bar 'byung ba gsungs pa la dgos pa yod de, de la brten nas dngos po la bden 'dzin ldog la, de log na 'dod pa dang lta ba la chags pa dang bcas pa la sogs mi 'byung ba'i phyir
snga ma.english: We could link this to what we were discussing earlier by saying- Let's consider the way in which the Buddha has described things happening in a dependent relationship. There was a purpose for this description; Because by depending on this explanation, we can stop our tendency of holding things to be real. And if we can stop that, then we don't get these particular problems, such as attachment towards desirable objects, and towards our own viewpoints. How we disengage from pain

snga ma.acip: MIG SOGS KYI RANG MTSAN SNANG BA LA LTOS TE MA 'KHRUL BA'I TSAD MAS NI MIG SOGS DON DAM PAR YOD PAR 'JAL DGOS KYI DON DAM PA'I KHYAD PAR DOR BA'I MIG SOGS TZAM PO 'JAL MI RUNG BA'I PHYIR, RTAGS SNGA MA LEGS LDAN RANG GI KHAS BLANGS KYIS GRUB STE,
snga ma.wylie: mig sogs kyi rang mtshan snang ba la ltos te ma 'khrul ba'i tshad mas ni mig sogs don dam par yod par 'jal dgos kyi don dam pa'i khyad par dor ba'i mig sogs tsam po 'jal mi rung ba'i phyir, rtags snga ma legs ldan rang gi khas blangs kyis grub ste
snga ma.english: Relative to the appearance of the actual expression of the eye or such, an accurate perception which was not mistaken would have to be considering an eye or such as something that existed in an ultimate sense; but it would be wrong to say that it was considering just the general form of the eye and the like, without regard to the distinction of it being ultimate. As such, the first part of the reason given here is validated by Master Bhavaviveka's own position.

snga ma.acip: SNGA MA 'PHAGS PA DANG PHYI MA SO SKYE LA YOD PA'O, ,LAM MA ZHUGS NA SBYIN PA YOD KYANG SBYIN PA'I PHAR PHYIN MED CING GZHAN LNGA LA'ANG 'DRA'O,,
snga ma.wylie: snga ma 'phags pa dang phyi ma so skye la yod pa'o, ,lam ma zhugs na sbyin pa yod kyang sbyin pa'i phar phyin med cing gzhan lnga la'ang 'dra'o
snga ma.english: The former type of giving is possessed by realized beings; and the latter is had by normal beings.[67] It is possible for a person to perform an act of giving before they enter one of the paths; but it is not possible then for this to be the perfection of giving. And the same is true for the other five perfections.

snga ma.acip: BDEN GRUB KYI MTSAN DANG MTSAN MA MED PAR BSTAN PAS SGRO 'DOGS KYI MTHA' SEL BA'I PHYIR RO, ,DE'I SNGA MAS GZUGS SKU DANG PHYI MAS CHOS KYI SKU BSTAN TE NGO BO NYID SKU GTZO CHE'O,,
snga ma.wylie: bden grub kyi mtshan dang mtshan ma med par bstan pas sgro 'dogs kyi mtha' sel ba'i phyir ro, ,de'i snga mas gzugs sku dang phyi mas chos kyi sku bstan te ngo bo nyid sku gtso che'o
snga ma.english: The text though also states that there exist no signs, and no signs that would indicate any nature, which also exist truly. This fact keeps us from the extreme of asserting the existence of something which actually does not exist. The former of these two is referring to the physical body of a Buddha. The latter is referring to the reality body, and chiefly to the essence body. Bodhisattvas of the last 500 years [K25b]

snga ma.acip: BDAG GIR 'DZIN PA'I DON SNGA MA DANG CUNG MI 'DRA'O, ,DE LTA BU'I 'DU SHES RAGS PA MI 'JUG PA NI BDAG MED RTOGS PA'I SKABS LA DGONGS SO,,
snga ma.wylie: bdag gir 'dzin pa'i don snga ma dang cung mi 'dra'o, ,de lta bu'i 'du shes rags pa mi 'jug pa ni bdag med rtogs pa'i skabs la dgongs so
snga ma.english: Thus the meaning of grasping to something as belonging to the self is a bit different than before. When the text says that these bodhisattvas entertain no such coarse conceptions, it is referring specifically to the occasions at which one realizes the lack of a self-nature.

snga ma.acip: PHAR PHYIN ZHES PA'I SGRA DON NI, 'KHOR BA'I RGYA MTSO'I PHA ROL TU PHYIN PAR BYED PA DANG PHYIN ZIN PA'I DON TE, SNGA MA LTAR NA SLOB LAM NA YOD CING, PHYI MA NI SANGS RGYAS KYI SA NA YOD DE RNAM MKHYEN DANG DON GCIG GO ,
snga ma.wylie: phar phyin zhes pa'i sgra don ni, 'khor ba'i rgya mtsho'i pha rol tu phyin par byed pa dang phyin zin pa'i don te, snga ma ltar na slob lam na yod cing, phyi ma ni sangs rgyas kyi sa na yod de rnam mkhyen dang don gcig go
snga ma.english: Here is a bit on the literal meaning of the expression "perfection," or "gone to the other side."[92] This term connotes either that thing which takes you to the other side of the ocean of cyclic life, or else the state of having already reached that other side. Taken the former way, the expression refers the perfection of wisdom as it exists on the paths of those who are still learning.[93] Taken the latter way, it refers to the perfection of wisdom which exists at the level of a Buddha, and is equivalent to the knowledge of all objects.

snga ma.acip: SNGA MA LAS GZHAN YANG RAB 'BYOR RIGS KYI BU'AM BU MO GANG MDO SDE 'DI 'DZIN 'CHANG SOGS BYED CING DON NYAMS SU LEN PA'I SEMS CAN DE DAG NI NAD SNA TSOGS DANG 'THAB RTZOD 'TSANG 'DRU DANG BCING RDEG SOGS KYIS MNAR BA DANG SHIN TU MNAR BA'I SDUG BSNGAL MYONG BAR 'GYUR BA YOD SRID KYANG, SKYON CHEN PO MA YIN TE,
snga ma.wylie: snga ma las gzhan yang rab 'byor rigs kyi bu'am bu mo gang mdo sde 'di 'dzin 'chang sogs byed cing don nyams su len pa'i sems can de dag ni nad sna tshogs dang 'thab rtsod 'tshang 'dru dang bcing rdeg sogs kyis mnar ba dang shin tu mnar ba'i sdug bsngal myong bar 'gyur ba yod srid kyang, skyon chen po ma yin te
snga ma.english: There is furthermore some additional text at this point which differentiates it from the preceding, similar passage. Lord Buddha says, "Think further, o Subhuti, of any son or daughter of noble family who holds or carries or does any of the other actions mentioned with this sutra; who puts it into practice. Living beings like this may well suffer from a whole variety of illnesses; they may come to live in conflict, they may be criticized, they may be imprisoned or beaten and others of the like. It is possible that they might experience, in fact, intense suffering—but this will be no great problem for them.

snga ma.acip: DE CI'I PHYIR ZHE NA, RAB 'BYOR, SEMS CAN DE DAG GIS TSE RABS SNGA MA'I MI DGE BA'I LAS NGAN SONG DU SKYE BAR 'GYUR BA GANG DAG BYAS PA DAG TSE 'DI NYID LA MNAR BAS, TSE RABS SNGA MA'I MI DGE BA'I LAS DE DAG 'BYANG BAR 'GYUR TE, SANGS RGYAS KYI BYANG CHUB KYANG 'THOB PAR 'GYUR BA'I PHYIR RO,,
snga ma.wylie: de ci'i phyir zhe na, rab 'byor, sems can de dag gis tshe rabs snga ma'i mi dge ba'i las ngan song du skye bar 'gyur ba gang dag byas pa dag tshe 'di nyid la mnar bas, tshe rabs snga ma'i mi dge ba'i las de dag 'byang bar 'gyur te, sangs rgyas kyi byang chub kyang 'thob par 'gyur ba'i phyir ro
snga ma.english: Why is it so? Because, o Subhuti, such beings are purifying non-virtuous karma from the entire string of their previous lives, karma that would have taken them to the three lower realms. As they purify this karma, it causes them to suffer here in this life. As such they will succeed in cleaning away the karma of these non-virtuous deeds of their previous lifetimes, and they will as well achieve the enlightenment of a Buddha.

snga ma.acip: RGYU MTSAN DE CI'I PHYIR ZHE NA, SEMS CAN DE DAG GIS NI TSE RABS 'DI DANG SNGA MA'I DUS SU MI DGE BA'I LAS CHEN PO NGAN SONG GSUM DU SKYE BAR 'GYUR BA'I LAS GANG DAG BYAS PA DE DAG THAMS CAD KYI 'BRAS BU NI TSE 'DI NYID KYI THOG LA SMIN TE SDUG BSNGAL GYIS MNAR BA DE'I STOBS KYIS TSE RABS SNGA MA'I MI DGE BA'I LAS DE DAG THAMS CAD 'BYANG BA STE DAG PAR 'GYUR TE, SANGS RGYAS KYI BYANG CHUB KYANG MYUR DU THOB PAR 'GYUR RO,,
snga ma.wylie: rgyu mtshan de ci'i phyir zhe na, sems can de dag gis ni tshe rabs 'di dang snga ma'i dus su mi dge ba'i las chen po ngan song gsum du skye bar 'gyur ba'i las gang dag byas pa de dag thams cad kyi 'bras bu ni tshe 'di nyid kyi thog la smin te sdug bsngal gyis mnar ba de'i stobs kyis tshe rabs snga ma'i mi dge ba'i las de dag thams cad 'byang ba ste dag par 'gyur te, sangs rgyas kyi byang chub kyang myur du thob par 'gyur ro
snga ma.english: And for what reason is this so? These living beings have committed karma—both in this life and in the string of their previous lives—which is very serious non-virtuous karma, and which would have taken them to a birth in the three lower realms. The fruits of all the karma of this kind that they possess within them will now flower here, within this very same life. But the power of the suffering that strikes them now will purify and clean them of each and every non-virtuous deed of their previous lifetimes, and they will in fact go on to achieve the enlightenment of the Buddha very quickly.

snga ma.acip: RAB 'BYOR, SANGS RGYAS BCOM LDAN 'DAS DE DAG NGAS MNYES PAR BYAS NAS THUGS BYUNG BAR MA BYAS PA GANG YIN PA DANG, PHYI MA'I DUS LNGA BRGYA THA MAR GYUR PA NA, MDO SDE 'DI LEN PA DANG, 'DZIN PA DANG, KLOG PA DANG, KUN CHUB PAR BYED PA GANG YIN PA LAS, RAB 'BYOR, BSOD NAMS KYI PHUNG PO 'DI LA BSOD NAMS KYI PHUNG PO SNGA MAS BRGYA'I CHAR YANG MI PHOD, STONG GI CHA DANG, 'BUM GYI CHA DANG, GRANGS DANG, CHA DANG, BGRANG BA DANG, DPE DANG, ZLA DANG, RGYUR YANG MI BZOD DO,,
snga ma.wylie: rab 'byor, sangs rgyas bcom ldan 'das de dag ngas mnyes par byas nas thugs byung bar ma byas pa gang yin pa dang, phyi ma'i dus lnga brgya tha mar gyur pa na, mdo sde 'di len pa dang, 'dzin pa dang, klog pa dang, kun chub par byed pa gang yin pa las, rab 'byor, bsod nams kyi phung po 'di la bsod nams kyi phung po snga mas brgya'i char yang mi phod, stong gi cha dang, 'bum gyi cha dang, grangs dang, cha dang, bgrang ba dang, dpe dang, zla dang, rgyur yang mi bzod do
snga ma.english: But then Subhuti, there are those who, in the days of the last five hundred, will take up this sutra, and hold it, and read it, and comprehend it. And I tell you, o Subhuti, that the great mountains of merit that I collected from pleasing all those Buddhas, all those Conquerors, and from never disturbing their hearts, would not come to a hundredth of the mountains of merit that these ones to come will create. Nor would it come to a thousandth part, nor one part in a hundred thousand, nor any other countable part, any part at all; the difference could never be put in numbers; there is no example I could use; no comparison; no reason at all to attempt any comparison.

snga ma.wylie: 'di ltar bshad par bya ste, skyes bu lus chung ngu zhig rim gyis skyes nas cher song ba'i lus ni snga ma la ltos te lus chen po zhes tha snyad
snga ma.english: BYED PA LTAR,It seems to me though that the intent of the passage could be explained in the following way. Think of a person who starts with a small body which gradually grows larger and larger. We can apply the expression "large body" to the body at the end of this process, since it is large relative to the body at earlier points of the process.[429]

snga ma.wylie: gang gis shes rab kyi pha rol tu phyin pa 'di las tha na tshig bzhi pa'i tshigs su bcad pa tsam bzung nas gzhan dag la yang bstan na, rab 'byor, bsod nams kyi phung po 'di la bsod nams kyi phung po snga ma des brgya'i char yang mi phod pa nas rgyu'i bar du yang nye bar mi bzod do
snga ma.english: Suppose that someone else were to take up, and teach to others, even so little as a single verse of four lines from this perfection of wisdom. I tell you, o Subhuti, that the mountain of merit created by the first person would not come to even a hundredth part of the mountain of merit created by the second; it would not come to any of the parts we spoke of before, all the way up to saying that there would be no reason to attempt any comparison between the two.

snga ma.acip: 'JIG RTEN NA RIL POR RAGS PA LING PO CHA MED GCIG TU GRUB PAR 'DZIN PA GANG GSUNGS PA'I 'DZIN PA DE YANG DON DAM PAR 'DZIN PAR GRUB PAR MA MCHIS SO ZHES PA'I SNGA MAS GZUNG BYA DANG, 'DIS 'DZIN PA YANG DON DAM PAR GRUB PAR STON PAR BSHAD DO,,
snga ma.wylie: 'jig rten na ril por rags pa ling po cha med gcig tu grub par 'dzin pa gang gsungs pa'i 'dzin pa de yang don dam par 'dzin par grub par ma mchis so zhes pa'i snga mas gzung bya dang, 'dis 'dzin pa yang don dam par grub par ston par bshad do
snga ma.english: And thus it is that the One Thus Gone has said that even the "tendency to grasp things as one whole solid thing"—as gross, discrete entities that are singular things not made of parts—described by the One Thus Gone is a kind of grasping that could never exist anyway. The first part above then is meant to demonstrate that what is grasped to could never exist in any ultimate sense, while this last part is to demonstrate that what does the grasping could never exist in this sense either.

snga ma.acip: DE CI'I PHYIR ZHE NA DANG, DE CI'I SLAD DU ZHE NA GNYIS KYI PHYIR DANG SLAD DU NI GTAN TSIGS SAM, RGYU MTSAN YIN ZHING SKAD DOD AA THA ZHES PAR 'DRA YANG, SNGA MA NI STON PA'I GSUNGS TE ZHE SA MED LA, PHYI MA RAB 'BYOR GYI GSUNG NI ZHE SAR BSGYUR BA'O,,
snga ma.wylie: de ci'i phyir zhe na dang, de ci'i slad du zhe na gnyis kyi phyir dang slad du ni gtan tshigs sam, rgyu mtshan yin zhing skad dod aa tha zhes par 'dra yang, snga ma ni ston pa'i gsungs te zhe sa med la, phyi ma rab 'byor gyi gsung ni zhe sar bsgyur ba'o
snga ma.english: There are a number of terms in the Tibetan translation of the root text which we have been referring to here in expressions like "Why is it so?"—these are the Tibetan terms chiy chir she na and chiy ledu she na. The Tibetan words chir and ledu contained in these terms are both meant to refer to a reason—a reason "why" or "because of which" something is true. Now it's true that the original Sanskrit for both of these terms is the same—atha [spelled simply atha]—but the Tibetan translators used the former of the two Tibetan words when the Teacher was speaking (since it is not an honorific form, one used when speaking to a person who is higher) and the latter when Subhuti was speaking (since it is an honorific form, as he is addressing Lord Buddha).

snga ma.acip: CHOS RNAMS DON DAM DPYOD BYED KYI RIGS PAS DPYAD MI BZOD CING, 'PHAGS PA'I MNYAM GZHAG GI GZIGS NGOR GNYIS SNANG GI SPROS PA THAMS CAD NYE BAR ZHI BAS DE'I NGOR SPROS BCAS KYI TSUL DU BRJOD MI NUS PA NI SNGA MA LAS KYANG ZAB STE, SMRA BSAM BRJOD MED SHES RAB PHA ROL PHYIN, ,ZHES GSUNGS PA LTAR RO,,
snga ma.wylie: chos rnams don dam dpyod byed kyi rigs pas dpyad mi bzod cing, 'phags pa'i mnyam gzhag gi gzigs ngor gnyis snang gi spros pa thams cad nye bar zhi bas de'i ngor spros bcas kyi tshul du brjod mi nus pa ni snga ma las kyang zab ste, smra bsam brjod med shes rab pha rol phyin, ,zhes gsungs pa ltar ro
snga ma.english: There is not a single object in the universe which can stand up under ultimate analysis; and this entire elaboration of things, where things appear one way but exist in another, fades before the vision of the deep meditation of a realized being. It is impossible then to describe the way in which this elaboration does appear to their vision; and this is a version of things' being indescribable which is still more profound than the one we explained earlier. And thus it is that it is said that "the perfection of wisdom is beyond all words, beyond all description." The nine messages

snga ma.acip: DE CI'I PHYIR ZHE NA, RAB 'BYOR, SEMS CAN DE DAG GIS TSE RABS SNGA MA'I MI DGE BA'I LAS NGAN SONG DU SKYE BAR 'GYUR BA GANG DAG BYAS PA DAG TSE 'DI NYID LA MNAR BAS, TSE RABS SNGA MA'I MI DGE BA'I LAS DE DAG 'BYANG BAR 'GYUR TE, SANGS RGYAS KYI BYANG CHUB KYANG 'THOB PAR 'GYUR BA'I PHYIR RO,,
snga ma.wylie: de ci'i phyir zhe na, rab 'byor, sems can de dag gis tshe rabs snga ma'i mi dge ba'i las ngan song du skye bar 'gyur ba gang dag byas pa dag tshe 'di nyid la mnar bas, tshe rabs snga ma'i mi dge ba'i las de dag 'byang bar 'gyur te, sangs rgyas kyi byang chub kyang 'thob par 'gyur ba'i phyir ro
snga ma.english: Why is it so? Because, o Subhuti, such beings are purifying non-virtuous karma from the entire string of their previous lives, karma that would have taken them to the three lower realms. As they purify this karma, it causes them to suffer here in this life. As such they will succeed in cleaning away the karma of these non-virtuous deeds of their previous lifetimes, and they will as well achieve the enlightenment of a Buddha.

snga ma.acip: GANG GIS SHES RAB KYI PHA ROL TU PHYIN PA 'DI LAS THA NA TSIG BZHI PA'I TSIGS SU BCAD PA TZAM BZUNG NAS GZHAN DAG LA YANG BSTAN NA, RAB 'BYOR, BSOD NAMS KYI PHUNG PO 'DI LA BSOD NAMS KYI PHUNG PO SNGA MA DES BRGYA'I CHAR YANG MI PHOD PA NAS RGYU'I BAR DU YANG NYE BAR MI BZOD DO,,
snga ma.wylie: gang gis shes rab kyi pha rol tu phyin pa 'di las tha na tshig bzhi pa'i tshigs su bcad pa tsam bzung nas gzhan dag la yang bstan na, rab 'byor, bsod nams kyi phung po 'di la bsod nams kyi phung po snga ma des brgya'i char yang mi phod pa nas rgyu'i bar du yang nye bar mi bzod do
snga ma.english: Suppose that someone else were to take up, and teach to others, even so little as a single verse of four lines from this perfection of wisdom. I tell you, o Subhuti, that the mountain of merit created by the first person would not come to even a hundredth part of the mountain of merit created by the second; it would not come to any of the parts we spoke of before, all the way up to saying that there would be no reason to attempt any comparison between the two.

snga ma.english: Or perhaps a third objection: "I can admit that, in lifetimes that have already passed, then every living being may have been my mother.  But what's past is past--and so it's wrong to say that they are mothers of mine."

snga ma.acip: TSE RABS SNGA MA'I MA DANG TSE 'DI'I MA GNYIS KYANG MA YIN PA LA YANG KHYAD PAR MED, DRIN GYIS BSKYANGS PA LA YANG KHYAD PAR MED PAS SEMS CAN THAMS CAD BDAG GI MA CIS KYANG YIN SNYAM DU BSAM,
snga ma.wylie: tshe rabs snga ma'i ma dang tshe 'di'i ma gnyis kyang ma yin pa la yang khyad par med, drin gyis bskyangs pa la yang khyad par med pas sems can thams cad bdag gi ma cis kyang yin snyam du bsam
snga ma.english: Nor, you see, is there any difference then between all those who have been your mother throughout the entire string of your past lives and the person who is your mother in this present life.  They are all equally your mother, and equally have they all loved and taken care of you.  And so the simple, undeniable fact is that every single living being is my own mother. [Conclude the meditation as before, and in between sessions do things like reviewing this subject in scripture.] * * * What Think You? In those days he composed a great many songs of his spiritual life.  Here is one of them.

snga ma.acip: DE YANG BLO PHYI MA DE SHUGS CHES NA BLO SNGA MA DE YAL NAS STONG SANG ZHIG MA GTOGS GANG YANG MI YONG BAS SHES PA BYINGS NGA'O SNYAM PA'I BLO DE'I NGO BOR BRENG CHAGS SU BSKYED NAS, SHES PA'I CHA SHAS PHRA MO ZHIG GIS BRTAG DGOS LA,

snga ma.english: Now it may happen that the second part of the mind may get too strong: and then the first part of it will just disappear into thin air.  If this happens you won't get anywhere, just some sensation of something lost.  It's crucial therefore that you maintain this little side section of you mind to observe what's going on, even in the face of that constant stream of the part of your mind which is thinking me, me, at its deepest levels.

snga ma.acip: (ZHES BRJOD CING, BGEGS LA 'BIGS PA'I BSAM PAS PHYOGS BZHI STENG 'OG GNYIS TE DRUG TU MDA' 'PHANG ZHING DE'I TSE SLOB DPON GYIS SNGAGS SNGA MA BRJOD PAR BSAM,)

snga ma.english: (Thinking that they are striking the demons that keep you from your spiritual goals, shoot then arrows, six times: in the four directions, and up and down as well.  Think that, as you shoot them, your Master is chanting the first of the two mantras above.)
