snga ma.acip: RTZA LTUNG DE LA KUN DKRIS CHEN PO'I CHOS RNAMS TSANG BA DGOS PAS NA RTZA LTUNG GZHAN LA'ANG RIGS PA MTSUNGS SO, ,DE LA YANG DANG YANG DU ZHES PA NI RGYUN MA CHAD PA'I DON TE SNGA MA SPYAD NAS DA DUNG SPYOD 'DOD MA LOG PA'O, ,DES KYANG DGA' BAR BYED PA NI BYA BA DES SEMS LA RANGS PA 'THOB PA'O, ,'GYOD PAR MI BYED PA NI YON TAN DU LTA BA ZHES GSUNGS PA'I DON NYES DMIGS SU MI LTA BA'O, ,PHYIR 'CHOS PAR MI BYED PA NI RANG LA LTOS PA'I NGO TSA SHES PA DANG GZHAN LA LTOS PA'I KHREL YOD KYIS NYES PA DE DANG DE DAG LA 'DZEM PA MED PA'O,
snga ma.wylie: rtsa ltung de la kun dkris chen po'i chos rnams tshang ba dgos pas na rtsa ltung gzhan la'ang rigs pa mtshungs so, ,de la yang dang yang du zhes pa ni rgyun ma chad pa'i don te snga ma spyad nas da dung spyod 'dod ma log pa'o, ,des kyang dga' bar byed pa ni bya ba des sems la rangs pa 'thob pa'o, ,'gyod par mi byed pa ni yon tan du lta ba zhes gsungs pa'i don nyes dmigs su mi lta ba'o, ,phyir 'chos par mi byed pa ni rang la ltos pa'i ngo tsha shes pa dang gzhan la ltos pa'i khrel yod kyis nyes pa de dang de dag la 'dzem pa med pa'o
snga ma.english: The conditions of the various "greater chains" must be present for us to commit this particular root downfall, of disparaging our Master; as such, this same rule follows for all the other root downfalls as well.  When they say "doing it over and over again," it means committing this action constantly, having done it in the past and having no desire to stop doing it again now and later. The person should as well do it "with a sense of satisfaction," which refers to the person feeling glad for having committed the action.  "Without any feeling of regret" means "seeing it as a virtue," which itself means failing to see that the action was a mistake.  "Making no attempt to repair the damage" means failing to avoid doing the particular negative act, as one possesses no sense of shame relative to oneself, and no sense of consideration for how it will cause others to feel. ***

snga ma.acip: ,BYA BA CI ZHIG BYAS PAS LTUNG BAR 'GYUR BA NI, DE LA SMOD PAR BYED NA'O, ,SMOD LUGS NI SNGA MA LA SKYON GDAGS 'DOD KYI KUN SLONG GIS SKYON GANG YANG RUNG BA BRJOD PA YIN LA, PHYI MA LA NI SKYON GDAGS 'DOD KYI KUN SLONG GIS BUD MED KYI RTEN SPYI LA SMOD TSIG TU 'GRO BA'I SKYON BRJOD BYAS PA STE, DE YANG BUD MED KYI GO BA DGOS PAR BDUD RTZI ZLA BA DANG LAKshAMI KA RAS BSHAD PA NI PHYI MA LA DGOS SAM SNYAM MO,
snga ma.wylie: bya ba ci zhig byas pas ltung bar 'gyur ba ni, de la smod par byed na'o, ,smod lugs ni snga ma la skyon gdags 'dod kyi kun slong gis skyon gang yang rung ba brjod pa yin la, phyi ma la ni skyon gdags 'dod kyi kun slong gis bud med kyi rten spyi la smod tshig tu 'gro ba'i skyon brjod byas pa ste, de yang bud med kyi go ba dgos par bdud rtsi zla ba dang lakShami ka ras bshad pa ni phyi ma la dgos sam snyam mo
snga ma.english: What kind of action do we have to do to commit this root downfall?  We commit it "when we disparage Them."  The way in which we disparage Them, in the former case [where the woman is a deity], is when we express any criticism of them, with a motivation of wanting to say something critical.  We disparage Them in the latter case [where she is a human woman] when we express any kind of criticism in the form of disparaging the female sex in general--again out of a motivation of wanting to say something critical. The Nectar Moon, and Lakshmikara as well, state here that the woman involved must also hear and understand what we are saying; but it would seem to me that this is required only in the latter case. ***

snga ma.acip: 'DIR DAM TSIG RDO RJES KU RU KU L+LE LA SOGS PA DANG RANG GI PHYAG RGYA'I BUD MED LA SMAD PA LA RTZA LTUNG DANG BUD MED GZHAN LA SHAN 'DRA RU MDZAD CING 'DUS PA'I RGYAN LA SOGS PA 'GA' ZHIG LAS KYANG RANG GI RIG MA KHYAD PAR CAN LA SMAD PA LA BSHAD PA SNANG NA'ANG RANG GI LUGS NI RANG GI PHYAG RGYA LTA BU LA LCI BA'I KHYAD PAR YOD MOD KYANG RTZA LTUNG DU 'GRO BA'I MTSAMS SNGA MA LTAR RO,
snga ma.wylie: 'dir dam tshig rdo rjes ku ru ku l+le la sogs pa dang rang gi phyag rgya'i bud med la smad pa la rtsa ltung dang bud med gzhan la shan 'dra ru mdzad cing 'dus pa'i rgyan la sogs pa 'ga' zhig las kyang rang gi rig ma khyad par can la smad pa la bshad pa snang na'ang rang gi lugs ni rang gi phyag rgya lta bu la lci ba'i khyad par yod mod kyang rtsa ltung du 'gro ba'i mtshams snga ma ltar ro
snga ma.english: On this particular point, Damtsik Dorje [not the one who is the author of the final readings of this course] says that we commit this root downfall only when we disparage women who are a divine being like Kurukulle, or our own spiritual partner.  He then says that disparaging other women is only an approximation of this downfall. We also see explanations in works such as the Jewel of the Collection which say that this root downfall refers to disparaging that extraordinary being, our own Woman of Knowledge. Nonetheless, our own final position is that--although there is quite certainly a question of a much graver karma in the case where we disparage a woman such as our own spiritual partner--one has nonetheless crossed the line in this downfall when they have acted as we've already described it above. ***

snga ma.acip: SLOB DPON NI RANG GI BLA MA LA BYED PA DANG SLOB DPON GYI DBANG BSKUR BA LA BYED PA GNYIS 'GREL PAR GSUNGS KYANG SNGA MA SDOM PA BSGRAG PA DANG MTHUN NO,
snga ma.wylie: slob dpon ni rang gi bla ma la byed pa dang slob dpon gyi dbang bskur ba la byed pa gnyis 'grel par gsungs kyang snga ma sdom pa bsgrag pa dang mthun no
snga ma.english: The word "Master" here has been applied in the commentary to both the person who is serving as our own Lama, and to the one who has granted us the Empowerment of the Master.  It is the former sense though which is consistent with the term in the section of the initiation where the vows are proclaimed.

snga ma.acip: 'DI BRGYAD DAM TSIG CES SOGS RKANG PA GSUM NI, DE YANG SNGA MA RNAMS KYI DON MDOR HRIL GYIS SGRIL NA, SNGAR BSHAD PA LTAR GYI G-YON PA'I KUN SPYOD THAMS CAD BYED PA DANG , RGYUD 'DIR DBANG BSKUR BA'I SGRUB PA PO DANG SLOB DPON LA MI BRNYAS SHING CI NUS KYIS MCHOD PA RNAMS NI DAM TSIG DANG PO DANG ,
snga ma.wylie: 'di brgyad dam tshig ces sogs rkang pa gsum ni, de yang snga ma rnams kyi don mdor hril gyis sgril na, sngar bshad pa ltar gyi g-yon pa'i kun spyod thams cad byed pa dang , rgyud 'dir dbang bskur ba'i sgrub pa po dang slob dpon la mi brnyas shing ci nus kyis mchod pa rnams ni dam tshig dang po dang
snga ma.english: We turn next to the three lines [in the Tibetan] that include "This...the eight pledges."  Now we could summarize the points given above in the following way.  The first pledge is that we should, as explained earlier on, observe all the various forms of leftways behavior.  We should never berate those practitioners who have been empowered to follow this secret teachings, nor our Master, and we should further make offerings to them, to the best of our ability.

The first pledge is that we should, as explained earlier on, observe all the various forms of leftways behavior.  We should never berate those practitioners who have been empowered to follow this secret teachings, nor our Master, and we should further make offerings to them, to the best of our ability."}

snga ma.acip: DE LA DAM TSIG BRGYAD KYI GRANGS DANG NGOS 'DZIN BYED LUGS SNGA MA RNAMS KYI BZHED TSUL MANG DU YOD LA, YID RTON PA'I BSHAD PA LA BRTEN NAS NGES SHES MA DRANGS NA BSRUNGS KYANG 'BRAS BU CHUNG BAS,
snga ma.wylie: de la dam tshig brgyad kyi grangs dang ngos 'dzin byed lugs snga ma rnams kyi bzhed tshul mang du yod la, yid rton pa'i bshad pa la brten nas nges shes ma drangs na bsrungs kyang 'bras bu chung bas
snga ma.english: Now holy beings of the past have expressed a wide variety of positions on the exact way in which the eight pledges are divided, and how they are described.  If though you attempt to keep these pledges without a clear understanding of them derived from relying upon a credible source, the results you gain will be minimal. [Translator's note: The section beginning from here, up to the next translator's note below, is taken almost verbatim from Je Tsongkapa's "Cow that Produces Every Wish," being an Extensive Explanation of the Practice of Realization for the Secret Teaching of the Conqueror, the Glorious Sphere of Highest Bliss (Heruka), found at S5320.]

snga ma.acip: ,BDUN DANG BCU DRUG GI KHYAD PAR NI BI BH'U T'IS MA BSGOMS GYUR KYANG ZHES BSHAD PA LTAR LAM SGOM PA'I BRTZON PA DANG LDAN MI LDAN YIN TE SNGA MA LA GANG YANG SGOM PA DANG LDAN ZHES GSUNGS PAS SO,
snga ma.wylie: bdun dang bcu drug gi khyad par ni bi bhU tIs ma bsgoms gyur kyang zhes bshad pa ltar lam sgom pa'i brtson pa dang ldan mi ldan yin te snga ma la gang yang sgom pa dang ldan zhes gsungs pas so
snga ma.english: What decides whether it's within sixteen lives or within seven?  This is what Vibhuti Chandra is saying when he says that we achieve the goal within sixteen lifetimes "even without the other practices"--the point is that sixteen applies to a case where a person does not exert themselves in the practice of the path, whereas the seven is a reference to a person who does have some level of practice. ***

snga ma.acip: DE GNYIS RANG RANG GI MTSAN MED KYI RNAL 'BYOR DU GYUR PA'I STONG NYID RTOGS PA'I LHAG MTHONG NAS STONG NYID MNGON SUM DU MA RTOGS TSUN CHAD KYI LAM RNAMS DE GNYIS RANG RANG GI SBYOR LAM YIN PA SOGS THAMS CAD SNGA MA'I RIGS 'GRE SBYAR NAS SHES PAR BYA'O,,
snga ma.wylie: de gnyis rang rang gi mtshan med kyi rnal 'byor du gyur pa'i stong nyid rtogs pa'i lhag mthong nas stong nyid mngon sum du ma rtogs tshun chad kyi lam rnams de gnyis rang rang gi sbyor lam yin pa sogs thams cad snga ma'i rigs 'gre sbyar nas shes par bya'o
snga ma.english: Consider next all the paths that occur within the period that begins with attaining extraordinary insight which perceives emptiness, and which represents a deep practice where there are no longer any signs, for the particular one of the two classes here; on up to the point where we are just about to see emptiness directly.  These paths together constitute the path of preparation for whichever one of the two classes here we are talking about. These and all the rest of the presentation for these two classes continues then to follow the same pattern as we had for the previous class.

snga ma.acip: 'O NA BSKYED RIM LA SLOB PA DES RDZOGS RIM BZHIN DU DMIGS SKOR SNGA MA BSGOMS PAS BRTAN PA THOB PA NA PHYI MA LA 'PHO BA YIN NAM, 'ON TE SGRUB THABS KYI MGO MJUG THAMS CAD THUN GCIG LA SGOM PA YIN SNYAM NA,
snga ma.wylie: 'o na bskyed rim la slob pa des rdzogs rim bzhin du dmigs skor snga ma bsgoms pas brtan pa thob pa na phyi ma la 'pho ba yin nam, 'on te sgrub thabs kyi mgo mjug thams cad thun gcig la sgom pa yin snyam na
snga ma.english: The following question might come up in your mind: When you talk about training oneself in the stage of creation, is it similar to the same process in the stage of completion, where we move up to each successive practice once we have established ourselves firmly in the previous one?  Or is it rather that, in a single session, we go from the beginning to the end of our practice to reach the Angel?

Or is it rather that, in a single session, we go from the beginning to the end of our practice to reach the Angel?"}

snga ma.acip: DE LTAR BSGOM PA'I DGOS PA YOD DE, SROG RTZOL SNGA MA GNYIS KYIS SNYING GAR RLUNG SDUD MA NUS PA SDUD PAR BYED LA, RDZAS THIG BSGOM PA 'DIS SNYING GAR RLUNG BSDUS PA'I BOGS 'DON DU 'GRO BA'I PHYIR RO,
snga ma.wylie: de ltar bsgom pa'i dgos pa yod de, srog rtsol snga ma gnyis kyis snying gar rlung sdud ma nus pa sdud par byed la, rdzas thig bsgom pa 'dis snying gar rlung bsdus pa'i bogs 'don du 'gro ba'i phyir ro
snga ma.english: Now there is a certain point to doing the practices we've described here.  The two earlier forms of practice for mastering the life-wind help us gather the winds at the heart--something we were unable to do before.  And the meditation on a drop of substance acts as a powerful aid in getting the winds to gather at the heart.

And the meditation on a drop of substance acts as a powerful aid in getting the winds to gather at the heart."}

snga ma.acip: THIM PA'I RTAGS SA CHU ME RLUNG BZHI SNGA MA PHYI MAR THIM PA NA RIM BZHIN SMIG RGYU DU BA MKHA' SNANG ME KHYER LTA BU'I SNANG BA 'CHAR, RLUNG SNANG BA LA THIM PAR BRTZAMS PA NA MAR ME 'BAR BA LTA BU'I SNANG BA 'CHAR,
snga ma.wylie: thim pa'i rtags sa chu me rlung bzhi snga ma phyi mar thim pa na rim bzhin smig rgyu du ba mkha' snang me khyer lta bu'i snang ba 'char, rlung snang ba la thim par brtsams pa na mar me 'bar ba lta bu'i snang ba 'char
snga ma.english: Here are the signs that the winds are dissolving within.  As each preceding one of the four elements--of earth, water, fire, and wind--dissolves into each succeeding one, then we experience visions that resemble, respectively, a mirage; smoke appearing in the sky; and fireflies.  When the element of wind starts to dissolve into the stage called "light," then we experience a vision which resembles a burning butter lamp.

As each preceding one of the four elements--of earth, water, fire, and wind--dissolves into each succeeding one, then we experience visions that resemble, respectively, a mirage; smoke appearing in the sky; and fireflies. snga ma.acip: RTAGS 'DI DAG SNGA MA LAS PHYI MA GSAL DU SONG PA'I DPE YIN ZHES PA DANG , RTAGS CAN GYI SHES PA BRTAN G-YO'I TSAD YIN ZHES PA DANG , SMIG RGYU SOGS DANG 'DRA BA'I SNANG BA 'CHAR BA YIN ZHES PA'I BZHED PA GSUM 'BYUNG BA LAS PHYI MA LEGS PAR GSUNGS SO,,
snga ma.wylie: rtags 'di dag snga ma las phyi ma gsal du song pa'i dpe yin zhes pa dang , rtags can gyi shes pa brtan g-yo'i tshad yin zhes pa dang , smig rgyu sogs dang 'dra ba'i snang ba 'char ba yin zhes pa'i bzhed pa gsum 'byung ba las phyi ma legs par gsungs so
snga ma.english: There are three different positions on these various signs.  Some say that the objects mentioned are only illustrations that represent an increasingly greater brightness and clarity as we move from one step to the next.  Others say that they are meant to represent the relative degree of stability, or lack of distraction, to the states of mind in which the signs are appearing.  Still others say that we actually experience a vision which is similar to the mirage and the rest.  The last of these is stated to be the best.

snga ma.acip: RANG BZHIN SNANG BA LA THIM PA YANG RANG BZHIN GYI RTOG PAS YUL 'DZIN BA'I NUS PA LOG PA'O, ,STONG PA BZHI SNGA MA PHYI MAR THIM PA'ANG DES SHES PAR BYA'O,,
snga ma.wylie: rang bzhin snang ba la thim pa yang rang bzhin gyi rtog pas yul 'dzin ba'i nus pa log pa'o, ,stong pa bzhi snga ma phyi mar thim pa'ang des shes par bya'o
snga ma.english: So too when we say that the "nature" has dissolved into the light, what we mean is that the ability of the discursive thought which sees a nature in things to hold its object has collapsed.  From this you can understand as well the process by which each preceding form of the four types of emptiness dissolves into each succeeding form.

From this you can understand as well the process by which each preceding form of the four types of emptiness dissolves into each succeeding form."}

snga ma.acip: MAS BRTAN LAS MA LANGS PA'I YAS BABS KYI DGA' GZHI NI SNGA MA'I MAS BRTAN LAS BDE BA CHE ZHING , BZHI KA LHAN SKYES SU 'JOG DGOS PA DANG , MAS BRTAN LAS LANGS PA'I RJES SU SKYES PA'I YAS BABS KYI DGA' BZHI NI SNGA MA LAS BDE BA CHE BA DANG BZHI KA LHAN SKYES YIN PA'I NGES PA MED PAR GSUNGS LA,
snga ma.wylie: mas brtan las ma langs pa'i yas babs kyi dga' gzhi ni snga ma'i mas brtan las bde ba che zhing , bzhi ka lhan skyes su 'jog dgos pa dang , mas brtan las langs pa'i rjes su skyes pa'i yas babs kyi dga' bzhi ni snga ma las bde ba che ba dang bzhi ka lhan skyes yin pa'i nges pa med par gsungs la
snga ma.english: It is stated that the four forms of bliss associated with the descent of the element from the top--the ones that occur after one has come out of the filling from the bottom--are more blissful than those of this previous filling from the bottom; all four would have to be considered simultaneous bliss.  And the four forms of bliss which come during the descent from the top after one has already come out of meditation on the filling from the bottom are more blissful than the previous one, although there it is no certainty that all four will be simultaneous bliss. [Translator's note: The DGA' GZHI in all manuscripts available to us is a miscarving for DGA" BZHI; see S5313, f. 3b.  The reference here is also corrupted in all available manuscripts; it should read (as per the same text and folio), MAS BRTAN LAS LANGS PA'I YAS BABS KYI BZHI NI, SNGA MA'I MAS BRTAN LAS BDE BA CHE ZHING,]

snga ma.acip: MAS BRTAN GYI LHAN SKYES KYI DUS SU BDE STONG SBYAR TE BSGOMS STOBS KYIS, RLUNG SNGA MA MA LANGS PA'I STENG DU SNGAR MA BSDUS PA'I KHYAB BYED KYI RLUNG RAGS PA 'GA' ZHIG 'DUS NAS ZHUGS GNAS THIM GSUM BYED PA DANG , YAS BABS DANG MAS BRTAN GYI DGA' BZHI 'DREN PA YOD PAR GSUNGS PA'I PHYIR,
snga ma.wylie: mas brtan gyi lhan skyes kyi dus su bde stong sbyar te bsgoms stobs kyis, rlung snga ma ma langs pa'i steng du sngar ma bsdus pa'i khyab byed kyi rlung rags pa 'ga' zhig 'dus nas zhugs gnas thim gsum byed pa dang , yas babs dang mas brtan gyi dga' bzhi 'dren pa yod par gsungs pa'i phyir
snga ma.english: It is stated, in addition, that there is a case where we can use the power of our practice--joining bliss and voidness--during the point of simultaneous bliss as the element fills from the bottom to gather in some number of gross forms of the pervasive wind which we have not already gathered in.  These are placed in on top of the previous winds, which are still not rising.  We then bring the winds to enter, stay, and dissolve--and this brings on the four forms of bliss in the descent from the top and the filling from the bottom.

snga ma.acip: KHA CIG ,SGYU LUS THOG MAR 'GRUB PA'I TSE LUS RAGS PA LAS PHYI ROL DU LDANG DGOS TE, GSAL SGRON LAS, ZUNG 'JUG GI SKU 'DI THOG MAR 'GRUB NA LUS SNGA MA LAS GO SA LOGS SU GNAS PA'I TSUL GYIS 'GRUB LA, ZHES DANG ,
snga ma.wylie: kha cig ,sgyu lus thog mar 'grub pa'i tshe lus rags pa las phyi rol du ldang dgos te, gsal sgron las, zung 'jug gi sku 'di thog mar 'grub na lus snga ma las go sa logs su gnas pa'i tshul gyis 'grub la, zhes dang
snga ma.english: Someone else might make the following claim: It must be the case that--when we first attain the body of illusion--it rises outside of the gross body.  This is true because the Lantern states, When we first attain the precious body of the combination of the two, we achieve it in a way where it occupies a space which is discrete from that of the previous body.

This is true because the Lantern states, When we first attain the precious body of the combination of the two, we achieve it in a way where it occupies a space which is discrete from that of the previous body."}

snga ma.acip: LONGS SKU LUS SNGA MA LAS GO SA LOGS SU DANG POR 'GRUB PA DANG , DE NAS LUS SNGA MA LA ZHUGS PA'I SPRUL SKU 'DZIN TSUL YANG SNGAR BSHAD PA BZHIN DU SHES PAR BYA STE, ZHES GSUNGS PA'I PHYIR DANG , DAG MA DAG GI SGYU LUS 'GRUB TSUL 'DRA BAR BSHAD PA'I PHYIR ZHES ZER,
snga ma.wylie: longs sku lus snga ma las go sa logs su dang por 'grub pa dang , de nas lus snga ma la zhugs pa'i sprul sku 'dzin tshul yang sngar bshad pa bzhin du shes par bya ste, zhes gsungs pa'i phyir dang , dag ma dag gi sgyu lus 'grub tshul 'dra bar bshad pa'i phyir zhes zer
snga ma.english: It also says-- The paradise body is at first attained in a place which is discrete from that of the previous body.  It should be understood that--as we described above--we then go on to re-enter this previous body, in the way that someone would take on a body of emanation. And after all, it is stated that the ways in which we attain the pure body of illusion and the impure body of illusion are the same.

snga ma.acip: DE'I RGYU MTSAN YANG ZUNG 'JUG THOB TSE LUS PHRA RAGS GNYIS SNGA MA'I LAS KYIS 'PHANGS PA'I RTEN DANG BRTEN PA'I 'BREL BA BSGOMS STOBS KYIS CHAD PAS, LUS RAGS PA GTAN DU SPANGS TE GNAS PAR 'DOD NA GNAS PAR NUS LA, GDUL BYA'I DON DU 'DZIN PAR 'DOD NA YANG JI LTAR 'DOD PA LTAR NUS PA YIN NO,,
snga ma.wylie: de'i rgyu mtshan yang zung 'jug thob tshe lus phra rags gnyis snga ma'i las kyis 'phangs pa'i rten dang brten pa'i 'brel ba bsgoms stobs kyis chad pas, lus rags pa gtan du spangs te gnas par 'dod na gnas par nus la, gdul bya'i don du 'dzin par 'dod na yang ji ltar 'dod pa ltar nus pa yin no
snga ma.english: Now the reason for this is the following.  Consider how--when we attain the combination of the two--the power of our practice puts an end to the connection between the subtle and gross bodies: this connection of one thing providing the basis and the other thing relying upon this basis, a connection which has been projected into this life by the deeds we did in our past lives.  If one wishes at this point to abandon the gross body forever and remain only in the new, then they are capable of doing so; and if instead they decide to hold onto this body, for the sake of their disciples, then they can are also capable of doing that--whichever they desire.

snga ma.acip: BAR DOR 'TSANG RGYA BA'I SGYU LUS NI SNGA MA'I LAS KYI 'PHEN PA ZAD PA'I STOBS KYIS LUS RAGS PA DANG RTEN DANG BRTEN PA'I 'BREL BA CHAD PAS LUS RAGS PA GTAN DU 'DOR NUS KYANG , TSE 'DIR TSANG RGYA BA'I MA DAG PA'I SGYU LUS NI LUS RAGS PA DANG RTEN DANG BRTEN PA'I 'BREL BA RAGS PA CHAD KYANG PHRA BA MA CHAD PAR GSUNGS PAS, DON GYI 'OD GSAL MA SKYES BAR DU SNGA MA'I LUS RAGS PA GTAN DU 'DOR MI NUS PA YIN NO,,
snga ma.wylie: bar dor 'tshang rgya ba'i sgyu lus ni snga ma'i las kyi 'phen pa zad pa'i stobs kyis lus rags pa dang rten dang brten pa'i 'brel ba chad pas lus rags pa gtan du 'dor nus kyang , tshe 'dir tshang rgya ba'i ma dag pa'i sgyu lus ni lus rags pa dang rten dang brten pa'i 'brel ba rags pa chad kyang phra ba ma chad par gsungs pas, don gyi 'od gsal ma skyes bar du snga ma'i lus rags pa gtan du 'dor mi nus pa yin no
snga ma.english: Now as for the body of illusion where we reach enlightenment in the state inbetween, the wearing out of the past karma which was projecting things causes the relationship of a basis and something relying upon this basis to end, with respect to the gross body.  We are therefore able at this point to discard, forever, the gross body.  It is however stated about the impure body of illusion in a case where we become enlightened in this same lifetime that--even though the gross form of this relationship of a basis and something which relies on it, with reference to the gross body, may come to an end--the subtle form of this relationship is not then ended.  As such, we are incapable of discarding our previous gross body completely until such time as we have given birth to the actual clear light.

snga ma.acip: 'O NA RIN CHEN LTA BU'I GDUL BYAS TSE GCIG LUS GCIG LA 'TSANG RGYA BA MED PAR THAL, ZUNG 'JUG THOB TSE SNGA MA'I LUS RAGS PA BRJE DGOS PA'I PHYIR ZER NA MA KHYAB STE, LUS RAGS PA BRJE BA LA 'DOR BAS MA KHYAB PA'I PHYIR,
snga ma.wylie: 'o na rin chen lta bu'i gdul byas tshe gcig lus gcig la 'tshang rgya ba med par thal, zung 'jug thob tshe snga ma'i lus rags pa brje dgos pa'i phyir zer na ma khyab ste, lus rags pa brje ba la 'dor bas ma khyab pa'i phyir
snga ma.english: One might respond with the following claim-- Well if that's true, then there can't be any case where a disciple who is like a jewel reaches enlightenment "in a single life, in a single body."  Because you've just said that--when a person attains the combination of the two--then they must do so by changing the gross body of their previous existence. Our reply is that--although the latter statement is correct--it doesn't necessitate the former.  And this is so because changing the gross body doesn't necessarily mean that we discard it.

snga ma.acip: 'DI'I 'OD GSAL DANG NYER THOB LA PHRA RAGS KYI KHYAD PAR YOD DE, SNGA MA NI GNYUG SEMS DANG , PHYI MA NI DE LA LTOS NA CUNG ZAD RAGS PA YIN PA'I PHYIR DANG , SNANG MCHED THOB GSUM GANG RUNG LA GNYUG SEMS MA YIN PAS KHYAB PA'I PHYIR DANG , GNYUG SEMS GNYUG SEMS MA YIN PAR 'GYUR NA LHAN SKYES KYI SEMS SU BSHAD DU MI RUNG BAR 'GYUR BA'I PHYIR ZHES ZER NA GANG LTAR KHAS LEN PA NI DPYAD PAR BYA'O,,
snga ma.wylie: 'di'i 'od gsal dang nyer thob la phra rags kyi khyad par yod de, snga ma ni gnyug sems dang , phyi ma ni de la ltos na cung zad rags pa yin pa'i phyir dang , snang mched thob gsum gang rung la gnyug sems ma yin pas khyab pa'i phyir dang , gnyug sems gnyug sems ma yin par 'gyur na lhan skyes kyi sems su bshad du mi rung bar 'gyur ba'i phyir zhes zer na gang ltar khas len pa ni dpyad par bya'o
snga ma.english: It is moreover true that there is a difference in subtlety between the clear light and the stage of attainment here--because the former is a primordial form of mind, whereas the latter is, compared to it, slightly more gross.  And the fact is that--if something is any one of the three stages of light, proliferation, and attainment--then it cannot be a primordial state of mind.  And if something which were a primordial state of mind were to become something which were not a primordial state of mind, then we could never speak of it as an inborn state of mind. Which position we're going to accept here is something that merits further examination.

snga ma.english: Tilopa gently caresses His disciple's broken body, healing it back to the way it was before.  And then He says to him, "This then is the wishing jewel which is shared: the instructions for you to actually travel to the paradise of Uddiyana, and reach there the Angels of Wisdom." And so He grants Naropa, in their entirety, secret teachings such as the practice for reaching the enlightened partner named the Lady of the Simultaneous.  These He gives in three parts: the Teaching on the Immutable Reality, which is like the king; the Rites of the Three Families, which is like the minister; and the Advices on the Holy Deeds of Joining, which is like the people of the kingdom. snga ma.english: He lays His holy hand upon His disciple, gently, and restores his body.  And then He grants Naropa the Teaching on the Bardo.

snga ma.acip: SPYOD RGYUD, RNAL 'BYOR RGYUD, RNAL 'BYOR BLA NA MED PA'I RGYUD DE RGYUD SDE BZHI LAS, SNGA MA GSUM GYI LAM LA BRTEN NAS TSE GCIG LA SANGS RGYAS THOB PA YOD KYANG, SNYIGS DUS KYI TSE THUNG GCIG LA SANGS RGYAS THOB PA MED, RNAL 'BYOR BLA MED KYI LAM LA BRTEN NA MCHOG GI GO 'PHANG SNYIGS DUS KYI TSE THUNG GCIG LA 'THOB PAR NUS PHYIR MCHOG TU GYUR PA BLA MED KYI RGYUD YIN,
snga ma.wylie: spyod rgyud, rnal 'byor rgyud, rnal 'byor bla na med pa'i rgyud de rgyud sde bzhi las, snga ma gsum gyi lam la brten nas tshe gcig la sangs rgyas thob pa yod kyang, snyigs dus kyi tshe thung gcig la sangs rgyas thob pa med, rnal 'byor bla med kyi lam la brten na mchog gi go 'phang snyigs dus kyi tshe thung gcig la 'thob par nus phyir mchog tu gyur pa bla med kyi rgyud yin
snga ma.english: These four groups of the secret teachings are those known as the secret teachings of action, of activity, of practice, and of unsurpassed practice.  It is possible to achieve Buddhahood in one life by using the paths of the first three groups, but not in one life of the kind we have nowadays, for we are in the era of decline, and our lives are too short.  You can however achieve the ultimate goal in a short life like this if you use the path of unsurpassed practice, and thus it is truly unsurpassed, the highest of secret teachings.

snga ma.acip: YAB BKA' BDE MCHOG LA RTZA BSHAD SBYAR NAS BSHAD PA'I GRUB CHEN GYI LUGS MI 'DRA BA MANG YANG GTZO CHE ZHING DAR KHYAB CHE BA NI KUN SPYOD L'U AI'I SKOR, RTZA RGYUD NAG PO'I SKOR, ZAB DON DRIL BU'I SKOR TE L'U NAG DRIL GSUM GYIS BKRAL BA RNAMS YIN, DRIL BU'I SKOR NI, GRUB CHEN DRIL BU PA'I LUGS KYI BDE MCHOG LUS DKYIL DANG BCAS PA STE SNGA MA GNYIS LAS 'DI ZA BA,
snga ma.wylie: yab bka' bde mchog la rtsa bshad sbyar nas bshad pa'i grub chen gyi lugs mi 'dra ba mang yang gtso che zhing dar khyab che ba ni kun spyod lU ai'i skor, rtsa rgyud nag po'i skor, zab don dril bu'i skor te lU nag dril gsum gyis bkral ba rnams yin, dril bu'i skor ni, grub chen dril bu pa'i lugs kyi bde mchog lus dkyil dang bcas pa ste snga ma gnyis las 'di za ba
snga ma.english: There are a great number of different systems by which accomplished saints of the past have given explanations of the Word of the Man in the secret teachings of Highest Bliss, using both the root texts and their commentaries.  But those that are the chief ones, and which have found the most widespread following, are the explanations by the Three: by Luyipa, Kirshnapada, and Ghantapada.  These explanations are known by the names of The Activities--the Collection of Luyipa; The Secret Root Text--the Collection of Kirshnapada; and The Profound Meaning--the Collection of Ghantapada.  The Collection of Ghantapada consists of the practice of Highest Bliss, along with its Secret World of the Body, according to the system of the great saint Ghantapada.  This collection is even deeper than the other two mentioned.

snga ma.acip: DE LA BDUD RTZI RIL BU DGOS KYANG, RNYING LUGS KYI RTZA BRGYAD STONG SBYAR ZHES PA SHA LNGA BDUD RTZI LNGA SOGS DNGOS SU 'DRES PA'I BDUD RTZI CHOS SMAN BSRE MI RUNG ZHING, 'DI DANG DGE LDAN PA'I BDUD RTZI RIL BU LA KHYAD PAR CHE STE, DGE LUGS LA SHA DANG BDUD RTZIR AA RU RA SOGS KYIS DOD THUB SBYAR BA YIN, SNGA MAS DNGOS SU BSRES PAS RANG GI RTOGS PAS MA 'CHUN NA NYES PA RLABS CHEN 'BYUNG BA'I NYEN YOD,
snga ma.wylie: de la bdud rtsi ril bu dgos kyang, rnying lugs kyi rtsa brgyad stong sbyar zhes pa sha lnga bdud rtsi lnga sogs dngos su 'dres pa'i bdud rtsi chos sman bsre mi rung zhing, 'di dang dge ldan pa'i bdud rtsi ril bu la khyad par che ste, dge lugs la sha dang bdud rtsir aa ru ra sogs kyis dod thub sbyar ba yin, snga mas dngos su bsres pas rang gi rtogs pas ma 'chun na nyes pa rlabs chen 'byung ba'i nyen yod
snga ma.english: For this practice you will need a nectar pill; but it is improper to mix together a dharma elixir like the "Concoction of Eight Thousand Fundamental Substances" used in the Nyingma tradition, where they add in the real things: the five fleshes, five nectars, and so on. There is a very great difference between this and the nectar pill of the Virtuous Ones.  In the tradition of the Way of Virtue, we mix together cherry plum and similar ingredients to substitute for the fleshes and nectars.  With the other custom, because you have blended in the actual substances, there is a very real danger that you will commit a tremendous bad deed if your realizations are not high enough to sustain the practice.

snga ma.acip: DES NA YID SPRUL LAM, BSHAMS NA BYIN RLABS KYANG BYA DGOS LA, DE NI 'DI DANG 'BUL BYA GNYIS LAS, NGAG 'DON DU SNGA MA LTAR YOD PAS, DE BSANGS BYED KYI NANG MCHOD BYIN RLABS DGOS SHING,
snga ma.wylie: des na yid sprul lam, bshams na byin rlabs kyang bya dgos la, de ni 'di dang 'bul bya gnyis las, ngag 'don du snga ma ltar yod pas, de bsangs byed kyi nang mchod byin rlabs dgos shing
snga ma.english: As such, we must as well bless the offerings--whether we are offering them in our imagination, or actually setting them forth physically.  What we have here are both what we use to bless the offerings, and the offerings themselves; given that the recitation here is the way we noted it before, we must first then bless the inner offering which we use to clear the offerings.

What we have here are both what we use to bless the offerings, and the offerings themselves; given that the recitation here is the way we noted it before, we must first then bless the inner offering which we use to clear the offerings."}

snga ma.acip: DE LAS BYANG SEMS KYI RTZA LTUNG DANG NYES BYAS, DE LAS SNGAGS KYI RTZA LTUNG SBOM PO SOGS KYI NYES PA RNAMS SNGA MA SNGA MA LAS PHYI MA PHYI MA 'BYUNG NYE LA CHES LCI BA CHAR BZHIN DU 'BAB PAS LAS 'BRAS DANG BSDUR NA NYIN GCIG GI SDIG LTUNG YANG NGAN SONG GSUM DU SKYE BA 'BUM PHRAG RE BLANGS KYANG RDZOGS MTHA' MED PA LTAR BSAGS BZHIN PA YIN,
snga ma.wylie: de las byang sems kyi rtsa ltung dang nyes byas, de las sngags kyi rtsa ltung sbom po sogs kyi nyes pa rnams snga ma snga ma las phyi ma phyi ma 'byung nye la ches lci ba char bzhin du 'bab pas las 'bras dang bsdur na nyin gcig gi sdig ltung yang ngan song gsum du skye ba 'bum phrag re blangs kyang rdzogs mtha' med pa ltar bsags bzhin pa yin
snga ma.english: Beyond that we continually commit the root downfalls and secondary violations of the bodhisattva vows; and beyond that we continually commit the serious offenses and other root breaches against the secret vows.  The higher we go in these three sets of offenses, the more easy it is for us to commit them, and the more serious are the consequences of doing so.  These bad deeds too fall down on us in a shower.

The higher we go in these three sets of offenses, the more easy it is for us to commit them, and the more serious are the consequences of doing so.  These bad deeds too fall down on us in a shower."}

snga ma.acip: YANG, KU SU LU NI 'DU SHES GSUM PA'AM, MA BCOS LHUG PA'I DON TE, SPROS MED DANG BCOS MED KYI NGANG NAS NANG GI NYAMS LEN BZANG BA ZHIG LA BYED PAS, 'DI'ANG NANG GI YON TAN LA MA BLTOS BAR PHYI'I SPYOD LAM LA BLTOS NAS BTAGS PA YIN PAS SNGA MA DANG 'DI GNYIS KA'I 'BAB SO GCIG TU 'ONG,
snga ma.wylie: yang, ku su lu ni 'du shes gsum pa'am, ma bcos lhug pa'i don te, spros med dang bcos med kyi ngang nas nang gi nyams len bzang ba zhig la byed pas, 'di'ang nang gi yon tan la ma bltos bar phyi'i spyod lam la bltos nas btags pa yin pas snga ma dang 'di gnyis ka'i 'bab so gcig tu 'ong
snga ma.english: There is also a word kusulu, which can refer to one of those "three thought" people, who think only of eating, sleeping, and going to the bathroom.  This same term can mean unartificial, or natural.  It describes a person who is keeping up a pure practice within themself, without any artifice, without any pretense.  The word is applied then on the basis of the person's outer behavior, without regard to their inner qualities.  Thus the two words, kusali and kusulu, really amount to the same thing.

This same term can mean unartificial, or natural.  It describes a person who is keeping up a pure practice within themself, without any artifice, without any pretense. snga ma.acip: GSUM PA BLA MA BSTIM PA'I ZHAL SHES LA, DUS GSUM SANGS RGYAS ZHES SOGS KYIS GSOL BA BTAB PAS GZHAL YAS KHANG DANG BRGYUD PA'I BLA MA RNAMS KYI SENG KHRI RNAMS KYANG BSDU, BLA BRGYUD RNAMS SANGS RGYAS RDO RJE CHOS RANG GI SLOB MA RNAL 'BYOR MA LA THIM PA SOGS BLA MA SNGA MA SNGA MA RNAMS RANG RANG GI SLOB MA PHYI MA PHYI MA RNAMS LA BYIN GYIS RLOB PA'I TSUL DU RIM BZHIN THIM MTHAR,
snga ma.wylie: gsum pa bla ma bstim pa'i zhal shes la, dus gsum sangs rgyas zhes sogs kyis gsol ba btab pas gzhal yas khang dang brgyud pa'i bla ma rnams kyi seng khri rnams kyang bsdu, bla brgyud rnams sangs rgyas rdo rje chos rang gi slob ma rnal 'byor ma la thim pa sogs bla ma snga ma snga ma rnams rang rang gi slob ma phyi ma phyi ma rnams la byin gyis rlob pa'i tshul du rim bzhin thim mthar
snga ma.english: This brings us to the third of the private instructions, which is bringing the Lama to melt inside us.  First make the supplication that includes the words "every single Buddha of the past, present, and future."  Because of your supplication the palace, and the lion thrones of the lineage Lamas as well, are withdrawn. These Lamas themselves begin to melt into each other, starting with Dharma of Diamond the Buddha, who melts into His disciple, the Angel of Diamond. Each Lama of the previous generation melts into His of Her disciple of the succeeding generation, as if to impart thereby Their blessings.

snga ma.acip: BLA MA STIM PA'I ZHAL SHES NI, DUS GSUM SANGS RGYAS THAMS CAD CES SOGS GSOL BA LAN GSUM GDAB PAR BYA STE, BDAG GI RGYUD SKAD CIG SNGA MA LA MA DAG PA'I SHES PA 'DI SKAD CIG PHYI MA DAG PA'I YE SHES SU BSGYUR BAR BYIN GYIS BRLAB TU GSOL SNYAM PA DANG,
snga ma.wylie: bla ma stim pa'i zhal shes ni, dus gsum sangs rgyas thams cad ces sogs gsol ba lan gsum gdab par bya ste, bdag gi rgyud skad cig snga ma la ma dag pa'i shes pa 'di skad cig phyi ma dag pa'i ye shes su bsgyur bar byin gyis brlab tu gsol snyam pa dang
snga ma.english: Now we will cover the oral instructions on how to dissolve the Lamas into you.  Begin by reciting three times the verse which goes, "[I make supplication to the precious Lamas whose nature is that of] every single Buddha of the past, present and future..."  As you recite this prayer think to yourself, "Please grant me Your blessing that my mindstream, which in this first instant is impure, be transformed into pure wisdom by the very next instant."

snga ma.acip: RGYUD DANG RGYUN GNYIS DON GCIG PAS SKAD CIG PHYI MA DE SKAD CIG SNGA MA 'DAS PA'I RIGS 'DRA'I RGYUN GYI SKAD CIG SNGA MA SKAD CIG PHYI MA MIN LA SKAD CIG PHYI MA YANG SKAD CIG SNGA MA MIN NO,
snga ma.wylie: rgyud dang rgyun gnyis don gcig pas skad cig phyi ma de skad cig snga ma 'das pa'i rigs 'dra'i rgyun gyi skad cig snga ma skad cig phyi ma min la skad cig phyi ma yang skad cig snga ma min no
snga ma.english: The words mindstream and continuum have the same meaning here.  The second instant of something is the continuum of a similar thing once the first instant has passed.  This doesn't however mean that the first instant is the second instant, or that the second instant is the first.

The second instant of something is the continuum of a similar thing once the first instant has passed.  This doesn't however mean that the first instant is the second instant, or that the second instant is the first."}

snga ma.acip: RDO RJE 'CHANG RDO RJE RNAL 'BYOR MAR STIM, DE'I SENG KHRI'ANG RNAL 'BYOR MA'I SENG KHRI LA STIM PA SOGS BLA MA LNGA MA SNGA MAS PHYI MA PHYI MA BYIN GYIS BRLABS NAS RTOGS PA MNYAM STE THUGS YID GCIG TU 'DRIS PA'I TSUL DU GA-YON SKOR DU BSDUD PA DANG, PHYI MA PHYI MAS SNGA MA SNGA MA'I YON TAN RNAMS BRNYES PA'AM RTOGS PA'I TSUL DU GA-YON SKOR DU BSDUD PA GNYIS GANG BYAS KYANG 'GAL BA MED MOD, NGAG 'DON DU SNGA MA LTAR YOD PAS DE BZHIN BYA,
snga ma.wylie: rdo rje 'chang rdo rje rnal 'byor mar stim, de'i seng khri'ang rnal 'byor ma'i seng khri la stim pa sogs bla ma lnga ma snga mas phyi ma phyi ma byin gyis brlabs nas rtogs pa mnyam ste thugs yid gcig tu 'dris pa'i tshul du ga-yon skor du bsdud pa dang, phyi ma phyi mas snga ma snga ma'i yon tan rnams brnyes pa'am rtogs pa'i tshul du ga-yon skor du bsdud pa gnyis gang byas kyang 'gal ba med mod, ngag 'don du snga ma ltar yod pas de bzhin bya
snga ma.english: Now the Keeper of the Diamond melts into the Angel of Diamond.  His lion throne melts into Her own throne.  As this melting continues, each of the Lamas grants his blessing to the next Lama in the lineage by making them of equal realization.  Going around to the left then all of the Lineage Lamas are collected together as if their holy minds were becoming one. You can also think that--as they dissolve into each other--each later Lama attains or reaches all of the good qualities of the Lamas who came before Him or Her.  Although there is no contradiction between either of these two ways of thinking, you should follow the first way, as this is how the recitation goes.

snga ma.acip: GZHI DUS KYI BAR DO BA NI TSE TSAD JI LTAR RING YANG ZHAG BDUN MA GTOGS MI THUB, DENG SANG KHA CIG GIS, 'GA' ZHIG SHI NAS SKYE BA LEN SA MA BYUNG BAR, BAR DO'I GNAS SKABS RANG NA BSDAD YOD PA DANG, DE YANG SKYE BA SNGA MA'I LUS KYI CHA BYAD DU LO ZLA MANG PO ZHIG TU SDOD PAR MTHONG THOS KYI SKAD BYED,
snga ma.wylie: gzhi dus kyi bar do ba ni tshe tshad ji ltar ring yang zhag bdun ma gtogs mi thub, deng sang kha cig gis, 'ga' zhig shi nas skye ba len sa ma byung bar, bar do'i gnas skabs rang na bsdad yod pa dang, de yang skye ba snga ma'i lus kyi cha byad du lo zla mang po zhig tu sdod par mthong thos kyi skad byed
snga ma.english: The lifespan of a being in the original state between death and birth can never be more than seven days, at the very longest.  Nowadays you see some people who say that there are special cases, where a person dies and is unable to take their rebirth, and so resides there in the state between.  People make claims that they have actually seen or heard such beings, and that these beings retain the same bodily appearance they had in their life just passed, and that they stay this way for a period of many months, or even years.

snga ma.acip: MDZOD LAS, SNGON DUS SRID 'BYUNG SHA TSUGS CAN, ,ZHES GSUNGS PA'I DGONGS DON MA RNYED PAR, KHA CIG GIS SNGON DUS KYI SRID PA ZHES PA BAR DO'I SNGON MA SKYE BA SNGA MA DER NGOS BZUNG NAS DE'I LUS CAN YIN PAR SMRA BA DANG,
snga ma.wylie: mdzod las, sngon dus srid 'byung sha tshugs can, ,zhes gsungs pa'i dgongs don ma rnyed par, kha cig gis sngon dus kyi srid pa zhes pa bar do'i sngon ma skye ba snga ma der ngos bzung nas de'i lus can yin par smra ba dang
snga ma.english: The Treasure House includes a line that says "They have the image of the being before."  Some people have misconstrued the actual meaning of these words, and have "being before" to mean the person of the previous life, the one that came before the state between death and life.  They purport therefore that the being in this state between possesses the same kind of body as they had before.

snga ma.acip: DE LTAR BAm YIG BAR DO'I MTSON DON NAM MKHAR BZHAG PA'I RANG LUGS LTAR MA BYAS PAR, STONG PA'I NGANG LAS GSAR DU BSKYED PA NI GZHI LAM 'BRAS GSUM LA SBYAR NA MI MTHUN PAR MA ZAD, BAm YIG NAM MKHAR BZHAG PA N'A RO'I GZHUNG CHUNG DU, DBUS SU NI BAm YIG GO, ZHES PA'I DGONGS PA YIN PAS SNGA MA NI GZHUNG CHUNG DANG 'GAL ZHING, RTZA RGYUD LAS, 'JUG PA SGRA LA SOGS PA NAS, ,ZHES GSUNGS PA'I SOGS KHONGS NAS BSTAN PA'I DGONGS PA DANG YANG MI MTHUN GSUNGS,
snga ma.wylie: de ltar baM yig bar do'i mtshon don nam mkhar bzhag pa'i rang lugs ltar ma byas par, stong pa'i ngang las gsar du bskyed pa ni gzhi lam 'bras gsum la sbyar na mi mthun par ma zad, baM yig nam mkhar bzhag pa nA ro'i gzhung chung du, dbus su ni baM yig go, zhes pa'i dgongs pa yin pas snga ma ni gzhung chung dang 'gal zhing, rtsa rgyud las, 'jug pa sgra la sogs pa nas, ,zhes gsungs pa'i sogs khongs nas bstan pa'i dgongs pa dang yang mi mthun gsungs
snga ma.english: Doing this step the other way--that is, producing a letter vam all over again, out of a state of emptiness--bears no correlation to the three stages of our original state, the path, and the final result.  Having the vam stand in empty space is the intent of the line in the Short Classics of Naropa which says, "In the center is a letter vam."  Therefore that other explanation contradicts the Short Classics.  It is also at odds with the intent of the root text of the secret teaching, as revealed in the section around the lines that read, "The practice is from the sound and the rest."

snga ma.acip: DE'I NANG DU GTUM DRAG LA SOGS PA'I DUR KHROD CHEN PO BRGYAD KYIS LAM YONGS RDZOGS MTSON ZHING, DUR KHROD SA LUGS PA NANG DANG DGE LUGS PA ME RI'I PHYIR BSGOM PA GNYIS KAR KHUNGS DANG 'BREL ZHING, SNGA MA NI SLOB DPON AA BHYA KA RA'I RDO RJE'I PHRENG BA'I THIG CHOG GI RJES SU 'BREL BA'O, ,
snga ma.wylie: de'i nang du gtum drag la sogs pa'i dur khrod chen po brgyad kyis lam yongs rdzogs mtshon zhing, dur khrod sa lugs pa nang dang dge lugs pa me ri'i phyir bsgom pa gnyis kar khungs dang 'brel zhing, snga ma ni slob dpon aa bhya ka ra'i rdo rje'i phreng ba'i thig chog gi rjes su 'brel ba'o,
snga ma.english: In the middle are Savage Wrath and the rest of the eight great burial grounds, which symbolize the entirety of the Buddhist path. In the Sakya system, the burial grounds are inside the mountain of fire, and in the Gelukpa system they are outside of it.  Both interpretations have authoritative sources.  The first one is connected to the Ritual for Drawing Secret Worlds in the secret teachings of the String of Diamonds, as taught by Master Abhyakara.

snga ma.acip: 'KHOR LO SNGA MA LTAR NA PHYI NANG GNYIS KYI RTZIBS BCU DRUG ,RANG LUGS THUN MONG MIN PAR 'KHOR LO'I RTZIBS BRGYAD DANG NOR BU'I GZHOGS KHA BRGYAD BSDOMS PAS BCU DRUG ,RDO RJE NAG PO'I PHRENG BA PHYI NANG GNYIS BSDOMS PA BCU DRUG STE KHYON SUM CU SO GNYIS KYIS SPYI BO'I RTZA 'DAB SUM CU SO GNYIS MTSON, 'KHOR LOS DBU SKRA MI SGRIB PA DANG, DBU SKRAS 'KHOR LO MI SGRIB PAR BSGOM DGOS,
snga ma.wylie: 'khor lo snga ma ltar na phyi nang gnyis kyi rtsibs bcu drug ,rang lugs thun mong min par 'khor lo'i rtsibs brgyad dang nor bu'i gzhogs kha brgyad bsdoms pas bcu drug ,rdo rje nag po'i phreng ba phyi nang gnyis bsdoms pa bcu drug ste khyon sum cu so gnyis kyis spyi bo'i rtsa 'dab sum cu so gnyis mtshon, 'khor los dbu skra mi sgrib pa dang, dbu skras 'khor lo mi sgrib par bsgom dgos
snga ma.english: Each spoke of the circular headdress, as we spoke of above, has an inner and outer section, totaling then 16 pieces.  In our own system though we have a unique way of arriving at this number 16, by adding together the eight spokes of the wheel and the eight facets of the jewels at the top.  We then add another 16 for the two strings of black diamonds, inside and out, which brings us to a total of 32.  This represents the 32 petals of the chakra at the center tip of the head.  In your meditation don't let the headdress block Her hair, nor Her hair block the headdress.

snga ma.acip: GDU BU LA DBYE NA DRUG STE, DPUNG PA GNYIS LA DBUS DANG GA-YAS GA-YON DU RDO RJE RTZE GSUM PA'I GZHUNG GSUM LA RUS PHRENG LNGA BSNOL MAR BTANG BA'I DRA BA NYIS GSHIBS DANG DRA PHYED GSUM GSHIBS 'PHYANG BA, DE BZHIN DU ZHABS KYI BOL GNYIS DANG, PHYAG GI MKHRIG MA GNYIS SU SNGA MA LAS PHYI MA PHYI MA RNAMS RIM GYIS THUNG BA,
snga ma.wylie: gdu bu la dbye na drug ste, dpung pa gnyis la dbus dang ga-yas ga-yon du rdo rje rtse gsum pa'i gzhung gsum la rus phreng lnga bsnol mar btang ba'i dra ba nyis gshibs dang dra phyed gsum gshibs 'phyang ba, de bzhin du zhabs kyi bol gnyis dang, phyag gi mkhrig ma gnyis su snga ma las phyi ma phyi ma rnams rim gyis thung ba
snga ma.english: She wears a total of six bracelets and anklets.  Two are on Her upper arms, and are made with three-pointed diamonds strung from the middle to the left and to the right with five intertwined strands of bone beads.  Hanging from these bracelets are pairs of loops and triads of half-loops.  At her two ankles and her two wrists she wears anklets and bracelets like these, each one progressively smaller than before.

snga ma.acip: SEMS 'DZIN NI, SNGA MA RNAMS LA SHAR SGOM LAM TZAM SONG RJES DE RNAMS MA BRJED PA'I STENG DU, MGUL LA SHA'I RI MO STE GNYER MA GSUM GYI STENG MA MI GSAL BA'I TSUL DANG, PADMA R'A GA'I BUM PA LTA BU, NU MA GNYIS KYI BAR DOG PA, NU 'BUR MTHO ZHING 'PHRANG BA BCAS LA NGA RGYAL DANG SBRAGS NAS ZAB GSAL GNYIS MED KYI RNAL 'BYOR BSKYANG BAR BYA'O,
snga ma.wylie: sems 'dzin ni, snga ma rnams la shar sgom lam tsam song rjes de rnams ma brjed pa'i steng du, mgul la sha'i ri mo ste gnyer ma gsum gyi steng ma mi gsal ba'i tshul dang, padma rA ga'i bum pa lta bu, nu ma gnyis kyi bar dog pa, nu 'bur mtho zhing 'phrang ba bcas la nga rgyal dang sbrags nas zab gsal gnyis med kyi rnal 'byor bskyang bar bya'o
snga ma.english: Let's go back to the visualization.  Do a quick review meditation of all the details that came before.  Then, without forgetting those details, add some of these new ones. There are three lines of flesh, or wrinkles, at Her throat.  The upper one is not very clear.  The cleavage between Her two breasts is shaped like a ruby vase; and Her nipples are erect and hard.  Get the visualization clear, and then think of all this as yourself. With this, you maintain the deep practice of indivisible depth and clarity.

snga ma.acip: 'O NA JI LTAR YIN ZHE NA, RANG RDO RJE 'CHANG DU GNAS PA DE LAS THA MAL PA'I LUS KYI CHA SHAS RE CHAD NAS THIM PAS GZHAL YAS KHANG SKAD CIG GI SNGA MA DES NYE BAR LEN PA'I RGYU DANG, SKAD CIG PHYI MA RANG GI LUS DES LHAN CIG BYED PA'I RKYEN BYAS NAS GRUB PA LTAR RO,
snga ma.wylie: 'o na ji ltar yin zhe na, rang rdo rje 'chang du gnas pa de las tha mal pa'i lus kyi cha shas re chad nas thim pas gzhal yas khang skad cig gi snga ma des nye bar len pa'i rgyu dang, skad cig phyi ma rang gi lus des lhan cig byed pa'i rkyen byas nas grub pa ltar ro
snga ma.english: How then are we supposed to do this practice?  Hold your visualization of yourself as the Keeper of the Diamond, and then imagine that pieces from the channels of your normal body break off and then sink into the crystal palace at your heart.  The first instant of the palace provides the material cause, and in the next instant comes a piece of your body that provides the contributing factor, for the mandala.

snga ma.acip: SNGA MA GNYIS SU RTZA'I PHYI SNER BSGOMS PA BAS RNAL 'BYOR MA'I SKABS 'DIR RTZA'I NANG SNE 'DUS MDO SNYING GAR BSGOM PA SHIN TU ZAB LA 'JUG PA BDE ZHING , RLUNG DBU MAR 'DU SLA BA DANG , BYIN RLABS KYANG SHIN TU CHE ZHING MYUR BAS 'DI YAB BKA' LA MED PA'I YUM BKA'I ZAB KHYAD YIN,
snga ma.wylie: snga ma gnyis su rtsa'i phyi sner bsgoms pa bas rnal 'byor ma'i skabs 'dir rtsa'i nang sne 'dus mdo snying gar bsgom pa shin tu zab la 'jug pa bde zhing , rlung dbu mar 'du sla ba dang , byin rlabs kyang shin tu che zhing myur bas 'di yab bka' la med pa'i yum bka'i zab khyad yin
snga ma.english: So in the other two cases we are meditating on the outer ends of the channels, whereas here in the teaching of the Holy Angel we are meditating on the heart, the nexus where all the inner ends of the channels converge.  This fact makes the practice of the secret world of your body here in Her ritual infinitely more profound than those others, and much easier to carry out; it facilitates gathering the inner wind into the central channel, and the power it has to bless your being is immense, and immediate.  These then are extraordinary features of the word of the Wife, that are not found in the word of the Man.

snga ma.acip: RIGS BDAG RANG CHAS SU BSKYED PA DANG , DBANG BSKUR NAS RGYAS GSAR DU GDAB PA GNYIS RGYAS BSDUS TZAM LAS ZAB MI ZAB KYI KHYAD MED CING , SNGA MA NI RGYAL PO LA BU GCIG LAS MED NA DE SKYES MA THAG NAS RGYAL POR NGES PA LTA BU DANG ,
snga ma.wylie: rigs bdag rang chas su bskyed pa dang , dbang bskur nas rgyas gsar du gdab pa gnyis rgyas bsdus tsam las zab mi zab kyi khyad med cing , snga ma ni rgyal po la bu gcig las med na de skyes ma thag nas rgyal por nges pa lta bu dang
snga ma.english: There is a little difference in the length of the ritual between turning yourself into the Lord of Enlightened Kind, complete with His own attire, or being marked by Him again subsequent to the empowerment.  It is not the case though that one has any more profound significance than the other.  The first way is like when the king of the land has a son, and no son has been born before him.  Within the moment of his birth it is already assured that he is King.

snga ma.acip: SGRUB THABS 'DON DUS TSIG DON SNGA MA SNGA MA MA BRJED PA'I STENG DU PHYI MA PHYI MA BSNON GYIN TSIG BSHAR DU MA SONG BAR BSGOMS DON RNAMS YID LA NGES PAR BYED,

snga ma.english: As you recite the ritual for becoming Her here, try to retain in your mind the meaning of each part that is finished and try to build on that with each part yet to come.  Don't get caught up in the flow of the words; try rather to take each point in the meditation and learn to grasp its importance fully.

snga ma.acip: RJE RIN PO CHES, BSGOM 'DOD KYIN 'PHRO LA BCAD KYIN BYAS TE BSGOMS NA SNGA MA RES KYANG 'JUG SNYING 'DOD, CES GSUNGS PA DANG,
snga ma.wylie: rje rin po ches, bsgom 'dod kyin 'phro la bcad kyin byas te bsgoms na snga ma res kyang 'jug snying 'dod, ces gsungs pa dang
snga ma.english: As the Precious Lord has pointed out, If you're always wanting to meditate, then you should always be trying to stop the mind from flying out while you meditate: great masters of the past agree as well that this is the essence of the practice.

snga ma.acip: 'DI LA KHA CIG GIS, DE LTAR BSKYED PA'I SKU DE GZHAN GYI YIN PAS DE LA NGA RGYAL BYED PA MI RIGS SNYAM NA, SKYON MED DE, DPER NA DA LTA'I RANG GI LUS 'DI YANG SKYE BA SNGA MA NAS RANG GIS KHYER TE 'ONGS PA MIN PAR PHA MA'I KHU KHRAG LAS GRUB PAS GZHAN GYI YIN YANG NGA'I LUS SO SNYAM DU 'DZIN PA DANG,
snga ma.wylie: 'di la kha cig gis, de ltar bskyed pa'i sku de gzhan gyi yin pas de la nga rgyal byed pa mi rigs snyam na, skyon med de, dper na da lta'i rang gi lus 'di yang skye ba snga ma nas rang gis khyer te 'ongs pa min par pha ma'i khu khrag las grub pas gzhan gyi yin yang nga'i lus so snyam du 'dzin pa dang
snga ma.english: Now some people might think to themselves, "The holy body that you are creating this way is somebody else's; it doesn't make sense to feel supreme confidence that is you."  But there's no such problem.  Consider for example the body you have right now; it didn't get here because you packed it up and brought it with you from your previous life.  It's made from the sperm and blood of your father and mother, so it's somebody else's too.  But you still consider it yours, don't you?

snga ma.acip: DE LTAR 'BYUNG BA'I RGYU MTSAN YANG THU'U BKVAN RIN PO CHE SOGS DAM PA SNGA MA RNAMS KYIS GSUNGS BA LTAR BSGRUB BYA'I YUL DU GYUR PA'I MKHA' 'GRO MA GRANGS MED RNAMS BSDU NA YUL NYER BZHI DUR KHROD BRGYAD GLING BZHI RI RAB BCAS SO BDUN DU BZHUGS PA'I DPA' BO DANG RNAL 'BYOR MA RNAMS SU 'DU ZHING, DE KUN KYANG GTZO MO RDO RJE RNAL 'BYOR MAR 'DU,
snga ma.wylie: de ltar 'byung ba'i rgyu mtshan yang thu'u bkvan rin po che sogs dam pa snga ma rnams kyis gsungs ba ltar bsgrub bya'i yul du gyur pa'i mkha' 'gro ma grangs med rnams bsdu na yul nyer bzhi dur khrod brgyad gling bzhi ri rab bcas so bdun du bzhugs pa'i dpa' bo dang rnal 'byor ma rnams su 'du zhing, de kun kyang gtso mo rdo rje rnal 'byor mar 'du
snga ma.english: The reason why this is true can be found in the sacred words of Tuken Rinpoche, and other Holy Ones of days gone by.  The infinite number of Holy Woman Angels whom you could ever hope to reach are all present in the Warriors and Holy Angels who reside in the thirty seven lands: in the twenty four sacred places, the eight burial grounds, and the four continents--together with Mount Supreme.  All of them are present as well in the central figure, the Holy Angel of Diamond herself.

snga ma.acip: DE NAS LTE BA'I RTZA 'KHOR GYI DBUS SU CHOS 'BYUNG NYIS BRTZEGS DGA' 'KHYIL DANG BCAS PA DE'I DBUS SU ZLA GDAN GYI STENG DU BAm YIG N'A DA DKAR LA DMAR BA'I MDANGS CAN RTZE MO NAS ME 'BAR LA KHAD PA DANG, SPYI BO'I RTZA 'KHOR GYI DBUS SU ZLA GDAN LA GAm YIG DKAR PO THIG LE ZLA GDAN LA REG PA'I MGO THUR LTA 'O RKYAL THOG LA BTAGS PA LTA BU BYANG SEMS 'DZAG LA KHAD PA'I TSUL DU BSAM, 'DIR 'KHOR LO GNYIS MA DANG BZHI MA BYED PA'I LUGS GNYIS LAS 'DI SNGA MA'O, ,
snga ma.wylie: de nas lte ba'i rtsa 'khor gyi dbus su chos 'byung nyis brtsegs dga' 'khyil dang bcas pa de'i dbus su zla gdan gyi steng du baM yig nA da dkar la dmar ba'i mdangs can rtse mo nas me 'bar la khad pa dang, spyi bo'i rtsa 'khor gyi dbus su zla gdan la gaM yig dkar po thig le zla gdan la reg pa'i mgo thur lta 'o rkyal thog la btags pa lta bu byang sems 'dzag la khad pa'i tshul du bsam, 'dir 'khor lo gnyis ma dang bzhi ma byed pa'i lugs gnyis las 'di snga ma'o,
snga ma.english: In the middle of your navel chakra picture the two-tiered dharma star together with its bliss swirls.  In the middle of the star is a vam syllable sitting atop a moon disk.  Its crook is colored a mix of white and red, and its tip is about to burst into flames.  Next picture another moondisk at the center of the chakra at the tip of you head.  Atop the moon is a white vam syllable.  It is turned upside down with the dot resting on the cushion.  It is just about to start dripping down the white element like a bag of milk hanging from the ceiling.  Of the two ways of closing this practice, using either two or four chakras, we will follow the first and use just these two.

snga ma.acip: SANG THO RANGS NAM GYI SUM CHA LUS PA NA 'OD GSAL GYI NGANG LAS LDANG BA'I RNAL 'BYOR GYIS LANGS LA, GOS TSAGS LEGS PAR BYAS TE KHRUS KYI RNAL 'BYOR TSUL BZHIN DU BYA, BLA MA SNGA MA 'GA' ZHIG GIS MTSAMS KYI RING LA KHRUS MI BYED PA DANG , SKRA SEN MI 'BREG PA ZAB GNAD YIN KHUL BYED MOD KYANG MNGON BRJOD BLA MA LAS,
snga ma.wylie: sang tho rangs nam gyi sum cha lus pa na 'od gsal gyi ngang las ldang ba'i rnal 'byor gyis langs la, gos tshags legs par byas te khrus kyi rnal 'byor tshul bzhin du bya, bla ma snga ma 'ga' zhig gis mtshams kyi ring la khrus mi byed pa dang , skra sen mi 'breg pa zab gnad yin khul byed mod kyang mngon brjod bla ma las
snga ma.english: The next morning, while there is still a third of the watch of the night to go, rise out of the state of the clear light and do the Practice of Waking.  Dress for the occasion and do the practice of bathing thoughtfully.  Some Lamas of the past have kept to a custom of not bathing or cutting their hair or fingernails for the entire length of their retreat, as if this were some important practice.  However, the explanatory teaching of Highest Bliss called The Expression says:

snga ma.acip: BSNYEN YIG SNGA MA 'GA' ZHIG MTHUN GYI SGANG LA JA BTUNG BA DANG , CHAB TOG LTA BUR CHAB BSANG BYA RUNG BAR BSHAD PA NI PHYAG LEN HA CANG RTZING BAR MNGON NO,,
snga ma.wylie: bsnyen yig snga ma 'ga' zhig mthun gyi sgang la ja btung ba dang , chab tog lta bur chab bsang bya rung bar bshad pa ni phyag len ha cang rtsing bar mngon no
snga ma.english: Some older retreat texts have said that it is all right to stop in the middle of a session to drink tea or go to the bathroom in a chamber pot.  This kind of behavior during the mantras though seems too rough to me.

This kind of behavior during the mantras though seems too rough to me."}

snga ma.acip: DE LTAR SNGAGS GRANGS LONGS NAS YE SHES 'BEBS SNGAGS BZLA BA BLA MA SNGA MA DAG MA GSUNGS KYANG BYAS NA PHUN SUM TSOGS PA'I YAN LAG TU 'GYUR BAS,
snga ma.wylie: de ltar sngags grangs longs nas ye shes 'bebs sngags bzla ba bla ma snga ma dag ma gsungs kyang byas na phun sum tshogs pa'i yan lag tu 'gyur bas
snga ma.english: After completing the required number of recitations, you should recite the secret worlds of the rain of wisdom.  Some Lamas of the past have said that you don't need to do this, but it will be a really excellent part of your retreat if you do.

Some Lamas of the past have said that you don't need to do this, but it will be a really excellent part of your retreat if you do."}

snga ma.acip: 'DI DANG GONG GI BSNYEN PA'I SNGON 'GRO'I 'DON CHA DGE BSNYEN RDO RJE RAB BRTAN GYI NGOR STZAL BA GNYIS CHO GA'I GO RIM DANG, 'DON CHA'I TSIG ZUR PHRAN BU MTHUN MIN RNAMS DAM PA SNGA MA'I PHYAG BZHES KYI KHYAD PAR MI 'DRA BA SO SOR YOD PA MI NYAMS PA'I SLAD DU DE LTAR GNANG BA TZAM LAS,
snga ma.wylie: 'di dang gong gi bsnyen pa'i sngon 'gro'i 'don cha dge bsnyen rdo rje rab brtan gyi ngor stsal ba gnyis cho ga'i go rim dang, 'don cha'i tshig zur phran bu mthun min rnams dam pa snga ma'i phyag bzhes kyi khyad par mi 'dra ba so sor yod pa mi nyams pa'i slad du de ltar gnang ba tsam las
snga ma.english: Certain details--the order of the steps to the ritual, and some of the wording used--would seem to be a bit at odds between this presentation [which again has not all been included by the present translators] and the earlier one here: the preliminary recitation which our Lama granted to that layman with lifetime vows, Dorje Rabten.  These differing sections though were purposely included by our Lama in order to preserve different customs of the practice which have been followed by the Holy Ones of the past in our lineage.

These differing sections though were purposely included by our Lama in order to preserve different customs of the practice which have been followed by the Holy Ones of the past in our lineage."}

snga ma.acip: DE ZIN NAS BDAG BSKYED SNGA MA'I MTSAMS NAS 'DON RAN PA NA, RANG NYID LHAR GSAL SOGS RKANG PA SNGA MA GNYIS 'DRA BA LA, SLAR YANG ZHAL PHYAG YONGS RDZOGS PA, ,CHU LAS NYA LDANG SOGS NAS, MTSAN PAR GYUR, ,CES BRJOD CING BSAM NA SNGA MA'I NYES PA KHEGS GSUNGS,
snga ma.wylie: de zin nas bdag bskyed snga ma'i mtshams nas 'don ran pa na, rang nyid lhar gsal sogs rkang pa snga ma gnyis 'dra ba la, slar yang zhal phyag yongs rdzogs pa, ,chu las nya ldang sogs nas, mtshan par gyur, ,ces brjod cing bsam na snga ma'i nyes pa khegs gsungs
snga ma.english: Then start the other ritual.  When you have completed it and are ready to continue reciting from where you left off in the first ritual, then pronounce this same verse again, leaving the first two lines the same, and reading after that, "As quick as a fish flicks on the surface, I'm again all complete in head and arms."  Finish the rest of the verse as before.  By doing this, said our Lama, you avoid the problem we mentioned.

snga ma.acip: DE YANG 'JIGS BYED KYI KHRO BCU'I SRUNG 'KHOR SHIN TU ZAB PAS DMIGS PA GSAL POS BSGOM PA GNAD CHE BAS SNGA MA DE'I PHYI ROL DU 'DI GSAL GDAB KYANG CHOG GSUNGS,

snga ma.english: Now the circle of protection of the ten fierce Angels, the one found in the teachings on the Lord of Terror, is extremely deep and subtle.  As such it is crucial that your meditation on this circle be very clear in the visualization.  For this reason, said our Lama, it is acceptable that you visualize this outside of the other circles.

snga ma.english: As for where we are now in the visualization, add now to the previous parts the vision of Her precious right and left eyes; Her holy nose; Her sacred mouth, teeth, fangs, tongue, lips, and ears--all as we've described them before.

snga ma.acip: DKYIL CHOG SKABS SPYAN 'DREN GNYIS BYUNG BA NA, SNGA MA DAM TSIG PA LA YE SHES PA BSTIM PA DANG, PHYI MA SPYAN 'DREN PA'I DBANG DU BYAS, DE YANG STENG GI NAM MKHAR RTZA BRGYUD KYI BLA MA,
snga ma.wylie: dkyil chog skabs spyan 'dren gnyis byung ba na, snga ma dam tshig pa la ye shes pa bstim pa dang, phyi ma spyan 'dren pa'i dbang du byas, de yang steng gi nam mkhar rtsa brgyud kyi bla ma
snga ma.english: If we perform the invitation in the ritual for the secret world twice, then the first repetition is for bringing the Beings of Wisdom to melt into the Beings of Pledge.  Then with the latter we actually invite Them all to come.

snga ma.acip: SEMS 'DZIN SNGA MA'I STENG DU 'KHOR LO SO SO'I DBU RGYAN, SNYAN RGYAN, MGUL RGYAN, PHYAG GDUB, ZHABS GDUB, SE RAL KHA, 'OG PAG SOGS RE RE NAS DPYAD SGOM GYIS GSAL SNANG BTON NAS SNGAR BZHIN 'JOG SGOM BYA,

snga ma.acip: DE YANG BSNGO BYA'I DGE BA GANG YANG RUNG BA DMIGS YUL DU BYAS TE DE 'DI'I RGYUR 'GYUR BAR SHOG CIG SNYAM DU SMON PA NI BSNGO SMON GNYIS KA DANG, ,BSNGO BYA'I DGE BA DA MIGS YUL DU MA BYAS PAR 'DI 'GRUB PAR SHOG CIG SNYAM DU SMON PA NI, SMON LAM YIN LA BSNGO BA MIN PAR GSUNGS SO, ,DES NA BSNGO BA DANG SMON LAM GNYIS KA YIN PA DANG, SMON LAM YIN LA BSNGO BA MIN PA GNYIS YOD PA LAS 'DIR NI SNGA MA YIN NO,,
snga ma.wylie: de yang bsngo bya'i dge ba gang yang rung ba dmigs yul du byas te de 'di'i rgyur 'gyur bar shog cig snyam du smon pa ni bsngo smon gnyis ka dang, ,bsngo bya'i dge ba da migs yul du ma byas par 'di 'grub par shog cig snyam du smon pa ni, smon lam yin la bsngo ba min par gsungs so, ,des na bsngo ba dang smon lam gnyis ka yin pa dang, smon lam yin la bsngo ba min pa gnyis yod pa las 'dir ni snga ma yin no
snga ma.english: Now it has been spoken that when you bring to mind any particular good deed which you have done, and you pray by thinking to yourself, "May it act as a cause for such and such a desired result," this is both a dedication and a prayer.  But when you don't bring to mind any of your past good deeds, and you simply pray by thinking to yourself, "may such and such happen," this is a prayer but not a dedication.  So there are two kinds of prayer: the kind that is both a dedication and a prayer, and the kind that is a prayer but not a dedication, and our prayer here is the former.

snga ma.acip: NYAL LUGS SNGA MA LTAR NA BDE STONG GI NGANG NAS CHU LAS NYA LDANG BA LTAR RANG NYID RJE BTZUN MA RGYAN YOD LA PHYAG MTSAN MED PA'I RNAM PAR LDANG ZHING,
snga ma.wylie: nyal lugs snga ma ltar na bde stong gi ngang nas chu las nya ldang ba ltar rang nyid rje btsun ma rgyan yod la phyag mtshan med pa'i rnam par ldang zhing
snga ma.english: For those who slept in the first method, then rise out of the realm of bliss and voidness like a fish that leaps suddenly out of a still lake.  You are in the form of the Holy Angel, with your ornaments but without your accoutrements.

You are in the form of the Holy Angel, with your ornaments but without your accoutrements."}

snga ma.acip: YANG SEMS BSKYED KYI KHONGS SU TSAD MED BZHI 'DUS PA LA DGONGS NAS SEMS BSKYED DANG TSAD MED NGO BO GCIG TU N'A RO PA DANG SA CHEN BZHED PA LAS 'DIR NI PHYI MA BZHIN YIN PAR GSUNGS KYANG, SEMS BSKYED KYI KHONGS SU TSAD MED BZHI TSANG TSUL GZHUNG SNGA MA RNAMS SU MA GSAL YANG, THAMS CAD MKHYEN PA DHARMA BHA DRA DPAL BZANG POS RJE BDAG NYID CHEN PO'I DGONGS PA BZHIN GSAL BAR GSUNGS PA ZIN BRIS SU 'KHROD PA LTAR DANG,
snga ma.wylie: yang sems bskyed kyi khongs su tshad med bzhi 'dus pa la dgongs nas sems bskyed dang tshad med ngo bo gcig tu nA ro pa dang sa chen bzhed pa las 'dir ni phyi ma bzhin yin par gsungs kyang, sems bskyed kyi khongs su tshad med bzhi tshang tshul gzhung snga ma rnams su ma gsal yang, thams cad mkhyen pa dharma bha dra dpal bzang pos rje bdag nyid chen po'i dgongs pa bzhin gsal bar gsungs pa zin bris su 'khrod pa ltar dang
snga ma.english: On the other hand, the four limitless thoughts can be considered part of the Wish for enlightenment, and it is with this in mind that holy Naropa and Sachen assert that the Wish and the limitless are one and the same.  In our present context, it has been stated that they are taken in this latter way.  But it is unclear in the earlier scriptures exactly how all four limitless thoughts are found within the Wish for enlightenment.  However, the all-knowing glorious pure one, Dharma Bhadra, has made this clear in his Notes,17 in keeping with the true intent of that high Lord himself, Tsongkapa.

snga ma.acip: GZHAN YANG SKYABS YUL BSDUS PA'I SKABS DANG, BDAG GI RJE BLA MA'I BSNYEN YIG TU GSAL BA LTAR BDAG BSKYED BSDUS PA'I SKABS RTZA BA'I BLA MA DPA' BO RDO RJE CHOS GCIG BU GSAL BTAB NAS, DE NYID LA KUN 'DUS NOR BU LUGS ZHES SKYABS GNAS THAMS CAD TSANG TSUL LA YIG CHA SNGA MA RNAMS SU, BRGYUD PA'I BLA MA THAMS CAD THUGS YID GCIG TU 'DRES PAS BLA MA KUN 'DUS, PHUNG PO LNGA RGYAL BA RIGS LNGA'I NGO BO YIN PAS SANGS RGYAS DKON MCHOG, THUGS RGYUD LA YOD PA'I LUNG RTOGS KYI YON TAN CHOS, PHYI NANG GI SKYE MCHED BYANG SEMS KYI NGO BOR BZHUGS PA DGE 'DUN,
snga ma.wylie: gzhan yang skyabs yul bsdus pa'i skabs dang, bdag gi rje bla ma'i bsnyen yig tu gsal ba ltar bdag bskyed bsdus pa'i skabs rtsa ba'i bla ma dpa' bo rdo rje chos gcig bu gsal btab nas, de nyid la kun 'dus nor bu lugs zhes skyabs gnas thams cad tshang tshul la yig cha snga ma rnams su, brgyud pa'i bla ma thams cad thugs yid gcig tu 'dres pas bla ma kun 'dus, phung po lnga rgyal ba rigs lnga'i ngo bo yin pas sangs rgyas dkon mchog, thugs rgyud la yod pa'i lung rtogs kyi yon tan chos, phyi nang gi skye mched byang sems kyi ngo bor bzhugs pa dge 'dun
snga ma.english: Now let's consider that point of the practice where we dissolve the refuge objects.  According to what my Holy Lama has detailed in his retreat manual, at the point when we dissolve the image before us, we are visualizing our Root Lama, Dharma of Diamond the Warrior, alone.  And by visualizing like this, we are practicing the way of the all-encompassing gem. Here is how all the places of refuge are found complete in this one Being, as it has been described in the commentaries of old.  They are the All-Encompassing Lama, because the hearts of each and every Lineage Lama have blended into Their own.  They are the Buddha Jewel, for Their five heaps are the essence of those Victorious Buddhas of the Five Families.  They are the Dharma Jewel, by holding in Their mindstream those qualities of both scriptural knowledge and realizations.  And They are the Sangha Jewel, because Their outer and inner doors of sense are of the nature of those who have the Wish.

snga ma.acip: GZHAN YANG 'DI'I SKABS KYI RANG LUS TSOGS SU 'BUL BA LA, RNYING MA PA RNAMS KU SU LU ZHES PA MA BCOS LHUG PA'I DON DANG, SA CHEN SOGS GSAR MA BA RNAMS KU SA LI ZHES PA DGE BA CAN LA 'JUG PAS SNGA MA MA DAG PAR GSUNGS KYANG, BDAG GI RJE BLA MAS DE GNYIS KA DAG PA YIN TE,
snga ma.wylie: gzhan yang 'di'i skabs kyi rang lus tshogs su 'bul ba la, rnying ma pa rnams ku su lu zhes pa ma bcos lhug pa'i don dang, sa chen sogs gsar ma ba rnams ku sa li zhes pa dge ba can la 'jug pas snga ma ma dag par gsungs kyang, bdag gi rje bla mas de gnyis ka dag pa yin te
snga ma.english: Also in this deep practice of the Lama is the part where we offer up our own body as a sacred feast.  Those Ancient Ones of the old school call this Kusulu, which has connotations of being uncontrived or natural.  Those in the newer traditions, such as Sachen, call it Kusali, which means "virtuous."  Some people have said that the former word is a corruption; however, my Holy Lama holds that both these two are correct, and explains why in the following way.

snga ma.acip: DE BZHIN DU TSAR CHEN GYI MKHA' SPYOD BSGRUB PA'I NYE LAM LAS, BAm YIG BRIS PA'I MTHAR MDUN NAS G-YON SKOR GYIS AOm GSUM MA'I SNGAGS 'PHRENG MGO PHYIR BSTAN KHOR YUG TU BRIS, DE YANG AOm GSUM, DE'I RJES SU SARBA, ZHES PA NAS, SV'A H'A RNAMS RIM PA BZHIN DU BRI BA MA RTOGS 'BRU RE RE NAS LDOG BAR MI MDZAD, CES PA'I BAR DANG, 'DI LA SHAR DRANG POR AOm DANG, ZHES PA NAS, LHOR N'I BRIS NA CHA SNYOM PAR 'GYUR RO, ,ZHES PA'I BAR SNGA MA DANG KHYAD PAR GTAN NAS MED PAR GSUNGS,
snga ma.wylie: de bzhin du tshar chen gyi mkha' spyod bsgrub pa'i nye lam las, baM yig bris pa'i mthar mdun nas g-yon skor gyis aoM gsum ma'i sngags 'phreng mgo phyir bstan khor yug tu bris, de yang aoM gsum, de'i rjes su sarba, zhes pa nas, svA hA rnams rim pa bzhin du bri ba ma rtogs 'bru re re nas ldog bar mi mdzad, ces pa'i bar dang, 'di la shar drang por aoM dang, zhes pa nas, lhor nI bris na cha snyom par 'gyur ro, ,zhes pa'i bar snga ma dang khyad par gtan nas med par gsungs
snga ma.english: In the same way, he says, Lord Tsarchen in his Quick Path for Reaching Heaven states: After drawing the vam letter, draw the string of secret words of the Triple Om in a counter-clockwise way, starting in front with the letters facing outside and circling around the edge.  So first come the three Oms.  After this comes the Sarva... And he continues up to: Sva Ha, drawing them in groups like this, but without turning each separate letter around backwards. Then he goes on to say: And if the Om is drawn straight to the East, and... And he continues this up to: ...and the Ni drawn straight to the South, it will come out in equally-divided segments. And these statements by Lord Tsarchen, he concludes, are not in any way different from the previous quotation.

snga ma.acip: 'DI'I AOm LA SOGS PA'I YI GE SNGA MA RNAMS RNAM SNANG LA SOGS PA'I YAB KYI SA BON DANG, BAm LA SOGS PA'I YI GE RJES MA RNAMS PHAG MO LA SOGS PA'I YUM GYI SA BON YIN LA, GO CHA'I SNGAGS RNAMS YUM GTZO BOR BYED KYANG RJES SU YOD PA NI YUM STONG PHYOGS SHES RAB KYI CHA YIN PAS G-YON GTZO BOR BYAS PA YIN NO,,
snga ma.wylie: 'di'i aoM la sogs pa'i yi ge snga ma rnams rnam snang la sogs pa'i yab kyi sa bon dang, baM la sogs pa'i yi ge rjes ma rnams phag mo la sogs pa'i yum gyi sa bon yin la, go cha'i sngags rnams yum gtso bor byed kyang rjes su yod pa ni yum stong phyogs shes rab kyi cha yin pas g-yon gtso bor byas pa yin no
snga ma.english: On these disks, the letters of Om and the rest which come first in each pair are the seed syllables of male deities such as Vairochana.  The letters like vam and the rest which follow them are the seed syllables of female deities such as the Sow.  Here it is the female secret words which provide the main function as armor, but the reason they come second is that the woman is the side of wisdom--emptiness and so forth, and so we are placing them foremost to the left.

snga ma.acip: DE YANG LUGS SNGA MAR YID BZLAS KYI RJES SU ZHAR BYUNG RDZOGS RIM 'BYUNG YANG LCANG SKYA'I DGONGS PA LTAR ZHAR BYUNG RDZOGS RIM DANG PO'I RJES SU YID BZLAS BYA BAR GSUNGS PAS,
snga ma.wylie: de yang lugs snga mar yid bzlas kyi rjes su zhar byung rdzogs rim 'byung yang lcang skya'i dgongs pa ltar zhar byung rdzogs rim dang po'i rjes su yid bzlas bya bar gsungs pas
snga ma.english: Now in previous systems, the incidental completion-stage practice comes after the mental recitation.  But as it is thought by Chankya Rinpoche, we should do the incidental completion-stage practice first, and then afterwards do the mental recitation.

snga ma.acip: DE'I PHYIR SNGA MA BTANG SNYOMS SU BZHAG NAS PHYI MA STON PA LA, DPE GSUM GYIS DON GCIG 'JAL BAR BYED PA NI, BSHAN PA SROG GI GNAD LA MKHAS PA, SHING MKHAN SHING GI GNAD LA MKHAS PA, SGYU MA MKHAN 'KHRUL 'KHOR GYI GNAD LA MKHAS PA STE DPE GSUM GYI DON, RNAL 'BYOR PA SA LAM GYI GNAD LA MKHAS PA 'DI 'JAL PAR GZHUNG BZHIN NO,,
snga ma.wylie: de'i phyir snga ma btang snyoms su bzhag nas phyi ma ston pa la, dpe gsum gyis don gcig 'jal bar byed pa ni, bshan pa srog gi gnad la mkhas pa, shing mkhan shing gi gnad la mkhas pa, sgyu ma mkhan 'khrul 'khor gyi gnad la mkhas pa ste dpe gsum gyi don, rnal 'byor pa sa lam gyi gnad la mkhas pa 'di 'jal par gzhung bzhin no
snga ma.english: As such, we will leave off explaining the former method--teaching the thing directly--and proceed now directly to the latter method of working through a medium.  To start off, we can say that we use three examples to illustrate a single point.  The first is that of a butcher who is a master at recognizing the one crucial point that life hangs upon.  And then there is the woodcutter who is a master at recognizing the one crucial point that the tree stands upon.  And then finally there is the magician who is a master at recognizing the one crucial point that the entire house of horrors turns upon.  A yogi who is a master of the one crucial point from which all the spiritual levels and paths proceed is one who grasps, as the text describes, the point that these three examples illustrate.

snga ma.acip: DPAL PHAG MO GRU PAS MDZAD PA NA YANG, SNGON DU DBANG BZHI RDZOGS PAR BSKUR BA'I LUGS MDZAD 'DUG PAS, MAR LUGS LA'ANG RGYUD KYI GZHUNG DANG GDAMS NGAG 'DZIN PA'I BLA MA SNGA MA CHEN PO RNAMS KYI BZHED PAS, DBANG BZHI YONGS SU RDZOGS PAR THOB PA CIG NGES PAR DGOS SO,,
snga ma.wylie: dpal phag mo gru pas mdzad pa na yang, sngon du dbang bzhi rdzogs par bskur ba'i lugs mdzad 'dug pas, mar lugs la'ang rgyud kyi gzhung dang gdams ngag 'dzin pa'i bla ma snga ma chen po rnams kyi bzhed pas, dbang bzhi yongs su rdzogs par thob pa cig nges par dgos so
snga ma.english: In the works of the glorious Pakmo Drupa also the proper system is to first grant the disciple an initiation complete with all four empowerments.  Thus we can say that, in the system of Marpa as well, the great Lamas of the past--those who have held both the secret books and the private instructions--believed that it was necessary to be granted an initiation complete with all four empowerments; and so it is absolutely certain that one should do so.

Thus we can say that, in the system of Marpa as well, the great Lamas of the past--those who have held both the secret books and the private instructions--believed that it was necessary to be granted an initiation complete with all four empowerments; and so it is absolutely certain that one should do so."}

snga ma.acip: BLA MA CHE BA SNGA MA GZHAN RNAMS KYANG RIM PA GNYIS KA SGOM DGOS PAR BZHED PAS, BSKYED RIM LA MI 'KHRID NA, RGYUD SDE DANG DE'I DGONGS 'GREL TSAD LDAN RNAMS DANG 'GAL LA, RANG GI LUGS DANG YANG 'GAL BAS RDZOGS RIM GYI SNGON DU BSKYED RIM LA BSLAB PAR BYA STE,
snga ma.wylie: bla ma che ba snga ma gzhan rnams kyang rim pa gnyis ka sgom dgos par bzhed pas, bskyed rim la mi 'khrid na, rgyud sde dang de'i dgongs 'grel tshad ldan rnams dang 'gal la, rang gi lugs dang yang 'gal bas rdzogs rim gyi sngon du bskyed rim la bslab par bya ste
snga ma.english: Other great Lamas of the past too have held the position that one must practice both the stages; and so if one were to fail to teach their disciple the stage of creation, they would  be acting in contradiction to the collection of secret teachings, and the commentaries upon them.  They would further be acting in contradiction to their own lineage, and so one should always train oneself in the stage of creation before practicing the stage of completion.

They would further be acting in contradiction to their own lineage, and so one should always train oneself in the stage of creation before practicing the stage of completion."}

snga ma.acip: 'KHRUL 'KHOR DANG STONG RA SGOM PA MED KYANG, RJE BTZUN MID LA NAS SGOM PO BA LA BRGYUD PA LA SNGA MA MED CING, PHYI MA YOD PA'I LUGS BZHIN DU 'DIR 'CHAD PA LA GNYIS YOD PA'I DANG PO 'KHRUL 'KHOR NI,
snga ma.wylie: 'khrul 'khor dang stong ra sgom pa med kyang, rje btsun mid la nas sgom po ba la brgyud pa la snga ma med cing, phyi ma yod pa'i lugs bzhin du 'dir 'chad pa la gnyis yod pa'i dang po 'khrul 'khor ni
snga ma.english: There are not, however, the two steps of the machine of the body and the empty form.  In the tradition as it was passed down from the holy Milarepa through Gampopa though, the three practices mentioned first are not followed, and the latter two are.  We will follow this system in our explanation here; so we begin with the first of the two, the machine of the body.

snga ma.acip: DE NAS GA YON PA YANG SNGA MA BZHIN DU DPUNG MGO GA YON PA BAR DU BKUG LA BRDAB SLAR YANG LAG PA GNYIS RDO RJE KHU TSUR BCANGS PA SNYING KHA NAS THAD KAR MDUN NGOS SU SHUGS CHE BAR GSHIBS LA BRKYANG, DE NAS GA YAS SU LAG PA GNYIS BRKYANGS NAS SNGA MA BZHIN DGUG LA BRDAB BO,,
snga ma.wylie: de nas ga yon pa yang snga ma bzhin du dpung mgo ga yon pa bar du bkug la brdab slar yang lag pa gnyis rdo rje khu tshur bcangs pa snying kha nas thad kar mdun ngos su shugs che bar gshibs la brkyang, de nas ga yas su lag pa gnyis brkyangs nas snga ma bzhin dgug la brdab bo
snga ma.english: Now use your left arm to bend your arms back as far as your left shoulder and beat your side, as before.  Then once more grasp your hands in fists of diamond and thrust them ahead of you, straight out from your heart, lined up together, and with force.  After that stretch your arms out to the right of you, bending and beating your side like you did before.

snga ma.acip: SPYI BO'I RTZA 'KHOR GYI DBUS SU ZLA GDAN LA HAm YIG DKAR PO THIG LE ZLA GDAN LA REG PA'I MGO THUR LTA 'O RKYAL THOG LA BTAGS PA LTA BU BYANG SEMS 'DZAG LA KHAD PA'I TSUL DU BSAM, 'DIR 'KHOR LO GNYIS MA DANG BZHI MA BYED PA'I LUGS GNYIS LAS 'DI SNGA MA'O,,
snga ma.wylie: spyi bo'i rtsa 'khor gyi dbus su zla gdan la haM yig dkar po thig le zla gdan la reg pa'i mgo thur lta 'o rkyal thog la btags pa lta bu byang sems 'dzag la khad pa'i tshul du bsam, 'dir 'khor lo gnyis ma dang bzhi ma byed pa'i lugs gnyis las 'di snga ma'o
snga ma.english: Next picture another moondisk at the center of the chakra at the tip of you head.  Atop the moon is a white ham syllable.  It is turned upside down with its dot resting on the cushion.  It is just about to start dripping down the white element, like a bag of milk hanging from the ceiling.  Of the two ways of doing this practice, using either two or four chakras, we will follow the first and use just these two.
