Of the two ways of doing this practice, using either two or four chakras, we will follow the first and use just these two."}

snga ma.acip: LUGS 'DI LA RTZA'I GSAL GI GNAS CHA BRTAN PO RING DU SGRUB PA DANG, MI SGRUB PA GNYIS SNANG NA'ANG, SNGA MA LTAR BYAS NA LEGS PA YIN TE, GRUB CHEN LVA BA PA'I GZHUNG LAS, RTZA'I GSAL SNANG SGRUB PAR BSHAD DO,,
snga ma.wylie: lugs 'di la rtsa'i gsal gi gnas cha brtan po ring du sgrub pa dang, mi sgrub pa gnyis snang na'ang, snga ma ltar byas na legs pa yin te, grub chen lva ba pa'i gzhung las, rtsa'i gsal snang sgrub par bshad do
snga ma.english: Now it seems that, as this system has been passed down, you can either invest some time in assuring that your vision of the channels, and your ability to maintain this vision, is strong; or you can go on without reaching this point.  It's better though if you do it the former way; the great and accomplished saint, Kambala, is making this same point in his text when He says that one must reach a point of clarity in the vision of the channels.

snga ma.acip: DE LA LTE BA DANG MGRIN PA'I 'KHOR LO NI AE YIG 'BRU GSUM GYI DBYIBS SHES RAB DANG , SNYING GA DANG SPYI BO'I 'KHOR LO NI Wm YIG ZLUM PO'I DBYIBS THABS YIN LA, SNGA MA GNYIS KHA GYEN DU BLTA ZHING PHYI MA GNYIS THUR DU BLTA STE,
snga ma.wylie: de la lte ba dang mgrin pa'i 'khor lo ni ae yig 'bru gsum gyi dbyibs shes rab dang , snying ga dang spyi bo'i 'khor lo ni wM yig zlum po'i dbyibs thabs yin la, snga ma gnyis kha gyen du blta zhing phyi ma gnyis thur du blta ste
snga ma.english: Now the chakras at the navel and the throat have the triangular shape of the Sanskrit version of the sacred syllable e [e], a shape which represents wisdom.  The chakras the heart and the tip of the head have the circular shape of the Sanskrit of the sacred syllable vam [vam@ ], a shape representing method. The former two chakras face upwards, and the latter two face downwards.

snga ma.acip: SNGA MA GNYUG SEMS KYI NGO BO MTHONG BA LA, LTE BAR RLUNG ZHUGS GNAS THIM GSUM BYAS TE LTE BA'I RTZA MDUD GROL BAR MA ZAD, KHYAB BYED KYI RLUNG TSUN CHAD SNYING GA'I DBU MA'I NANG DU 'DUS NAS GNYUG SEMS ZHU BDE'I NGO BOR BSKYED DGOS SHING,
snga ma.wylie: snga ma gnyug sems kyi ngo bo mthong ba la, lte bar rlung zhugs gnas thim gsum byas te lte ba'i rtsa mdud grol bar ma zad, khyab byed kyi rlung tshun chad snying ga'i dbu ma'i nang du 'dus nas gnyug sems zhu bde'i ngo bor bskyed dgos shing
snga ma.english: In order to see the former of the two--that is, the nature of the primal mind--you must bring the winds to enter in, stay within, and dissolve into the channel of the navel, thereby releasing its knot.  Not only that, you must also take all the winds, up even to the pervading one, and gather them into the central channel of the heart--thus endowing the primal mind with a quality where it can easily be melted down.

snga ma.acip: DE LTA BU'I GNYUG SEMS DES STONG NYID DON SPYI'I TSUL DU RTOGS PA NA DPE'I 'ONG GSAL DANG, MNGON SUM DU RTOGS PA NA DON GYI 'OD GSAL THOB PA YIN LA, SNGA MA LA DE DAG KHA PHYOGS TZAM YANG MED PAS KHYAD PAR SHIN TU CHE GSUNGS,
snga ma.wylie: de lta bu'i gnyug sems des stong nyid don spyi'i tshul du rtogs pa na dpe'i 'ong gsal dang, mngon sum du rtogs pa na don gyi 'od gsal thob pa yin la, snga ma la de dag kha phyogs tsam yang med pas khyad par shin tu che gsungs
snga ma.english: When a primal mind that does have this quality perceives emptiness by employing a mental picture, you have achieved the approximate clear light.  When it perceives emptiness directly, then you have reached the actual clear light.  That other act of seeing the mind involves nothing which even approaches what we have described here, and so the difference between the two--said our Lama--is enormous.

snga ma.acip: BZHIN DU SNGA MA CHOS NYID DNGOS STON NI, GNYUG SEMS KYI GNAS TSUL TZAM BSHAD PA YIN PAS DES DE LA GO BA TZAM CHAGS PA LAS GNYUG SEMS MNGON DU MI 'GYUR LA,
snga ma.wylie: bzhin du snga ma chos nyid dngos ston ni, gnyug sems kyi gnas tshul tsam bshad pa yin pas des de la go ba tsam chags pa las gnyug sems mngon du mi 'gyur la
snga ma.english: Here teaching the nature of the thing directly is like the first example.  Because what you do in this case is nothing more than explain what the primal mind is like, the person can only get a general idea of it; they doesn't actually reach it.

snga ma.acip: LTA BA'I SKOR YANG SA LUGS RJES MA TSOS BOD SNGA MA'I LTA BA DANG BSTUN NAS GSUNGS SHING, RJE'I DGONGS PA DANG MI MTHUN PA SNANG BAS RANG LUGS LA MI DGOS GSUNGS,
snga ma.wylie: lta ba'i skor yang sa lugs rjes ma tshos bod snga ma'i lta ba dang bstun nas gsungs shing, rje'i dgongs pa dang mi mthun pa snang bas rang lugs la mi dgos gsungs
snga ma.english: In the matter of the correct view of emptiness as well, the later followers of the Sakya tradition began to teach the concept of this viewpoint of reality in the same way that the early Tibetans did.  It appears that this way of teaching it, said our Lama, does not accord with the thought of Lord Tsongkapa, and so it has no place in our own school.

snga ma.acip: DES NA STENG 'OG GI RLUNG GNYIS KA KHA SBYOR DGOS LA, DE GNYIS DUS CIG TU MI 'THEN PAR RIM GYIS THEN NAS BYED DGOS PA LA, DMIGS BSAL CAN GYI DGOS PA GZHAN MA BYUNG NA STENG RLUNG SNGON LA THEN NAS, LTE BAR MNAN PA'I RJES SU 'OG RLUNG YAR LA THEN LA SNGA MA'I SAR GNON PA YIN LA, DE LA 'THEN THEBS RE RES CHOG GI GSUM GSUM MI DGOS SO,,
snga ma.wylie: des na steng 'og gi rlung gnyis ka kha sbyor dgos la, de gnyis dus cig tu mi 'then par rim gyis then nas byed dgos pa la, dmigs bsal can gyi dgos pa gzhan ma byung na steng rlung sngon la then nas, lte bar mnan pa'i rjes su 'og rlung yar la then la snga ma'i sar gnon pa yin la, de la 'then thebs re res chog gi gsum gsum mi dgos so
snga ma.english: As such, we must join the upper and lower winds, and do so not by drawing them forth at the same time, but rather one after the other.  If there is no compelling reason to do otherwise, one should draw the upper wind down first, pressing it against this region of the navel.  After that we should draw the lower wind up and press it to where we brought the first.  It's sufficient to do so once with each wind; there is no need to repeat the process three times each.

snga ma.acip: DE LA RI DVAGS SRED NI SMIG RGYU'O, ,RTAGS BZHI PO 'DI SNGA MA LAS PHYI MA GSAL DU SONG BA LA SMIG RGYU SOGS DANG 'DRA BAR GSUNGS KYI, DE RNAMS DANG 'DRA BA'I SNANG BA 'CHAR BA MIN ZHES PA DANG, KHA CIG RTAGS CAN GYI SHES PA BRTAN GA YO'I TSAD YIN ZHES PA DANG, KHA CIG DU BA SOGS DANG 'DRA BA'I SNANG BA 'CHAR BA LA BZHED PA GSUM BYUNG BA NI, PHYI MA NYID LEGS PA YIN NO,,
snga ma.wylie: de la ri dvags sred ni smig rgyu'o, ,rtags bzhi po 'di snga ma las phyi ma gsal du song ba la smig rgyu sogs dang 'dra bar gsungs kyi, de rnams dang 'dra ba'i snang ba 'char ba min zhes pa dang, kha cig rtags can gyi shes pa brtan ga yo'i tshad yin zhes pa dang, kha cig du ba sogs dang 'dra ba'i snang ba 'char ba la bzhed pa gsum byung ba ni, phyi ma nyid legs pa yin no
snga ma.english: The expression "temptation of a forest creature" here is a reference to a mirage.  Now there are three different positions that people take on what the signs mean.  Some say that the point is that your vision becomes clearer and clearer as you move up through the four latter signs, and this is why the passage mentions that they are like a mirage and the rest; they would say that it's not the point that you actually see something like the various objects mentioned. Still others say that the breadth of your vision--of the state of mind experiencing the signs--is being compared to objects of the outer world and the creatures who roam upon it.  Finally some say that you actually have visions of objects that resemble the smoke and the rest.  Only the last of these three is correct.

snga ma.acip: THABS SNGA MA LA 'BYUNG BA LA YANG PHYIN CI LOG GI SA'I RLUNG LA SOGS PA RNAMS LDOG RUNG DU SONG BA DANG, CUNG ZAD LOG PA DANG GTAN NAS LOG PA'I RTAGS GSUM 'ONG BAR BSHAD PA LTAR, DBANG PO'I SGO RNAMS NAS PHYIR HA CANG GA YO BA'I RLUNG CUNG ZAD NANG DU LDOG PAR RTZOM PA DANG, CUNG ZAD LOG PA DANG, DBU MAR CUNG ZAD TSUD PA SOGS KYI RTAGS NAS BZUNG STE,
snga ma.wylie: thabs snga ma la 'byung ba la yang phyin ci log gi sa'i rlung la sogs pa rnams ldog rung du song ba dang, cung zad log pa dang gtan nas log pa'i rtags gsum 'ong bar bshad pa ltar, dbang po'i sgo rnams nas phyir ha cang ga yo ba'i rlung cung zad nang du ldog par rtsom pa dang, cung zad log pa dang, dbu mar cung zad tshud pa sogs kyi rtags nas bzung ste
snga ma.english: When the signs occur in relation to the former method, three are explained as happening in conjunction with three stages that occur with undesirable winds relating to the element of earth and the rest; that is, where these winds are getting close to stopping; where they have in part stopped; and where they stop completely. These correspond to states of the winds related to the doors of sense--winds which are excessively active.  These states would be where these winds have just started to turn inwards; where they have turned in slightly; where they have been slightly inserted into the central channel; and so on.

snga ma.acip: DH'U T'I'I NANG GI GTUM MO THOG MAR LTE BA DANG GSANG GNAS NAS 'BAR BA DANG, DH'U T'I'I PHYI'I GTUM MO PHAL PA 'BAR BA DANG, DROD 'BAR TSUL LA LUS KYI GTING NAS 'BAR BA DANG, SHA LPAGS KYI BAR LTA BU KHA NAS 'BAR BA DANG, DANG POR 'BAR BA'I DROD KYI RGYA CHUNG BA DANG CHE BA DANG, DROD GYEN DU 'CHUG PA BUL BA DANG MYUR BA DANG, DROD 'THUG PA DANG SRAB PA RNAMS KYI SNGA MA RNAMS BZANG LA, PHYI MA RNAMS DE TZAM DU MI BZANG BA
snga ma.wylie: dhU tI'i nang gi gtum mo thog mar lte ba dang gsang gnas nas 'bar ba dang, dhU tI'i phyi'i gtum mo phal pa 'bar ba dang, drod 'bar tshul la lus kyi gting nas 'bar ba dang, sha lpags kyi bar lta bu kha nas 'bar ba dang, dang por 'bar ba'i drod kyi rgya chung ba dang che ba dang, drod gyen du 'chug pa bul ba dang myur ba dang, drod 'thug pa dang srab pa rnams kyi snga ma rnams bzang la, phyi ma rnams de tsam du mi bzang ba
snga ma.english: Each of the former members of the following pairs is higher, and each of the latter members is not as high: Inner fire within the channel of dance, burning first at the navel and the secret place; as opposed to ordinary inner fire, burning outside the channel of dance. A distinction in how the warmth burns; that is, whether it burns from the very depths of the body, or just "on the surface," meaning in the skin and the flesh beneath the skin. Whether the initial warmth burns at a particular spot or in a more generalized area. Whether the warmth invades the body upwards in a very slow way, or more suddenly. Whether the warmth is a very deep experience or a more shallow one.

snga ma.acip: 'GREMS PA'I TSUL SNGA MA MANG POS BYED MOD KYANG, RLUNG DH'U T'IR THIM NAS BYANG SEMS ZHU BA DANG, DE LTAR MIN PAR ZHU BA'I KHYAD PAR PHYE NAS, DE LA BYANG SEMS GZUNG DKA' SLA DANG, DE BTZAN THABS SU LDOG DGOS MI DGOS DANG LDOG PA LUS LA MA BKRAM NA NAD DU 'GYUR MI 'GYUR GYI KHYAD PAR PHYED PA'I RNAM GZHAG MI SNANG NGO,,
snga ma.wylie: 'grems pa'i tshul snga ma mang pos byed mod kyang, rlung dhU tIr thim nas byang sems zhu ba dang, de ltar min par zhu ba'i khyad par phye nas, de la byang sems gzung dka' sla dang, de btsan thabs su ldog dgos mi dgos dang ldog pa lus la ma bkram na nad du 'gyur mi 'gyur gyi khyad par phyed pa'i rnam gzhag mi snang ngo
snga ma.english: And so even if you are a person who has learned and used many methods of distributing the element earlier, there are certain distinctions to be recognized based on whether the element of enlightenment has melted down through the dissolution of the winds in the central channel, or through some other means: this will determine whether it is difficult or easy to retain the element of enlightenment; and whether you have to use forceful means to stop it; and whether, once you have stopped it, you will get sick if you fail to distribute it through the body.  I have not personally come across any other presentation of this practice that makes these important distinctions.

snga ma.acip: RANG GI LUS ME LONG LA SHAR BA RANG LA BSTIMS NAS, RANG GZUGS BRNYAN BZHIN DU GTAN LA 'BEBS PA NI SNGA MA DE'I ZHOR LA SONG ZIN PAS, DE TZAM ZHIG LA SBYONG BA DBANG PO SHIN TU RTUL BA LA, STON NA MA GTOGS 'GANGS CHUNG,
snga ma.wylie: rang gi lus me long la shar ba rang la bstims nas, rang gzugs brnyan bzhin du gtan la 'bebs pa ni snga ma de'i zhor la song zin pas, de tsam zhig la sbyong ba dbang po shin tu rtul ba la, ston na ma gtogs 'gangs chung
snga ma.english: There is this custom where one looks at one's reflection in a mirror, and then imagines that this reflection has melted into oneself. The point here though--of establishing to your own mind that your existence is like that of a reflection in a mirror--is something that you would already have come to understand by the way while you were going through the exercise we just mentioned. As such, setting a disciple to practicing no more than this is something you'd only want to do for those of very dullest of faculties; it's not a method of any great importance.

snga ma.acip: BSKYANGS NA, LHA'I SKU MDUN GYI ME LONG LA SHAR BA LA BLTAS NAS DE BLOS BTON TE, RANG LA BSTIMS NAS RANG LHA SKU SGYU MA BZHIN DU SGOM PA NI, SNGA MA'I ZHAR LA GRUB ZIN CING, SNGA MA STOBS CHE BAS PHYI MA CHA CHUNG,
snga ma.wylie: bskyangs na, lha'i sku mdun gyi me long la shar ba la bltas nas de blos bton te, rang la bstims nas rang lha sku sgyu ma bzhin du sgom pa ni, snga ma'i zhar la grub zin cing, snga ma stobs che bas phyi ma cha chung
snga ma.english: If you can continue to maintain this kind of practice, then you can easily give up mentally on that idea of staring at the reflection of some picture of an Angel in a mirror. This is because the whole point of having this reflection melt into you, and meditating upon how you now have the body of an Angel which is like an illusion, has again already been accomplished with the practice you have completed before; and since this previous practice is so much more powerful, the latter is of little use.

snga ma.acip: DE LA SNGAGS KYI THUN MONG MA YIN PA'I RMI LAM 'DZIN LUGS GTZO BO NI SNGA MA YIN LA, PHYI MA NI THUN MONG BA PHAL PA'O,,
snga ma.wylie: de la sngags kyi thun mong ma yin pa'i rmi lam 'dzin lugs gtso bo ni snga ma yin la, phyi ma ni thun mong ba phal pa'o
snga ma.english: Now the primary and unique method, in the secret way, of achieving recognition during your dreams is the first of the above; the latter is the common one, the ordinary one.

snga ma.acip: SNGA MA GNAS MTHOS PA DANG, DMIGS PA CUNG GSAL BAS GNYID HA CANG SRAB MOR SONG BA LA, NOR BUR GNYID 'THUG GI GNAS SKABS SKYED PA'I THIG LE YOD PAS, DER SEMS GTAD NA GNYID SRAB 'THUG SNYOMS PAR 'GYUR RO, ,DE'I RIGS PAS SROD DANG, THO RANGS KYI DUS KYI SGO NAS CHA SNYOM PA YANG SHES PAR BYA'O,,
snga ma.wylie: snga ma gnas mthos pa dang, dmigs pa cung gsal bas gnyid ha cang srab mor song ba la, nor bur gnyid 'thug gi gnas skabs skyed pa'i thig le yod pas, der sems gtad na gnyid srab 'thug snyoms par 'gyur ro, ,de'i rigs pas srod dang, tho rangs kyi dus kyi sgo nas cha snyom pa yang shes par bya'o
snga ma.english: What happened before was that the spot you were using was too high up, or else the visualization was too vivid, which made your sleep too light. Now there is a drop that forms at the jewel when you are sleeping very deeply, and if you focus your mind on it then the relative depth of your sleep will even out. This means, logically, that we can surmise that the relative depth of sleep is even as well, simply due to the time of day, in the evening and at daybreak.

snga ma.acip: LUNG STON LA YANG PHYI MA'I LUNG STON 'GA' RE BDEN PAR SNANG YANG, PHAL MO CHE NGES PA MIN LA, SNGA MA YIN NA RMI LAM GYI DGE SBYOR GYI GNAD GZHAN 'GA' ZHIG DANG, RLUNG BYANG BA'I GNAD 'GA' ZHIG LA BRTEN NAS MI 'KHRUL BA BYA BA'I THABS SHIG YOD PAR SNANG NGO,,
snga ma.wylie: lung ston la yang phyi ma'i lung ston 'ga' re bden par snang yang, phal mo che nges pa min la, snga ma yin na rmi lam gyi dge sbyor gyi gnad gzhan 'ga' zhig dang, rlung byang ba'i gnad 'ga' zhig la brten nas mi 'khrul ba bya ba'i thabs shig yod par snang ngo
snga ma.english: As far as being able to predict the future from dreams, it is true that on occasion you will see something of the future and then it will come true.  With the great majority of these apparent signs of the future though there is no certainty that they will actually occur.  It does though appear to be the case that, when the former happens, it indicates that there is a method of predicting the future in an unerring way, by utilizing certain other keys to the spiritual practice of dreams, and through certain key elements in how you work with your winds.

snga ma.acip: YANG GZHAN DAG SKYE BA SNGA PHYI GNYIS KA'I GZUGS CAN DU BSHAD 'DUG PAS, BAR DO'I ZHAG BDUN GYI PHYED ZHAG PHYED DANG BZHIR SKYE BA SNGA MA'I LUS DBYIBS DANG, DE'I DUS KYI SNANG BA 'BYUNG, ZHAG PHYED DANG BZHIR SKYE BA PHYI MA'I LUS DBYIBS DANG, DE'I DUS KYI SNANG BA 'BYUNG BA DANG,
snga ma.wylie: yang gzhan dag skye ba snga phyi gnyis ka'i gzugs can du bshad 'dug pas, bar do'i zhag bdun gyi phyed zhag phyed dang bzhir skye ba snga ma'i lus dbyibs dang, de'i dus kyi snang ba 'byung, zhag phyed dang bzhir skye ba phyi ma'i lus dbyibs dang, de'i dus kyi snang ba 'byung ba dang
snga ma.english: Still others have described intermediate beings as having both the appearance they had in their last life and the one that they are to take in their next life.  They say that for the first 3� days--that is, for half of seven days--in the intermediate state they have the bodily form of their former life.  Then for the next 3� days they have the bodily form of their next life, and also take on the actual appearance they will have at that time.

snga ma.acip: ZHAG SNGA MA PHYED DANG BZHI SONG BA'I MTSAMS NAS, RANG SHI BA DANG BAR DOR GNAS PA SHES PA YIN ZHES ZER MOD KYANG, KHUNGS RNAM DAG YE MI SNANG ZHING, SGRUB BYED RNAM DAG GZHAN YANG MI 'DUG PAS RTOG BTAGS SO,,
snga ma.wylie: zhag snga ma phyed dang bzhi song ba'i mtshams nas, rang shi ba dang bar dor gnas pa shes pa yin zhes zer mod kyang, khungs rnam dag ye mi snang zhing, sgrub byed rnam dag gzhan yang mi 'dug pas rtog btags so
snga ma.english: They also claim that, when you reach the juncture represented by the end of the first 3� days, you realize that you have died, and that you are living in the intermediate state.  There doesn't appear though to be any authoritative source at all for this idea, and no other compelling evidence for it either, and so it is a simple fabrication.

snga ma.acip: YANG KHA CIG ,SKYE SHI BAR DO LA 'DOD CHAGS SHAS CHE BAS 'DOD CHAGS DANG BSRE BA YIN, RMI LAM BAR DO LA GTI MUG DANG BSRE BA YIN, SRID PA BAR DO LA ZHE SDANG SHAS CHE BAS ZHE SDANG DANG BSRE BA YIN, ZHES ZER BA YANG MI 'THAD PA SNGA MAS RTOGS PAR NUS LA,
snga ma.wylie: yang kha cig ,skye shi bar do la 'dod chags shas che bas 'dod chags dang bsre ba yin, rmi lam bar do la gti mug dang bsre ba yin, srid pa bar do la zhe sdang shas che bas zhe sdang dang bsre ba yin, zhes zer ba yang mi 'thad pa snga mas rtogs par nus la
snga ma.english: Still others have made the following claim.  They say that, since the "intermediate being" between birth and death has a greater part of desire, it represents blending with desire.  And the "intermediate being" in the dream state represents blending with ignorance.  The "intermediate being" of the intermediate state has a greater part of repulsion, and so it represents blending with repulsion.  The fact that this idea is incorrect can be grasped from the previous discussions.

snga ma.acip: YANG MAR PAS MDZAD ZER BA CIG TU, 'DOD CHAGS DANG ZAG MED DU BSRE BA, ZHE SDANG DANG SGYU LUS SU BSRE BA, GTI MUG DANG 'OD GSAL DU BSRE BA 'BYUNG YANG, SNGA MA GNYIS LA YID BRTAN MA SNANG NGO,,
snga ma.wylie: yang mar pas mdzad zer ba cig tu, 'dod chags dang zag med du bsre ba, zhe sdang dang sgyu lus su bsre ba, gti mug dang 'od gsal du bsre ba 'byung yang, snga ma gnyis la yid brtan ma snang ngo
snga ma.english: There is, even further, a book which people claim was written by Lord Marpa which does include the lines-- You blend desire with the immaculate, Repulsion with the body of illusion, And dark ignorance with clear light. But the former two don't appear to be credible.

snga ma.acip: 'DI LA BOD KYI MKHAS PA SNGA MA RNAMS LE LO CAN BAR DOR 'TSANG RGYA BA ZHES PA'I THA SNYAD MDZAD DE, LE LO MED KYANG TSE 'DIR SPYOD PA BYED PA'I YO BYAD MA TSANG BA BAR DOR 'TSANG RGYA BA CIG KYANG YOD PAS, MING DE NI PHYOGS GCIG GIS BTAGS PA'O,,
snga ma.wylie: 'di la bod kyi mkhas pa snga ma rnams le lo can bar dor 'tshang rgya ba zhes pa'i tha snyad mdzad de, le lo med kyang tshe 'dir spyod pa byed pa'i yo byad ma tshang ba bar dor 'tshang rgya ba cig kyang yod pas, ming de ni phyogs gcig gis btags pa'o
snga ma.english: This type of person has been referred to by certain Tibetan masters of the past as the "lazy kind, who reaches enlightenment in the intermediate state."  The point is not that they are really lazy though, just that there are certain individuals who, during the lives they were just in, lacked a full set of the material needs required to become enlightened.  As such, this name applies specifically to a certain group among this first type.

snga ma.acip: TSE 'DIR LAM GOMS PA'I RNAL 'BYOR PA DE MNGAL DU SKYE BAR MA NGES PAS, SKYE GNAS GZHAN GSUM DU YANG SKYE BA 'ONG BAS, SNGAR BZHIN GANG SNANG LHA DANG, LHA SKU SGYU MA DANG, SGYU MA RANG BZHIN GYIS STONG BZHIN DU DER SNANG BA'I DON LA NGES PAR DRANGS NAS, LEGS PAR BSKYANGS NA PHA MA BLA MA YAB YUM DANG, YI DAM YAB YUM DU SGOM PA SOGS KYANG SNGA MA'I NANG DU LHAG DANG BCAS PA 'ONG BAR SNANG BAS DE BZHIN DU BYA'O,,
snga ma.wylie: tshe 'dir lam goms pa'i rnal 'byor pa de mngal du skye bar ma nges pas, skye gnas gzhan gsum du yang skye ba 'ong bas, sngar bzhin gang snang lha dang, lha sku sgyu ma dang, sgyu ma rang bzhin gyis stong bzhin du der snang ba'i don la nges par drangs nas, legs par bskyangs na pha ma bla ma yab yum dang, yi dam yab yum du sgom pa sogs kyang snga ma'i nang du lhag dang bcas pa 'ong bar snang bas de bzhin du bya'o
snga ma.english: Now it is no certain thing that a deep practitioner who has practiced the path in this life is going to take rebirth in a womb: any one of the other three ways of taking birth is also something that could happen.  As such it is important, ahead of time, to reach a deep understanding of how everyone who appears to you is an Angel; and how the body of an Angel is illusory; and how the point of the illusion is that--even though these things have no nature of their own--they appear as though they did.  It would seem that, if you were really able to maintain all this well, then you could see your father and mother as the holy Lama man and wife, or as close Angel man and wife, or as anything of the like: and you'd be even better off than before.

snga ma.acip: DE LA GOMS PA MANG DU BYAS PA LA BRTEN NAS, SGYU MA'I SKU SGRUB DGOS PAS, 'DIR 'OD GSAL SNGA MA DE LAS KHYAD PAR DU GYUR PA CIG SPYOD DGOS SO, ,DE YANG SGYU MA'I LUS DNGOS SAM RJES MTHUN PA'I RTEN CIG LA BRTEN NAS 'OD GSAL DU 'JUG PA CIG YIN NO,,
snga ma.wylie: de la goms pa mang du byas pa la brten nas, sgyu ma'i sku sgrub dgos pas, 'dir 'od gsal snga ma de las khyad par du gyur pa cig spyod dgos so, ,de yang sgyu ma'i lus dngos sam rjes mthun pa'i rten cig la brten nas 'od gsal du 'jug pa cig yin no
snga ma.english: And since it is the case that one must master this kind of clear light through constant practice if one hopes to attain the illusory body, then one must obviously be practicing a clear light which is far more extraordinary than the kinds we've just described.  There is moreover a practice where one enters into clear light based on a mental and physical configuration involving either an actual or an approximate illusory body.

snga ma.acip: DANG POR GNYID KYI 'OD GSAL 'DZIN PA LA PHAL CHE BAS GNYID 'THUG DRAGS NA ZIN DKA' LA, CUNG SRAB NA 'DZIN SLA BAS DANG PO'I DUS SU NI, PHYI MA LTAR BYAS LA, GOMS NAS BRTAN PA NA SNGA MA LTAR BYA STE, GNYID GCOG PA NI MI DGOS SO, ,'ON KYANG GNYID SHIN TU 'THUG PA LA AE ZIN LTA 'DOD NA NI, DE LTAR YANG BYA'O,,
snga ma.wylie: dang por gnyid kyi 'od gsal 'dzin pa la phal che bas gnyid 'thug drags na zin dka' la, cung srab na 'dzin sla bas dang po'i dus su ni, phyi ma ltar byas la, goms nas brtan pa na snga ma ltar bya ste, gnyid gcog pa ni mi dgos so, ,'on kyang gnyid shin tu 'thug pa la ae zin lta 'dod na ni, de ltar yang bya'o
snga ma.english: When people are first trying to learn to recognize the clear light in their sleep, the majority find it difficult to do so when their sleep is too deep.  If your sleep is a little lighter though it can be easier; and so in the beginning you should follow the latter system.  When though you have gotten good at the practice and it is very stable, then you can go on to the former system, except that it's not necessary to interrupt your sleep.  If though your sleep is very sound and you have doubts about whether you will be able to attain recognition, and you think it may help, then you can try this too.

snga ma.acip: 'DI'I 'DAB MA LA AA NU TA RA 'GOD PA DANG MI 'GOD PA'I LUGS GNYIS SNANG BA LA, SNGA MA'I LUGS KYIS SHAR GYI 'DAB MA LA AA, LHOR NU, NUB TU TA, BYANG DU RA BKOD NAS GNYID DU 'GRO LA KHAD PA NA, AA LA SEMS GTOD,
snga ma.wylie: 'di'i 'dab ma la aa nu ta ra 'god pa dang mi 'god pa'i lugs gnyis snang ba la, snga ma'i lugs kyis shar gyi 'dab ma la aa, lhor nu, nub tu ta, byang du ra bkod nas gnyid du 'gro la khad pa na, aa la sems gtod
snga ma.english: At this point we find two different versions; with one, you place the syllables ah, nu, ta and ra on the petals of the lotus--in the other, you do not.  In the former version you position the ah on the eastern petal, nu on the southern, ta on the western, ra on the northern.  Just as you are about to fall off to sleep, you focus your mind on the ah.

In the former version you position the ah on the eastern petal, nu on the southern, ta on the western, ra on the northern.  Just as you are about to fall off to sleep, you focus your mind on the ah."}

snga ma.acip: DE LA SAD DUS SU SROG DH'U T'IR SDUD PA SOGS NUS PA ZHIG GIS, GNYID DU 'GRO KHAR SNGAR BSHAD PA LTAR, SNYING KHA'I DH'U T'I'I NANG DU DMIGS PA GTAD NAS BSKYANGS NA, DGE SBYOR SNGA MA'I GNAD KYIS RLUNG SNYING KHA'I DBU MA'I NANG DU 'DU BAR SHIN TU SLA BA ZHAG 'ONG NGO,,
snga ma.wylie: de la sad dus su srog dhU tIr sdud pa sogs nus pa zhig gis, gnyid du 'gro khar sngar bshad pa ltar, snying kha'i dhU tI'i nang du dmigs pa gtad nas bskyangs na, dge sbyor snga ma'i gnad kyis rlung snying kha'i dbu ma'i nang du 'du bar shin tu sla ba zhag 'ong ngo
snga ma.english: Suppose then that a person has been able during their waking hours to gather the life winds into the channel of dance does the meditation we described before as they fall off to sleep.  If they focus their mind upon the meditation object in the channel of dance as they do fall off, and maintain this focus, then--due to the crucial point of the spiritual practices they have undertaken previously--getting the winds to gather within the central channel at the heart is something that comes to them with great ease.

snga ma.acip: DE LA PHUNG PO LA SOGS PA NI ZHES PA NI, RAGS PA'I PHUNG SOGS KYI SNANG BA, KHAMS PHRA BA ZHES PA RLUNG LA THIM PA'I DUS YIN TE, SA CHU ME GSUM SNGA MA PHYI MA LA THIM NAS, ME RLUNG LA THIM PA'I DUS SO,,
snga ma.wylie: de la phung po la sogs pa ni zhes pa ni, rags pa'i phung sogs kyi snang ba, khams phra ba zhes pa rlung la thim pa'i dus yin te, sa chu me gsum snga ma phyi ma la thim nas, me rlung la thim pa'i dus so
snga ma.english: Now the phrase "heaps and such" in the quotation refers to the appearance of your gross heaps and so on.  The "subtle element" is a reference to that point in time when the dissolution into the element of wind is occurring: it refers to the point where--once each preceding element of the three of earth, water, and fire has dissolved into the next--the fire is now dissolving into the element of wind.

snga ma.acip: DUS 'DIR ZHES PA NI GNYID KYI DUS SO, ,SEMS GSUM RAB TU ZHUGS PA NI SNGA MA PHYI MA LA ZHUGS PA'O, ,DE GSUM GYI GSUM PA'I DUS NI DRAN PA NYAMS PA'O, ,PHYIS NI ZHES PA NI NYER THOB KYI RJES THOGS SU'O,,
snga ma.wylie: dus 'dir zhes pa ni gnyid kyi dus so, ,sems gsum rab tu zhugs pa ni snga ma phyi ma la zhugs pa'o, ,de gsum gyi gsum pa'i dus ni dran pa nyams pa'o, ,phyis ni zhes pa ni nyer thob kyi rjes thogs su'o
snga ma.english: The phrase "during this time" in the quotation refers to the sleeping period.  The three states of mind being "finally entered" means when each previous one has gone into each succeeding me.  And in the third of these three, you lose consciousness.  "Later on" means subsequent to the stage of attainment.

The three states of mind being \"finally entered\" means when each previous one has gone into each succeeding me.  And in the third of these three, you lose consciousness.  \"Later on\" means subsequent to the stage of attainment."}

snga ma.acip: YANG RGAS PAS SHIN TU SDUG BSNGAL BAR MTHONG BA DANG, NAD DRAG PO'I SDUG BSNGAL MA BZOD NAS 'PHO BA BYED NA, SNGAR BZHIN DU BYA MI RUNG BAR GSUNGS PAS, 'DI'I GDAMS NGAG KHA CIG TU SNGA MA LA 'PHO BA BYA, ZHES PA NI PHYIN CI LOG TU SMRA BA CHEN PO'O,,
snga ma.wylie: yang rgas pas shin tu sdug bsngal bar mthong ba dang, nad drag po'i sdug bsngal ma bzod nas 'pho ba byed na, sngar bzhin du bya mi rung bar gsungs pas, 'di'i gdams ngag kha cig tu snga ma la 'pho ba bya, zhes pa ni phyin ci log tu smra ba chen po'o
snga ma.english: Now some people, following this former statement, have asserted that it is wrong for an elderly person who is experiencing great pain, or a person who can no longer tolerate suffering some serious illness, to turn to the practice of sending on their consciousness.  And so we see in certain books of advices on the practice the statement that "sending on our consciousness can only be done before."  This though is an incredibly twisted position.

And so we see in certain books of advices on the practice the statement that \"sending on our consciousness can only be done before.\"  This though is an incredibly twisted position."}

snga ma.acip: YANG PHYIR DBAB LA SNYING KHAR H'Um DANG, LTE BAR AA GNAS PAR BSAM, ZHES 'BYUNG BAS, YAR RES AA H'Um LA THIM PAR BSAM ZHES ZER YANG SNGA MA LTAR BYAS NA BDE'O,,
snga ma.wylie: yang phyir dbab la snying khar hUM dang, lte bar aa gnas par bsam, zhes 'byung bas, yar res aa hUM la thim par bsam zhes zer yang snga ma ltar byas na bde'o
snga ma.english: There is a statement in scripture that we should "bring it back down, seeing the hung staying at the heart, and the ah at the navel."  Based on this, some have said that each time up we should see the ah melt into the hung; but the fact is that if you do it the first way we described it the practice is easier.

snga ma.acip: MA THUB PA DANG NANG DU DAL BUS RNGUB, YANG PHYIR 'GRO DUS SNGA MA LTAR BYA'O, ,DE LTAR YANG YANG BSGOMS PAS, 'BYONGS PA'I RTAGS THED {@ms THOD?} PA 'GUL BA DANG, 'TSAG PA DANG 'PHAR BA SOGS 'BYUNG NGO,,
snga ma.wylie: ma thub pa dang nang du dal bus rngub, yang phyir 'gro dus snga ma ltar bya'o, ,de ltar yang yang bsgoms pas, 'byongs pa'i rtags thed {@MS thod?} pa 'gul ba dang, 'tshag pa dang 'phar ba sogs 'byung ngo
snga ma.english: When you feel that you can hold the retention no longer, then inhale gently.  When the breath is ready again to exit, follow the same steps as before.  Some signs that you are becoming proficient are that the skullcup will begin to shift on its own, or drip, or rise up.

snga ma.acip: DE'I PHYIR 'DI NAS RNAM SHES 'THON NAS PHA ROL GYI GRONG DU MA ZHUGS PA'I BAR YOD KYANG, BAR SRID MTSAN NYID PA'ANG MIN NO, ,DES NA LUS SNGA MA LA BRTEN PA'I CHOS KYI DRAN PA LA SOGS PA SNGA MA DOR BA'I RGYU MTSAN GYIS NYAMS PA YANG MED DO,,
snga ma.wylie: de'i phyir 'di nas rnam shes 'thon nas pha rol gyi grong du ma zhugs pa'i bar yod kyang, bar srid mtshan nyid pa'ang min no, ,des na lus snga ma la brten pa'i chos kyi dran pa la sogs pa snga ma dor ba'i rgyu mtshan gyis nyams pa yang med do
snga ma.english: As such, we can say as well that--even though there is some period here between the time that our consciousness exits our old body and the time that it enters the city--neither is there any real "being during the time between death and rebirth."  And therefore it is not the case either that we have failed in our vows, with regard to our previous body, by rejecting our earlier spiritual intentions, or anything of the like.

snga ma.acip: 'DI'I KA DPE RTZA BA'I SDOM SNGA MA YIN ZER BA DANG, KA DPE PHYI MA YIN ZER BA GNYIS 'DUG PA'I SNGA MA LA, MI MTHUN PA CHER YOD PA GNYIS SNANG ZHING, PHYI MA LA MAR PAS MDZAD PA YIN ZER BA'I 'GREL PA CIG KYANG SNANG MOD KYANG, 'DUS PA'I MAN NGAG MAR PAS MDZAD ZER BA SOGS KHA GA-YAR MANG PO SNANG BAS, MTHA' CIG TU YID CHES PA DKA' BAR SNANG NGO,,
snga ma.wylie: 'di'i ka dpe rtsa ba'i sdom snga ma yin zer ba dang, ka dpe phyi ma yin zer ba gnyis 'dug pa'i snga ma la, mi mthun pa cher yod pa gnyis snang zhing, phyi ma la mar pas mdzad pa yin zer ba'i 'grel pa cig kyang snang mod kyang, 'dus pa'i man ngag mar pas mdzad zer ba sogs kha ga-yar mang po snang bas, mtha' cig tu yid ches pa dka' bar snang ngo
snga ma.english: Now we see two versions of the original treatise for this work, the "root summary." One is referred to as the "earlier," and the other the "later." The earlier has a great number of inconsistencies. We further do admittedly see a commentary to the later version that people say was written by Marpa; but given that you hear so many wild statements--such as that the advices on the Secret Collection were written by Marpa--it seems difficult to say that we can believe this unequivocally.

snga ma.acip: N'A RO'I CHOS DRUG GI GTUM MO'I SKOR RLUNG DBU MAR THOG MAR BSDU BA LA'ANG MED THABS MED, 'DI NYID GTZO BO KYEE RDOR NAS GSUNGS PA'I MAN NGAG YIN YANG ZAB DRAGS SHING BYIN RLABS KYI TSAN KHA CHE PA'I DBANG GIS DAM PA SNGA MA TSOS BDE GSANG 'JIGS GSUM SOGS KYI RDZOGS RIM LA SBYAR BAR MDZAD,
snga ma.wylie: nA ro'i chos drug gi gtum mo'i skor rlung dbu mar thog mar bsdu ba la'ang med thabs med, 'di nyid gtso bo kyee rdor nas gsungs pa'i man ngag yin yang zab drags shing byin rlabs kyi tshan kha che pa'i dbang gis dam pa snga ma tshos bde gsang 'jigs gsum sogs kyi rdzogs rim la sbyar bar mdzad
snga ma.english: The various points on the practice of inner heat from the Six Practices of Naropa are also something that you cannot do without as you first practice to gather the inner winds into the central channel.  This in itself is principally an instruction that originated in the teachings of Lo Diamond, but because it was so extremely profound, and had such a tremendously powerful blessing, holy Lamas of the past applied it as well to the presentations of the stage of completion in the three secret teachings of Highest Bliss, the Secret Collection, and Frightener, among others.

This in itself is principally an instruction that originated in the teachings of Lo Diamond, but because it was so extremely profound, and had such a tremendously powerful blessing, holy Lamas of the past applied it as well to the presentations of the stage of completion in the three secret teachings of Highest Bliss, the Secret Collection, and Frightener, among others."}

snga ma.acip: TSE 'DIR LAM GOMS PA'I RNAL 'BYOR PA DE MNGAL DU SKYE BAR MA NGES PAS, SKYE GNAS GZHAN GSUM DU YANG SKYE BA 'ONG BAS, SNGAR BZHIN GANG SNANG LHA DANG, LHA SKU SGYU MA DANG, SGYU MA RANG BZHIN GYIS STONG BZHIN DU DER SNANG BA'I DON LA NGES PAR DRANGS NAS, LEGS PAR BSKYANGS NA PHA MA BLA MA YAB YUM DANG, YI DAM YAB YUM DU SGOM PA SOGS KYANG SNGA MA'I NANG DU LHAG DANG BCAS PA 'ONG BAR SNANG BAS DE BZHIN DU BYA'O,,
snga ma.wylie: tshe 'dir lam goms pa'i rnal 'byor pa de mngal du skye bar ma nges pas, skye gnas gzhan gsum du yang skye ba 'ong bas, sngar bzhin gang snang lha dang, lha sku sgyu ma dang, sgyu ma rang bzhin gyis stong bzhin du der snang ba'i don la nges par drangs nas, legs par bskyangs na pha ma bla ma yab yum dang, yi dam yab yum du sgom pa sogs kyang snga ma'i nang du lhag dang bcas pa 'ong bar snang bas de bzhin du bya'o
snga ma.english: Now it is no certain thing that a deep practitioner who has practiced the path in this life is going to take rebirth in a womb: any one of the other three ways of taking birth is also something that could happen.  As such it is important, ahead of time, to reach a deep understanding of how everyone who appears to you is an Angel; and how the body of an Angel is illusory; and how the point of the illusion is that--even though these things have no nature of their own--they appear as though they did.  It would seem that, if you were really able to maintain all this well, then you could see your father and mother as the holy Lama man and wife, or as close Angel man and wife, or as anything of the like: and you'd be even better off than before.

snga ma.acip: DE LA GOMS PA MANG DU BYAS PA LA BRTEN NAS, SGYU MA'I SKU SGRUB DGOS PAS, 'DIR 'OD GSAL SNGA MA DE LAS KHYAD PAR DU GYUR PA CIG SPYOD DGOS SO, ,DE YANG SGYU MA'I LUS DNGOS SAM RJES MTHUN PA'I RTEN CIG LA BRTEN NAS 'OD GSAL DU 'JUG PA CIG YIN NO,,
snga ma.wylie: de la goms pa mang du byas pa la brten nas, sgyu ma'i sku sgrub dgos pas, 'dir 'od gsal snga ma de las khyad par du gyur pa cig spyod dgos so, ,de yang sgyu ma'i lus dngos sam rjes mthun pa'i rten cig la brten nas 'od gsal du 'jug pa cig yin no
snga ma.english: And since it is the case that one must master this kind of clear light through constant practice if one hopes to attain the illusory body, then one must obviously be practicing a clear light which is far more extraordinary than the kinds we've just described.  There is moreover a practice where one enters into clear light based on a mental and physical configuration involving either an actual or an approximate illusory body.

There is moreover a practice where one enters into clear light based on a mental and physical configuration involving either an actual or an approximate illusory body."}

snga ma.acip: DANG POR GNYID KYI 'OD GSAL 'DZIN PA LA PHAL CHE BAS GNYID 'THUG DRAGS NA ZIN DKA' LA, CUNG SRAB NA 'DZIN SLA BAS DANG PO'I DUS SU NI, PHYI MA LTAR BYAS LA, GOMS NAS BRTAN PA NA SNGA MA LTAR BYA STE, GNYID GCOG PA NI MI DGOS SO, ,'ON KYANG GNYID SHIN TU 'THUG PA LA AE ZIN LTA 'DOD NA NI, DE LTAR YANG BYA'O,,
snga ma.wylie: dang por gnyid kyi 'od gsal 'dzin pa la phal che bas gnyid 'thug drags na zin dka' la, cung srab na 'dzin sla bas dang po'i dus su ni, phyi ma ltar byas la, goms nas brtan pa na snga ma ltar bya ste, gnyid gcog pa ni mi dgos so, ,'on kyang gnyid shin tu 'thug pa la ae zin lta 'dod na ni, de ltar yang bya'o
snga ma.english: When people are first trying to learn to recognize the clear light in their sleep, the majority find it difficult to do so when their sleep is too deep.  If your sleep is a little lighter though it can be easier; and so in the beginning you should follow the latter system.  When though you have gotten good at the practice and it is very stable, then you can go on to the former system, except that it's not necessary to interrupt your sleep.  If though your sleep is very sound and you have doubts about whether you will be able to attain recognition, and you think it may help, then you can try this too.

snga ma.acip: 'DI'I 'DAB MA LA AA NU TA RA 'GOD PA DANG MI 'GOD PA'I LUGS GNYIS SNANG BA LA, SNGA MA'I LUGS KYIS SHAR GYI 'DAB MA LA AA, LHOR NU, NUB TU TA, BYANG DU RA BKOD NAS GNYID DU 'GRO LA KHAD PA NA, AA LA SEMS GTOD,
snga ma.wylie: 'di'i 'dab ma la aa nu ta ra 'god pa dang mi 'god pa'i lugs gnyis snang ba la, snga ma'i lugs kyis shar gyi 'dab ma la aa, lhor nu, nub tu ta, byang du ra bkod nas gnyid du 'gro la khad pa na, aa la sems gtod
snga ma.english: At this point we find two different versions; with one, you place the syllables ah, nu, ta and ra on the petals of the lotus--in the other, you do not.  In the former version you position the ah on the eastern petal, nu on the southern, ta on the western, ra on the northern.  Just as you are about to fall off to sleep, you focus your mind on the ah.

Just as you are about to fall off to sleep, you focus your mind on the ah."}

snga ma.acip: DE LA SAD DUS SU SROG DH'U T'IR SDUD PA SOGS NUS PA ZHIG GIS, GNYID DU 'GRO KHAR SNGAR BSHAD PA LTAR, SNYING KHA'I DH'U T'I'I NANG DU DMIGS PA GTAD NAS BSKYANGS NA, DGE SBYOR SNGA MA'I GNAD KYIS RLUNG SNYING KHA'I DBU MA'I NANG DU 'DU BAR SHIN TU SLA BA ZHAG 'ONG NGO,,
snga ma.wylie: de la sad dus su srog dhU tIr sdud pa sogs nus pa zhig gis, gnyid du 'gro khar sngar bshad pa ltar, snying kha'i dhU tI'i nang du dmigs pa gtad nas bskyangs na, dge sbyor snga ma'i gnad kyis rlung snying kha'i dbu ma'i nang du 'du bar shin tu sla ba zhag 'ong ngo
snga ma.english: Suppose then that a person has been able during their waking hours to gather the life winds into the channel of dance does the meditation we described before as they fall off to sleep.  If they focus their mind upon the meditation object in the channel of dance as they do fall off, and maintain this focus, then--due to the crucial point of the spiritual practices they have undertaken previously--getting the winds to gather within the central channel at the heart is something that comes to them with great ease.

snga ma.acip: DE LA PHUNG PO LA SOGS PA NI ZHES PA NI, RAGS PA'I PHUNG SOGS KYI SNANG BA, KHAMS PHRA BA ZHES PA RLUNG LA THIM PA'I DUS YIN TE, SA CHU ME GSUM SNGA MA PHYI MA LA THIM NAS, ME RLUNG LA THIM PA'I DUS SO,,
snga ma.wylie: de la phung po la sogs pa ni zhes pa ni, rags pa'i phung sogs kyi snang ba, khams phra ba zhes pa rlung la thim pa'i dus yin te, sa chu me gsum snga ma phyi ma la thim nas, me rlung la thim pa'i dus so
snga ma.english: Now the phrase "heaps and such" in the quotation refers to the appearance of your gross heaps and so on.  The "subtle element" is a reference to that point in time when the dissolution into the element of wind is occurring: it refers to the point where--once each preceding element of the three of earth, water, and fire has dissolved into the next--the fire is now dissolving into the element of wind.

snga ma.acip: DUS 'DIR ZHES PA NI GNYID KYI DUS SO, ,SEMS GSUM RAB TU ZHUGS PA NI SNGA MA PHYI MA LA ZHUGS PA'O, ,DE GSUM GYI GSUM PA'I DUS NI DRAN PA NYAMS PA'O, ,PHYIS NI ZHES PA NI NYER THOB KYI RJES THOGS SU'O,,
snga ma.wylie: dus 'dir zhes pa ni gnyid kyi dus so, ,sems gsum rab tu zhugs pa ni snga ma phyi ma la zhugs pa'o, ,de gsum gyi gsum pa'i dus ni dran pa nyams pa'o, ,phyis ni zhes pa ni nyer thob kyi rjes thogs su'o
snga ma.english: The phrase "during this time" in the quotation refers to the sleeping period.  The three states of mind being "finally entered" means when each previous one has gone into each succeeding me.  And in the third of these three, you lose consciousness.  "Later on" means subsequent to the stage of attainment.

snga ma.acip: YANG RGAS PAS SHIN TU SDUG BSNGAL BAR MTHONG BA DANG, NAD DRAG PO'I SDUG BSNGAL MA BZOD NAS 'PHO BA BYED NA, SNGAR BZHIN DU BYA MI RUNG BAR GSUNGS PAS, 'DI'I GDAMS NGAG KHA CIG TU SNGA MA LA 'PHO BA BYA, ZHES PA NI PHYIN CI LOG TU SMRA BA CHEN PO'O,,
snga ma.wylie: yang rgas pas shin tu sdug bsngal bar mthong ba dang, nad drag po'i sdug bsngal ma bzod nas 'pho ba byed na, sngar bzhin du bya mi rung bar gsungs pas, 'di'i gdams ngag kha cig tu snga ma la 'pho ba bya, zhes pa ni phyin ci log tu smra ba chen po'o
snga ma.english: Now some people, following this former statement, have asserted that it is wrong for an elderly person who is experiencing great pain, or a person who can no longer tolerate suffering some serious illness, to turn to the practice of sending on their consciousness.  And so we see in certain books of advices on the practice the statement that "sending on our consciousness can only be done before."  This though is an incredibly twisted position.

snga ma.acip: YANG PHYIR DBAB LA SNYING KHAR H'Um DANG, LTE BAR AA GNAS PAR BSAM, ZHES 'BYUNG BAS, YAR RES AA H'Um LA THIM PAR BSAM ZHES ZER YANG SNGA MA LTAR BYAS NA BDE'O,,
snga ma.wylie: yang phyir dbab la snying khar hUM dang, lte bar aa gnas par bsam, zhes 'byung bas, yar res aa hUM la thim par bsam zhes zer yang snga ma ltar byas na bde'o
snga ma.english: There is a statement in scripture that we should "bring it back down, seeing the hung staying at the heart, and the ah at the navel."  Based on this, some have said that each time up we should see the ah melt into the hung; but the fact is that if you do it the first way we described it the practice is easier.

snga ma.acip: MA THUB PA DANG NANG DU DAL BUS RNGUB, YANG PHYIR 'GRO DUS SNGA MA LTAR BYA'O, ,DE LTAR YANG YANG BSGOMS PAS, 'BYONGS PA'I RTAGS THOD PA 'GUL BA DANG, 'TSAG PA DANG 'PHAR BA SOGS 'BYUNG NGO,,
snga ma.wylie: ma thub pa dang nang du dal bus rngub, yang phyir 'gro dus snga ma ltar bya'o, ,de ltar yang yang bsgoms pas, 'byongs pa'i rtags thod pa 'gul ba dang, 'tshag pa dang 'phar ba sogs 'byung ngo
snga ma.english: When you feel that you can hold the retention no longer, then inhale gently.  When the breath is ready again to exit, follow the same steps as before.  Some signs that you are becoming proficient are that the skullcup will begin to shift on its own, or drip, or rise up.

When the breath is ready again to exit, follow the same steps as before.  Some signs that you are becoming proficient are that the skullcup will begin to shift on its own, or drip, or rise up."}

snga ma.acip: DE'I PHYIR 'DI NAS RNAM SHES 'THON NAS PHA ROL GYI GRONG DU MA ZHUGS PA'I BAR YOD KYANG, BAR SRID MTSAN NYID PA'ANG MIN NO, ,DES NA LUS SNGA MA LA BRTEN PA'I CHOS KYI DRAN PA LA SOGS PA SNGA MA DOR BA'I RGYU MTSAN GYIS NYAMS PA YANG MED DO,,
snga ma.wylie: de'i phyir 'di nas rnam shes 'thon nas pha rol gyi grong du ma zhugs pa'i bar yod kyang, bar srid mtshan nyid pa'ang min no, ,des na lus snga ma la brten pa'i chos kyi dran pa la sogs pa snga ma dor ba'i rgyu mtshan gyis nyams pa yang med do
snga ma.english: As such, we can say as well that--even though there is some period here between the time that our consciousness exits our old body and the time that it enters the city--neither is there any real "being during the time between death and rebirth."  And therefore it is not the case either that we have failed in our vows, with regard to our previous body, by rejecting our earlier spiritual intentions, or anything of the like.

snga ma.acip: 'DI'I KA DPE RTZA BA'I SDOM SNGA MA YIN ZER BA DANG, KA DPE PHYI MA YIN ZER BA GNYIS 'DUG PA'I SNGA MA LA, MI MTHUN PA CHER YOD PA GNYIS SNANG ZHING, PHYI MA LA MAR PAS MDZAD PA YIN ZER BA'I 'GREL PA CIG KYANG SNANG MOD KYANG, 'DUS PA'I MAN NGAG MAR PAS MDZAD ZER BA SOGS KHA GA-YAR MANG PO SNANG BAS, MTHA' CIG TU YID CHES PA DKA' BAR SNANG NGO,,
snga ma.wylie: 'di'i ka dpe rtsa ba'i sdom snga ma yin zer ba dang, ka dpe phyi ma yin zer ba gnyis 'dug pa'i snga ma la, mi mthun pa cher yod pa gnyis snang zhing, phyi ma la mar pas mdzad pa yin zer ba'i 'grel pa cig kyang snang mod kyang, 'dus pa'i man ngag mar pas mdzad zer ba sogs kha ga-yar mang po snang bas, mtha' cig tu yid ches pa dka' bar snang ngo
snga ma.english: Now we see two versions of the original treatise for this work, the "root summary." One is referred to as the "earlier," and the other the "later." The earlier has a great number of inconsistencies. We further do admittedly see a commentary to the later version that people say was written by Marpa; but given that you hear so many wild statements--such as that the advices on the Secret Collection were written by Marpa--it seems difficult to say that we can believe this unequivocally.

snga ma.acip: SNGA MA GANG DU GSUNGS PA'I RGYUD DER NI PHYI MA GNYIS KYANG GSUNGS LA, NANG GI LUS LA GNAD DU BSNUN PA'I THABS GSUNGS PA'I RGYUD DER YANG PHYAG RGYA GNYIS DANG MNYAM PAR SBYOR BA YANG GSUNG PA YIN TE,
snga ma.wylie: snga ma gang du gsungs pa'i rgyud der ni phyi ma gnyis kyang gsungs la, nang gi lus la gnad du bsnun pa'i thabs gsungs pa'i rgyud der yang phyag rgya gnyis dang mnyam par sbyor ba yang gsung pa yin te
snga ma.english: Secret teachings which do mention the former though also mention the latter; and teachings of this kind which describe the method of working at crucial points of our inner body also describe how we undertake the act of union with the two different kinds of partners.

snga ma.acip: PHAR PHYIN GYI THEG CHEN DU PHYAG RGYA'I SBYOR BA LA BRTEN NAS MI BSGOM YANG STONG NYID BSGOMS PAS ZHI MTHAR MI LTUNG BA NI BSOD NAMS KYI TSOGS KYI DBYE BA MTHA' YAS PA'I RGYA CHEN PO LA BSLABS PA'I DBANG GIS YIN LA, DE LTAR SLOB NA'ANG ZAB PA DANG RGYA CHE BA GNYIS KYI NANG NAS SNGA MA LA GTZO BOR MI SLOB KYI PHYI MA LA GTZO BOR SLOB PA YANG ZHI BA'I MTHAR LTUNG BA 'GOG PA'I PHYIR YIN NO,,
snga ma.wylie: phar phyin gyi theg chen du phyag rgya'i sbyor ba la brten nas mi bsgom yang stong nyid bsgoms pas zhi mthar mi ltung ba ni bsod nams kyi tshogs kyi dbye ba mtha' yas pa'i rgya chen po la bslabs pa'i dbang gis yin la, de ltar slob na'ang zab pa dang rgya che ba gnyis kyi nang nas snga ma la gtso bor mi slob kyi phyi ma la gtso bor slob pa yang zhi ba'i mthar ltung ba 'gog pa'i phyir yin no
snga ma.english: Now in the greater way of the open teachings of the perfections, we never do our practice using union with a spiritual partner; the fact that we do meditate on voidness and still manage to avoid the extreme of a lower peace here is due to the fact that we have trained ourselves in the "widespread" practices--in infinite forms of the methods used to amass the collection of merit.  There is that classical division into the profound side of the teachings and the widespread side of them; and the very fact that one is in that path trained primarily in the latter, rather than the former, is aimed at preventing one from falling into the extreme of a lower peace.

snga ma.acip: DKON BRTZEGS KYI LUNG SNGA MAS BYANG SEMS KYI NYON MONGS 'GA' ZHIG GIS SANGS RGYAS KYI CHOS SKYED PAR BSTAN PAS, NYON MONGS GANG YIN GYIS SANGS RGYAS THOB PA LA GEGS MI BYED PAR BSTAN LA,
snga ma.wylie: dkon brtsegs kyi lung snga mas byang sems kyi nyon mongs 'ga' zhig gis sangs rgyas kyi chos skyed par bstan pas, nyon mongs gang yin gyis sangs rgyas thob pa la gegs mi byed par bstan la
snga ma.english: The point of the first part of the quotation from the Mountain of Jewels is to say that certain of the mental afflictions that a bodhisattva has can be used to help produce the qualities of an enlightened being.  As such, the quotation is indicating, it's not the case that every kind of mental affliction acts as an obstacle to attaining enlightenment.

snga ma.acip: DER MA ZAD, SLOB PA'I ZUNG 'JUG PAS LAS RGYA LA BRTEN PAR BSHAD PA YANG MI 'THAD PAR THAL TE, DES NYON MONGS SPANGS ZIN PAS CHAGS PA DANG GTAN NAS BRAL ZIN PA'I PHYIR RO, ,DES NA LUGS SNGA MA NYID 'THAD PAR SEMS SO,,
snga ma.wylie: der ma zad, slob pa'i zung 'jug pas las rgya la brten par bshad pa yang mi 'thad par thal te, des nyon mongs spangs zin pas chags pa dang gtan nas bral zin pa'i phyir ro, ,des na lugs snga ma nyid 'thad par sems so
snga ma.english: Not only that, but all the explanations we see that a person at the point of the Union of the Two where we are still learning practices with an actual partner would all have to be incorrect as well; since by that juncture they would have already eliminated within them all the mental afflictions, they would of course already have reached a state completely free of desire.  As such, it is my belief that the former of the two original positions is the correct one.

snga ma.acip: PHYAG RGYA LA 'DEBS BYED DANG GDAB BYA DANG, BTAB PA GSUM YOD PA LAS, SNGA MA LTAR NA GDAB GNAS DE DANG, PHYI MA LTAR NA DANG PO GNYIS CI RIGS SU SBYAR RO,,
snga ma.wylie: phyag rgya la 'debs byed dang gdab bya dang, btab pa gsum yod pa las, snga ma ltar na gdab gnas de dang, phyi ma ltar na dang po gnyis ci rigs su sbyar ro
snga ma.english: With relation to a seal or mudra then we can say that there are three elements: what does the pressing of the seal, what is pressed for the seal, and the action of pressing the seal.  In the former explanation our partner is the place where the seal is applied; in the latter, you could say it was either one of the first two elements. * * * We see a similar explanation in a text by His Holiness the First Panchen Lama entitled The Essence of the Ocean of Attainments: An Explanation of the Creation Stage of the Glorious Secret Collection (Guhya Samaja), King of All the Secret Teachings (ACIP digital text S00265, f. 63a):

In the former explanation our partner is the place where the seal is applied; in the latter, you could say it was either one of the first two elements. * * * We see a similar explanation in a text by His Holiness the First Panchen Lama entitled The Essence of the Ocean of Attainments: An Explanation of the Creation Stage of the Glorious Secret Collection (Guhya Samaja), King of All the Secret Teachings (ACIP digital text S00265, f. 63a):"}

snga ma.acip: BDE BA CHEN PO 'DREN PA'I THABS RLUNG DBU MA'I NANG DU ZHUGS GNAS THIM GSUM BYED PA'I RKYEN LA, NANG GI RKYEN NI RDOR BZLAS DANG BUM PA CAN LTA BU'I RLUNG SBYONG BYED PA DANG, RTZA DBU MA'I GNAD CHE SAR THIG LE SOGS LA DMIGS PA GTAD NAS BSGOM PA DU MA YOD KYANG 'DIR NI SNGA MA GNYIS SO,,
snga ma.wylie: bde ba chen po 'dren pa'i thabs rlung dbu ma'i nang du zhugs gnas thim gsum byed pa'i rkyen la, nang gi rkyen ni rdor bzlas dang bum pa can lta bu'i rlung sbyong byed pa dang, rtsa dbu ma'i gnad che sar thig le sogs la dmigs pa gtad nas bsgom pa du ma yod kyang 'dir ni snga ma gnyis so
snga ma.english: As for methods of bringing on this great bliss, there are certain aids which help us to take the inner winds through this three-fold process of entering, staying, and dissolving in the central channel.  Here first there are inner aids; there are many forms of them, including practices for working with the inner winds such as the Recitation of Diamond and holding the capsule--as well as meditations where we focus the mind upon inner drops and the like at particularly crucial points of the central channel.  Here though [in the teachings of the Wheel of Time] we use the former two.

snga ma.acip: DE LTAR PHYI ROL GYI BUD MED MA RNYED NA YE RGYA LA BRTEN PAR BSHAD PA NI, YE RGYAS PHYI'I BUD MED BSTEN PA LTAR GYI BDE BA CHEN PO'I TING NGE 'DZIN BSKYED MI NUS PA YIN LA, PHYI'I BUD MED RNYED KYANG DE SPANGS NAS YE RGYA LA BRTEN PAR GSUNGS PA NI SNGA MA LAS BZLOG PA LA DGONGS SO,,
snga ma.wylie: de ltar phyi rol gyi bud med ma rnyed na ye rgya la brten par bshad pa ni, ye rgyas phyi'i bud med bsten pa ltar gyi bde ba chen po'i ting nge 'dzin bskyed mi nus pa yin la, phyi'i bud med rnyed kyang de spangs nas ye rgya la brten par gsungs pa ni snga ma las bzlog pa la dgongs so
snga ma.english: When they state this way that--if you can't find an outer woman, then you can practice with an imaginary one--it's with reference to the fact that practice with an imaginary partner doesn't have the capacity to bring on in us the meditation of great bliss in the same way that practice with an actual partner does.  To say though that you do find an outer woman, and then leave off practicing with Her, and practice instead with an imaginary woman, is to interpret the lines in a completely opposite way than what we've seen above.

snga ma.acip: SGRON GSAL 'GYUR RNYING LAS, SEMS BRTAN PA THOB PAS PHYI'I PHYAG RGYA LA BRTEN PA ZHES 'BYUNG YANG 'GYUR SNGA MA BDE'O,,
snga ma.wylie: sgron gsal 'gyur rnying las, sems brtan pa thob pas phyi'i phyag rgya la brten pa zhes 'byung yang 'gyur snga ma bde'o
snga ma.english: Now it is true that the older translation of the Lamp that Illuminates says here that "Once you've reached a firm understanding, then you can practice with an outer partner," but the above translation seems preferable.

snga ma.acip: DE LA YANG RLUNG SEMS GNYIS SNYING KHAR BSDUS PA'I SDUD RIM DANG BYANG SEMS RDO RJE'I RTZER PHAB PA LAS STONG PA BZHI BSKYED PA GANG BYED KYANG NUS MOD KYANG, GTZO BOR NI SNGA MA BYED DO,,
snga ma.wylie: de la yang rlung sems gnyis snying khar bsdus pa'i sdud rim dang byang sems rdo rje'i rtser phab pa las stong pa bzhi bskyed pa gang byed kyang nus mod kyang, gtso bor ni snga ma byed do
snga ma.english: It is admittedly true that you can elicit the four forms of bliss both through a practice of the stages of dissolution which brings both the winds and thoughts to gather at the heart, and by having the element of enlightenment descend to the tip of the diamond rod; but the main practice here is the former.

These you can learn from the texts on the Five Stages in the secret teachings of Highest Bliss. * * * In His Great Book on the Stages of the Way of the Secret Word, Je Rinpoche describes these four in terms of the progression of a process (S05281, f. 408b):"}

snga ma.acip: DES NA BDE BA CHEN PO RTZAL DU BTON NAS 'CHAD DGOS PA LA BDE CHEN 'DREN PA'I THABS SU NANG GI RDO RJE LUS KYI GNAD CHE SAR DMIGS PA GTAD DE SGOM PA DANG, SHES RAB MA'I GZUGS KYI RNAM PA CAN LA BRTEN NAS BDE CHEN 'DREN PA GNYIS LAS, SNGA MA NI BLA MED KYI RGYUD SDE KHYAD PAR CAN RNAMS LAS MI 'DRA BA MANG DU GSUNGS SO,,
snga ma.wylie: des na bde ba chen po rtsal du bton nas 'chad dgos pa la bde chen 'dren pa'i thabs su nang gi rdo rje lus kyi gnad che sar dmigs pa gtad de sgom pa dang, shes rab ma'i gzugs kyi rnam pa can la brten nas bde chen 'dren pa gnyis las, snga ma ni bla med kyi rgyud sde khyad par can rnams las mi 'dra ba mang du gsungs so
snga ma.english: Therefore the only task remaining to them was to concentrate on explaining great bliss.  They first treat the various methods for bringing on this bliss; on the inside, we do meditations where we direct our focus towards the most important of the crucial points of the diamond body.  And then we can also bring on the bliss by practicing with the form of a Woman of Wisdom.  Of these two methods, the former is described in the most exceptional works of the unsurpassed group in a great many different ways.

snga ma.acip: DAM TSIG GI PHYAG RGYA LA BRTEN TSUL SNGAR BSHAD PA DE BRTAN PA NA, LAG PA ZHES BYA BA'I PHYAG RGYA'I SGO NAS ZHES PA'I DON, BLA MA SNGA MA KHA CIG LAG PA'I PHYAG RGYA DNGOS LA 'CHAD, SNGA MA GZHAN KHA CIG LAG PA DANG 'DRA BAR BYANG SEMS 'BYIN PA'I BYA BA BYED PA'I PHYAG RGYA MO DNGOS LA 'CHAD KYANG,
snga ma.wylie: dam tshig gi phyag rgya la brten tshul sngar bshad pa de brtan pa na, lag pa zhes bya ba'i phyag rgya'i sgo nas zhes pa'i don, bla ma snga ma kha cig lag pa'i phyag rgya dngos la 'chad, snga ma gzhan kha cig lag pa dang 'dra bar byang sems 'byin pa'i bya ba byed pa'i phyag rgya mo dngos la 'chad kyang
snga ma.english: We see a section in the scripture which says, "Once your practice with a partner of pledge, as we've described it above, is firm, then we work with the type of partner which is described as the 'partner or mudra of the hands'."  Some Lamas of the past have explained this expression as referring to an actual mudra or sacred gesture performed with the hands.  Other Lamas of days gone by have explained it as referring to an actual female partner, since they draw out the element of the enlightenment in the same way that it would be done by using the hands.

snga ma.acip: 'DI LA 'JIG PA MED PA'I PHYAG RGYA ZHES PA, 'GYUR BA MED PA ZHES BSGYUR BA BDE BAS, DAM TSIG GI PHYAG RGYA 'GYUR BA MED PA'I BDE CHEN TE, 'DI BSGRUB BYA YIN LA, PHYAG RGYA SNGA MA GSUM NI SGRUB BYED YIN NO,,

snga ma.english: This type of partner is spoken of as an "indestructible" partner, but the word would be better translated from the Sanskrit as an "immutable" partner.  As such, the partner of pledge is themselves immutable bliss--the thing which we seek to achieve.  And then the former three types of partners are the means which we use to achieve this one.

snga ma.acip: DE LTAR NA SNGAGS LA 'JUG PA'I GDUL BYA DBANG PO RAB LA RIG MA'I 'DOD YON LA CHAGS MA CHAGS GNYIS LAS PHYI MA LA PHYAG CHEN SGOM PA GSUNGS SHING, SNGA MA LA PHYI'I RIG MA LA CHAGS PA YOD MED GNYIS LAS PHYI MA LA YE RGYA SGOM PA DANG, SNGA MA LA DAM RGYA DANG LAS RGYA GNYIS GNANG BAR BZHED PAS,
snga ma.wylie: de ltar na sngags la 'jug pa'i gdul bya dbang po rab la rig ma'i 'dod yon la chags ma chags gnyis las phyi ma la phyag chen sgom pa gsungs shing, snga ma la phyi'i rig ma la chags pa yod med gnyis las phyi ma la ye rgya sgom pa dang, snga ma la dam rgya dang las rgya gnyis gnang bar bzhed pas
snga ma.english: We can say then that there are two different divisions to disciples who have entered into the secret way and who possess the best of faculties: those who are still attached to the objects of pleasure relating to their Woman of Knowledge, and those who are not.  It is stated that the latter should meditate upon the Great Seal.  The former can be further divided into those who are attracted to an outer Woman of Knowledge and those that are not.  The position taken then is that the latter of these two should be meditating upon an imaginary partner, while the former is allowed both a partner of pledge and an actual partner.

snga ma.acip: DES NA MA RMONGS PA'I KHYAD PAR BSHAD PA YANG DKA' BAR SNANG LA DBANG PO RNON PO'I KHYAD PAR YANG DKA' STE, THABS LA MA RMONGS PA LA BYED NA SNGA MA DANG ZLOS SHING, 'DOD YON GYI CHAGS PA LAM DU BYED PA LA 'DOD NA DE SNGAGS KYI GDUL BYA RAB TU MI SNANG BAS GTZO BO'I GDUL BYA LA KHYAD PAR DE MED PA'I PHYIR RO,,
snga ma.wylie: des na ma rmongs pa'i khyad par bshad pa yang dka' bar snang la dbang po rnon po'i khyad par yang dka' ste, thabs la ma rmongs pa la byed na snga ma dang zlos shing, 'dod yon gyi chags pa lam du byed pa la 'dod na de sngags kyi gdul bya rab tu mi snang bas gtso bo'i gdul bya la khyad par de med pa'i phyir ro
snga ma.english: Given this, we would have to say that it's a difficult thing to define just what it would mean to "not be in the dark."  Which means it would be a difficult thing to say just what it was that made somebody a person "with sharp faculties."  If we say that it refers to someone who is no longer in the dark about the method side of things, then we run the danger of repeating what we've already said.  If we say it refers to someone who knows how to use desire for objects of the senses as a spiritual path, then it wouldn't seem that this person could be the very highest form of practitioner in the way of the secret word--because the primary disciple wouldn't possess this particular distinction.

snga ma.acip: YAB YUM SNYOMS PAR ZHUGS PA LAS, BYANG CHUB KYI SEMS RDO RJE NOR BU'I RTZE MOR SLEB PA NA BDE BA JI LTA BU ZHIG SKYE BA NGOS 'DZIN PA SNGA MA DAM TSIG GI PHYAG RGYA'I SKABS SU BSHAD PA BZHIN NYE BAR BRTAGS TE BDE STONG LA GOMS PA
snga ma.wylie: yab yum snyoms par zhugs pa las, byang chub kyi sems rdo rje nor bu'i rtse mor sleb pa na bde ba ji lta bu zhig skye ba ngos 'dzin pa snga ma dam tshig gi phyag rgya'i skabs su bshad pa bzhin nye bar brtags te bde stong la goms pa
snga ma.english: And then the Man and the Woman go into union.  The element of enlightenment reaches the tip of the diamond rod, and we learn to identify just which of the blisses is coming to us.  And then we undertake the same analysis that we described in the part about the partner of pledge: we accustom ourselves to the practice of bliss and voidness.

snga ma.acip: ,DZAMBU GLING RNAMS LEGS SKYES PA'I, ,LAS KYI SA PAR RAB TU GRAGS, ,LEGS BYAS DANG NI NYES BYAS LAS, ,MCHOG DANG 'BRING DANG THA MA YI, ,SKYE BA SNGA MA'I RNAM SMIN 'DIR, ,SKYE BO KUN LA MTHONG BAR 'GYUR, ZHES GSUNGS PA'I PHYIR,

snga ma.acip: 'DI BRGYAD DAM TSIG CES SOGS RKANG PA GSUM NI, DE YANG SNGA MA RNAMS KYI DON MDOR HRIL GYIS SGRIL NA, SNGAR BSHAD PA LTAR GYI G-YON PA'I KUN SPYOD THAMS CAD BYED PA DANG, RGYUD 'DIR DBANG BSKUR BA'I SGRUB PA PO DANG SLOB DPON LA MI BRNYAS SHING CI NUS KYIS MCHOD PA RNAMS NI DAM TSIG DANG PO DANG,
snga ma.wylie: 'di brgyad dam tshig ces sogs rkang pa gsum ni, de yang snga ma rnams kyi don mdor hril gyis sgril na, sngar bshad pa ltar gyi g-yon pa'i kun spyod thams cad byed pa dang, rgyud 'dir dbang bskur ba'i sgrub pa po dang slob dpon la mi brnyas shing ci nus kyis mchod pa rnams ni dam tshig dang po dang
snga ma.english: We turn next to the three lines [in the Tibetan] that include "This...the eight pledges."  Now we could summarize the points given above in the following way.  The first pledge is that we should, as explained earlier on, observe all the various forms of leftways behavior.  We should never berate those practitioners who have been empowered to follow this secret teachings, nor our Master, and we should further make offerings to them, to the best of our ability.

snga ma.acip: BLA MA SNGA MA RNAMS THOGS MED MIN, ZHES BTON NAS DAM TSIG MED PA SOGS LA, NYON MONGS PA'I 'DOD PA'I DBANG GIS THOGS PA MED PAR BYED PA MIN, ZHES ZER MOD KYANG, 'GREL PA RNAMS NAS, GNYIS SU MED DANG THOGS MED PA, ,ZHES BTON NAS 'CHAD PAS, DE LTAR DU BYA'O,,
snga ma.wylie: bla ma snga ma rnams thogs med min, zhes bton nas dam tshig med pa sogs la, nyon mongs pa'i 'dod pa'i dbang gis thogs pa med par byed pa min, zhes zer mod kyang, 'grel pa rnams nas, gnyis su med dang thogs med pa, ,zhes bton nas 'chad pas, de ltar du bya'o
snga ma.english: We do admittedly see explanations by Lamas of the past where they recite the line as "not untouchable," and claim that it means that we should never do the act where we are untouchable or unstoppable with someone for example who lacks the proper pledges, simply because we overcome by afflicted desire.  The classical commentaries though read the line as "Indivisible and untouchable" and then go on to explain it in these terms--so we should do the same.

snga ma.acip: SNGA MA RNAMS DRUG PA GSANG GNAS SOGS BYIN GYIS RLOB PA SOGS DANG, BDUN PA NI, DGA' BA LA SOGS PA LA DMIGS TE MNYAM PAR 'JOG PA'I BSAM GTAN, TSANGS PA MI GNAS PA'I MYANG 'DAS KYI DON DU SPYOD PA LA 'CHAD MOD KYANG, 'GREL PA GSUM LTAR LEGS SO,,
snga ma.wylie: snga ma rnams drug pa gsang gnas sogs byin gyis rlob pa sogs dang, bdun pa ni, dga' ba la sogs pa la dmigs te mnyam par 'jog pa'i bsam gtan, tshangs pa mi gnas pa'i myang 'das kyi don du spyod pa la 'chad mod kyang, 'grel pa gsum ltar legs so
snga ma.english: Some people in days gone by have interpreted the sixth pledge as meaning that we should be engaging in practices like blessing places of the body such as the secret place.  They say that the seventh pledge is that we should focus on the bliss and so on, maintaining a single-point concentration in union; and that "celibacy" refers to engaging in activities of desire for the purpose of reaching a nirvana where nothing remains.  It's good though if we interpret these things as the three commentaries do.

snga ma.english: The three commentaries read the line as "Partake of it in every way, constantly, without any anger"; but the previous translations are more clear.  And the way in which we "partake in every way" is, incidentally, that we take the element up upon our tongue and drink it down.

snga ma.acip: DAM TSIG BRGYAD KYI GRANGS BYED LUGS DANG, NGOS 'DZIN BYED LUGS SNGA MA RNAMS LA TSUL GZHAN YOD KYANG, PAndI TA GSUM GYI DGONGS PA NI SNGA MA LTAR YIN PAS YID CHES PAR SNANG NGO,,

snga ma.english: There have been other systems, among Lamas of the past, for how we enumerate the eight pledges, and how we identify just what they refer to.  The thinking of the three sages though is as we have described it above, and so it appears that you can safely believe their presentation.

snga ma.acip: 'DIR DAM TSIG RDO RJES KU RU KU LLE LA SOGS PA DANG RANG GI PHYAG RGYA'I BUD MED LA SMAD PA LA RTZA LTUNG DANG BUD MED GZHAN LA SHAN 'DRA RU MDZAD CING 'DUS PA'I RGYAN LA SOGS PA 'GA' ZHIG LAS KYANG RANG GI RIG MA KHYAD PAR CAN LA SMAD PA LA BSHAD PA SNANG NA'ANG RANG GI LUGS NI RANG GI PHYAG RGYA LTA BU LA LCI BA'I KHYAD PAR YOD MOD KYANG RTZA LTUNG DU 'GRO BA'I MTSAMS SNGA MA LTAR RO,,
snga ma.wylie: 'dir dam tshig rdo rjes ku ru ku lle la sogs pa dang rang gi phyag rgya'i bud med la smad pa la rtsa ltung dang bud med gzhan la shan 'dra ru mdzad cing 'dus pa'i rgyan la sogs pa 'ga' zhig las kyang rang gi rig ma khyad par can la smad pa la bshad pa snang na'ang rang gi lugs ni rang gi phyag rgya lta bu la lci ba'i khyad par yod mod kyang rtsa ltung du 'gro ba'i mtshams snga ma ltar ro
snga ma.english: On this particular point, Samaya Vajra says that we commit this root downfall only when we disparage women who are a divine being like Kurukulle, or our own spiritual partner.  He then says that disparaging other women is only an approximation of this downfall. We also see explanations in works such as the Jewel of the Collection which say that this root downfall refers to disparaging that extraordinary being, our own Woman of Knowledge. Nonetheless, our own final position is that--although there is quite certainly a question of a much graver karma in the case where we disparage a woman such as our own spiritual partner--one has nonetheless crossed the line in this downfall when they have acted as we've already described it above.

snga ma.acip: ,ZHES GSUNGS PA'I SNGA MA GNYIS KYI DON PHYI MA GNYIS KYI SHUGS BSTAN GYIS BDE BAR SPYAD PA'I PHAN YON DANG, PHYI MA'I DNGOS BSTAN GYIS DKA' THUB KYI SPYOD PA BYED PA'I NYES DMIGS BSTAN NO,,

snga ma.english: The meaning of the first half of this verse can be inferred from what the second half says--that is, we realize that the first part then refers to the benefits of activities which are more comfortable.  And then the latter part is explicitly presenting the problems of undertaking activities involving spiritual hardships.

snga ma.acip: YANG SHIN TU RTZUB PA'I LUGS BYED NA, GZHAN THAMS CAD SNGA MA DANG 'DRA BA LAS, RLUNG NON PA'I DUS GCIG CES BYA BA'I TSAD NI PUS MO LA BSKOR BA GSUM DANG SE GOL GSUM BSDOMS PA LA GCIG CES BYA STE, KHAMS DANG SBYAR LA SNGA DRO'I THUN LNGA KA LA DE LTA BU LNGA, NYIN PHYED KYI THUN CHUNG LNGA LA RE RE BSNAN PAS GNYIS GNYIS SU BYAS TE THUN CHUNG THA MA LA BCU, DGONGS MO GSUM BYA STE, THUN CHUNG THA MA LA BCO LNGA DE BZHIN DU BSGRES LA, ZHAG GSUM MAM, LNGA'AM, BDUN NAM, BCO LNGAR BSGOM PAR BYA'O,,
snga ma.wylie: yang shin tu rtsub pa'i lugs byed na, gzhan thams cad snga ma dang 'dra ba las, rlung non pa'i dus gcig ces bya ba'i tshad ni pus mo la bskor ba gsum dang se gol gsum bsdoms pa la gcig ces bya ste, khams dang sbyar la snga dro'i thun lnga ka la de lta bu lnga, nyin phyed kyi thun chung lnga la re re bsnan pas gnyis gnyis su byas te thun chung tha ma la bcu, dgongs mo gsum bya ste, thun chung tha ma la bco lnga de bzhin du bsgres la, zhag gsum mam, lnga'am, bdun nam, bco lngar bsgom par bya'o
snga ma.english: If you wish to do this practice in a very drastic way, then do everything the same as before, only every time it says to hold your breath for a single time, make it a "single time" that lasts for a total of three rounds on the knees and three fingersnaps.   If your physical constitution allows it, hold your breath for one more each of these "single times" during each of the five sessions of the early period of the day.   Add then one each for each of the sessions of the period of the middle of the day, thus doubling to ten by the final session of this period.   By the evening then you have tripled, reaching fifteen by this period's final session.   Continue to increase in this pattern as you meditate over the length of three, five, seven, or fifteen days.

snga ma.wylie: de nas gsum pa dbu ma kha dbye ba'i man ngag tsaNDA lI rnal 'byor 'byor dngos ni, lus sngar bas kyang skyil krung dam du bca', ro stod dgye bar bya'o,, mnyam gzhag gi phyag rgya bya, mig sna rtser dbab, srung ba'i 'khor lo dang lha dran pa la sogs pa thams cad snga ma dang 'dra bar byas la
snga ma.english: Now third come the instructions for opening the central channel: the actual deep practice of the fire within.  First put your legs into a crossed position, even tighter than before.  Lift and straighten your torso, and put your hands into the gesture of meditation.  Drop your eyes to the area of your nose, and bring to mind the circle of protection, yourself as the secret Angel, and so forth--everything as you did it before.

snga ma.acip: YANG NYI MA GNYIS PA'I THUN CHUNG DANG PO LA BSKOR BA DANG SE GOL GNYIS, DE NAS RE RE SPEL LA SNGA MA BZHIN BYA ZHING NYI MA GSUM PA LA BSKOR BA DANG SE GOL GSUM, BZHI PA LA BZHI, LNGA BA LA LNGA, DRUG PA LA DRUG, NYI MA BDUN PA LA BDUN, DE LTAR NYIN ZHAG BCU BZHI'O,, NYIN ZHAG BCO LNGA BA'I THUN DANG PO LA BSKOR BA DANG SE GOL BRGYAD, BAR PA LA DGU, PHYI DRO'I CHA LA BCUS SBYANG NGO,,
snga ma.wylie: yang nyi ma gnyis pa'i thun chung dang po la bskor ba dang se gol gnyis, de nas re re spel la snga ma bzhin bya zhing nyi ma gsum pa la bskor ba dang se gol gsum, bzhi pa la bzhi, lnga ba la lnga, drug pa la drug, nyi ma bdun pa la bdun, de ltar nyin zhag bcu bzhi'o,, nyin zhag bco lnga ba'i thun dang po la bskor ba dang se gol brgyad, bar pa la dgu, phyi dro'i cha la bcus sbyang ngo
snga ma.english: During the first group of brief sessions on the second day then build up your practice by doing two rounds and fingersnaps, and for the rest just increase everything on the pattern for the day before.  This means that by the third day you're starting with three rounds and fingersnaps; on the fourth with four; on the fifth with five; on the sixth with six; and on the seventh with seven.  Keeping going this way for a total of fourteen days.  During the first group of brief sessions on the fifteenth day, do eight rounds and fingersnaps; for the middle group do nine; and for the final group of the daytime do ten.

snga ma.acip: DES BSLUS SAM MA BSLUS NA, DANG PO BYUNG BA'I ZLA BA 'OG RNAMS KYI ZHAG LA BRTAG, DE DAG LA SNGA MA BZHIN BYUNG NA DUS SU 'CHI BA'I LTAS YIN PAS 'PHO BA BYA, GAL TE ZLA BA 'OG MA RNAMS LA MA BYUNG NA, PHYI DE LO'I DUS NA BRTAG, DE DAG LA MA BYUNG NA 'CHI BA BSLUS PA YIN,
snga ma.wylie: des bslus sam ma bslus na, dang po byung ba'i zla ba 'og rnams kyi zhag la brtag, de dag la snga ma bzhin byung na dus su 'chi ba'i ltas yin pas 'pho ba bya, gal te zla ba 'og ma rnams la ma byung na, phyi de lo'i dus na brtag, de dag la ma byung na 'chi ba bslus pa yin
snga ma.english: To determine whether death has been ransomed or not, check on the days of the months following the first month of the signs.  If the same thing happens with your breath as before, it's an indication that you're going to die at the expected time, and so you should transfer your consciousness.  If the same thing doesn't happen in the months that follow, then check the following year at the same time.  If you still don't get the previous indications, then you have managed to ransom death.

snga ma.acip: ('JIG RTEN PA RNAMS ZHABS KYI GDAN) ZHES PA'I 'JIG RTEN PA NI KHA CIG TSANGS PA SOGS PHYOGS SKYONG BCU LA 'DOD CING, 'JIG RTEN SKYONG BA BZHI SOGS LA'ANG BSHAD DGOS PAR SEMS LA, LHA DE RNAMS GDAN GYI NGO NGOR MOS PA TZAM DANG, LHA'I RNAM PA CAN GNYIS LAS SNGA MA BDE,
snga ma.wylie: ('jig rten pa rnams zhabs kyi gdan) zhes pa'i 'jig rten pa ni kha cig tshangs pa sogs phyogs skyong bcu la 'dod cing, 'jig rten skyong ba bzhi sogs la'ang bshad dgos par sems la, lha de rnams gdan gyi ngo ngor mos pa tsam dang, lha'i rnam pa can gnyis las snga ma bde
snga ma.english: These "and the worldly" are said then to "provide His platform."  Some commentators upon this line say that the "worldly" mentioned here are the Pure One and the rest; and it seems to me that you would have to explain them as well as beings such as the Four Protectors of the World.  There is an option here where you could either simply imagine that these worldly gods constituted the essence of the platform, or that the platform actually took the appearance of the gods--the former of these would seem to be more workable. Bringing Forth the Retinue

snga ma.english: In some texts we see a different idea: There are 101 which can be treated with medicine And 101 which respond to constant care; Yet another 101 can be cured with both, And there are 101 which nothing can help. snga ma.acip: BCU TSAN SNGA MA NI RGYUD SDE GONG MA DANG, PHYI MA NI 'OG MA'I SLOB DPON GYI MTSAN NYID YIN PAR BSHAD LA, GZHAN YANG, DKYIL 'KHOR SOGS (BRI BA DANG,) MDO SNGAGS KYI CHOS ('CHAD) PA LA YANG (MKHAS PA'I RDO RJE 'DZIN PA'I GTZO) BO STE DE 'DRA BA'I SNGAGS KYI SLOB DPON (LA) ZHES SO,,
snga ma.wylie: bcu tshan snga ma ni rgyud sde gong ma dang, phyi ma ni 'og ma'i slob dpon gyi mtshan nyid yin par bshad la, gzhan yang, dkyil 'khor sogs (bri ba dang,) mdo sngags kyi chos ('chad) pa la yang (mkhas pa'i rdo rje 'dzin pa'i gtso) bo ste de 'dra ba'i sngags kyi slob dpon (la) zhes so
snga ma.english: The first set of ten is explained as presenting the qualifications of a Master in the highest group of the secret teachings, while the second set present those of a Master in the lower groups of these teachings.  You can also describe the Master of the Secret Word as someone who is a master at drawing things like a secret world, and who is as well a master of explaining both the open and the secret teachings.  And it is to one such as this, to the King of the Holders of Diamond, that we make our supplication.

snga ma.acip: MDOR NA SKYE SHI 'PHOS NAS NGO MA SHES PA MA GTOGS, TSE SNGA MA RNAMS SU (YANG YANG) MA BYAS TE (DRIN GYIS BSKYANGS PA'I TSUL) LEGS PAR (BSAM NAS,)
snga ma.wylie: mdor na skye shi 'phos nas ngo ma shes pa ma gtogs, tshe snga ma rnams su (yang yang) ma byas te (drin gyis bskyangs pa'i tshul) legs par (bsam nas,)
snga ma.english: To sum then, these Mothers of mine have paid me every form of kindness, over and over again, during my past lives--it's just that, because of the fact that I have changed lives so many times, been born and died again so many times, that I now fail to recognize them for who they are.  This is something we must contemplate upon, carefully.
